author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Have meat cut into small cubes.
Roll in flour, aeasoned with salt and pepper, and brown in a little hot lard.
Brown the chopped onions in lard.
Mix the tomato puree with boiling water, heat and pour over meat and onion.
Add bay leaves and simmer 1 hour.
Add minced onion, celery, grcen pepper, carrots and potatoes.
Simmer until all ingredients are done—about 1 hour.
Liquid may be thickened with flour for gravy.
recipes.name: Beef Stew

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 1 pound beef chuck, or round steak

instructions: Soak kidney in cold salted water for 30 minutes.
Cut meat in 1-inch cubes.
Drain kidney and cut into even smaller cubes.
Let sliced onion brown slowly in lard or butter, then add meats and brown well on all sides.
Add salt, pepper and worcestershire sauce and 1/2 cup boiling water.
Simmer slowly for 2 hours or until very tender.
Mix the flour with 1/4 cup cold water and stir into the meat to thicken it.
Transfer to baking dish or individual casseroles and cover top with thin pastry with hole in center for escape of steam.
Bake 30 minutes in a 375° f oven.
recipes.name: Beefsteak and Kidney Pie

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: mushroom
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup mushroom, stems and pieces (if desired)

instructions: Dip liver in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes, then cut in fine cubes and dredge with flour.
Chop onion, green pepper and mushrooms and let fry in butter or oil with the chopped liver until liver is lightly browned (about 10 minutes).
Add tomatoes, seasonings and garlic, and cover.
Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes.
Serve over boiled spaghetti with a sprinkling of grated dry cheese over the top.
recipes.name: Savory Beef Liver and Spaghetti

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Clean tripe carefully and simmer 1 hours in water to cover, until tender.
Drain.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and cut into oblong pieces the size of an oyster.
Dip in bread crumbs, then in beaten egg to which has been added cold water, then dip in crumbs again.
Fry in hot lard 350° f for 2 minutes on each side.
recipes.name: Tripe Oysters

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Wash hearts and remove enough of center portion to permit addition of the dressing or stuffing.
Dice bacon and fry until crisp.
Combine with bread crumbs.
Season with finely minced onion.
Season cavity in hearts, fill with stuffing, and fasten with skewers.
Roll in flour and brown quickly in hot lard, in a heavy kettle.
Add a small amount of water.
Cover and cook slowly in a moderate oven (350° f) until the hearts are done— 2 to 2-1/2 hours.
Thicken the liquid for gravy if desired.
recipes.name: Baked Stuffed Beef Heart

instructions: Cut oxtails into small pieces, season and roll in flour.
Brown in hot lard in a deep heavy kettle.
Add water and allspice.
Cover.
Simmer 2 to 3 hours or until meat drops from bones.
Strain.
Remove all meat from bones.
To broth, add meat, vegetables and more water if needed.
Simmer 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Serve very hot.
For a thicker soup, cook 1/2 cup rice in the broth with the vegetables.
recipes.name: Oxtail Soup

instructions: Have ribs cut into sections two to three inches long.
Brown in lard.
Brown minced onion.
Add all remaining ingredients to short ribs.
Cover and cook slowly or bake in a moderate oven (350° f) 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until tender.
recipes.name: Barbecued Short Ribs

ingredients.name: minced celery leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon minced celery leaves, or celery

ingredients.name: tomato soup or tomato puree
ingredients.raw: 2 cup tomato soup or tomato puree

instructions: Score steak on both aides.
Cover with mixture of vinegar, salt, pepper, onion and other minced vegetables and let stand for an hour or more.
Sear meat in drippings or lard.
Place in shallow baking dish with mixture in which meat has soaked.
Pour tomato soup or puree over meat and bake for 2 hours at 325°f, or until meat is tender.
recipes.name: Steak with Spanish Sauce

instructions: Combine first eight ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Form into small balls, about 1 1/2 inches in diameter and roll in flour.
Brown balls lightly in lard.
Mix sauce ingredients together thoroughly and boil for three minutes.
Add meat balls and simmer 45 minutes, until meat is well cooked.
Pour mixture over platter of cooked spaghetti and serve with sprinkling of dry grated cheese.
recipes.name: Meat Balls with Spaghetti Sauce

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Brown the onion, green pepper and beef in butter or beef fat in a frying pan.
Add the seasonings.
Make a regulation biscuit dough and spread dough with meat mixture and roll like jelly roll.
If dough is too soft, chill in refrigerator first, then cut in 1 1/2-inch slices.
Place in greased pan, cut side up, brush tops with melted butter.
Bake 20-25 minutes at 450° f.
Serve with brown gravy or cheese sauce.
recipes.name: Beef Biscuit Roll

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Brown meat in lard.
Season.
Add tomatoes, water, sliced onion, and celery.
Cover and cook slowly, or bake in a moderate oven (350° f) about 2 hours.
recipes.name: Crosscut Beef Shank Stew

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: -4 pound rump or chuck pot roast
ingredients.raw: 3 -4 pound rump or chuck pot roast

instructions: Select a three or four-pound rump or chuck pot roast.
Season with salt and pepper.
Brown well on all sides, adding 2 tablespoons of lard to kettle, if necessary.
When browned, spread prepared horseradish over the meat.
Add 1 cup water, cover closely and cook at a simmering temperature about 3 1/2 hours.
Turn the pot roast once or twice so that it will cook evenly.
Thicken the liquid and add water for gravy.
recipes.name: Beef Pot Roast with Horseradish

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Melt butter and add flour.
Add milk slowly, stirring constantly until mixture boils.
Drain horse-radish, combine with lemon juice, seasonings, and pimiento.
Add to cream sauce.
Serve hot with brisket of beef.
recipes.name: Horseradish Sauce

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Select a three or four-pound piece of fresh beef brisket.
Cover with hot water.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook at a simmering temperature three to four hours or until tender.
recipes.name: Beef Brisket with Horseradish

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Precooking: (to be done immediately on receipt of sweetbreads) soak sweetbreads in cold water for 30 minutes, then simmer very gently for 20 minutes in water to which 1 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar have been added for each quart of water used.
Drain, drop into cold water, and remove loose membrane.
Use at once or keep in refrigerator.
Season whole precooked sweetbreads.
Dip in crumbs, beaten egg, and again in crumbs.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove to hot pan and keep warm.
Brown sweetbreads in hot drippings.
recipes.name: Sweetbreads and Bacon

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 2 pound beef chuck, or neck meat

instructions: Cut meat into 1-inch cubes.
Let onions brown in butter, then add meat and let it brown lightly.
Add caraway seed, marjoram, chopped garlic, and enough paprika to effect a noticeable red color.
Add water and sait, cover and simmer for 2 1/2 hours.
Add more water if necessary.
Whole potatoes may be added to the goulash 1 hour before done.
Some goulash recipes call for the addition of tomatoes.
Strained tomatoes may be substituted for water in this recipe.
recipes.name: Hungarian Goulash

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Soak brains in cold salted water 1/2 hour.
Skin and remove all fiber.
Cut or chop into small pieces.
Put into frying pan in which butter, onions and parsley have been heated.
Stir until brains are cooked 10-12 minutes.
Add eggs beaten with 2 tablespoons cold water.
Cook over moderate fire and stir until set.
Season, and serve on toast.
Garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Beef Brains and Scrambled Eggs

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cut short ribs into individual squares and flour them.
Brown slowly on all sides in lard, allowing 20-30 minutes for browning.
Add seasonings, onion (minced), and 1/2 cup water.
Cover closely and simmer for 2 hours.
Add vegetables, cut small, and continue cooking for 30-40 minutes.
Remove meat to platter, thicken the vegetable gravy with 1 tablespoon flour stirred into 1/2 cup water.
recipes.name: Braised Short Ribs of Beef with Vegetables

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cover meat with boiling water.
If fresh brisket is used, add 11% tablespoons salt to cooking water.
Simmer slowly in covered kettle 3 to 5 hours or until tender.
Forty-five minutes before serving add onions and carrots.
Fifteen minutes later add quartered cabbage.
Cook beets separately.
Serve on a large platter, with the meat in the center and the vegetables arranged around it.
recipes.name: New England Dinner

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Chop onion.
Brown onion and celery in lard.
Combine with green pepper, salt, eggs, bread crumbs and water to makc a dressing.
Add half of the dressing (1 1/2 cups) to the meat, mixing well.
Pat out half the meat mixture in a two-quart loaf pan.
Cover with remaining dressing, then top with remaining meat mixture.
Bake in a moderate oven (350° f) 1 1/4 hours.
Baste twice with tomato juice and butter to keep loaf moist.
recipes.name: Western Ranch Meat Loaf

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Add water and seasonings to beef shank and simmer about 2 hours or until tender.
Pick meat from bones and return meat to stock.
Add vegetables, soup stock and barley.
Simmer 25-30 minutes.
Add worcestershire sauce and serve.
recipes.name: Beef Shank Barley Soup

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: blade or round bone chuck steak
ingredients.raw: 1 pound blade or round bone chuck steak, cut 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Rub the flour, salt and pepper into the steak.
Brown slowly in hot skillet.
When brown on both sides add the mushroom soup, cover tightly and let simmer for 1 hour.
recipes.name: Chuck Steak with Mushroom Gravy

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cut oxtail in short lengths for ox joints, roll in flour and brown in 1 tablespoon butter slowly, about 15 minutes.
Add water, tomatoes and seasonings; simmer about 2 hours or until tender.
Brown carrots, onions, garlic and turnips in 1 tablespoon butter 3-4 minutes; add to meat and cook 1/2 hour longer.
Add lemon juice the last 10 minutes of cooking.
recipes.name: Braised Ox Joints

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: to 3 lbs. beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 to 3 lbs. beef chuck, or rump

instructions: Brown meat slowly in lard.
When well browned add tomato juice, salt and garlic.
Cover tightly and simmer until tender, approximately 3 1/2 hours.
Add vegetables 45 minutes before done.
recipes.name: Tomato Pot Roast

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cover with cold water, bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours, or until tender.
Keep tongue in the liquid until cool enough to handle, then remove outer skin.
Serve in thin slices, cold.
recipes.name: Beef Tongue and Spinach (Smoked or Pickled)
recipes.yield: 4 servings to the pound of meat

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cover with cold water, add 1/2 teaspoons salt to each quart of water; bring to a boil.
Simmer slowly until tender.
Allow 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours.
Keep tongue in the liquid until cool enough to handle, then remove outer skin.
Serve hot slices with hot piquant sauce or cooked spinach or other greens dressed with french dressing.
recipes.name: Beef Tongue and Spinach (Fresh)
recipes.yield: 4 servings to the pound of meat

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cut ribs in pieces for serving.
Place in baking dish.
Slice onions over the top and add other ingredients.
Cover and cook in a moderate oven (350° f) about 2 hours.
recipes.name: Barbecued Spareribs

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Soak the brains in cold water.
Remove membranes.
Simmer very gently for 15 minutes in water to which 1 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon of vinegar have been addedtoeach quart ’ of water.
Drain; chill in cold water.
Drain.
Season, roll in flour and fry in hot fat until nicely browned on both sides—about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Fried Pork Brains

author: American Meat Institute

ingredients.name: pork tenderloin
ingredients.raw: pork tenderloin, cut crosswise in 2-in. pieces

ingredients.name: light cream
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup light cream, or top milk

instructions: Place each slice of pork tenderloin between pieces of waxed paper and flatten with wooden potato masher or mallet.
Season with salt and pepper; sprinkle with flour, sauté in lard or bacon drippings until well browned.
Place in baking dish.
Add 1/2 cup light cream or top milk to drippings in pan, bring to a boil and pour over meat.
Cover and simmer, or bake in moderate oven (350° f) about 1/2 hour, or until tender.
One large tenderloin will provide 6 pieces.
Allow 1 to 2 pieces per portion.
recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin Baked in Cream

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Place spareribs and water in covered pan.
Simmer for 2 hours.
Add sauerkraut, and cook for 15-20 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Spareribs and Sauerkraut

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Fry the salt pork until crisp, then remove the pieces.
Cook the onion in the fat for a few minutes, then add the crisp salt pork, celery and bread cubes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread one section of the spareribs with the dressing.
Cover with the other section and sew or tie in place.
Sprinkle the outside with salt and pepper and rub with flour.
Lay the stuffed ribs on a rack in an open roasting pan and bake, uncovered, in a 350° f oven for 30 minutes to the pound (about 2 hours).
recipes.name: Celery Stuffed Spareribs

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Soak brains in cold salted water 1/2 hr.
Skin and remove all fiber.
Cut or chop into small pieces.
Put into frying pan in which butter, onion and parsley have been heated.
Stir until brains are cooked (10-12 min).
Add eggs beaten with 2 tablespoons cold water.
Cook over moderate fire and stir until set.
Season and serve on toast.
Garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Pork Brains and Eggs

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Brown country style backbones.
Add seasoning, cover and cook in a moderate oven (350° f) for about 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until well-done.
Pork always requires thorough cooking at moderate temperature to bring out the full rich flavor.
recipes.name: Backbones Farm Style

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Slice liver in 1/2-inch slices.
Cut in 1-in pieces.
Season and dredge with four.
Brown sliced onion and liver in lard (or bacon drippings).
Add tomatoes.
Cover and cook slowly 20 to 30 minutes.
Serve over the hot lima beans.
recipes.name: Pork Liver with Spanish Sauce and Lima Beans

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Dredge meat with flour; brown in lard.
Pour tomatoes over meat, add seasonings, onion, carrots and green pepper.
Place in covered pan and cook in slow oven (325° f) for 1 hour.
recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin Creole

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cut kidneys in half, remove outer membrane and heavy veins.
Soak 1 hr in cold salted water.
Drain; add fresh cold water; bring to boiling point.
Drain; blanch under cold water.
Cut into thin slices.
Dust lightly with flour and cook very slowly in fat for thirty minutes.
Season with paprika and salt.
Beat the eggs and add the milk or water, salt and pepper.
Cook in fat until done.
Place scrambled eggs in center of platter with kidneys in border around them.
recipes.name: Pork Kidneys and Scrambled Eggs

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Wipe the meat with a damp cloth.
Cover with water and allow to simmer until nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Season.
Prepare vegetables and add carrots and onions whole.
Cook fifteen minutes and add whole potatoes.
Cook twenty minutes and add quartered cabbage.
Cook until cabbage is done.
recipes.name: Country 'Boiled' Dinner

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Let slices of liver stand in hot water for 10 minutes and then grind with the onion and bacon.
Add eggs, crumbs, parsley and seasonings and pack firmly into a loaf pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350° f.
May be sliced cold if desired.
recipes.name: Pork Liver Loaf

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Barely cover the pork feet with cold salted water.
Heat to boiling point and simmer until tender, about 3 hours.
Arrange on a greased baking sheet and bake in a hot oven (450° f) until browned.
recipes.name: Baked Pork Feet

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Remove heavy veins from kidneys.
Cube kidneys and and soak 1 hr in cold salted water.
Drain; add fresh cold water; bring to boiling point.
Drain; add 3 cups cold water.
Bring to boiling point, skim, add sliced onions and seasonings.
Simmer about 1 hr until kidneys are tender.
Brown flour in fat and gradually add kidneys and stock, stirring constantly.
Cook slowly about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Pork Kidney Stew

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Place whole knuckles in boiling salted water.
Cover and simmer until meat is tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
20 minutes before serving, pour off most of water and add the sauerkraut.
Let heat thoroughly.
Serve the meat on a bed of sauerkraut.
recipes.name: Pork Knuckles and Sauerkraut

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Wash and clean hearts.
Slice or chop the hearts into 3/4-inch pieces across the grain.
Season.
Roll in four and brown in bacon fat, in a heavy kettle.
Add sliced onions, tomatoes and hot water.
Cook slowly, covered, on top of the stove for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Add carrots the last hour.
Add more water from time to time if original amount cooks away.
Thicken liquid for gravy.
recipes.name: Fricasseed Pork Hearts

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Cover pork feet with cold water; add carrot, onion, celery, salt and spices; simmer gently about 3 hrs or until tender enough for bones to slip out.
Drain, slip out bones and press into shape with hands.
Place between two platters with a weight on top; let cool overnight.
Separate; dip in melted butter; roll in fine bread crumbs.
Let stand in refrigerator after patting well.
Pan-broil on lightly greased skillet to a golden brown, turning frequently.
Garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Pan-Broiled Boneless Pork Feet

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Have backbone loosened from ribs so that carving will be easy.
Season with salt and pepper and place with the fat side up, bones down, in an open roasting pan.
Make an incision and insert a meat thermometer so that the center of the bulb reaches the center of the fleshiest part of the meat.
Put the roast in a moderate oven (350° f) and cook without covering and without adding water.
It will be done when the meat thermometer registers 185° f.
Allow about 30 min.
Per pound for roasting.
Make a gravy from part of the drippings and season it with sage.
recipes.name: Roast Loin of Pork

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Dip chops in flour and brown well on both sides in lard or meat drippings.
Season with salt and pepper, add mustard in tiny dots to each chop and pour milk (undiluted) over meat.
Cover and cook in 350° f oven for 45-50 minutes.
Serve on chop plate garnished with parsley or celery leaves.
recipes.name: Pork Chops Braised in Milk

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Wash hearts and remove all veins and tough fibers.
Cut in small pieces and cover with water for 15 min.
Drain; add boiling water to cover.
Add cut carrot, onion and celery.
Simmer gently 3-4 hrs.
Mix flour and melted butter and stir into the hot stew.
Add vinegar and salt, and stir until thickened.
Serve with border of steamed rice.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
recipes.name: Stewed Pork Hearts with Rice Border

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Wash the pork feet.
Cover them with cold water and cook them (do not boil) for about 2 or 3 hours, until tender.
Season, and serve on hot platter with spinach or other greens.
recipes.name: Pork Feet and Greens

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Lay the ham fat side up on a rack in an open roasting pan.
Sprinkle cut surface with salt and pepper.
Make incision and insert meat thermometer so that center of bulb reaches center of fleshiest part, (bulb should not rest on fat or bone.
) Place ham, uncovered, in moderate oven (350° f.
) And roast until done.
It will be done when thermometer registers 185° f.
Allow about 30 min per pound for roasting.
When almost done, remove from oven, and take off rind (if not already removed).
Score fat in diagonal lines, stick with whole cloves, rub surface with brown sugar-mustard mixture.
Return to oven to finish.
recipes.name: Roast Fresh Ham

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Have chops cut double thickness and pocketed for stuffing on bone side of chop.
Rub inside and out with salt.
Make dressing by mixing crumbs, pineapple, juice, seasonings, celery, beaten egg and melted butter.
Pack into pockets in chops.
Place chops on rack in roasting pan, sprinkle with salt and pepper and place in 350° f.
Oven for 1 1/4 hrs.
recipes.name: Pineapple Stuffed Pork Chops

author: American Meat Institute
instructions: Pan-broil the bacon.
Season and dredge the liver with flour and braise in 4 cup of bacon drippings.
After browning add 2 tablespoons of catch- up to 1/4 cup of water and simmer approximately 20-25 minutes.
recipes.name: Braised Pork Liver and Bacon

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: crushed ready-to-serve wheat cereal
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cup crushed ready-to-serve wheat cereal, flakes

instructions: Set oven for moderate, 350 degrees.
Mix and sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spices.
Add cereal flakes, walnuts, and apple.
Combine egg, brown sugar, buttermilk, and shortening.
Add.
Mixx just enough to moisten dry ingredients.
Do not beat.
Turn into greased loaf pan 8 by 4 by 3 inches.
Bake 1 hour.
recipes.name: Apple Walnut Loaf

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Sift together flour, baking soda, salt, and sugar.
Combine eggs and buttermilk: stir into flour mixture: beat until smooth: add shortening.
Bake on hot griddle.
Serve with butter and syrup.
recipes.name: Buttermilk Griddle Cakes

ingredients.name: daily chocolate milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup daily chocolate milk, (also called chocolate drink)

instructions: Mash banana to a pulp.
Add chocolate milk and vanilla.
Shake well.
Or, slice banana into an electric blender, add remaining ingredients, and blend until thick and creamy.
recipes.name: Chocolate-Banana Milkshake

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cups evaporated milk diluted with
ingredients.raw: 3 cup whole milk, or 1 1/2 cups evaporated milk diluted with

instructions: Combine cocoa, sugar, and salt in saucepan.
Add water: boil 2 minutes, stirring.
Add milk; heat thoroughly but do not boil.
Add vanilla.
Beat with rotary egg beater.
recipes.name: Cocoa

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the oil, and add the lemon juice slowly.
Add the salt and paprika.
Beat one minute.
Add the cheese.
Serve very cold, poured over the asparagus salad.
recipes.name: Asparagus Salad Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: carmelized syrup or maple syrup
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon carmelized syrup or maple syrup

instructions: Mix the cream, vanilla and syrup.
Add the sugar (sifted) until the right consistency to spread.
Spread carefully between the layers and on the top.
Set aside to cool, and to allow the icing to 'set.
' More sugar may be needed in making the icing.
recipes.name: Confectioner's Icing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix all the ingredients in the order given.
Stir well for two minutes, and place in a buttered mould.
Steam two hours on the stove or in the fireless cooker.
Serve hot with lemon sauce.
recipes.name: Steamed Date Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the ingredients in the order named.
Shake thoroughly in a glass jar.
Serve cold.
recipes.name: Bettina's Russian Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix thoroughly the beans, celery, pimento, egg, salt and paprika.
Add the salad dressing and serve on a piece of crisp lettuce.
recipes.name: Bettina's Green String Bean Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Heat the vinegar, add the cloves, sugar, salt and pepper.
Pour over the beets, cut in one-third inch slices.
Allow to stand one hour before serving.
recipes.name: Bettina's Spiced Beets

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the corn, egg, bread crumbs, salt, pepper and sugar.
Shape into cakes two inches in diameter and one-half an inch thick.
Grease a griddle or a frying-pan thoroughly, and when very hot, place fritters on the pan.
When brown on one side, turn over onto the other side.
Serve hot, with syrup.
recipes.name: Corn Oysters

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place the sponge cakes around the edges of a moistened mould.
Soak the gelatin in cold water five minutes.
Add the hot milk.
Stir until it dissolves.
Add the sugar and vanilla.
Allow the gelatin mixture to cool.
When it begins to thicken, fold in the cream.
Beat until the mixture holds its shape.
Pour into the mould.
Allow to remain two hours in a cold place.
recipes.name: Charlotte Russe

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the salt, paprika, celery salt, olive oil and lemon juice.
Beat one minute.
Add the tomatoes and green pepper.
Place in the ice box for half an hour.
Arrange the lettuce leaves on salad plates.
Place two slices of tomato on each portion.
Pour the oil mixture over the tomatoes.
recipes.name: Tomato Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Pick over the currants, leaving the berries on the stems.
Wash and drain.
Place in an enamel preserving kettle and add one cup of water.
Cook slowly until the currants are white.
Strain through a jelly bag.
Boil the juice five minutes in a shallow pan.
It is better to boil small quantities at a time, as this makes the jelly much clearer.
When the juice has all been boiled, measure, and add an equal amount of heated sugar.
Boil three minutes, or until it jells when tried on a cold saucer.
Pour into sterilized glasses.
Allow to stand in the sun twenty-four hours.
Cover with boiling paraffin and put away in a cool, dark place.
This recipe makes about five glasses or two and a half pints.
recipes.name: Currant Jelly

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the cheese, nuts, butter and salt thoroughly.
Spread evenly over the double wafers.
Bake in a moderate oven until a delicate brown on the top.
recipes.name: Wafers Bettina

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange the pieces of lettuce on the salad plates.
Sprinkle with salt, arrange on each portion a slice of pineapple, four white cherries, four pecan nuts and one maraschino cherry.
Place one tablespoon of salad dressing on each slice of pineapple, then arrange the fruits and nuts in any desired design.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Fruit Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the fat and flour carefully, add the water, salt and paprika.
Cook one minute, stirring constantly, add one-half of the milk and cook until the mixture gets very thick.
Beat one minute, add the rest of the milk and cook again, still stirring continuously.
When the sauce is very thick and creamy, add the mushrooms.
Stir over a hot fire for one minute.
This allows the mushrooms to get hot.
Serve one tablespoonful of the mixture around each croquette.
The sauce may be reheated by adding two tablespoons of milk, and placing over a hot fire.
recipes.name: Mushroom Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix and beat thoroughly the lemon juice, salt and paprika.
Add the oil very slowly.
Beat for three minutes.
Add one tablespoon to each portion of the salad.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: French Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the neufchatel and cottage cheese, the salt, paprika, cream and salad dressing.
Stir until very creamy.
Spread on a piece of waxed paper to the thickness of one inch.
Place in the refrigerator, on the ice if possible.
When cold and hard, cut in pieces three-fourths of an inch square.
Place a cube in the center of the grapefruit circle on each side plate.
recipes.name: Cheese Mixture

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange two pieces of lettuce on each salad plate.
Carefully peel the grapefruit and remove all the tough fibres and the white skin.
Cut the grapefruit into one-inch pieces.
Arrange the pieces in a circle upon the lettuce leaves.
In the center of the circle, place the cheese mixture.
Pour the salad dressing over the lettuce, cheese and grapefruit.
recipes.name: Blackstone Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and mix well.
Add the egg-yolks which have been well beaten.
Mix and sift the flour, baking powder and salt, and add these, with the orange juice and the orange and lemon extracts to the first mixture.
Beat vigorously for two minutes.
Fill a twelve-inch square pan which has been prepared with waxed paper, with the mixture.
Bake thirty minutes in a moderate oven.
When cool, cover with the icing and cut into twelve pieces.
recipes.name: Bettina Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the cheese, pickles, olives and salt.
Add the salad dressing.
Spread this mixture between two thin pieces of buttered bread.
Press firmly together and cut into fancy shapes.
recipes.name: Bettina Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: nut meats
ingredients.raw: 1 cup nut meats, cut in small pieces

ingredients.name: oranges
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup oranges, cut in small pieces

instructions: Mix the pineapple, nut meats, oranges, marshmallows, cherries and figs.
Mix the whipped cream and the salad dressing.
Pour this over the fruit.
Serve on lettuce leaves which have been washed and placed on serving plates.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Fruit Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the cherries, sugar, flour and salt.
Allow to stand five minutes.
Add the water.
Pour the mixture into a deep glass or china baking dish.
Mix and sift the flour, taking powder, salt and sugar.
Cut in the butter with a knife.
Add the milk, mixing until a soft dough is formed.
Shape it with the hands to fit over the cherries.
Make three slits in the dough to permit the steam to escape.
Place in a moderate oven and bake for thirty minutes.
Serve in the baking dish.
Plain cream or whipped cream should be served with the cobbler.
recipes.name: Cherry Cobbler

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Roll 1/4 of white bread dough in circle 9 inches in diameter and 1/4 inch thick.
Cut into 12 wedges.
Roll up each wedge starting at round edge.
Place on greased baking sheet with pointed end under; shape like crescents; brush with melted butter or margarine; sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Let rise.
Bake as for pocketbook rolls.
recipes.name: Poppy Seed Half-Moons

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for hot, 400f.
Cream shortening and sugar until light and fluffy: stir in eggs, then corn meal.
Mix and sift flour, baking powder, and salt.
Stir currants into flour mixture.
Add to corn meal mixture.
Add milk; stir just enough to moisten.
Spoon into greased muffin pans.
Bake 25 minutes.
recipes.name: Quaker Muffins

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Scald milk; stir in sugar, salt, and shortening; stir until sugar dissolves; cool to lukewarm.
Sprinkle yeast on water; stir till dissolved.
Add milk mixture.
Stir in 3 cups of the flour; beat till smooth.
Stir in remaining flour.
Turn out on a lightly floured board.
Knead: fold dough over toward you.
Press down away from you with the heel of your hand.
Give dough a quarter turn.
Continue until dough is smooth and elastic, and does not stick to the board.
Place in a greased bowl; brush top with melted shortening.
Cover with a damp cloth; let rise in warm place 80Â° to 85Â° until doubled in bulk (about 1 hour).
Punch down: turn out on lightly floured board.
Divide dough in half.
Shape into 2 loaves: place in greased loaf pans, 8 by 4 by 3 inches.
Cover with a damp cloth: let rise in a warm place 80f to 85f until center of dough is slightly higher than the edges of the pans, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile set oven for hot, 400f.
Bake 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Remove from pans immediately and cool on a rack.
recipes.name: White Bread Loaf

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: melted butter
ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoon melted butter, or margarine, divided

ingredients.name: grated process American cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 cup grated process American cheese, (1/2 pound)

instructions: Cook spinach as directed on package.
Cook onion in 2 tablespoons of the butter or margarine until tender; add to spinach.
Preheat broiler.
Place fish fillets in a greased shallow baking pan; dot with remaining butter: sprinkle with lemon juice.
Broil 2 inches below heat (without turning) 8 to 10 minutes or until easily flaked with a fork but still moist.
Melt cheese in milk until smooth.
Transfer fish to baking dish 12 by 8 by 2 inches.
Top with spinach; pour cheese sauce over all.
Broil 4 inches below heat until golden.
recipes.name: Broiled Fillets Florentine

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: sea scallops
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound sea scallops, fresh or frozen, cut

instructions: Defrost sea scallops, if frozen.
Cook sea scallops 5 minutes in boiling salted water to cover; drain.
Cut in halves or quarters.
Add to vichysoisse; heat to serving temperature but do not allow to boil.
Garnish with cut chives.
recipes.name: Quick Scallop Chowder

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.raw: 6 scallions, (spring onion) or 1 tablespoon finely cut chives

instructions: Rub tureen or large bowl with garlic clove; spear garlic with toothpick and leave in bowl.
Add tomatoes and cucumber.
Slice scallions with about 2 inches of green tops; add with celery.
Add oil and vinegar.
Sprinkle with salt, freshly ground pepper, and monosodium glutamate; mix well.
Add tomato juice.
Chill at least 3 hours.
Remove garlic.
Serve with hot cheese crackers.
recipes.name: Salad Soup

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Scald milk.
Add shortening, sugar, and salt.
Stir until sugar dissolves; cool to lukewarm.
Dissolve yeast in water; combine with milk mixture.
Stir in half the flour; add eggs; beat well.
Add enough of remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Turn out on lightly floured board; knead till smooth and elastic.
(See recipe for white bread) put in a greased bowl; brush with shortening; cover; let rise in a warm place, 80Â° to 85Â° till double in bulk (about 2 hours).
Turn out on floured board; roll into a rectangle 8 by 12 inches.
Brush with butter.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up like jelly roll; shape into a ring on greased baking sheet; pinch ends.
From the outside, cut through the ring toward center almost all the way through in 1- inch slices.
Fan out slices slightly to side.
Brush with shortening; cover; let rise about 45 minutes or till double in bulk.
Meanwhile set oven for moderate 375f.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
While warm spread with confectioners' sugar icing; sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
recipes.name: Scandinavian Coffee Cake

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: blueberries
ingredients.note: fresh or well drained; canned or frozen
ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup blueberries, fresh or well drained; canned or frozen

instructions: Set oven for hot, 400f.
Cream shortening; add sugar gradually, creaming thoroughly.
Beat eggs; add.
Mix and sift 1-2/3 cups flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add alternately with milk to first mixture.
Mix blueberries with remaining flour; stir in lightly.
Bake in greased muffin pans 1/2 hour.
recipes.name: Blueberry Muffins

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for hot, 425f.
Grease a 9 by 13-inch baking pan.
Prepare biscuit mix as directed on package.
Roll out on a lightly floured board, in rectangle about 8 by 16 inches.
Brush with melted butter or margarine.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Sprinkle over dough.
Roll up like jelly roll, and press long edge firmly to keep from unrolling.
Cut in 1-inch slices.
Place, cut side up, in pan.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes.
recipes.name: Cinnamon Whirls

author: Oracle Ace
Lillian Buziak

ingredients.name: hoisin sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon hoisin sauce, plus additional for wraps

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.raw: 1 cucumber, peeled, seeded, chopped, about 1 1/4 cup

ingredients.name: small mint
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup small mint, sprigs for garnish

instructions: Heat peanut oil in heavy skillet over medium-high heat add onion and saute until slightly brown, approx 3 min.
Add turkey and saute until cooked through, breaking up any large pieces, approx 7 min.
Fold in peanut sauce, hoisin sauce, and 1 tbl soy sauce; heat through.
Stir in cucumber and chopped mint season to taste with salt and pepper.
Transfer turkey mixture to bowl.
Place mint sprigs and lettuce leaves on platter.
To make wraps, brush lettuce leaf with hoisin sauce, spoon turkey mixture onto lettuce leaf, add a few mint sprigs, fold in sides over filling, roll up, and enjoy.
recipes.name: Asian Turkey Wraps

author: Oracle Ace
Vikki Lira
instructions: Heat olive oil in a sautÃƒÂ© pan over medium high heat.
Add onions and garlic and saute until soft, approximately 5 minutes.
Add green chile and sautÃƒÂ© for 3-4 minutes more until chile is heated through.
Remove from heat.
Trim excess fat from pork roast and season with salt & pepper.
Place pork roast in a large slow cooker (5-6 quarts).
Cover roast with onion mixture.
Add chicken broth to cover roast entirely.
Add oregano and optional tomatoes/tomatillos.
Cover pot and cook for 6-8 hours on medium-low.
At end of cook time, remove roast from slow cooker.
Let cool for a few minutes.
Roast should easily break into a few manageable chunks.
Trim fat and shred meat into bite size pieces using 2 forks.
Skim excess fat from cooked broth.
Add shredded meat back to slow cooker.
Heat on medium until meat is warmed through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve in bowls with warm corn tortillas and avocado slices on the side.
recipes.name: Chile Verde

author: Oracle Ace
Lewis Cunningham
instructions: In a large pan, sautÃƒÂ© the vegetables in the butter and olive oil.
Cook until tender.
Add the cayenne and salt.
Stir.
Add the flour and continuously stir until the roux dark-ens.
Never stop stirring.
When it starts to smell like peanuts, you can stop or you can go for a darker roux.
Pour in the water and stir well.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until the liquid is sort of thick.
Add the crawfish and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Pour over rice or french bread.
recipes.name: Crawfish EXAtouffee

author: Oracle Ace
Dan Hotka
instructions: Cook the sausage well, drain off the grease.
Put all soups/tomatoes/cooked sausage in a pan.
Add water till it is soup but still rather thick.
Heat over medium heat.
Serve it hot with the cheese sprinkled on top.
recipes.name: Dan Hotkey's Pizza Soup

author: Oracle Ace
Marcelle Kratochvil
instructions: Mix flour with the semolina and add the salt.
Mix milk with yolks separately.
Add to the flour/semolina mix.
Beat with gusto until soft and bubbly.
Put to the side.
Cut bread rolls into cubes.
Fry them with butter.
Make sure its not soggy but toasted.
Add the cubes to the dough.
Grab a large amount of the dough and make a large roll that will just fit into the saucepan.
Get a very large deep saucepan of boiling water (no need for a lid).
Boil the dumpling for 30 minutes.
Remove the dumping carefully.
Rest on a towel to drain the excess water.
Let it cool down and slice the dumpling thickly, cover in dill sauce 15.
Serve with wine.
Add any meat dish on the side.
A good beef or large pork works well, especially if it complements the wine.
recipes.name: Plump up the DBA

author: Oracle Ace
Brendan Tierney
instructions: Fill a container with warm-ish water (not too warn).
Add the sugar, honey and yeast.
Give it a good stir to mix all the ingredients and let it sit 5 minutes.
While waiting weigh the flour and place in a bowl for mixing.
Add the mustard power and give it a good mix.
At this stage you should see the yeast doing its magic in the container.
It will be creating a foam on top of the liquid mixture.
Slowly add the liquid into the bowl, mixing all the time, using your fingers and hand.
Make sure that you get the foam mixed in.
When fully mixed you should have a nice dough mixture.
Cover the bowl with cling film and place in a warm room or airing cupboard for 30 minutes.
At this point it should have risen to be at least twice it original size.
Spend the next 3 to 5 minutes kneading the dough, or until you cannot knead it anymore.
Get a baking tray and slightly dust it with some of the flour.
Place the dough on the baking tray and roll out the dough so that it is approx 1 to 2cm thick.
Leave it to rise again in a warm room for another 30 minutes.
Place it in a pre-heated oven at 180c for 19 minutes.
Take it off the baking tray and leave it to cool on a wire frame'.
recipes.name: Predictive Analytics Bread

author: Oracle Ace
Brendan Tierney

ingredients.name: sprigs of oregano
ingredients.raw: sprigs of oregano, fresh or dried

instructions: Tear the ciabatta into small 2cm pieces.
Put into a roasting tray, drizzle with olive oil and toss with the fennel seeds, the oregano and a pinch of salt.
Mix so that the bread is coated then put under a high grill for 10 minutes or until golden.
Roughly chop together the capers with some of the basil leaves and the jarred peppers.
Crush over the garlic cloves or chop finely.
Add all of the tomatoes, roughly chopped.
Put into a large bowl with a splash of red wine vinegar, a good drizzle of olive oil and salt and pepper to taste.
Add the ciabatta.
Toss and gently squeeze the whole mixture together with your hands.
Top with the rest of the basil leaves and finely grated parmesan to serve.
Serve a generous portion and enjoy.
recipes.name: Tuscan Salad

author: Oracle Ace
Lewis Cunningham
instructions: Chop the onion.
Mix the oil, spices, onion, beans and tuna in a bowl.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Serve cold on crackers.
recipes.name: White Bean & Tuna Salad

author: Oracle Ace
John Flack
instructions: Combine flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs and whisk in oil, milk, sugar and vanilla extract.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients.
Stir until no dry flour is seen.
Heat your waffle iron and cook according to the manufacturer's instructions.
recipes.name: Whole Wheat Waffles

author: Oracle Ace
Matjz & Eva

ingredients.name: few spoons of lard
ingredients.raw: few spoons of lard, with cracklings

instructions: Roast the buckwheat flour in an ungreased iron pan until the aroma appears, stirring constantly.
Pour the salted boiling water over the flour.
Stir until it begins to form.
Cover the pan and place over very light heat for ten minutes so that flour swells.
Brown cracklings in lard.
Garnish over zganci.
recipes.name: Zganci

author: Oracle Ace
Floyd Teter

ingredients.name: liquid smoke
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon liquid smoke, (apple, hickory or pecan)

instructions: Cut a series of 1/2-inch slashes in the ham in a crosshatch pattern.
Rub the ham with the oil and sprinkle it with the black pepper.
Put the ham in a crock pot on medium heat and cook to an internal temperature of 150 degree fahrenheit.
Should take around 3-4 hours, depending on your crock pot.
Mix the bbq sauce and the brown sugar.
Glaze the ham with the mix.
Continue cooking the ham to an internal temperature of 160 degrees.
Remove from the crock pot, let rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Slice & serve.
recipes.name: ACEd Up Ham

author: Oracle Ace
Debra Lilley
instructions: Place a pineapple slice under each chicken piece s in bottom of baking tray.
Put tray in hot oven and allow to start cooking whilst you prepare sauce.
Chop peppers and onions and place in pan with small amount of oil.
Stir over low heat until soft.
Add rest of pineapple chopped to pan and pineapple juice from tins.
Add curry powder and corn flour to about 1 cup water per person.
Mix all together and simmer until consistency of thick cream.
Pour over chicken.
Cover tray with foil and cook for at least an hour (check chicken before serving).
Serve with rice.
recipes.name: Chicken Hawaii

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: boned lamb
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 pound boned lamb, cut in 2-inch cubes

instructions: Heat fat in a large, heavy saucepan.
Add lamb.
Brown on all sides.
Add salt, pepper, and enough water to just cover meat.
Bring to boil; lower heat; simmer 1 to 1/2 hours or until lamb is almost tender.
Add vegetables and celery salt.
Simmer 10 minutes longer.
Add more salt and pepper, if necessary.
Drop dumpling batter on stew by tablespoonfuls, being sure each spoonful rests on a piece of meat.
Cook, uncovered, 10 minutes over low heat.
Cover; cook 10 minutes longer.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
recipes.name: Irish Stew with Dumplings

author: Oracle Ace
Brendan Tierney
instructions: Place the minced lamb in a large bowl with the onion and garlic.
Mix together until well combined and then divide the mixture into equal portions.
About the size of a gold ball.
Using wet hands, shape into patties and then arrange on a baking tray.
Preheat the grill.
Place the baking tray with the patties under the grill and cook for 10 minutes or until cooked through and golden brown, turning once.
Wrap the pita breads in tinfoil and place in a pre-heated oven (160c) for 5 minutes to warm through.

Or you can use your toaster to assemble, place two of the lamb patties in to the pitta, with a teaspoonful of the hummus, a few pieces of the rocket and give it a like drizzle of the sweet chili sauce.
recipes.name: Lamb in Pitas

author: Oracle Ace
Ronald Bradford
instructions: Preheat oven to 325c.
Place tomatoes in cooking dish.
Lightly salt and pepper pork.
Lightly brown in frying pan (2-3 mins).
Place pork in cooking disk, cover lightly with tomatoes.
Pork cooks for 90+ minutes.
Reduce temperature 25c per 30 minutes.
There does not seem any issues over-cooking.
Remove pork and place into container.
Separate with fork & knife.
Pork should just fall away.
Add some of the tomato juice from cooking disk to container.
Add sauce to your liking.
recipes.name: MyPorkQL

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: boned pork shoulder
ingredients.raw: boned pork shoulder, with deep pocket

instructions: Cook onion in butter or margarine until golden brown; combine with remaining stuffing ingredients.
Set oven for moderate, 350f.
Fill pocket in pork shoulder with stuffing; fasten with small skewers laced together with white twine.
Place pork on rack in open roaster.
Roast, figuring 40 minutes per pound.
recipes.name: Apple-Stuffed Pork Shoulder

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: center cut uncooked ham
ingredients.raw: 1 center cut uncooked ham, slice, 1 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Set oven for moderate, 350f.
Cut slashes in fat of ham about 2 inches apart.
Stud fat with whole cloves.
Place ham in deep pan or casserole.
Add pineapple juice.
Combine brown sugar and cinammon; sprinkle on ham.
Bake 2 hours, basting every half hour with the pineapple juice in pan.
recipes.name: Baked Ham Slice

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for hot, 400f.
Cover bottom of baking dish with lemon and onion slices.
Sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper.
Lay fillets on top.
Cover (if pan does not have a cover, use foil).
Bake 20 minutes.
Remove cover; combine remaining ingredients: spread over top.
Broil 3 inches below heat until browned.
recipes.name: Baked Ocean Perch

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Have spareribs cut in serving size pieces.
Brown slowly in two 10-inch skillets; put in a baking pan.
Pour fat from skillet, melt butter in skillet; add onion; cook until brown.
Add next 9 ingredients; simmer 20 minutes.
Set oven for moderate 350f.
Pour sauce over ribs.
Bake, covered, 1 1/2 hours.
recipes.name: Barbecued Spareribs

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: stewing beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 3 pound stewing beef chuck, , heel of round, or neck

instructions: Cut beef in 1-inch cubes; dredge with flour.
Heat fat in a large, heavy saucepot.
Brown meat on all sides.
Add salt, pepper, sugar, tomato sauce, and water.
Simmer, covered.
1 1/2 hours, or until meat is almost tender.
Scrape carrots, slice 1-inch thick.
Peel onions; add with carrots to meat.
Cover; cook 30 minutes.
Add oregano or marjoram and peas.
Cook 15 minutes or until meat and vegetables are done.
If desired, thicken gravy before serving.
recipes.name: Beef and Vegetable Stew

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Dip meat in buttermilk; coat with crumbs.
Chill several hours.
Heat fat in 10-inch skillet.
Brown meat on both sides.
Add tomato juice.
Cover; simmer 1 hour or until tender.
Add more tomato juice if meat becomes dry during cooking.
Make pan gravy, if desired.
recipes.name: Breaded Veal Cutlet

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: freshened salt cod
ingredients.raw: 2 cup freshened salt cod, or finnan haddie

instructions: Soak fish for 1 hour in cold water to cover, changing water twice.
Drain; cover with boiling water; simmer 15 minutes; drain; flake; add to sauce with eggs.
Serve with baked potatoes.
recipes.name: Creamed Salt Fish

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine all ingredients except fat: mix well; shape into 6 patties.
Heat fat in 10-inch skillet.
Brown patties on all sides; lower heat; cook to desired degree of doneness.
recipes.name: Hamburgers

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: fine dry bread crumbs
ingredients.raw: 1 cup fine dry bread crumbs, or corn meal

instructions: Cut fillets into serving-size pieces.
Sprinkle with salt.
Mix egg and milk in a flat dish.
Dip fish in egg mixture, then in bread crumbs.
Heat fat about 1/8-inch deep, in a skillet.
Add fish; fry over medium heat, turning to brown evenly.
Reduce heat to low and cook 10 minutes, or until it flakes easily with a fork.
Drain well.
recipes.name: Pan-Fried Fish Fillets

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Cut veal in 1/2-inch pieces.
Add cold water and 1 teaspoon monosodium glutamate.
Bring slowly to boil; lower heat: simmer 1 hour.
Wash beans; break off tips; remove strings, if any.
Break into 1-inch pieces; add to veal: cover; cook 25 minutes or until tender.
Melt butter or margarine: blend in flour, sugar, salt, and remaining monosodium glutamate.
Measure liquid from green bean mixture; add enough water to make 4 cups; add to flour mixture with vinegar.
Cook, stirring until smooth and thickened; return to green bean mixture.
Add savory, parsley, and pepper.
Cook, uncovered, over low heat 15 minutes.
Top each serving with generous mound of mashed potatoes.
recipes.name: Veal and Green Bean Stew

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Sprinkle surface of fish with monosodium glutamate.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Brush with melted butter.
Place on greased broiler rack in broiler, with surface of fish about 2 inches below heat.
Broil about 8 minutes on each side, brushing often with melted butter or margarine.
recipes.name: Broiled Swordfish Steaks

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Heat waffle baker according to manufacturer's directions.
Mix and sift flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat egg yolks until light.
Combine with milk.
Add milk mixture slowly to dry ingredients, stirring until batter is smooth.
Add melted shortening.
Beat egg whites stiff, but not dry: fold in.
recipes.name: Extra Crisp Waffles

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for moderate, 350f.
Grease 8-inch square pan.
Combine biscuit mix and sugar.
Add shortening, egg, vanilla, and 1/3 cup milk.
Beat 1 minute.
Gradually stir in remaining milk.
Turn into pan.
Bake about 30 minutes or till light brown.
Meanwhile mix remaining ingredients.
Spread on baked cake.
Broil 3 inches from heat for 3 minutes or till topping browns.
Cut in squares.
recipes.name: Jiffy Coffee Cake

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: mushed ripe banana
ingredients.raw: 1 cup mushed ripe banana, (2 or 3 medium bananas)

instructions: Set oven for moderate, 350f.
Mix and sift first 4 ingredients.
Cream shortening and peanut butter; add sugar gradually while creaming.
Continue to cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs; beat well.
Stir in dry ingredients alternately with mashed bananas: mix well; but do not beat.
Spoon batter into well greased loaf pan, 8 by 4 by 3 inches.
Bake 1 hour.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Loaf

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the lemon juice, salt, paprika and parsley.
Add the oil slowly, beating vigorously with a dover egg-beater or a fork.
Beat until the mixture becomes a little thick.
Pour over the salad.
recipes.name: Bettina’s French Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange two pieces of lettuce on each salad plate.
Cut the tomatoes in half and arrange on the lettuce.
Place three slices of cucumber on each piece of tomato.
Add a tablespoon of cheese to each portion.
Sprinkle with celery salt, salt and paprika.
Serve at once with french dressing.
recipes.name: Vegetable Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and hull the strawberries, and cut in halves with a spoon.
Add the sugar, mix well, and set in a cold place.
Mix the tapioca, the sugar and the salt.
Add the boiling watcr slowly.
Cook ten minutes in the upper part of the double boiler.
Add the vanilla.
When cold, add the strawberries.
Serve very cold with plain or whipped cream.
recipes.name: Strawberry Tapioca

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the asparagus and cut it in six-inch pieces.
Cook for ten minutes in boiling salted water (longer if necessary).
Rinse with cold water, handling carefully.
Arrange six stalks on each piece of lettuce.
Serve with salad dressing.
recipes.name: Asparagus Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place the cream in a round-bottomed, chilled bowl.
Beat until thick and fluffy.
Add the sugar, lemon and vanilla.
Mix well.
Pile lightly on the orange tapioca and serve very cold.
recipes.name: Whipped Cream

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Stir the tapioca into the orange and lemon juice.
Add the sugar and salt.
Let it stand for three minutes while boiling the water.
Add the water.
Place directly over the fire.
Stir constantly and cook till thick (about three minutes).
Peel the orange and break apart in sections.
Line a glass serving dish with it and pour the tapioca over the sections.
Serve cold with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Orange Tapioca

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cook the whole onions in boiling water until tender, but not broken.
When the fork pierces them easily, drain off the water and rinse in cold water.
This makes them firm for stuffing.
Remove the centers carefully.
Add the removed portion, chopped fine, to the crumbs, egg, parsley, salt, butter and celery salt.
Mix thoroughly.
Fill the holes with the mixture.
Place the onions in a small pan.
Sprinkle the salt over the onion and pour over it the milk.
Bake in a moderate oven for twenty minutes.
recipes.name: Stuffed Onions

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix and sift the sugar, flour, salt, baking powder and cinnamon.
Add the egg-yolk, water and vanilla.
Beat one minute.
Add the egg white stiffly beaten.
Mix well.
Add the butter, melted.
Divide the mixture, and to half add the melted chocolate.
Prepare a loaf-cake pan or a small round tin with waxed paper.

Fill it with both mixtures, first placing in it a tablespoon of the plain mixture, then a tablespoon of the chocolate mixture, then the plain, until all is used, and the pudding has a marbled appearance.
Bake thirty minutes in a moderate oven.
Serve warm with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Baked Marble Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the salmon liquor.
Add the flour, salt and paprika and mix well.
Add the milk and cook two minutes.
Add the egg, pickle and parsley, mix well, and pour around the loaf.
recipes.name: Salmon Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Flake the salmon apart with a silver fork, add the crumbs, salt and paprika.
Beat the egg and add the milk.
Add to the first mixture.
Place in a well-buttered mould and bake in a moderate oven for twenty-five minutes.
Allow to stand three minutes, remove from the mould, and place on a warmed platter.
Pour salmon sauce around the loaf and serve at once.
recipes.name: Salmon Loaf

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and pepper and mix well.
Gradually stir in the milk.
Cook until it thickens slightly.
Add the beaten egg-yolk, cook one minute and serve immediately with one cup of diced carrots.
recipes.name: Bechamel Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Carrots should not be peeled, but after being scrubbed well they should be scraped with a knife.
Cut into one- half inch cubes, cook in boiling water (salted) twenty-five minutes, or until soft when pierced with a knitting needle.
Drain and serve with bechamel sauce.
recipes.name: Creamed Carrots

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Trim and wipe chops one-half inch thick, which are cut from the thick part of the leg.
Season with salt and pepper and roll in flour.
Put the fat (bacon fat or lard) in the pan, and when hot, add the chops.
Brown both sides evenly and allow to cook ten minutes.
recipes.name: Veal Chops

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: shelled peanuts
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup shelled peanuts, broken in halves

instructions: Cut the bananas in one-fourth inch cubes.
Add the lemon juice, mixing thoroughly.
Add the peanuts, celery, salt and paprika.
Add the salad dressing, mixing lightly with a silver fork.
Pile on the lettuce leaves which have been washed and arranged on a serving dish.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Banana Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add the rice, tomato pulp, onion, salt, paprika and celery leaves to the meat stock.
Cook for twenty minutes over a slow fire.
Strain and serve in hot soup dishes or bouillon cups.
recipes.name: Bettina Soup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the cheese, pimento, salt and paprika and mix into a paste.
Spread carefully on top of the wafers.
Place in a moderate oven until a delicate brown.
Serve with the salad.
recipes.name: Cheese Wafers

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the cottage cheese, salt, paprika, nut meats, dates and pimento thoroughly.
Add two tablespoons of salad dressing.
Arrange the pears on the lettuce leaves and place one tablespoon of the mixture on each portion.
Place a tablespoon of salad dressing on the top.
Serve very cold.
recipes.name: Pear Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt thoroughly, cut in the lard with a knife until the consistency of cornmeal add the milk, mxing with a knife until a soft dough is formed.
More milk may be needed; this depends on the consistency of the flour.
Pat into a rectangular shape, on a floured board or on a paper.
The dough should be half an inch thick.
Cream the butter, add the peanut butter and spread on the biscuit dough.
Sprinkle the currants on the top.
Roll up carefully, over and over like a cinnamon roll.
Cut off pieces half an inch wide and pat them down in a tin pan.
Bake eighteen minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter and Fruit Rolls

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: pimento liquor
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon pimento liquor , (the juice from the can)

instructions: Beat the egg-yolks, add the sugar, salt and flour.
Mix well and add the vinegar, pimento liquor and water.
Cook in a double boiler until very thick.
When cool, add the sour cream, and pour over the salad.
recipes.name: Bettina Salad Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the lettuce carefully and arrange on individual serving dishes.
Place upon each lettuce leaf a slice of tomato, three slices of cucumber and one-third of each of the other ingredients.
Sprinkle with salt and paprika.
Pour the salad dressing over the top and serve very cold.
recipes.name: Vegetable Salad

author: Oracle Ace
Sheeri Cabral

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: olive oil does not work well
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon vegetable oil, (olive oil does not work well)

instructions: Mix all ingredients together.
Drop a few drops of oil into a small pan (a crepe pan or other non-coated pan works well).
Pour a thin layer of the batter into the pan.
Tilt the pan to cover.
Turn the crepe over and watch that it does not burn.
Remove the crepe and lay it on a plate.
Stir the mixture occasionally.
Continue to make the crepes.
Let cool.
Roll the crepes and cut thin slices.
Unroll or "fluff" the slices into thin long noodles.
Place in a covered dish.
Refrigerate if not served on the same day.
recipes.name: Saba's Passover Noodles

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: .5 pounds ready-to-cook stewing chicken
ingredients.raw: 4 .5 pounds ready-to-cook stewing chicken, cut up

ingredients.name: onion studded with a few whole cloves
ingredients.raw: 1 onion studded with a few whole cloves

instructions: Simmer chicken with water and next 5 ingredients 1 1/2 to 2 hours until tender.
Remove chicken to a heated serving dish; keep warm.
Strain broth; skim off excess fat.
Measure 3 cups broth, adding water if necessary.
Mix flour and milk to smooth paste: add slowly to broth; cook over low heat, stirring until thickened.
Season to taste with additional salt and pepper: pour over chicken.
Serve with hot baking powder biscuits.
recipes.name: Chicken Fricassee

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: ready-to-cook frying chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 ready-to-cook frying chicken, (3 pounds) cut up

instructions: Wash chicken and dry well.
Heat fat in 10- or 12-inch skillet or chicken fryer over moderate heat.
Brown onions.
Add paprika and chicken; sprinkle with salt.
Cover; cook over very low heat 1 hour until tender, turning after first half hour.
Pour sour cream over chicken: heat.
recipes.name: Chicken Paprika

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: ready-to-cook broiler-fryer chicken
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 pound ready-to-cook broiler-fryer chicken, cut up

instructions: Melt fat and butter over low heat in a chicken fryer or large skillet.
Combine flour and salt.
Coat chicken with flour mixture; fry over low heat until browned on one side; turn to brown on all sides evenly.
Add water.
Cover; simmer 30 minutes, adding more water if necessary.
Uncover; cook 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Southern Fried Chicken

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for moderate 350f.
Combine first 6 ingredients.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Add onion and meat; mix well.
Line a loaf pan, 8 by 5 by 3 inches, with bacon across the width of pan.
Pack meat mixture into pan.
Bake 1 1/2 hours.
Remove from oven.
Invert meat loaf on baking sheet: lift off pan: raise oven temperature to very hot, 450f.
Return meat loaf to oven for about 10 minutes to crisp bacon.
recipes.name: Best Meat Loaf

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: (6-ounce) frozen orange juice
ingredients.raw: 1 can (6-ounce) frozen orange juice, concentrate, thawed

instructions: Set oven for slow, 325f.
Stuff duckling.
Place breast side up on rack in shallow open pan.
Roast, 3 to 4-pound duckling about 2 1/4 to 2 3/4 hour, 4 to 5-pound duckling about 2 3/4 to 3 hours, 5 in 6-pound duckling about 3 to 3 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile combine sugar, salt, and cornstarch.
Add thawed orange juice concentrate (do not dilute).
Stir over moderate heat until slightly thickened.
An hour before duckling is done brush entire surface with orange juice glaze.
Repeat every 15 minutes until duckling is done.
recipes.name: Glazed Roast Duckling

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Chop onion fine; cook in a 10- inch skillet in fat or salad oil until golden brown.
Add potatoes, meat, salt, pepper, worcestershire sauce, and water.
Cover; cook until potatoes are tender.
Thicken gravy with flour mixed to smooth paste in cold water.
Heat thoroughly.
recipes.name: Glorified Hash

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Remove membrane from kidney.
Split in half lengthwise: remove fat and white veins.
Slice crosswise, 14-inch thick: cut slices in pieces.
Cover pieces with cold water; let stand 1 hour; drain.
Repeat.
Place in 2-quart saucepan.
Add boiling water; simmer 1 hour.
Cover; simmer 1/2 hour longer or until liquid is reduced by half.
Mix flour and water to smooth paste; add to stew slowly, stirring constantly; simmer until thickened.
Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer few minutes.
Serve on toast.
Or, pour into 1 -quart casserole; top with pastry; bake at 425f for 15 minutes or until pastry is golden brown.
recipes.name: Kidney Stew Or Pie

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.raw: 4 pound beef, rump or sirloin tip

instructions: Combine first 9 ingredients; place meat in large, deep bowl; pour vinegar mixture over.
Refrigerate 36 to 48 hours, turning meat once or twice each day.
Remove meat; pat dry; rub lightly with a little flour; brown well on all sides in 2 tablespoons fat and 1 tablespoon butter or margarine.
Strain vinegar mixture; add 2 cups to meat; cover, simmer 3 hours.
Melt remaining butter or margarine; blend in flour and 1 tablespoon sugar; stir until rich brown.
Add remaining strained vinegar mixture.
Add to simmering meat mixture; simmer 1 hour longer or until meat is tender.
Remove meat.
Stir crushed gingersnaps into gravy; stir until thickened.
recipes.name: Sauerbraten

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for slow, 325f.
Melt butter in a 10-inch skillet.
Add onion.
Cook until golden brown.
Add next 6 ingredients and mix well.
Spread on steak.
Roll up like a jelly roll; tie securely with string.
Heat fat in the skillet.
Brown meat roll on all sides.
Sprinkle with additional salt and pepper; add the 1/2 cup boiling water.
Cover; bake 1 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
recipes.name: Stuffed Flank Steak

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Melt butter or margarine in 1- quart saucepan; add onion; cook until golden brown.
Add remaining sauce ingredients; cook over very low heat 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Prepare omelet.
Turn out on platter.
Place vegetable mixture between folded layers and around omelet.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Spanish Omelet

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Chop onions fine; cook in butter or margarine until soft but not brown.
Add remaining ingredients; mix thoroughly.
recipes.name: Bread Stuffing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: ready-to-cook broiler-fryer chicken
ingredients.raw: 2 pound ready-to-cook broiler-fryer chicken, cut up

instructions: Place chicken in shallow baking pan.
Combine remaining ingredients to make a marinade.
Pour over chicken.
Let stand in refrigerator at least 1 hour; turn chicken once.
Remove from marinade.
Place, skin side down, on broiler rack.
Put in preheated broiler 4 to 5 inches from heat.
Broil 12 minutes, basting often with marinade.
Turn; broil 15 minutes or until tender, continuing to baste.
recipes.name: Savory Broiled Chicken

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: ready-to-cook stewing chicken
ingredients.raw: 5 pound ready-to-cook stewing chicken, cut up

instructions: Place chicken in large kettle with next 6 ingredients.
Cover; bring to boil.
Simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until tender.
Remove chicken from bones and cut into bite-size pieces.
Skim fat from broth; measure 1/2 cup fat and 2 1/3 cups broth.
Heat the fat in 2-quart saucepan; blend in flour; stir in measured broth and milk.
Cook and stir constantly until thickened; boil 1 minute.
Add to chicken with carrots and onions.
Reheat.
Pour into a 3-quart baking dish.
Before mixing biscuits, set oven for 450f.
Arrange uncooked baking powder biscuits made with 2 cups biscuit mix over top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until biscuits are brown.
recipes.name: State of Maine Chicken Pie

author: Oracle Ace
Kellyn Pot'vin

ingredients.name: large lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 large lemon, or more depending on taste

instructions: In large sauce pan, prepare rice by bringing chicken broth, wine, garlic and butter to a boil.
Add rice, little by little, stirring constantly.
Once all moisture is absorbed, (about 20 min).
Remove from heat.
Add in cream, dill, curry and then squeeze in desired amount of lemon juice and zest.
If left too long, over cooked, simply add a small bit of water to again achieve desired risotto texture.
recipes.name: LMON Risotto

author: Oracle Ace
Kellyn Pot'vin
instructions: Preheat oven to 350f degrees.
Melt 4 tablespoons of the butter in a frying pan, add chopped onions, a pinch of salt and pepper, cooking up onions until soft.
Place cream, eggs, flour, sugar, 2 cups of the corn, a pinch of salt and pepper into a deep bowl, using beaters, blend until only slightly "lumpy" with the corn.
Add the cooked onion and the remaining corn, using the beaters on the lowest setting to simply mix well into the earlier mixture.
Grease a 2 quart oven safe baking dish and pour the mixture into the dish.
Sprinkle the fresh chives on top and back at 350 for 50-60 min.
The mixture is ready when set, but with still light movement in the middle.
Allow to set for 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Creamy CBO Pudding

author: Oracle Ace
Marcelle Kratochvil
instructions: Whisk cream, flour, salt and sugar.
Bring to boil, then simmer for 15 min.
Whilst simmering, grab some of the sauce and put in the fridge to cool down.
Mix yolks with some of the above sauce which has cooled down (to avoid the yolk cooking).
Once mixed, add it back into the simmering sauce and mix well.
Put vinegar into a saucepan and boil it.
When boiling add the dill and simmer.
Melt butter and add it to the dill.
Mix this butter/dill sauce with the main sauce and simmer.
recipes.name: Dill Sauce

author: Oracle Ace
Ronald Bradford
instructions: Dice butternut squash, fennel and brown onion.
Add to baking dish with generous amount of olive oil and mixed herbs mix ingredients.
Place in oven at 425f for 60 minutes.
Let stick of goat cheese sit at room temperature (or warm slightly on oven top).
Cook pasta.
Add goat cheese to bottom of mixing bowl, add cooked fresh pasta.
The heat will help melt cheese.
Add basil and pecans and mix.
Add cooked vegetables and mix.
recipes.name: NoPorkQL

author: Oracle Ace
Lewis Cunningham
instructions: Put all the ingredients in a microwave safe bowl.
Cover it and shake.
Nuke for 2 minutes.
Shake it up.
Nuke for 2 more minutes.
Shake it up.
See if the green beans are tender.
If they are, you can eat.
If not, nuke for 2 more minutes; rinse, repeat.
recipes.name: Quick Cabbage and Green Beans

author: Oracle Ace
Lewis Cunningham

ingredients.name: seasoned red or black beans
ingredients.raw: 15 ounce seasoned red or black beans

instructions: SautÃ© onions and garlic in large sauce pan.
Add beans, tomatoes and cayenne.
Bring the beans to a boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add instant rice.
Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove from heat and let sit for 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Quick Red Beans and Rice

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Have the tenderloin cut in two-inch pieces and flattened.
Place these in a small baking dish.
Sprinkle with salt and paprika and add the water.
Cover, and cook in a moderate oven for thirty-five minutes.
Turn and baste frequently.
When done, place on a heated platter, pour the parsley and lemon juice over the top and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and mix well.
Beat the egg-yolks until very thick, and add to the first mixture, mix and sift together the flour and baking-powder and add the milk alternately with the flour mixture, beating well.
· Beat two minutes after mixing.
Add the extract.
Pour to the thickness of one inch into flat pans lined with buttered paper.
Bake twelve minutes in a moderate oven.
Remove from the fire and when cool, cut into shapes with fancy animal cutters.
The individual cakes may be iced if desired.
recipes.name: Fancy Cakes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the lettuce carefully.
Roll and cut into fine shreds.
Arrange a portion on each serving plate.
Place a slice of pineapple on each portion and very carefully place the salad dressing on it so that it just covers the circle of pineapple.
Arrange two filberts on top to represent eyes, and cut the pimento in a strip to represent the mouth.
Cut small triangular pieces of pimento to represent the nose.
Arrange these as features on the pineapple and serve at once.
recipes.name: Clown Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cup ham, minced or ground fine

instructions: Chop the ham, eggs and pickles very fine.
Add the salt and salad dressing.
Cut the bread very thin and match the pieces in pairs.
Spread one of a pair with the ham mixture and spread the other side with butter which has been mixed and softened with a wooden spoon.
Place the two pieces of bread together and press firmly.
Moisten the cooky cutter with water and cut evenly the desired shape.
recipes.name: Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the corn starch and salt in the upper part of the double boiler.
Add the milk slowly, stirring all the time.
Add the sugar.
Place the upper in the lower part of the double boiler and cook, stirring occasionally to prevent lumping.
When very thick, add the egg-yolk, the vanilla and lemon extracts and the cocoanut.
Beat one minute.
Cook again for three minutes.
Place in a buttered baking dish.
Beat the egg-white and when very stiff, add the two tablespoons of sugar.
Pile lightly on the top of the pudding and place in a moderate oven for ten minutes to brown the meringue.
recipes.name: Cocoanut Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.raw: 3 cup cabbage, cut or chopped fine

ingredients.name: cracker or dry bread crumbs
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup cracker or dry bread crumbs

instructions: Wash the cabbage and chop into half inch pieces.
Cook in boiling water fifteen minutes.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
Make a white sauce by melting the butter, adding the flour and salt, and then adding the milk.
Cook two minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the cabbage, and pour into a well-buttered open baking dish.
Melt the one tablespoon of butter, add the crumbs and mix well.
Spread the buttered crumbs over the top of the cabbage.
Bake fifteen minutes in a moderate oven.
Serve in the dish.
recipes.name: Creamed Cabbage Baked

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: slice of ham
ingredients.raw: 1 pound slice of ham, two-thirds of an inch thick

instructions: Have a frying-pan very hot.
Add the ham and brown thoroughly on both sides.
Add the water and let boil for one minute.
Remove the ham.
Stick the cloves into it, and place it in the bottom of a casserole.
Add the parsley and paprika to the water in the pan, and pour; the liquid over the meat.
Cover and bake in a moderate oven for half an hour.
Roll the potatoes (which have been washed and peeled) in the flour, and add to the casserole.
Baste with the liquid.
Cover and cook three-fourths of an hour.
Serve in the casserole.
recipes.name: Sliced Ham and Potatoes en Casserole

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter and lard, add the sugar, and mix well.
Add the two eggs well beaten.
Mix and sift thoroughly the flour, baking powder, salt, cloves and cinnamon.
Add the dates and nuts.
Stir these dry ingredients into the first mixture.
Add the vanilla.
Mix thoroughly and drop from the end of the spoon upon a well larded and floured baking pan.
Bake fifteen minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Date Rocks

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the beans, celery, nut meats, green pepper, pickles and salt.
Add the salad dressing.
Serve very cold on lettuce leaves.
recipes.name: Bean Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cold boiled potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cold boiled potatoes, cut in 1/4 -inch cubes

instructions: Place one tablespoon of butter in a frying-pan and when hot add the onion.
Let the onion cook until it is brown.
Add the salt and parsley, the rest of the butter, the potatoes and the paprika.
Stir well.
Cook until the potatoes are well browned.
recipes.name: Lyonnaise Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the egg whites thoroughly, add the sugar, flour, salt and baking powder.
Mix well, add the dates, nuts and vanilla.
Pile lightly in a well-buttered baking-dish.
Place the dish in a pan of hot water and bake thirty minutes in a moderate oven.
Allow the pudding to remain in the oven a little while after the heat is turned off.
If cooled slowly, it will not fall.
The pudding may be baked in individual moulds if preferred, and may be served with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Date Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, paprika, celery salt, onion salt, salt and pimento.
Gradually add the milk and cook thoroughly for one minute.
Add the meat and allow the mixture to cool.
