When cool, shape into the desired shape, preferably conical.
Rollin the crumbs, dip in the egg and water mixed, then dip in the crumbs and allow to stand for fifteen minutes or more.
Fry in deep fat.
recipes.name: Ground Pork Croquettes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cut the slices of bread one-half an inch thick.
Butter, and sprinkle with salt.
Cut into strips, the length of the slice and half an inch wide.
Place on a tin pan, and cook directly under a fire or in an oven until a delicate brown.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Toasted Sticks

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cook the peas, water and sugar slowly for fifteen minutes.
Strain, and rub all the pulp through the strainer.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Mix thoroughly and gradually add the milk.
Boil one minute and add the pulp and liquid from the peas.
Cook one minute.
Serve in hot soup plates or bouillon cups.
recipes.name: Cream of Pea Soup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: When the water is boiling, add the salt.
Add the rice and allow it to boil twenty minutes.
More water may be needed.
Stir occasionally with a fork.
Pour iuto a strainer, and rinse thoroughly with cold water.
Toss into a buttered vegetable dish.
Sprinkle with paprika and dot with butter.
Set in a moderate oven for fifteen minutes.
recipes.name: Rice

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Strain the vegetables through the strainer, pressing thoroughly to remove all the pulp.
Add the stock and one-half a cup of water.
Reheat and serve for dinner with croutons or salted wafers.
recipes.name: Soup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove the pot roast meat from the kettle.
Strain the stock into a bowl.
To the flour, add the water.
Mix well, and gradually add the stock.
Mix and cook one minute.
Pour the gravy over the meat and reserve the remaining stock and vegetables for soup.
recipes.name: Gravy

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place the bacon drippings in a frying-pan.
Roll the beef in the flour, and when the fat is hot, add the beef and brown thoroughly on all sides.
Place the meat in a kettle, and add the vegetables.
Pour the water in the frying-pan to remove any fat.
Pour all over the meat.
Add the bay leaf, cloves and salt.
Cover closely and allow to cook very slowly for three and a half hours.
Turn the meat after the second hour.
This is a good fireless cooker recipe.
recipes.name: Pot Roast

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the vanilla with the coffee.
Add the powdered sugar slowly until the proper consistency to spread.
Spread over one layer and place the upper layer on the lower.
Place the icing on the top layer and on the sides.
More sugar may be needed.
recipes.name: Mocha Icing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and cream the mixture, add the egg-yolks, mix well and add the coffee, vanilla, flour and baking powder.
Beat two minutes.
Add the stiffly beaten egg- whites.
Pour the mixture into two layer-cake pans prepared with waxed paper.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.
When cool, spread with the mocha icing.
recipes.name: Mocha Cake

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Wash rice.
Pat dry with paper towels.
Heat fat or salad oil in deep heavy 2-quart saucepan.
Add rice; stir over low heat until each rice kernel is golden brown.
Add boiling water slowly and carefully as steam will rise.
Add salt.
Cover.
Simmer 25 minutes (do not lift cover or stir).
The rice should have absorbed all the water and be dry and flaky.
recipes.name: Browned Rice

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: grated processed American cheese
ingredients.raw: 3 cup grated processed American cheese, (3/4 pound)

instructions: Heat oven to moderate, 375f.
Cool scalded milk.
Combine next 7 ingredients in a large bowl.
Add milk; mix well.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon-colored; stir slowly into bread mixture.
Beat egg whites stiff but not dry; fold in.
Turn into greased 2-quart casserole; set in pan filled with warm water to 1 inch from top of casserole.
Bake 1 1/2 hours or until golden brown and firm at center.
recipes.name: Cheese fondue

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Follow directions for puffy omelet, adding 1/2 cup grated sharp cheddar cheese just before folding in egg whites.
Before putting omelet in oven, sprinkle top with an additional 1/2 cup of grated cheese.
recipes.name: Cheese Omelet

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for slow, 300f.
Heat milk but do not scald.
Melt butter or margarine in top of double boiler, blend in flour, salt, cayenne.
Add heated milk; stir over hot water until smooth and thickened.
Slice cheese into sauce; stir until cheese melts.
Remove from heat.
Beat egg yolks with a fork until well blended.
Add a little of the cheese sauce; stir mixture into remaining cheese sauce.
Beat egg whites stiff but not dry; fold in cheese sauce gently but thoroughly.
Turn into ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole to within 1 inch of top (if any is left, bake separately in small, ungreased baking dish).
Make a shallow path, using a teaspoon about 1 inch in from edge of casserole.
Bake 1 1/4 hours.
Do not open oven while baking.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Cheese Souffle

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Mix eggs, water, salt and pepper with fork.
Heat fat in 8-inch skillet just hot enough to sizzle a drop of water.
Pour in egg mixture.
It should set at edges at once.
Reduce heat.
As the mixture at the edges thickens, draw these portions with the fork toward the center so that the uncooked portions flow to the bottom.
Tilt skillet to hasten flow of uncooked eggs.
Shake skillet to keep omelet sliding freely.
Keep mixture as level as possible.
When eggs are set and surface is still moist, increase heat to brown bottom quickly.
Carefully loosen edge, fold in half or roll.
recipes.name: French Omelet

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Heat fat in a 10-inch skillet.
Add onion and garlic: cook until onion is soft, not brown.
Add meat; break into small pieces.
Cook and stir until lightly browned.
Add next 7 ingredients.
Bring to boil.
Cover; simmer 45 minutes.
Add mushrooms; heat to boiling.
Arrange macaroni on a platter.
Pour sauce over macaroni.
Sprinkle with cheese.
recipes.name: Macaroni with Meat Sauce

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Add tapioca, salt and pepper to milk; cook in double boiler 15 minutes or until tapioca is clear and mixture thickened, stirring frequently.
Add butter.
Cool; combine with egg yolks, stirring constantly.
Fold in egg whites.
Set oven for moderate 350f.
Pour egg mixture into hot buttered 9-inch frying pan.
Cook over low heat 3 minutes.
Transfer to oven; bake 15 minutes.
Omelet is done when an inserted knife comes out clean.
Cut across at right angles to handle of pan, being careful not to cut all the way through.
Fold carefully from handle to opposite side and serve on hot platter.
recipes.name: Puffy Omelet

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Mix eggs, milk, salt and pepper with fork or spoonâ€”mixing thoroughly if a uniform yellow is preferred or mixing slightly if streaks of white and yellow are preferred.
Heat fat in 8-inch skillet just hot enough to sizzle drop of water.
Pour in egg mixture.
Reduce heat promptly.
Cook slowly, lifting from the bottom and sides as the mixture thickens.
As the cooked mixture is lifted, the thin uncooked part should flow to the bottom.
Avoid constant stirring.
Cook until eggs are thickened throughout but still moist.
5 to 8 minutes.
recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Cook spaghetti in 3 quarts boiling water with 1 tablespoon salt until tender; drain.
Heat olive oil and butter or margarine; add garlic, oregano, and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook over low heat 5 minutes; pour over spaghetti; toss until spaghetti is well coated.
Add eggs; continue to toss until eggs coat spaghetti.
Serve with grated parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Spaghetti Roma

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Brown frankfurters in 10-inch skillet over medium heat.
Remove frankfurters.
Melt fat in skillet; add green pepper, onion, and rice.
Cook and stir over high heat until lightly browned.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Bring to boil: cover: simmer 15 minutes.
Replace frankfurters: simmer 5 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Spanish Franks

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Tie in a tiny round of cheese-cloth and hang over the side of the soup kettle.
recipes.name: Soup Bag

author: Oracle Ace
Sheeri Cabral
instructions: In a 2.
5 quart saucepan, combine brown sugar, evaporated milk and (if using) corn syrup.
Bring to a boil, stirring frequently.
Continue boiling and stirring frequently until the soft ball stage (238 degrees f, 116 degrees c).
Remove from heat and add vanilla and butter, but do not stir.
Let cool for 25 minutes, then beat with a wooden spoon until fudge just begins to thicken.
Add any add-ins and stir until fudge begins to lost its gloss.
Pour into a greased 8 inch x 8 inch cake pan.
When cool, cut into pieces.
recipes.name: Basic Fudge

author: Oracle Ace
Matjz & Eva
instructions: Dissolve yeast onto lukewarm milk in small bowl, then add sugar and combine.
Cover and let rise in warm place for about 10 minutes.
In big bowl scald milk and add butter.
Cool to lukewarm.
In small bow beat egg yolks and then add sugar, salt and vanilla.
Mix all the ingredients.
In large bowl, sift 3 cups flour.
Pour mixtures of prepared yeast, milk, butter, eggs and sugar into mixing bowl with 3 cups of flour.
Beat with electric mixer until smooth and elastic.
Keep adding remaining flour and mixing with a wood-en spoon.
Place on floured board and knead for about 15 minutes, adding flour as needed, to make non-sticking dough.
Place dough in a lightly bowl and turn to grease top.
Cover with a clean towel and let rise in warm place for about 2 hours until double in bulk.
When dough has doubled, punch it down, again let rise till doubled (45 minutes).
Meanwhile grease a round angel food cake pan.
See part 2 for filling and baking.
recipes.name: Big Walnut 12 Cake Part 1

author: Oracle Ace
Matjz & Eva

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cup milk, or half and half

instructions: First prepare dough from part 1.
Grind walnuts in food chopper with finest blade.
Melt butter in large saucepan and add milk, sugar and honey.
Then cook to rolling boil, taking care not to let it boil over.
Pour hot mixture over walnuts and then add vanilla and grated peel.
Mix thoroughly and allow to cool.
Beat egg whites till stiff, fold into cooled walnut mixture.
Punch down dough, on slightly floured surface roll.
Spread on the filling all over the dough.
Roll up jelly-roll fashion and place the loaf into the pan.
Let loaf rise until almost doubled (around 30 minutes).
Meanwhile start heating the oven to 190c.
Brush the top of the loaf with melted butter bake the loaf for 35 min when done, remove from the pan.
Lay upside down on rack to cool completely.
recipes.name: Big Walnut 12 Cake Part 2

author: Oracle Ace
Sheeri Cabral

ingredients.name: Baker's chocolate
ingredients.note: or 3/4 cup cocoa + 4 tablespoon butter or 12 oz chocolate chips, and reduce sugar from 4.5 cups to 3 cups.
ingredients.raw: 4 ounce Baker's chocolate, or 3/4 cup cocoa + 4 tablespoon butter or 12 oz chocolate chips, and reduce sugar from 4.5 cups to 3 cups.

instructions: Prepare basic fudge, but add in chocolate with the milk and sugar and *one* of the other ingredients.
recipes.name: Chocolate Fudge

author: Oracle Ace
Ronald Bradford
instructions: Cut up cream cheese and leave at room temperature.
Juice 4 lemons.
Add condensed milk, lemon juice, passion fruit pulp, and cream cheese to bowl and hand mix for consistency.
Beat thickened cream until firm.
Fold in thickened cream into bowl.
Pour into pie crusts.
Refrigerate 2-3 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Data Pie

author: Oracle Ace
instructions: Puree the mangoes in a blender.
Transfer to a bowl.
Pour the evaporated mile onto the mango puree, and the sugar and mix well in a separate bowl, pour in hot water and add the gelatin (and not the other way around or you will get lumpy bits).
Quickly stir until all the gelatin granules have dissolved and add to the pureed mangoes and mix well.
Ladle the mixer into 4 dishes.
Place on a tray and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
When ready to serve, briefly put the dishes in a baking pan filled with 1 in of hot water to help loosen the pudding.
Use a flat knife to run around the edges of the pudding.
Place a plate on top of the dish and quickly invert it - the pudding should fall onto the plate.
Squeeze over lime juice, dust with powdered sugar and decorate with lime zest and sprig of mint.
recipes.name: Mango Pudding

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Cook macaroni in boiling, salted water according to package directions.
Drain.
Set oven for moderate, 375f.
Melt butter or margarine; blend in flour.
1 teaspoon salt, and pepper.
Add milk; cook over low heat until smooth and thickened, stirring constantly.
Add cheese, onion, mustard, and worcestershire sauce; continue to cook until cheese melts.
Add macaroni.
Pour into a greased 2- quart casserole.
Top with crumbs.
Bake about 25 minutes or until browned.
recipes.name: Baked Macaroni and Cheese

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Wash rice thoroughly in 3 or 4 changes of water.
Place in greased 1 1/2 -quart casserole; add undiluted consomme and liquid from mushrooms.
Let stand 3 hours.
Set oven for moderate 350f.
Cover casserole; bake 45 minutes, adding a little water if rice becomes too dry.
Heat mushrooms in butter or margarine.
Remove rice from oven, lower heat to 300f.
Stir mushrooms and butter into rice.
Return to oven; bake uncovered until all liquid is absorbed.
recipes.name: Baked Wild Rice

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: package sliced American cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound package sliced American cheese, (8 slices)

instructions: Set oven for moderate, 350f.
Place 4 slices bread on bottom of shallow baking dish, cutting to fit.
Cover bread with half the cheese; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Repeat.
Combine remaining ingredients; pour over bread and cheese.
Bake 40 minutes or until top is golden brown, puffed, and shiny.
recipes.name: Bread and Cheese Puff

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and peel the onions.
Cook in one quart of water.
Allow to boil five minutes.
Change the water and continue boiling ten minutes.
Change the water again, and when thoroughly cooked (about fifteen minutes more), remove from the fire and drain.
Melt the butter, add the four and salt and mix thoroughly.
Add the milk and cook one minute.
Add the onions, and pour the mixture into a well-buttered baking dish.
Place the buttered crumbs on the top of the onions and bake in a moderate oven for twenty minutes.
recipes.name: Escalloped Onions

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, salt and baking powder.
Cut in the fat with a knife.
Add the soda to the milk, and when the effervescing ceases, add slowly to the dry ingredients, all the milk may not be needed.
When a soft dough is formed, toss onto a floured board.
Pat into shape, cut with a biscuit cutter, and place side by side on a tin pan or baking sheet.
Bake fifteen minutes in a moderately hot oven.
recipes.name: Sour Cream Biscuits

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Mix well, add the milk, and cook for one minute.
recipes.name: White Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the crumbs, tomato pulp, butter, parsley, pimento, salt, egg yolks and celery.
Cook for one minute.
Fill each onion case carefully with the mixture.
Then pour the white sauce about the onions before placing them in the oven.
recipes.name: Filling

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and peel the onions.
Cook for ten minutes in boiling water.
Rinse with cold water to make them firm.
Push out the centers.
Place the onions in a well-buttered baking pan and fill each onion with filling.
Place in a moderate oven for twenty minutes.
recipes.name: Stuffed Onions

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange two pieces of lettuce on each plate.
Slice an egg, a radish and an onion and arrange these upon the lettuce leaves.
Sprinkle each portion with a fourth of the seasoning.
Place two tablespoons of salad dressing on each portion.
Have all the ingredients cold before combining.
recipes.name: Egg and Lettuce Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove the meat from the pan in which it was cooked (also remove the potatoes) and add sufficient water to the stock in the pan to make one and a half cups all together.
Melt the butter, add the browned flour and a tablespoon of the stock.
Mix well, and add the salt and pepper.
Add the remaining stock; cook, stirring constantly for two minutes.
Pour into a heated gravy dish.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Gravy

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Allow the lamb to stand in cold water for ten minutes.
Remove and wipe dry.
Place the fat in a frying-pan.
Add the meat and cook until thoroughly browned on all sides.
Place in the fireless cooker (or a slow oven) and surround the meat with the potatoes.
Sprinkle with the salt and paprika.
Add the water.
If in the cooker, place the heated disks under and over the meat.
Cook two hours.
recipes.name: Leg of Lamb and Browned Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: of stale cake
ingredients.note: three by three by one inch
ingredients.raw: 3 slices of stale cake, (three by three by one inch)

instructions: Beat the cream until stiff, add the vanilla, marshmallows and sugar.
Arrange the cake in glass sherbet dishes.
Place a tablespoon of cherries and a tablespoon of juice on each slice.
Place one and a half tablespoons of the whipped cream mixture on each portion.
Allow to stand in a cold place for five minutes.
recipes.name: Sponge Cake with Whipped Cream

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the steamed rice, egg-yolk, butter, paprika, salt and parsley.
Shape into flat disks one inch thick and three inches in diameter.
Roll in flour.
Make an indentation in the center of each with a spoon, to hold the jelly.
Fry in hot deep fat until brown.
Drain, the wrong side up.
Heat in a hot oven and serve hot.
Place a cube of jelly in the center of each.
recipes.name: Rice Croquettes with Jelly

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wipe and trim the chops.
Place on a hot tin pan four inches from a direct hot fame (under a broiler).
Cook two minutes, turn and thoroughly cook the other side for two minutes.
Lower the flame a little, add the salt and pepper, and cook for eight minutes more, a little longer if the chops are very thick.
Remove to a warm platter, dot with butter, add the parsley and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Broiled Lamb Chops

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the eggs, add the sugar, salt, vanilla, and lemon extract.
Mix thoroughly.
Butter four custard cups.
Fill a pan four inches deep with hot (not boiling) water.
Set the cups in the pan and place in a moderately slow oven for thirty-five or forty minutes (or until a knife inserted in the custard comes out clean).
Serve cold with maple syrup poured over it.
recipes.name: Steamed Custard

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the salad dressing, add the oil, pickle, pimento, catsup, celery, nut meats, salt and paprika.
Beat one minute.
Pour three tablespoons of the mixture over each portion of the lettuce.
Serve very cold.
recipes.name: Bettina Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange the lettuce, which has been washed and chilled, upon three plates.
Sprinkle the lettuce with salt and serve with the bettina dressing.
recipes.name: Lettuce Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: round steak
ingredients.raw: 1 pound round steak, cut one inch thick

instructions: Place the meat, which has been wiped with a damp cloth, upon a meat board.
Cut into four pieces.
Pound the flour into the meat on both sides, using a meat pounder or the side of a heavy saucer.
Butter the casserole, add a layer of meat, then onions and green peppers.
Add the carrots.
Add the salt to the water and pour over the meat.
Cover closely.
Place in a moderate oven and allow to cook slowly for two hours.
More water may be needed before the meat is done.
Serve in the casserole.
recipes.name: Round Steak En Casserole

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash, peel, quarter and core the apples.
Add the water, cover the kettle with a lid and cook till apples are soft.
Add other ingredients.
Cook enough longer to dissolve the sugar.
Mash or put through a colander, if desired.
recipes.name: Apple Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Peel six medium sized onions under cold water.
Place in a stew-pan and cover with boiling water.
Boil five minutes, drain, cover again with boiling water and cook ten minutes.
Drain, recover with boiling water and cook ten minutes longer or until tender.
Serve with hot white sauce.
recipes.name: Creamed Onions

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound ground beef, from the round

ingredients.name: onion juice
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon onion juice, or onion salt

instructions: Soak the crumbs in milk for three minutes, add the meat, egg, nutmeg, onion juice, parsley, salt, green pepper and paprika.
Mix well.
Pat into shape one and one-half inches thick in a well buttered tin pan.
Cook five minutes under a very hot broiler.
Turn down the heat a little and cook ten minutes more.
Turn the steak into another buttered pan the same size and cook that side ten minutes.
Pie tins may be used to cook the meat in.
recipes.name: Bettina Steak

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add the cold water to the gelatin and allow it to stand five minutes.
Add the sugar and the lemon juice.
Mix well, and add boiling water.
When thoroughly dissolved, allow to cool.
When the mixture begins to congeal, or thicken, add the whipped cream, crushed macaroons, cherries and nut meats.
Beat until the mixture begins to thicken.
Pile lightly into a glass dish and set away to harden for one hour.
recipes.name: Bettina’s Sponge

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cooked potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked potatoes, cut in cubes

instructions: Roll the chicken in the flour.
Place the lard in the frying- pan, and when very hot, add the chicken, browning thoroughly on all sides.
Season with the salt.
Place in the casserole and add the boiling water.
Cover, and place in a moderate oven for one hour.
Melt the butter, and when hot, add the potatoes, carrots, onion, celery and salt.
Stir constantly, and when well-browned, add to the chicken mixture.
Allow to cook for half an hour.
More water may be needed.
Serve in the casserole.
recipes.name: Bettina's Chicken En Casserole

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Fry bacon crisp; drain on absorbent paper.
Cook onion and green pepper in 2 tablespoons of the bacon fat until soft but not brown.
Add kidney beans, tomatoes, seasonings, and cheese.
Stir over low heat until cheese melts.
recipes.name: Monterey Jack

author: Mabel
instructions: Cut raw potatoes in dice and parboil 10 minutes in salted water.
Same quantity cold chicken, diced.
Make sauce of chicken-broth, thickened with cornstarch, wet in hot water.
If not sufficient broth, use milk.
To 1 pint of liquor, use 1 egg, beaten.
Season to taste, celery and onion salt.
Put a layer of chicken, then potatoes, then sauce, etc.
Cover with cracker crumbs moistened in melted butter.
Bake one-half hour.
recipes.name: Scalloped Chicken

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: grated processed American cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 cup grated processed American cheese, (1/2 pound)

instructions: Melt cheese over hot water.
Heat soup with all remaining ingredients except egg; add to cheese.
Add egg.
Stir over hot water 5 minutes.
Serve on crisp toast or crackers.
recipes.name: Tomato Welsh Rarebit

author: F Robeson
instructions: Cook, roll into shape with eggs and bread-crumbs, and fry in deep fat.
recipes.name: Cheese Croquettes

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Blanch 50 chestnuts, remove husks and shell.
Boil 10 minutes.
Put into a stew-pan with 1 sliced onion, 1 stick sliced celery, salt and good veal stock to cover.
Put buttered paper over pan and stew 1 hour.
Rub through a tammy (fine sieve) into 1/2 pt milk and enough stock to make a nice consistency.
While hot, stir in yolk of 1 egg and 1/2 cup of cream and serve.
recipes.name: Chestnut Soup

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Make a rich white sauce with cream.
Season with walnut catsup and add yolks of 2 eggs, salt and chopped parsley and a little chopped chive.
Add chopped cooked fish till mixture will leave sauce-pan.
Pour into buttered dish to cool.
Cut in pieces and fry in deep fat.
Do not let mixture be too thick.
recipes.name: Fish Croquettes

author: John Ulber
instructions: Blend butter and flour.
Mash yolks of eggs in cream over fire.
Add slowly butter and flour, melted, salt and pepper and meat from three lobsters cut in rather large pieces.
Stir continually; add sherry and serve.
Serve white label bass with it.
recipes.name: Lobster Newburg

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Boil the onion with the milk and water.
Pour over the mashed potatoes; strain; add salt and pour over the egg yolks, slightly beaten and stirred smooth with a little cream, and serve immediately with toasted bread cut in squares.
recipes.name: Potato Soup

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Cut pumpkin in small pieces.
Sprinkle with salt and cook in boiling water 5 minutes.
Drain, mash, and into a cupful stir tablespoonful melted butter.
Pour boiling milk over croutons arranged in soup-dish and sugared.
Then add pumpkin, stirring well together.
Serve.
recipes.name: Pumpkin Soup

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar together, and work the butter into the rice.
Stir with this, the beaten eggs.
Season and make up very soft; chill in ice-box; mould in forms; crumb, roll in egg and milk, and then crumb again and fry in deep fat.
recipes.name: Rice Croquettes

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Put boiling water and salt over a quick fire ; stir in gradually the rolled oats till the mixture thickens, then cover and cook over boiling water 2 hours.
At the last moment stir in cheese and butter, and just before serving, an egg, beaten light.
recipes.name: Oatmeal with Cheese

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Cover lima beans with cold water; let stand overnight; drain.
Cover with boiling salted water: bring to boil; cook 1/2 hour.
Cook onions in fat or salad oil until golden brown: add remaining ingredients.
Drain beans; add.
Simmer in 1 1/2 -quart saucepan 1 hour or until beans are tender.
recipes.name: Spanish Lima Beans

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Melt the butter in a frying-pan, and break the eggs into this.
Stir in the gravy ; pepper and salt to taste ; stir quickly, until the whole is a soft yellow mass.
Have ready the fried toast, spread thickly with anchovy paste.
Heap the stirred egg on this and serve before it has time to harden.
recipes.name: Stirred Eggs

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Mix with hands to a loaf.
Bake this 2 hours and baste with water occasionally.
Shake crumbs on top, and butter.
recipes.name: Veal Loaf

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Wash beets; trim off roots and all but 1 inch of stems: add 1 cup boiling salted water.
Cover; cook until tender, about 40 to 50 minutes.
Drain; rub off skins under cold running water; remove stems.
Melt butter or margarine; add orange peel, orange juice, and salt.
Pour over beets; heat.
Garnish with unpeeled orange slices cut in small sections.
recipes.name: Beets California

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Melt butter, sugar and yolks of the eggs together and stir till cold.
Add all the whites and the juice of one very large lemon.
Beat all up and put in a mould.
Set in a pan of boiling water and boil i hour.
Serve with foamy sauce.
recipes.name: Boiled Souffle

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Fry a very little finely chopped onion in butter, having the other ingredients well mixed.
Stir them into the onion and cook until stiff enough to mould, but not till browned.
Set it aside, and when cool mould in forms, then dip them in the well-beaten whites of the eggs, roll in bread-crumbs and fry them brown.
recipes.name: Chicken Croquettes

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Heat fat in 10-inch skillet.
Add onion, green pepper, and meat.
Cook until brown, stirring occasionally.
Add next 6 ingredients.
Cover.
Simmer about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add more water if mixture gets too thick.
Combine garlic and salt; add with beans to meat mixture.
Heat.
recipes.name: Chili Con Carne

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Cut slices of cooked ham and warm in a glass of madeira.
Pour in some thick tomato puree and a little good brown sauce.
Season and turn pan on stove till mixture is hot.
Serve with cold dressed asparagus.
recipes.name: Ham Slices With Asparagus

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Melt butter or margarine: add flour; blend.
Add beet liquid; cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Add brown sugar, vinegar, salt, pepper, and cloves: stir until sugar dissolves.
Drain beets; add.
Heat thoroughly.
recipes.name: Harvard Beets

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add the vanilla and the sugar to the whipped cream.
Arrange the slices of cake on the plates.
Place one-fourth of the orange, divided into sections and sprinkled with sugar, on each slice.
Pile the whipped cream on the orange.
Place one tablespoon of nut meats and the remaining fourth of the orange (cut small) on each portion.
Do not arrange this dessert until just ready to serve.
recipes.name: Orange Dessert

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: pimento
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon pimento, cut in small pieces

instructions: Arrange the lettuce leaves on a plate.
Place a slice of tomato, two slices of green pepper, one tablespoon of pimento and one tablespoon of cheese on each serving.
Mix the salad dressing with salt, paprika, celery and onion salts.
Pour half of the mixture over a portion of the salad.
recipes.name: Bettina Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cut the slices of bread half an inch thick and cut pieces out of each with a shamrock cooky cutter.
Toast on each side until a delicate brown.
Butter and sprinkle with salt, serve warm with soup.
recipes.name: Shamrock Croutons

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the celery thoroughly, and cut into small pieces.
Add the small leaves and the water.
Simmer for thirty-five minutes.
Strain through a coarse strainer, rubbing all of the pulp through.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Add the milk and cook two minutes, stirring to prevent scorching.
Add the celery stock and the pulp.
Cook one minute.
Fill bouillon cups three-fourths full, add two pinches of parsley and one teaspoon of cream to each serving.
recipes.name: Cream of Celery Soup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Peel the grapefruit, remove the white part and the tough membrane, leaving the fruit.
Cut with the scissors into one- inch cubes.
Place in a bowl], add the sugar and allow to stand in a cold place for one hour.
Arrange the servings in six sherbet glasses.
Place one green cherry on the top of each and garnish the plate with smilax or a fern leaf.
Stand the sherbet glasses on a paper doily on a small serving plate.
Arrange a bit of the green leaf under the sherbet glass (on top of the doily) so that the green color will be visible through the glass.
recipes.name: Grapefruit Cocktail

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the egg-white, add part of the sugar.
Add the cream, vanilla and lemon extracts.
Keep beating.
Add the rest of the sugar gradually, a little more sugar may be needed.
Beat the icing till very fluffy and until it will spread without running off the cake.
Spread each layer.
recipes.name: Bettina Icing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar slowly and continue creaming.
Mix and sift the flour, baking powder and salt and add these and the milk, vanilla and lemon extracts to the butter and sugar.
Mix well and beat two minutes.
Beat the egg-whites till very stiff and fold these very carefully into the cake mixture.
When thoroughly mixed, fill the cake pans (which have been prepared with waxed paper) two-thirds of an inch deep with the mixture.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven, allow to stand five minutes, then slip a knife around the edges and remove the cake carefully from the pan.
Turn over, remove the paper and allow the cake to cool.
Ice on the bottom side.
When ready for serving, cut in two-inch squares.
recipes.name: Small Cakes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cold boiled chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cup cold boiled chicken, cut in 2/3-inch cubes

ingredients.name: button mushrooms
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup button mushrooms, cut in fourths

ingredients.name: pimento
ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoon pimento, cut in half-inch lengths

instructions: Boil the green pepper slowly for five minutes.
Drain off the water.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika, mix thoroughly, and add the milk, stirring constantly.
Cook three minutes or until quite thick.
Remove from the fire, beat one minute, reheat, add the egg-yolk, mix thoroughly, and add the chicken mixture.
Heat again.
Serve immediately by pouring over slices of toast.
To prepare the chicken mixture, thoroughly mix the chicken, half a teaspoon of salt, the mushrooms, the cooked green pepper and the pimento.
recipes.name: Chicken a la King

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Boil the sugar and the water five minutes without stirring.
Remove irom the fire.
Add the flavoring, and sufficient sifted powdered sugar to spread evenly on the cake.
recipes.name: White Icing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and heat.
Add all the dry ingredients mixed together alternately with the milk.
Beat two minutes.
Add the vanilla and the egg-whites, stiffly beaten.
Bake in square tin pans for twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Graham Cracker Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, mix well, add the milk slowly.
Add the salt and boil two minutes.
Dip the toasted bread into the white sauce, and when soft, remove to the serving dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the toast and serve hot.
One teaspoon of sugar may be added to the sauce.
recipes.name: Cream Toast

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter and lard, add the sugar, molasses and warm water; mix well.
Mix and sift the soda, ginger, cinnamon, salt and flour and add to the first mixture.
Beat one minute and pour into a well-buttered pan.
Bake in a moderate oven twenty-five minutes.
Serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Soft Gingerbread

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wipe the meat with a damp cloth, and cut into two-inch pieces.
Place the lard in a frying-pan, and when hot, add the onion cut fine and allow to brown.
Add the meat and brown.
Add the boiling water to the meat and onion, and cook one minute.
Pour all of the contents of the frying-pan into a sauce pan, and let it cook slowly for one hour.
Increase the heat a little to allow the stew to boil occasionally.
Add the potatoes cut in one-inch cubes, and the diced carrots.
In twenty minutes, add a cup of canned tomato pulp or fresh tomatoes to the stew.
Add the seasoning (salt and cloves), and cook ten minutes.
This allows two hours for the entire stew.
If at this time the stew does not seem thick enough, mix four tablespoons of water very slowly with two level tablespoons of flour, stir thoroughly, and pour slowly into the stew.
Allow to cook two minutes and serve.
recipes.name: Lamb Stew

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add salt to the egg, beat until thick and fluffy, add the sugar and baking powder and beat one minute.
recipes.name: Meringue

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the sugar, flour and salt.
Add slowly the egg-yolk, beaten, and the milk.
Stir well.
Cook ten minutes in a double boiler, stirring occasionally to prevent lumping.
Add vanilla and remove from the fire.
When partially cool, spread part of the filling over one layer of the cake.
Allow to stand five minutes and then add more filling.
Allow to stand two minutes.
Place the other layer on the top.
Spread a meringue over the whole and place in a hot oven long enough to brown it delicately.
recipes.name: Filling

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the egg.
Mix well.
Add the sugar and mix thoroughly.
Add the milk alternately with the flour and baking powder.
Mix thoroughly.
Add the flavorings.
Bake in two layer-cake pans, fitted with waxed paper, in a moderate oven for twenty minutes.
Spread the following filling between the layers.
recipes.name: Boston Cream Pie

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and core the apples.
Mix the sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and salt, and fill the cavity with the mixture.
Place the apples in a small pan, and pour a little water around them.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Bettina’s Baked Apples

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and scrape the carrots thoroughly, cover with boiling water, and allow to boil until tender when pierced with a knitting needle or a fork, about twenty minutes.
Drain and serve with sauce.
Carrots may be cut into three-fourth inch cubes or any fancy shapes, and will cook in less time.
For sauce, melt butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Mix well gradually add the milk, and cook the sauce until creamy.
recipes.name: Creamed Carrots

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Soak the gelatin in cold water for three minutes.
Add the boiling water, and when thoroughly dissolved add the sugar.
Allow to cool.
Beat the egg-white stiff.
When the gelatin begins to congeal, beat it until fluffy, add the extracts and then the egg-white.
Beat until stiff.
Pour into a moistened cake pan.
When hard and cold, remove from the pan, cut in one inch cubes and pile in a glass dish.
recipes.name: Marshmallow Pudding

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: well beaten till light; add slowly
ingredients.raw: 4 eggs, well beaten till light; add slowly

instructions: Cook the eggs, powdered sugar and brandy over range 5 minutes, stirring.
Set in pan of ice-water and beat till cold.
Then add the cream, vanilla and a pinch of salt!.
recipes.name: Mousselaine Sauce

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Moisten bread-crumbs with warm (not hot) water and add other ingredients, seasoning to taste.
recipes.name: Oyster Stuffing for Turkey

author: E N Roades
instructions: Remove seeds from pepper; chop fine with onions.
Chop tomatoes.
Add other ingredients and cook till thick.
recipes.name: Quick Chili Sauce

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Make a batter, not very stiff, with 1 quart of milk, 3 eggs and flour to bring it to a right consistency ; pare and core a dozen large apples and chop them to about the size of small peas, and mix well in the batter.
Fry in lard as you do doughnuts, and eat with powdered sugar and the juice of a lemon.
recipes.name: Apple Fritters

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Add part of cheese to corn and sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Beat in the yolks of 2 eggs.
Then fold in the stiffly beaten whites.
Remove the tops of the peppers; scoop out the seeds and fill with the mixture.
Sprinkle more grated cheese and the bread-crumbs on top and bake in a hot oven.
recipes.name: Cheese and Corn in Peppers

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Cut bread 1 inch thick, and butter.
Cut in cubes.
Alternate in layers in a buttered baking dish, with the grated cheese.
Mix beaten egg, milk, salt and paprika and pour over bread and bake until firm.
recipes.name: Cheese Custard

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Roll out a little at a time ; cut with a pastry-wheel; spread on buttered tins and bake 5 minutes in a hot oven.
recipes.name: Cheese Straws

author: Miss Hunter
instructions: Grate corn; beat eggs with a spoon and mix all ingredients together.
Butter deep earthen dish and pour mixture into it.
Bake slowly 2 hours.
When corn is old it will take 1 quart milk; when young, 1 pint.
recipes.name: Corn Pudding For A Vegetable

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Scrape carrots; cut in fourths.
Lengthwise; place in heavy skillet.
Add remaining ingredients: cover: cook over low heat, turning often until tender and glazed.
recipes.name: Glazed Carrots

author: E N Roades
instructions: Chop steak and pork fine.
Bake in a long tin about i hour.
recipes.name: Meat Loaf

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Add chili sauce to mayonnaise.
Blend thoroughly.
recipes.name: Russian Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine 1 cup dairy sour cream or yogurt with 1/2 cup mayonnaise; season to taste with salt and pepper.
recipes.name: Sour Cream or Yogurt Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Shred cabbage: cover with boiling salted water; cook about 8 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Drain.
Melt butter or margarine; blend in flour, salt and pepper.
Add milk; cook, stirring constantly until smooth and thickened.
Add cheese; stir until melted.
Add cabbage; mix well.
recipes.name: Cabbage in Cheese Sauce

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Break romaine into bite-size pieces.
Separate water cress into small sprays.
Cut lettuce into small chunks.
Add cucumber and tomatoes.
Cut ham and cheese into thin strips; arrange on top.
Just before serving toss well with dressing.
recipes.name: Chef's Salad

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Boil 4 hours.
recipes.name: Chili Sauce

author: Auntie Jackson
instructions: Simmer 2 hours.
recipes.name: Chili Sauce II

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Sift cocoa and sugar together; pour on boiling water and let it come to a boil and boil 1 minute.
When cold, beat in 1 teaspoonful vanilla.
recipes.name: Chocolate Sauce for Ice Cream

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Beat a glass of currant jelly with a silver fork, adding the candied orange-peel, cut in small pieces, and chopped mint leaves.
recipes.name: Currant Jelly with Fresh Mint for Lamb

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients.
Mix well.
Pour over green beans.
recipes.name: Green Beans Vinaigrette

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for slow 325f.
Combine all ingredients; mix well.
Divide among 4 to 6 baking cups.
Set in pan of warm water.
Bake 45 minutes, or until firm in center.
recipes.name: Individual Corn Puddings

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Mix well, add the milk, and cook for two minutes.
Add the hard-cooked egg sliced, or cut in small pieces.
Serve hot with the meat balls.
recipes.name: Egg Sauce for Meat Balls

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Soak the crumbs, milk and egg together for five minutes.
Add the beef, salt, paprika, parsley, onion and celery salt.
Shape into flat cakes one inch thick, two and a half inches in diameter.
Place the fat in the frying-pan and when hot, add the cakes.
Lower the flame and cook seven minutes over a moderate fire, turning to brown evenly.
Serve on a hot platter.
Garnish with parsley.
Serve with egg sauce.
recipes.name: Meat Balls

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cook half the sugar, the chocolate and the water until smooth and creamy (two minutes).
Add the milk while the mixture is hot.
Stir until smooth.
Beat the egg, add the rest of che sugar and the salt.
Add to the custard mixture.
Mix well.
Pour into two well-buttered custard moulds.
Place the moulds in a pan surrounded by hot water.
Set in a moderate oven and cook until a knife piercing it will come out clean, (generally thirty minutes.
) Allow to stand fifteen minutes in a warm place.
Unmould and serve cold.
recipes.name: Chocolate Custard

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place the lettuce leaves on the serving plates.
Arrange carefully portions of grapefruit, marshmallows, celery and cheese upon the lettuce.
Sprinkle with salt and paprika.
Pour the salad dressing over each portion and serve cold.
recipes.name: Grapefruit Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the ham, salt, crumbs and paprika.
Add the egg, well beaten, and the milk.
Pour into a well-buttered tin or aluminum individual moulds.
Place in a pan of hot water and bake in a moderate oven for thirty minutes.
Unmould on a platter.
Serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Ham Timbales

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add the milk slowly to the flour and salt, stirring constantly, until a smooth paste is formed.
Beat and add the remainder of the milk, and the egg.
Beat vigorously for three minutes.
Fill very hot gem pans three-fourths full.
Bake thirty minutes in a hot oven.
They are done when they have "popped" at least twice their size, and when they slip easily out of the pan.
Iron pans are the best.
recipes.name: Pop-Overs

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix and sift the dry ingredients.
Add the egg and the sour milk.
Beat two minutes.
Add the melted butter; beat one minute.
Fill well-buttered muffin pans one-half full.
Bake in a moderate oven twenty minutes.
recipes.name: Bettina’s Cakes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the cheese, add salt, pepper and vinegar.
Add the oil gradually.
Mix well, shake thoroughly.
Pour over the lettuce and serve.
recipes.name: Head Lettuce with Roquefort Cheese Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: slice of ham
ingredients.raw: 1 pound slice of ham, three-fourths of an inch thick

instructions: Remove the rind from ham.
Stick the cloves into both sides.
Place in a pan just the size of the meat.
Pour the vinegar, water, sugar and mustard (well mixed) over the ham.
Baste frequently.
Bake in moderate oven until crisp and tender (about forty-five minutes).
recipes.name: Bettina’s Baked Ham

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: liter of white bread
ingredients.raw: 1 liter of white bread, one day old

ingredients.name: yards each of red white and blue ribbon
ingredients.raw: 2 yards each of red white and blue ribbon

instructions: Cut the bread very thin with a sharp knife.
Remove all crusts.
Place a damp cloth around the prepared slices when very moist, and tender.
Spread with butter which has been creamed with a fork until soft.
Roll the sandwiches up carefully like a roll of paper.
Cut the ribbon into six-inch strips, and tie around the sandwiches.
Place in a bread box to keep moist.
Pile on a plate in log cabin fashion.
recipes.name: Washington’s Birthday Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: When the nut bread is one day old, cut in very thin slices.
Cream the butter and spread one piece of bread carefully with butter.
Place another piece on the top.
Press firmly.
Make all the sandwiches in this way.
Allow to stand in a cool, damp place for one hour.
Make a paper hatchet pattern.
Lay the pattern on top of each sandwich and with a sharp knife, trace around the pattern.
Cut through carefully and the sandwiches will resemble hatchets.
This is not difficult to do and is very effective.
Washington’s birthday sandwiches 1 loaf of white bread one day old 8 t-butter 2 yards each of red, white and blue ribbon cut the bread very thin with a sharp knife.
Remove ali crusts.
Place a damp cloth around the prepared slices when very moist, and tender.
Spread with butter which has been creamed with a fork until soft.
Roll the sandwiches up carefully like a roll of paper.
Cut the ribbon into six-inch strips, and tie around the sandwiches.
Place in a bread box to keep moist.
Pile on a plate in log cabin fashion.
recipes.name: Nut Bread Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flours, baking powder, salt, nut meats and sugar.
Break the egg in the milk and add to the dry ingredients.
Mix thoroughly, pour into a well-buttered bread pan and allow to rise for twenty minutes.
Bake in a moderate oven for fifty minutes.
recipes.name: Nut Bread for Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the pineapple, marshmallows, grapefruit, white cherries and nuts.
Add the salad dressing.
Serve immediately.
Place waxed paper in the paper cups of the small, black, three-cornered hats.
Place one serving of salad in each cup.
Put one teaspoon of whipped cream on top and half a cherry on that.
Stick a tiny silk american flag into each portion.
recipes.name: Washington Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash thoroughly the rinds of the fruits.
Weigh the fruit, and slice it evenly.
To each pound of fruit, add one quart of cold water.
Let the mixture stand for twenty-four hours.
Cook slowly for one hour.
Drain.
Weigh the cooked fruit, and add an equal weight of sugar.
Cook with the sugar for thirty minutes, or until it stiffens slightly when tried on a dish.
Pour into sterilized jelly glasses.
When cool seal with hot paraffin.
recipes.name: Orange Marmalade

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Add the salt to the white of an egg, and beat the egg-white very stiff.
Then add the sugar, baking powder, nuts, dates and lemon extract.
Drop from a teaspoon onto a buttered pan.
Bake in a slow oven until delicately browned, about twenty-five minutes.
recipes.name: Bettina's Date Kisses

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Make a delicate brown toast and butter each slice.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon, and place in a shaker.
Shake the desired quantities of sugar and cinnamon over the hot buttered toast.
Keep in a warm place until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Cinnamon Toast

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, bran and sugar.
Add the milk and water.
Beat vigorously for one minute and then add the butter.
Pour into a well-buttered bread pan and bake forty minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Gluten Bread

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the tomatoes, salt, paprika, cheese and celery.
Add half the bread crumbs.
Pour into a well-buttered baking dish.
Melt the butter, add the remaining crumbs and place on top of the mixture.
Bake twenty minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Baked Tomatoes and Cheese

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place the milk, onion and celery over the fire.
Allow to get very hot.
Remove from the fire and let stand for ten minutes.
Remove the celery and onion from the milk.
Melt the butter, add the flour.
Mix well and slowly add the milk.
Cook until the consistency of white sauce.
Add the egg, well beaten, the salt, paprika, and beef.
Pour into well-buttered individual dishes.
Place in a moderate oven and bake twenty-five minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to stand two minutes.
Remove from the moulds and garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Corned Beef au Gratin

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Soak the gelatin in cold water for five minutes.
Add the hot milk and allow it to dissolve thoroughly.
Add the sugar, salt, nut meats and rice, and mix well.
When thoroughly cooled, add the whipped cream.
Pour into a well-buttered mould, and allow to stand in a cool place for two hours.
Serve cold.
Whipped cream may be served with the parfait if desired.
recipes.name: Rice Parfait

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf

ingredients.name: calves' liver
ingredients.raw: 1 calves' liver, boiled and grated fine

ingredients.name: mushrooms
ingredients.raw: 1 can mushrooms, cooked and cut fine

instructions: Chop and mix all together.
Put in a bowl and place on ice.
recipes.name: Home-made Pate de Foie Gras for Sandwiches

author: M R J
instructions: Cut marshmallows in small pieces ; soak in juice of pineapple for several hours or all night.
Cut pineapple into small pieces and pecan nuts into halves.
Drain pineapple and marshmallows dry.
Serve with marshmallow and pineapple dressing.
recipes.name: Marshmallow and Pineapple Salad

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Add pimientos, chili sauce, pickles, olives, and onion to mayonnaise.
Whip cream; fold in.
recipes.name: Thousand Island Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Peel and cube apples; combine with cabbage.
Cut cheese in long narrow strips; add with salad dressing, salt, and cayenne to apple and cabbage mixture.
Serve in salad bowl; garnish with sliced stuffed olives.
recipes.name: Apple Cheese Cole Slaw

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: thinly sliced
ingredients.raw: 2 cup thinly sliced, unpeeled red apples

instructions: Combine potatoes, celery, green pepper, apples, and onion.
Add sour cream dressing; mix well.
Arrange on salad greens.
recipes.name: Apple-Potato Salad

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: day-old bread
ingredients.raw: 2 slices day-old bread, trimmed and cubed

instructions: Cut slashes in garlic cloves; add to salad oil; let stand several hours or overnight; remove garlic.
Put 2 tablespoons of this salad oil in an 8-inch skillet; add bread cubes; cook, stirring with a fork until crisp and brown on all sides.
Put greens in large salad bowl.
Break egg over greens.
Add remaining oil, vinegar, anchovies, cheese and bread croutons.
Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Toss until all traces of egg disappear.
recipes.name: Caesar Salad

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine sugar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Beat egg; add.
Add melted butter and cream; mix well.
Add vinegar very slowly; cook over hot water, stirring constantly until mixture thickens.
Chill.
Toss dressing with shredded cabbage; sprinkle with paprika.
recipes.name: Cole Slaw

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients in top of double boiler; stir in egg yolks, melted butter or margarine, and milk: blend well.
Add vinegar very slowly.
Cook and stir over hot water until mixture coats spoon.
Cool, then chill.
(If overcooked, this dressing will curdle).
recipes.name: Cooked Salad Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Sprinkle gelatine on cold water; dissolve over hot water; cool slightly.
Combine cottage cheese and mayonnaise.
Stir in gelatine.
Whip cream; fold in with lemon juice, tabasco, and sugar.
Add salt to taste.
Spoon into 5-cup ring mold; chill until firm.
Unmold.
Garnish with salad greens.
Fill center with fruit.
Serve sour cream dressing separately.
recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Dessert Salad

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Drain beans; combine with onion, relish, and ketchup.
Add enough mayonnaise or salad dressing to hold ingredients together.
Chill.
Serve on crisp lettuce; garnish with quartered tomatoes.
recipes.name: Kidney Bean Salad

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Entire wheat flour as needed for dough.
Mix in morning and let it rise till light.
Knead; put in tins and let rise again before baking.
recipes.name: Nut or Noisette Bread

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Fry in boiling lard, like doughnuts, only very small.
recipes.name: Rye Drop Cakes

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Put all ingredients in a jar with a tight-fitting cover.
Let stand several hours.
Remove garlic.
Shake thoroughly before using.
Blue cheese dressing: crumble 3 ounces blue cheese; stir into french dressing.
Zesty dressing: to french dressing add 1 teaspoon minced onion, 3 tablespoons tomato catsup and 1 teaspoon worcestershire sauce.
recipes.name: French Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine all ingredients; beat with rotary egg beater until light and fluffy.
recipes.name: Golden Salad Dressing

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine flour and sugar in top of double boiler; stir in egg.
Add fruit juices.
Stir over hot water until thickened.
Chill.
Whip cream; fold in.
recipes.name: Luscious Dressing

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Mix dry ingredients ; then add butter and eggs and vinegar and cook in double boiler till thick.
Cool and add enough cream to beat smooth.
When cold, add best of cream, whipped stiff.
Put in ice-box for several hours before serving.
recipes.name: Boiled Dressing for Marshmallow Pineapple Salad

author: Porter at Camp

ingredients.name: bread crumbs
ingredients.raw: 1 pint bread crumbs, soaked in boiling water

ingredients.name: corn meal
ingredients.raw: corn meal, enough for a thick batter

instructions: Steam for 5 hours.
recipes.name: Brown Bread

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Cut brown bread in thin slices and spread with the following mixture: boil together rest of ingredients.
Simmer till soft; add teaspoonful vanilla ; beat to a smooth paste and spread on bread.
Alternate slices of brown and white bread, buttered and pressed closely together and cut transversely, make attractive sandwiches.
recipes.name: Fig Sandwiches

author: Kate Harkness
instructions: Mix and spread on very thin bread.
recipes.name: Filling For Sandwiches

author: Mrs Chester Ballou Smith
instructions: Bake in moderate oven like gingerbread.
recipes.name: Graham Bread

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the bran, flour, soda, baking powder, salt, raisins and nuts.
Add the molasses, sugar, milk and water.
Stir well for two minutes.
Fill a well-buttered mould one-half full of the mixture.
Cover with the lid, well-buttered, and steam for two hours.
The steaming may be done in the fireless cooker, if desired.
recipes.name: Steamed Bran Bread

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Heat the oysters until tbey are plump.
Drain.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Mix well.
Add the milk slowly and cook until creamy.
(About two minutes.
) Add the oysters, and place one-third of the mixture in each well-buttered ramekin.
Melt the butter (two teaspoons) and add the crumbs, stirring well.
Place the buttered crumbs on top of the mixture in each ramekin.
Brown in the oven for fifteen minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley, and garnish with hard-cooked egg cut in slices.
recipes.name: Creamed Oysters in Ramekins

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Beat the egg-whites very stiffly.
Add very carefully the powdered sugar.
Cut and fold in the bread crumbs and the baking powder.
Add the chocolate, cinnamon and vanilla.
Drop the mixture from the tip of a spoon, two inches apart upon a well-greased pan.
Bake in a moderate oven twelve to fifteen minutes.
recipes.name: Chocolate Kisses

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix and sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut in the fat with a knife.
Add the egg and milk, using the knife toe make a soft dough.
Toss onto a floured board.
Roll out to a thickness of one-fourth an inch.
Cut out with a round cooky cutter, three inches in diameter.
Brush over with milk.
Fold over like pocket-book rolls.
Place in a tin pan and brush over the top with one tablespoon of milk to which has been added one teaspoon of sugar.
Bake in a moderate oven for twenty minutes.
recipes.name: Egg Rolls

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour and mix well.
Add the milk and cook one minute.
Add the salmon, salt, paprika, egg diced, lemon juice, pickle and parsley.
Mix thoroughly with a silver fork, being careful not to let the mixture get pasty.
Pour into a well-buttered baking dish, melt the butter and add the crumbs.
Place buttered crumbs on the top.
Bake twenty- five minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Escalloped Salmon

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix one tablespoon of the peach juice with the flour.
Gradually add the rest of the peach and lemon juice.
Add the salt.
Cook one minute.
Add the butter.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Peach Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mash two peach halves, add the egg, milk, vanilla, melted butter, flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix thoroughly.
Place a tablespoon of the mixture in the bottom of a well-buttered baking cup.
Add a peach half, and cover with the batter.
Sprinkle one tablespoon of granulated sugar on the top and bake twenty minutes in a moderate oven.
Turn from the cups and serve hot with peach sauce.
recipes.name: Peach Cup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Broil the bacon, cut each piece in three parts.
Butter a casserole and place in it a layer of peeled sliced potatoes.
Sprinkle part of the flour, salt and paprika over the potatoes, and add three pieces of bacon.
Continue in this manner until the dish is filled.
Pour the milk over the contents, and bake forty minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Potatoes Escalloped with Bacon

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Butter two individual moulds, and break an egg into each.
Mix the salt and pepper in the milk, and pour half of the mixture over each egg.
Melt the butter, and add the crumbs.
Place the buttered crumbs on top of each egg.
Bake in a moderate oven twenty minutes.
Serve in the moulds.
recipes.name: Baked Eggs

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, baking powder, 'c' sugar, dates and salt.
Add the egg, milk and vanilla.
Stir vigorously and beat one minute.
Add the melted butter.
Bake twenty minutes in a moderate oven, and serve hot with cream.
recipes.name: Date Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove the skin from the egg-plant, and cut into slices a quarter of an inch thick.
Sprinkle the slices with salt, pile one above the other, and place a weight on the top to extract the juice.
Allow to stand one hour.
Wash off, and cut into quarter of an inch cubes.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and pepper.
Mix well, gradually add the milk and cook two minutes.
Add the egg-plant and pour the whole mixture into a buttered baking dish.
Bake thirty minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Escalloped Egg Plant

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the potatoes thoroughly.
Cook in boiling water until tender when pierced with a knitting needle.
Drain and peel when cool enough to handle.
Cut in slices lengthwise, three- fourths of an inch thick.
Make a syrup by boiling the sugar, butter and water five minutes.
Lay the potatoes in a pan, sprinkle with salt and pour the syrup over them.
Cook in a moderate oven until the potatoes are browned, basting frequently.
recipes.name: Candied Sweet Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove the rind from long, thin slices of bacon.
Place two or more oysters upon each slice of bacon.
Sprinkle the oysters with salt and pepper.
Roll up and tie with a white string.
Sauté in a hot frying-pan until nicely browned.
Garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Pigs in Blankets

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, salt and sugar.
Add slowly the cherry juice and water.
Cook two minutes.
Add the cherries and extract.
Serve hot over the cold pudding.
recipes.name: Cherry Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix thoroughly the corn starch, sugar and salt.
Gradually add the cold water and then the juice.
Cook over hot water until the mixture becomes quite thick.
Add the egg-yolk.
Mix well, cool slightly and add the egg-white stiffly beaten.
Pour into a well-moistened custard mould.
Allow to stand for half an hour or more.
Serve with cherry sauce.
recipes.name: Corn Starch Fruit Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Boil the water, add the salt.
Add the macaroni cut in small pieces.
Boil until tender (about fifteen minutes) and drain.
Butter a baking dish.
Add a layer of macaroni, a layer of tomatoes and some green pepper.
Sprinkle with salt, celery and onion salt.
Add the cheese, and continue with the layers until the dish is full.
If available, use meat stock, if not, milk.
Pour the liquid over the mixture.
Melt the butter, add the crumbs and place on the top of the food.
Place the dish in a moderate oven, and allow to bake twenty-five minutes, or until brown.
recipes.name: Macaroni, Tomatoes and Green Peppers

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon lemon juice, or 1 tsp lemon extract

instructions: Beat the egg vigorously.
Add the sugar and mix well.
Add the hot water and stir vigorously.
Add the lemon juice.
Serve this sauce may be reheated if desired.
recipes.name: Foamy Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, soda, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, and suet.
Add the figs, raisins, molasses and milk.
Stir well.
Add the lemon extract.
Fill a well-buttered pudding mould two-thirds full.
Steam an hour and a half, with the water boiling.
Serve hot with foamy sauce.
recipes.name: Bettina’s Steamed Fig Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: veal round steak
ingredients.raw: 1 pound veal round steak, cut one-half an inch thick

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: either the white or the yolk
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon egg, (either the white or the yolk)

ingredients.name: cracker crumbs
ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup cracker crumbs, or dry bread crumbs

instructions: Wipe the meat with a damp cloth, and cut into four pieces.
Mix the egg, water, salt and paprika, and dip each piece of meat into the egg mixture.
Roll in the crumbs and pat the crumbs into the meat.
Place the lard in the frying-pan, and when hot, add the meat.
Brown well on one side, and then turn, allowing the other side to become the same even color.
Lower the flame under the meat, and cook thirty minutes, keeping the pan covered.
When the meat has cooked twenty- five minutes, add the butter to lend flavor to the lard.
recipes.name: Breaded Veal

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar thoroughly.
Add the dates, nut meats and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly, add the egg-yolks and mix well.
Beat the egg-whites until very stiff.
Cut and fold these into the mixture.
Pour into a loaf cake pan prepared with waxed paper.
Bake in a slow oven for fifty minutes.
recipes.name: Date Loaf Cake

author: Miss Anna Ballou

ingredients.name: saleratus
ingredients.note: dissolved in water and added to molasses
ingredients.raw: saleratus, dissolved in water and added to molasses

instructions: Put in buttered tin.
Pour water into molasses cup and pour over top.
Bake 1 hour in hot oven.
recipes.name: Baked Brown Bread

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Mash beans; add remaining ingredients.
Serve between thin slices of boston brown bread.
recipes.name: Boston Sandwiches

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Combine chicken, celery, walnuts, and olives with enough mayonnaise for easy spreading.
recipes.name: Chicken Filling

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Heat milk and pour over the meal and flour, into which the baking powder has been sifted with sugar and salt.
recipes.name: Corn Bread

author: Mrs E W Mason
instructions: Cream butter and sugar together.
Beat the eggs very light, separately, then sift the baking powder into the flour and add the milk last.
Bake 20 minutes.
Sometimes a little sour milk is needed.
recipes.name: Corn Muffins

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Stir cheese and evaporated milk over hot water until cheese melts.
Remove from heat.
Add frankfurters, mustard, and enough mayonnaise for easy spreading.
recipes.name: Frankfurter-Cheese Filling

author: Mrs Wilder
instructions: Wet with sweet milk and roll them thin.
recipes.name: Graham Crackers

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company

ingredients.name: ground cooked beef
ingredients.raw: 1 cup ground cooked beef, lamb, pork, or veal

instructions: Combine meat, celery, onion, and chili sauce with enough mayonnaise for easy spreading.
recipes.name: Hearty Meat Filling

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Boil together.
When lukewarm, add a cupful of yeast and let it rise.
recipes.name: Hop Yeast

author: E E B
instructions: Mixed first four ingredients.
When cool, add two eggs, beaten separately.
Bake in a shallow earthen dish in a very hot oven, and serve in the dish, like a pudding.
recipes.name: Indian Bannock

author: Evaporated Milk Association
instructions: All ingredients should be cold.
Mix milk, water and sugar.
Stir in the grapefruit juice slowly.
Canned or fresh juice may be used.
recipes.name: Grapefruit Nog

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Beat egg; add sugar.
Strain juice; add with water.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until thickened.
Cool before spreading.
recipes.name: Lemon Filling

author: Evaporated Milk Association
instructions: Milk and water should be cold.
Mix together and stir in the molasses.
A dash of nutmeg may be sprinkled on each serving if desired.
recipes.name: Molasses Milk Drink

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Take 1 egg and stir (not beat) the flour all in.
Then add the other eggs, salt and milk.
Cook on a griddle with a great deal of butter and turn over on a tin.
Can be eaten with sugar or preserves.
recipes.name: Pfannekuchen

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for hot 400f.
Sift flour; measure; mix and sift flour, salt, and baking powder.
Beat eggs until light and lemon-colored.
Add sugar to eggs gradually, beating constantly.
Sift small amount flour mixture on egg mixture; fold in.
Continue until flour mixture is all added.
Fold in vanilla extract.
Line jelly roll pan, 15 by 10 by 1 to inches, with waxed paper.
Grease paper and sides of pan.
Pour cake batter in pan.
Bake 13 minutes.
Remove cake from pan to damp cloth.
Remove paper.
Trim edges of cake.
Spread with lemon filling; roll up quickly.
Dust with confectioners' sugar.
recipes.name: Saybrook Lemon Jelly Roll

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf
instructions: Yolks of eggs, cream, flour and lemon mixed slowly together.
Add the whites, beaten stiff, with the rum and bake quickly in waffle-iron over a quick fire.
Scatter sugar over while hot.
recipes.name: Sour Cream Waffles

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf

ingredients.name: baking soda
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon baking soda, dissolved in sour milk

instructions: Make soft batter; roll out, cut and fry.
recipes.name: Sour Milk Doughnut

author: Isabel Harris Metcalf

ingredients.name: baking powder
ingredients.raw: 2 teaspoon baking powder, sifted in flour

instructions: Make soft batter; roll out, cut and fry.
recipes.name: Sweet Milk Doughnut

author: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company
instructions: Set oven for moderate 350f.
Beat egg whites until frothy: gradually beat in 1/2 cup of the sugar; continue beating until very stiff and glossy.
Set aside.
Mix and sift remaining sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt; add oil, 1/2 cup milk, and vanilla to dry ingredients.
Beat 1 minute.
Add remaining milk and egg yolks.
Beat 1 minute.
Fold in egg white mixture.
Spoon into two greased and floured deep 8-inch layer cake pans or two 9- inch layer cake pans.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool on rack.
The deep 8-inch layers may be cut crosswise to make 4 layers if desired.
recipes.name: Two-Egg Chiffon Cake

author: Mrs Harrison
instructions: Beat flour, milk and butter together and add eggs, beaten separately, very light.
Just before baking, add baking powder dissolved in a little water.
recipes.name: Waffles

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.raw: 1 pound sugar, for each lb of fruit

ingredients.name: cold water
ingredients.raw: 6 cup cold water, for each lb of fruit

instructions: Wash the grapefruit, lemons and orange carefully.
Cut each in quarters.
Slice the quarters through the rind and pulp, making thin slices.
Weigh the fruit, and for each pound allow six cups of cold water.
Allow to stand with the water on the fruit for twenty-four hours.
Let all boil gently until the rind is very tender.
No particular test can be given for this, as some fruit is much tougher than others.
Set aside for four hours.
Drain off the liquid.
Weigh the fruit mixture, and for each pound allow a pound of sugar.
Let cook slowly until the mixture thickens or 'jellies' when tried on a dish.
Be careful not to get the mixture too thick, as it will thicken somewhat more upon cooling.
recipes.name: Grapefruit Marmalade

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.note: from a jar of sweet pickles
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup vinegar, from a jar of sweet pickles

instructions: Soak the gelatin in cold water for ten minutes.
Heat the vinegar and when very hot pour into the gelatin mixture.
Stir until dissolved.
When partially congealed so that the fruit will not stay on the top, add the pickles, olives, peaches and rind.
Pour into a well-moistened layer mould or four small ones.
Set in a cold place one hour.
Unmould.
recipes.name: Bettina's Jelly Pickle

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the cream and extracts.
Gradually add the powdered sugar sifted through a strainer.
Add enough sugar to form a creamy icing which will easily spread upon the cake.
More than a cup of sugar may be needed.
recipes.name: Bettina's Confectioner Icing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and mix well.
Add the egg-yolks, the nut meats, and the flour and baking powder sifted together.
Then add the milk, vanilla and lemon extract.
Beat vigorously for two minutes.
Add the whites stiffly beaten.
Mix thoroughly and pour into two layer-cake pans prepared with buttered paper.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.
Ice with confectioner’s icing.
recipes.name: Hickory Nut Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the lettuce and arrange on salad plates.
Lay a slice of pineapple on the lettuce and half a pear, the hollow side up, on the pineapple.
Fill the cavity of the pear with salad dressing, and place one tablespoon of whipped cream on top of the salad dressing.
Arrange two nut-halves, two marshmallows and one cherry attractively on each portion.
Serve very cold.
recipes.name: Bettina Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the green pepper, cook slowly for two minutes, and then add the flour.
Mix well and add the milk slowly.
Cook until creamy.
Add the celery salt and the salt.
Wvhen very hot, add the beaten egg-yolk.
Mix well, and add the chicken and pimento.
Reheat.
Serve very hot on hot toast.
Do not cook the sauce any longer than absolutely necessary after the egg-yolk is added.
recipes.name: Chicken a la King

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cook the two tablespoons of sugar, water and chocolate together for one minute, stirring constantly.
Cream the butter, add the sugar, the whole egg and the flour, baking powder and soda sifted together.
Add the vanilla.
Beat two minutes.
Pour into two square layer-cake pans prepared with waxed paper.
Bake twenty-two minutes in a moderate oven.
Chocolate cakes burn easily and they should be carefully watched while baking.
Ice with white mountain cream icing.
recipes.name: Chocolate Nougat Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the potatoes and remove any bad places.
Add the water, and cook gently until tender.
Drain, and peel while still hot, by holding the potatoes on the end of a fork.
Mash with a spoon or a potato masher, adding the salt, butter, milk and paprika.
Beat one minute.
Pile lightly in a buttered baking dish, and place in a moderate oven about twenty minutes until a light brown.
recipes.name: Mashed Sweet Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: round steak
ingredients.raw: 1 pound round steak, two-thirds of an inch thick

instructions: Wipe the steak with a damp cloth, trim the edges to remove any gristle, and pound the flour into the meat, using a side af a heavy plate for the pounding.
This breaks up the tendons of the meat.
Place the bacon fat in a frying-pan and when hot, add the meat.
Brown thoroughly on each side.
Lower the flame.
Add the bay leaf, salt, pepper, onion and water.
Cover with a lid and allow to cook slowly for one and a half hours.
More water may be needed if the gravy boils down.
Pour the gravy over the meat when serving.
This recipe is good for the fireless.
recipes.name: Swiss Steak

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cook the 'c' sugar, milk, cream of tartar and butter until a soft ball is formed in cold water.
Remove from the fire and allow it to cool.
Beat until thick and creamy and add the nuts and vanilla.
Shape into a loaf two inches thick and two inches wide.
When cool and hard enough to cut, slice into one-fourth inch slices.
Wrap in waxed paper and pack in boxes.
recipes.name: Bettina's Peanut Fondant

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix and cook the same as chocolate fudge.
recipes.name: White Fudge

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
