Anchovy sauce or chopped parsley can be added to taste.
recipes.name: Melted Butter II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Mix the flour, lemon-juice and eggs together, stir in the water stir over the fire till the sauce has thickened add salt or sugar as required.
recipes.name: Lemon Sauce III

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Reduce the sugar and water by boiling to half the quantity, add the lemon juice and jam, and heat all thoroughly.
recipes.name: Jam or Marmalade Sauce

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Put the yolks into a stew-pan with the brandy and sugar.
Whisk this over the fire until it becomes a thick froth; do not let it boil, or the eggs will curdle.
recipes.name: German Sauce

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Melt the butter in a stew-pan, mix in the flour, and add the milk, and cook 3 minutes after it boils, stirring it all the time add the finely chopped whites of eggs, pepper and salt the sieved yolk to be used for decorating.
recipes.name: Egg Sauce II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Put the sugar into the cold water with the egg-shells, and stir frequently over the fire till all the sugar is dissolved and a thick syrup formed.
Strain well and boil up again .
recipes.name: Clarified Sugar

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Mix the cornflour to a smooth paste with the milk, then add the fish-liquor stir over the fire till the sauce boils then add the chopped parsley and salt.
recipes.name: Cheap Sauce for Boiled Fish

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Boil 1/2 pint of the liquor in which the meat has been cooked, then stir the flour in carefully.
Add the seasoning and capers.
If required for fish, this sauce must be made with fish liquor or milk instead of the liquor from the meat.
recipes.name: Caper Sauce (for Boiled Mutton)

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Soak the crumb of the roll in water, then strain away the water thoroughly ; beat the bread to a cream, put it in a saucepan with the stock and seasoning.
Bring it to the boil, then stir 2 or 3 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Bread Sauce

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: But the ground almonds in a saucepan with the water, and stew slowly about 3/4 hour, stirring occasionally.
Strain the milk through a piece of muslin.
recipes.name: Almond Milk

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen

ingredients.name: a few drops Worcester or soy sauce
ingredients.raw: a few drops Worcester or soy sauce

instructions: Mix the mustard quite smooth with the oil, add the sugar, the anchovy and worcester sauces.
Beat up the egg thoroughly, and add it and the vinegar to the other ingredients.
Beat all well together for io minutes.
Pour it into a bottle; it will keep well some time in a cool place.
recipes.name: Salad Cream

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Take equal quantities of carrots, turnips, french beans, haricot beans, cauliflower, green peas, potatoes, beetroot and celery, or any other vegetables that may be in season- boil till tender: the carrots and turnips together, the french beans and green peas together, the haricot beans (which must have been soaked overnight), cauliflower, and potatoes all separately.
When cold, cut all the vegetables into neat pieces.
Mix all well together, with some mayonnaise sauce, turn into a basin or mould.
When required, turn the salad on to a dish, and pour mayonnaise sauce over it.
recipes.name: Russian Salad

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Beat up yolk and seasoning; drop in the oil very gradually, stirring all the time, so that the paste gradually thickens.
Mix to a thick cream with tarragon vinegar.
Tartare sauce is made by the addition of 2 teaspoon chopped capers, 1 teaspoon finely chopped parsley, 1 teaspoon made mustard, or a pinch of cayenne.
recipes.name: Mayonnaise Sauce

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Shred the cabbage very fine, spread it over some flat surface, sprinkle with salt, and leave 24 hours, then rub the cabbage in a clean cloth.
Add the spice, tied up in a muslin bag, to the vinegar, and let it come to the boil meanwhile, place the cabbage in a jar which has a cover with the slices of beetroot on top.
When the vinegar boils, pour it over the cabbage, and cover close when it has become quite cold.
This pickle will be ready for use in a few days.
recipes.name: Red Cabbage, Pickled

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church

ingredients.name: cooked peas
ingredients.raw: 2 cup cooked peas, put through sieve

ingredients.name: a little lemon juice
ingredients.raw: a little lemon juice, or vinegar, if desired.

instructions: If too stiff, moisten with milk.
This may be used as a sandwich filling or the lemon juice or vinegar may be omitted and the mixture baked in a loaf.
recipes.name: Black-Eyed Peas and Cheese

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church

ingredients.name: cubes of stale bread
ingredients.raw: cubes of stale bread, to partly fill baking dish

instructions: Bake in a moderate oven until it gives custard test.
Variation for cheese pudding: break the bread in pieces, have about 1 cup, and soak in the milk; add cheese, egg, etc and bake.
recipes.name: Cheese Custard II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream cheese and butter - add flour.
Shape into balls about the size of a walnut.
Chill in refrigerator for at least four hours or store in freezer.
Bake in moderately hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Cheese Puffs

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: strawberry
ingredients.raw: 1 package strawberry, raspberry, or cherry flavored gelatin

ingredients.name: cherry juice
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cherry juice, and cold water

ingredients.name: pineapple juice
ingredients.raw: 1 cup pineapple juice, and cold water

instructions: Dissolve red gelatin in hot water; add drained cherry juice and enough water to make 1 cup.
Pour into mold and add cherries when partially set.
Dissolve green gelatin in hot water; add juice and water.
Chill in pan until it begins to thicken.
Add remaining ingredients and pour on top of firm red layer.
Chill until set.
recipes.name: Christmas Salad

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church

ingredients.name: fresh corn pulp or canned corn
ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cup dried corn, soaked 2 to 4 hours in 3 cups cold water and cooked about 1 hour
ingredients.raw: 1 quart fresh corn pulp or canned corn, or 1 1/2 cup dried corn, soaked 2 to 4 hours in 3 cups cold water and cooked about 1 hour

ingredients.name: fat salt pork
ingredients.raw: 1/4 pound fat salt pork, or drippings

instructions: Cut the pork in half-inch cubes and try out the fat.
Add onion to fat and cook until tender.
Add 1 pint water to onion and fat, and simmer.
When potatoes are parboiled, drain, and pour over them the strained water from the onion.
Add corn and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Add milk and seasonings.
Add crackers just as the chowder is put in the serving dish.
recipes.name: Corn Chowder III

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church

ingredients.name: one-inch blocks of left-over cereal
ingredients.note: such as fine hominy, cream of wheat, or farina
ingredients.raw: 1/4 pint one-inch blocks of left-over cereal, such as fine hominy, cream of wheat, or farina

instructions: Put the blocks of cereal in a baking dish, add the sauce to which the grated cheese has been added, and bake.
recipes.name: Gnocchi

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church
instructions: Pick over beans, wash carefully, and put to soak in cold water over night or several hours.
Drain.
Put beans and pork over fire with plenty of water to cover.
Cook slowly until soft, no definite time can be given as the beans differ in time required.
It may be from one to four hours.
When the beans are soft put in a deep baking pan and bake slowly at least four hours.
Stir occasionally and add more water as needed.
About an hour before serving add 1/2 cup cottolene, or other fat, and return to oven to brown.
If sweetened beans are preferred add 1/2 cup syrup when beans are first put in.
Oven.
recipes.name: Hampton Corn Bread II

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church
instructions: Make a sauce of the milk, flour, and butter.
When it thickens add cheese cut fine.
Remove from the fire and stir carefully while the cheese melts.
Too much heat will make it curdle.
Mix with the hominy, that has been heated before mixing and serve at once, or if desired sprinkle with buttered crumbs and bake just enough to brown crumbs.
recipes.name: Hominy with Cheese

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church
instructions: Cook the peas and rice separately.
Cook the onion in the bacon fat.
Add rice and peas and cook until dry.
Add seasoning.
recipes.name: Hoppin' John

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Filling: mix together: liver, ground fine, onion, salt, dash of pepper.
Sift together: flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in finely: shortening.
Stir in: milk.
Round up on lightly floured cloth covered board.
Knead lightly (about 30 seconds).
Roll or pat out about 1/4" thick.
Spread with liver filling, roll like a jelly roll.
Seal well by pinching the edges together, cut into 1" slices.
Place a little apart on a cookie sheet.
Bake at 425f for 10- 12 minutes; until golden brown.
Serve piping hot.
recipes.name: Liver Pinwheels

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Wash and clean 6 or more pig's feet and place in kettle to boil.
Cover with water.
Boil 1 hour.
Salt to taste, continue to boil until soft.
When cooked, place the meat in a stone jar.
Pour over this hot vinegar, which has been boiled with sliced onion and spice.
Let stand at least 2 days before using.
recipes.name: Nalozene Veprove Nozicky (Pickled Pigs Feet)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, or 2/3 cup brown sugar

instructions: Combine rice, milk, sugar, and salt; pour into greased 1-1/2 quart baking dish.
Bake in a slow oven (300f) one hour, stirring several times.
Add lemon peel, nutmeg, and raisins.
Continue baking 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Old-Time Rice Pudding

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Blend shortening, egg, and sugar.
Add pineapple and nuts.
Sift dry ingredients; add them to pineapple mixture until dough is stiff enough to drop.
Bake in 350f oven.
recipes.name: Pineapple Cookies

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Cut fish into serving pieces.
Wash quickly in cold water.
Dry with a cloth.
Salt and.
Pepper each piece, cover with cloth and let stand one half hour.
Dip into flour, beaten egg, and then in bread crumbs, and fry in one half lard and one half butter.
Fry uncovered slowly until golden brown on both sides.
A suitable sauce to serve with fish is equal portions of chili sauce and horse radish.
recipes.name: Smazeny Ryby (Fried Fish)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Brown spareribs.
Add salt and pepper.
Put sauerkraut in bottom of pan and sprinkle with the brown sugar.
Place ribs and potatoes over sauerkraut; add water.
Cover; bring pressure to 10 pounds and cook for 20 min.
Reduce pressure normally 5 minutes, then place pan under faucet.
recipes.name: Spareribs, Sauerkraut and Potatoes

author: Clarkson Woman's Club

ingredients.name: pork
ingredients.raw: 2 pound pork, head preferably jowl meat

instructions: Wash all meat well.
Cover with water.
Add salt.
Boil all together until done but not too soft.
If liquid boils down too much, add more water.
You should have at least 3 cups liquid when cooked.
Remove meat and remove bones, peel tongue, and cut all into about salt if needed.
Add pepper, onion (finely chopped) and vinegar.
Place the chopped meat into the liquid and again bring to a boil.
Pour into a deep bowl and place in the refrigerator to set.
Serve cold, sliced, with vinegar.
This may also be placed into fruit jars and sealed.
It may be kept in a cold place indefinitely.
recipes.name: Sulc (Pork Loaf)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Boil 3 minutes: butter, sugar, milk.
Add: peanut butter, oatmeal, cocoa, vanilla, salt.
Mix and place in small drops on waxed paper.
recipes.name: Unbaked Oatmeal Drop Cookies

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine and mix well ham, pork, bread crumbs, eggs, milk, pepper.
Arrange in bottom of well-greased pan pineapple slices with a maraschino cherry in each.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake in moderate oven (325f) for about 1 1/2 hours.
recipes.name: Upside-Down Loaf

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: large slice of ham
ingredients.raw: 1 large slice of ham, cut 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Cut the ham into six servings the size of the pineapple slices.
Place in a flat baking pan with a slice of pineapple on top of each ham slice.
Make six sweet potato cakes and put one on top of each of the above.
This may be topped with a marshmallow, if desired.
Mix the sugar, flour, butter, and pineapple juice together and pour over each serving.
Sprinkle each serving with crushed wheaties.
Bake one hour at 325f.
recipes.name: Baked Ham Special

author: Bertina A Leete
Edith Church
instructions: Heat milk in double-boiler.
When hot add hominy that has been washed and soaked in cold water.
Stir for a few minutes, then let cook for two hours.
Take from the fire and when lukewarm add eggs well beaten and salt, mix and beat all together.
Turn into buttered baking dish and bake thirty minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Baked Hominy Grits

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Boil the potatoes off cold, slice them into a salad bowl and sprinkle the chopped onion, parsley, and seasoning over them.
Beat up the yolk, and stir the oil and vinegar gradually into it pour this dressing over the potatoes mix with a fork, and garnish with lettuce.
recipes.name: Potato Salad II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Peel the onions.
And when some water with plenty of salt in it is boiling pour it over them, and let them remain in it for 24 hours keep them close covered till all the steam has evaporated.
After 24 hours wipe them dry.
Boil the vinegar, pepper, and ginger together, and pour this over the onions.
Cover tightly, and keep them several weeks before using.
recipes.name: Pickled Onions

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Wash the lettuce thoroughly, pull it to pieces with the fingers, dry it in a coarse cloth.
Wash the radishes, halve them; wash and pick the cress.
Boil the egg hard, cut the white into pieces, and mix it with the salading.
Pass the yolk through a sieve, and mix carefully with it the pepper, salt, mustard, oil and vinegar.
This dressing should be poured over the salad and very thoroughly mixed with it.
Ornament with small pieces of beetroot.
If preferred, use 3 tablespoonfuls of oil to 2 of vinegar.
recipes.name: Lettuce Salad

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen

ingredients.name: cold boiled French beans
ingredients.note: or 1 lb. cold boiled haricot beans
ingredients.raw: 1 pound cold boiled French beans, or 1 lb. cold boiled haricot beans

instructions: Boil the beans, strain and allow them to get cold (haricot beans must be soaked 12 hours before boiling).
Mix the ginger, pepper, salt, oil and vinegar carefully together, and pour this dressing over the beans.
Cauliflowers and cabbages can also be treated this way.
recipes.name: Bean Salad

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Put the flour into a basin with a pinch of salt, add the oil and tepid water gradually, then the white of egg, well beaten.
Peel the marrow, put it into boiling water, and boil until tender.
Cut it into slices, remove the seeds, dip each piece in the batter, and fry in hot fat or oil a golden brown.
recipes.name: Fried Vegetable Marrow

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Wash well in several waters, strip oif the leaves and place them in a saucepan of cold water with a little salt, and boil till tender.
Strain and squeeze them as much as possible, chop very fine on a board, put tack in the sauce- an with the dripping, pepper and salt, and mix well till thoroughly hot.
Serve decorated with hard-boiled eggs cut in quarters.
recipes.name: Turnip Tops or Spinach

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Wash them, throw them into boiling water with their skins on, and boil until tender.
Remove the outer skin.
Serve with pepper, salt, gravy or butter.
recipes.name: Spanish Onions

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Well wash the rice in cold water, then put it into the boiling water with the salt, and let it boil fast 15 to 20 minutes.
When it is quite tender, strain it into a colander, turn the cold water tap on to it for 2 or 3 seconds.
Then place it in a dry saucepan by the side of the fire, with the lid half on, to dry and get hot.
Shake it occasionally to prevent it burning, and serve.
recipes.name: Boiled Rice II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Boil the potatoes, mash them through a sieve, or beat them with a fork.
Add a little dripping or butter, and brown in the oven.
recipes.name: Mashed Potatoes III

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Brush the potatoes, peel them very thin, slice them, dry them, and fry them a light brown in hot fat.
recipes.name: Fried Potatoes

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Potatoes should be well brushed, dropped into a basin of cold salt and water, and when a saucepan of water boils they should be placed in it.
When a fork will pierce them easily, they are done.
The water must then be strained off, the saucepan drawn to the side of the fire, a clean cloth folded over the top of the saucepan, and the lid pressed down on to it.
This dries the potatoes, and makes them a good colour.
They should be held in a cloth and peeled, then re-heated for a minute.
New potatoes, if well brushed or scraped, do not require peeling.
recipes.name: Boiled Potatoes II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Choose potatoes of equal size.
Brush them very clean, drop them into a basin of cold salt and water, then dry them.
Place them on a baking sheet, and bake in a moderate oven.
When a fork will pierce them easily they are baked.
The skins should never be eaten.
Another way: brush the potatoes, peel them very thin, parboil them, then brown them under the meat.
recipes.name: Baked Potatoes II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Peel and wash them, place in cold water with a little salt and lemon-juice, and cook till soft.
They can be served either with gravy or butter sauce.
recipes.name: Jerusalem Artichokes II

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Soak over-night ; next morning put them in a jar in the oven with plenty of water, salt and a spoonful of sugar.
Stew gently for 3 or 4 hours, until quite tender.
A pinch of carbonate of soda may be added to the water, to improve the colour of the peas.
Serve either with gravy, or a little butter, pepper and salt.
recipes.name: Dried Green Peas

author: Mrs Lyle Garrett
instructions: Cook noodles in plenty of boiling, salted water until just tender.
Cook onion and celery in butter until tender, blend in flour, salt and mustard.
Ada milk.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Blend in worcestershire sauce, tabasco, flaked tuna, pimiento, parsley, olives, and cheese.
Mix with cooked noodles: and turn into a greased 3-quart casserole, top with buttered crumbs.
Bake one hour in moderate oven, 360 degrees.
recipes.name: Tuna Casserole

author: Mrs A H Lofgren
instructions: Scale fish and clean thoroughly.
Rinse well.
Place a cheesecloth in a large kettle and place the fish in this.
The cloth should be large enough to be knotted over the fish so the fish can be lifted out with the cloth.
Add water, salt, and the pickling spices.
Cover and simmer for about 40 minutes or until the fish is just tender.
Remove cover and let fish stand in broth overnight in refrigerator.
Lift out fish carefully.
Remove skin and backbone, keeping the fish as whole as possible.
Put the two sides of fish together on a platter.
Make a sauce by melting the butter.
Add flour, blend, add milk.
Cook and stir to thick sauce.
Salt to taste and add sugar.
Mix lemon juice with egg yolks and stir in.
Add mustard and chill.
When cold, fold in salad dressing and whipped cream spread over salmon that has been chilled.
Garnish.
recipes.name: Swedish Cold Salmon

author: Mrs L Friedman

ingredients.name: of fish
ingredients.note: 3 kinds, such as salmon, sturgeon, halibut, or fillets of other fish
ingredients.raw: 3 pound of fish, 3 kinds, such as salmon, sturgeon, halibut, or fillets of other fish

ingredients.name: white bread
ingredients.raw: 1 slice white bread, soaked in water

instructions: Remove skin and bones from fish.
Set fish aside.
Place skin, bones, carrots, onions, and celery in a kettle.
Cover with cold water, season with salt and pepper and cook until vegetables are soft.
Strain liquid.
To make fish balls, put fish and the large onion through grinder, then place in bowl and add eggs, bread, water, and seasonings.
Mix thoroughly.
Form fish mixture into balls and cook in prepared liquid for one hour.
recipes.name: Gefilte Fish

author: Mrs M M Lunning

ingredients.name: remaining milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup remaining milk, in baking dish

instructions: Cut fish fillets into serving size pieces.
Brush pieces with melted butter and sprinkle with salt, glutamate, and pepper.
Place in shallow baking dish and completely cover with milk.
Bake, uncovered 1 n a moderate oven, 350 degrees, for 30 minutes.
Remove fish to warm platter and keep warm, to serve over fish, make cream sauce as follows: melt butter and remove from heat.
Blend in flour until smooth and add 1 cup remaining milk gradually.
Return to heat and stir continually until thickened.
Add seasonings and if desired.
A, bit of parsley or pimiento for color.
recipes.name: Baked Fillets Margo

author: Mrs
instructions: Peel cucumbers, slice thin and sprinkle with salt.
Let stand a few minutes, rinse with cold water, drain well,.
Mix sour cream with vinegar, chives, dill seed, salt, pepper, and pepper sauce.
Combine with cucumber slices in a bowl, chill 2-3 hours.
Serve with thin slices of smoked salmon and triangles of buttered pumpernickel bread.
recipes.name: Smoked Salmon with Sour Cream Cucumber

author: Mrs
instructions: Dice onion and celery and brown in oil.
Add remaining ingredients except rice and simmer 2 -3 hours.
Before serving add rice and cook 20 minutes longer or until rice is tender.
recipes.name: Rezuto

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Pare whole melons; cut a slice from the top of each and reserve; scoop out seeds; shave bottom of each melon slightly so that it stands up well.
Blend milk with cheese- until smooth; use to frost melons and the reserved tops; sprinkle with nuts.
Set melons in center of a serving platter; fill with some of the fruit; surround with green leaves and rest of the fruit.
Set tops in place; refrigerate.
To serve: remove tops of melons; cut melons into wedges from top to bottom; spoon fruit onto each wedge.
Pass french dressing, if you wish.
recipes.name: Beauty Fruit Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Make crust of: graham crackers, butter, sugar.
Mix: eggs, sugar, cream cheese.
Spread the mixture over the top of the crust and bake at 325f for 20 minutes.
Whip cream, fold in blueberries, and lemon juice.
Spread filling over cooled pie crust.
Chill.
Serve.
recipes.name: Blueberry Delight

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Toast bread squares in shallow pan in 300f.
Oven for 20 minutes, or until golden brown, turning often.
Tear lettuce into bite-size pieces.
Rub salad bowl with garlic.
Just before serving, sprinkle cheese over greens.
Pour over greens the salad oil mixed with worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
Toss gently.
Break whole raw egg over greens; pour lemon juice over the salad.
Toss until all of the egg disappears and all of the greens are shiny.
Sprinkle bread crumbs over top of the salad; toss lightly, and serve at once.
recipes.name: Caesar Salad II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Put lemon through the food chopper, rind and all.
Mix lemon, sugar and salt together.
Wash apples, do not peel, out into 1/2 inch cubes.
Mix together lightly the shredded carrots, apples and lemon mixture.
Serve from a bowl or place a generous spoonful on salad greens on salad plates.
recipes.name: Carrot, Apple, and Lemon Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: lean pork
ingredients.raw: 1 pound lean pork, cut for chop suey

ingredients.name: veal
ingredients.raw: 1 pound veal, cut for chop suey

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.raw: 3 stalks celery, cut size of meat

instructions: Brown meat in fat, add celery and onion.
Cook until tender.
Add sugar.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.name: Chow Mein

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup soy sauce, may be omitted

instructions: Combine butter, flour and milk as for medium white sauce.
Add bean sprouts, mushrooms and soy sauce to white sauce.
Mix the two mixtures and heat.
Serve with dry chow mein noodles.
recipes.name: Cream Sauce Mixture

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift flour, salt into mixing bowl.
Cut in shortening.
Dissolve yeast in water.
Stir into flour mixture with sour cream, eggs, vanilla.
Mix well with hand.
Cover with damp cloth and refrigerate 2 hours.
Roll half of dough on sugared board into an oblong, 8x16.
Fold ends toward center, ends overlapping.
Sprinkle with sugar, roll again to same size.
Repeat a third time.
Roll about 1/4" thick but into strips 1x4".
Twist ends in opposite directions-stretching dough slightly.
Put in shape of horseshoe on ungreased baking sheet-pressing ends to keep shape,.
Repeat with rest of dough.
Heat oven to 375f (quick moderate).
Bake about 15 minutes or until delicately browned.
Take from the baking sheet immediately.
recipes.name: German Sour Cream Twists

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: small can crushed pineapple
ingredients.raw: 1 small can crushed pineapple, drain juice

instructions: Melt marshmallows with milk and let cool.
Add pineapple and whipped cream and fold into above.
Combine crackers and butter and line 8 or 9 inch pie plate.
Save 1/4 cup for the top.
Pour in marshmallow mixture and place in refrigerator over night.
Sprinkle 1/4 cup of cracker mixture on top; or whipped cream may be used for topping.
recipes.name: Marshmallow Dessert

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Clean brains.
Put them into warm water for one half hour.
Then peel them.
Wash in cold water - drain well.
Place the butter into the skillet to melt, add brains and salt, cook slowly stirring occasionally.
Cook uncovered for about 20 minutes.
Mix in the eggs and cook until eggs are done.
Pepper.
recipes.name: Michana vejce s Mozkem (Scrambled Eggs with Brains)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Simmer the giblets about water.
Soak bread (cubed) in broth from giblets or milk or part of each.
Saute onion, celery in margarine.
Combine with: poultry seasoning, marjoram, eggs, salt, diced giblets.
recipes.name: Nadivka (Dressing for Stuffing Poultry)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Boil water, allow to cool.
Pour over lemons, oranges, raisins, dandelion blossoms, and sugar.
Add yeast.
Let stand 10 days, then strain.
Let stand again 4 weeks.
Then put in jugs.
recipes.name: Vino Pampeliskove (Dandelion Wine)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: In each quart jar place dill, clove garlic, grape leaves, alum (the size of a pea), cucumbers which have been washed and trimmed (if they are large they may be quartered).
Bring to a boil and pour over the cucumbers, filling each jar with water, vinegar, salt.
This will make about 4 quarts.
Seal and allow to set for several weeks before using.
recipes.name: Zavareny Okurky s Koprem (Dill Pickles)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix together flour, sugar, egg, soda, salt and drained fruit cocktail.
Place in ungreased 8-inch square pan.
On top of this spread a mixture of the brown sugar and nuts.
Bake in moderately slow oven (300 degrees) one hour.
When cool, cut in squares and serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Fruit Cocktail Torte

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Beat egg yolks, sugar, and salt together until light and lemon colored.
Add cream, flavoring, cardamon seeds, and stiffly beaten egg whites.
Add flour and mix thoroughly.
Chill in refrigerator several hours or over night.
On a lightly floured board roll chilled dough out 1/8 inch thick and cut into diamond shapes about two inches in length.
Cut a slit near the top of one point and draw opposite point through the slit.
Fry in deep fat (360f) until golden brown.
Drain and sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
recipes.name: Hungarian Delicate Fritters

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix flour, soda, salt, and sift three times.
Cream butter, add sugar, cream well.
Add beaten egg, cherries (quartered), nuts, and mix well.
Add chocolate and cherry syrup and mix.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk.
Mix until smooth.
Pour into greased 9 inch pan.
Bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes.
recipes.name: Maraschino Cherry Chocolate Cake

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: poppy seed
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup poppy seed, soaked in milk

instructions: Mix crumbs and brown sugar.
Add butter.
Line a pie pan with mixture.
Cook milk, sugar, yolks, cornstarch, poppy seed, and vanilla in double boiler until thick.
Cool.
Pour into crust.
Beat egg whites with sugar until quite stiff.
Spread over filling.
Bake at 350f for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Poppy Seed Torte

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: In large saucepan, add onion and potatoes.
Cook covered for 15 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
Blend in milk, and salt.
Heat, but do not boil.
recipes.name: Potato Soup IV

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cook the noodles in boiling, salted water to which the garlic has been added, for 10 minutes.
Drain.
Mix, with other ingredients.
Put in a buttered casserole, and bake 45 minutes, in a moderate oven (350 f).
Sprinkle generously with cheese and paprika.
Return to oven for 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Scalloped Noodles, Hungarian Style

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter and add sugar gradually.
Add berries and nuts.
Mix well.
Fold wafer crumbs into beaten egg whites.
Arrange alternate layers of wafer mixture and fruit.
Chill at least 12 hours.
Cut into squares and serve with whipped cream and garnish with a whole berry, if desired.
recipes.name: Virginia Strawberry Supreme

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cut chocolate cake in half.
Place on a board or cookie sheet covered with paper.
Beat the egg whites with the vanilla and cream of tartar until frothy.
Add sugar gradually and continue beating until stiff and glossy (holds peaks when beater is removed).
Place cooled cake on several thicknesses of wrapping paper on a board and pan.
Cut neopolitan ice cream into 3 equal pieces and place on cake.
Cover cake and ice cream with meringue.
Make sure the ice cream is completely sealed in.
Bake in very hot oven (500f) for 3 minutes, until meringue is delicately brown.
Slip from board to platter.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Baked Alaska

author: Mrs F Kalm
instructions: Drain liquid from salmon and to it add strained tomatoes, salt, sugar, and pickling spices.
Bring mixture to a boil and strain.
Saute onion in butter until tender but not brown.
Add strained tomato mixture.
Remove any outside skin from salmon, cut in slices.
Lay slices in tomato mixture and simmer for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Point Adams Special

author: Mrs Mary Lum
instructions: Grind sturgeon twice, add remaining ingredients except onion, whip together thoroughly, add onion and mix.
Drop by small teaspoon into boiling chicken broth, and cook a few minutes until done.
For fish patties, eliminate chicken broth, form fish mixture into patties and fry on both aides in a small amount of peanut or salad oil.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Balls II

author: Anne Strachan
instructions: Combine all ingredients, except lettuce, being careful not to break the fish into small pieces.
Chill.
Serve in lettuce cups.
recipes.name: Rockfish Salad

author: Mrs Clifford Olsen

ingredients.name: large carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 large carrots, cut in 3/4 in. cubes

ingredients.name: fresh or thawed frozen cod
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound fresh or thawed frozen cod, filets

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound potatoes, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

ingredients.name: celery seed
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon celery seed, or 1/4 cup diced celery

instructions: Saute bacon in deep kettle or dutch oven until lightly browned.
Remove bacon and set aside.
In same kettle, saute onion slices until tender.
Add fish, cut in 2 1/2 inch pieces, add next seven ingredients.
Simmer covered, until vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add tomatoes, heat through.
Garnish with parsley and bacon bite.
recipes.name: Codfish Stew

author: Mrs Henry Larsen
instructions: Make rich cream sauce with milk, capers and chives.
Add 14 sturgeon balls and crabmeat.
Heat slowly in casserole or double boller; garnish with parsley and pimiento when serving.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Balls With Crab Supreme

author: Mrs Henry Larsen

ingredients.name: potato flour
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoon potato flour, or all-purpose flour

instructions: Grind sturgeon three or four times with onion.
Put into a bowl and beat with electric beater while adding the milk slowly, add remaining ingredients and continue beating for about 20 minutes (more beating the better).
Drop by tablespoon (the size of walnuts) in hot broth made from trimmings of sturgeon, with salt added.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes in broth, sturgeon balls may be frozen for future use.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Balls

author: Mrs C M Love
instructions: Marinate fish fillets in french dressing to cover for 1 hour.
Saute eggplant slices in oil.
Remove slices, and add parsley, onions, and seasonings, and saute.
Oil a 2 quart casserole, and alternate layers of sauteed seasonings, egg plant and fish fillets.
Top with tomato sauce that has been mixed with 1 can water and mushrooms.
Bake in hot oven, 450 degrees for 20 minutes.
Serve with garlic bread.
recipes.name: Armenian

author: A Y Engbretson
instructions: Place 1 fillet in bottom of baking dish.
Cover with a layer of mushrooms and sprinkle with 5 or 6 drops of garlic juice.
Cover with second fillet.
Place butter on top of fillet.
Bake in covered dish at 350f for 10 to 16 minutes.
Drain off liquor from baked fish.
Make a white sauce using some of the fish liquor.
Cover the fillets with the sauce.
Garnish and serve.
recipes.name: Fillet of Sole (Stuffed)

author: Carl Johnson
instructions: Soak salmon in fresh water 12 hours.
Cut into slices one-fourth inch thick.
Put a layer of pickling spice on bottom of a quart jar, then a layer of fish, a layer of onion slices; spice, fish, sugar, onion, etc.
When full, add vinegar to cover and let stand three days or more.
Makes one quart.
recipes.name: Pickled Salmon

author: J H Wood
instructions: For this method the salmon is split in halves along the backbone and nailed onto boards.
Allow one third pound fish per person.

Select rather thick boards that are about a foot longer and wider than you estimate the piece of fish will be, soak the boards in water over night or for several hours, at least, to prevent scorching before the fire.
Put a weight on the boards to keep them under water.
Wipe the fish and place it, skin side down, on the center of the board.
Sprinkle with salt.
Lay strips of bacon across fish and fasten fish to boards with large headed nails, putting nails through bacon and along edge of fish.
Drive nails into board only enough to hold fish in place.
Lean the planked salmon against a block of wood or other support at the edge of a medium fire.
Cook the fish rather slowly so as not to burn it or lose too much juice.
It should however, be thoroughly done and slightly brown on the surface when served.
A fish section of 1 1/4 inches in thickness requires one and one-half hours or more to cook.
Planked salmon must be watched carefully to see that it is cooking properly, and it may have to be moved occasionally toward or away from the fire.
When about one-fourth done, reverse plank so that the upper part lies next to the ground.
Later reverse boards again to lay them on the side.
To serve cut in desired number of rectangular sections.
Take up with a tablespoon or spatula.
Serve without skin.
Serve planked salmon with tartar sauce or quick tomato sauce, if desired.
recipes.name: Planked Salmon

author: Mrs Nils Sagen
instructions: Grind sturgeon and onion six times.
Add the unbeaten eggs.
Then add the remaining ingredients alternately with the milk.
Place in ungreased loaf pan.
Bake in pan of water 400f for 50 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350f and bake for 30 minutes longer.
Serve either hot or cold.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Loaf

author: Mrs

ingredients.name: melted butter
ingredients.raw: 1 cup melted butter, margarine or bacon drippings

instructions: Remove backbone from salmon.
Sprinkle inside of fish with salt and pepper.
Crush crackers.
Add carrots, onions, celery, parsley, seasonings, well beaten eggs, and melted butter, margarine, or bacon drippings.
Mix well and place in cavity of fish.
Place in greased baking dish and bake for 3 hours at 325f.
Remove from oven and remove top skin.
Cover with the following mixture of buttered toasted crumbs and minced onion.
Place in oven and brown for about 15 minutes.
Garnish and serve.
recipes.name: Baked Chinook Salmon with Vegetable Dressing

author: Mrs J Murto
instructions: Cut salmon into 4 or % pound chunks (crsgs-wise cut through the fishâ€”â€”not fillet).
Make a brine by dissolving boiling water and salt.
Cool brine well.
Put the salmon in a crock and cover with brine.
Use a weight to hold it down and permit the salmon to stand in the brine 24 hours in a cold place.
Remove salmon, wipe dry, and wrap in the following manner: wrap wax paper around the salmon.
Wrap a sheet of white wrapping paper around it.
Wrap 2 thicknesses of newspaper, which has been moistened until wet but still able to handle, around it.
Wrap with about 4 to 5 double pages of dry newspaper, and place on the alder coals.
Permit the fish to be in the coals 15 to 20 minutes per pound.
Turn the fish frequently as it cooks, so that all sides cook until all paper is burned except the last layer of wax paper, which also will be charred.
Peel off all burned paper and remove skin from fish.
Serve either hot or cold.
recipes.name: Indian Fish - Alder Wood Charcoal Salmon

author: Mrs Jerry Flecher
instructions: Melt fat in heavy skillet, add onion and half of crumbs, mix well.
Turn into deep bowl and mix in celery seed, parsley, relish, salt, pepper, thyme, and remaining crumbs.
Mix in just enough hot water to moisten dry crumbs.
recipes.name: Rex Sole Supreme Stuffing

author: Mrs Jerry Flecher
instructions: Melt butter over low heat.
Blend in flour and seasonings and cook over low heat, stirring until mixture is smooth.
Remove from heat.
Gradually stir in milk and cook until thickened.
Add parsley, then carefully stir in eggs.
recipes.name: Rex Sole Supreme Parsley Sauce

author: Mrs Jerry Flecher
instructions: Place alternating layers (3 of sole, 2 of stuffing) of rex sole and stuffing in well greased baking dish.
Brush with melted butter and bake in 375f to 400f oven until fish is done, basting occasionally with melted butter.
Place fish on serving platter, cover with sauce, sprinkle with paprika.
Garnish with parsley.
recipes.name: Rex Sole Supreme

author: Mrs Henry Larsen
instructions: Make rich cream sauce, add capers, sturgeon balls, chives.
Add crab meat.
Heat slowly in casserole or double boiler; garnish with parsley and pimiento when serving.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Balls De Luxe With Crab

author: Mrs Henry Larsen
instructions: Grind sturgeon three or four times with onion, put in electric beater, keep beating while adding milk slowly, add rest of ingredients, beat about 20 minutes (more beating the batter), drop part at a time by tablespoons in hot broth made from trimmings of sturgeon.
Cook 15 minutes, this recipe may be cut in half for smaller family.
Sturgeon balls may be frozen for further use.
recipes.name: Recipe for Sturgeon Balls

author: Mrs Harold Johnson

ingredients.name: medium potatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 medium potatoes, (boiled and mashed without milk)

instructions: Boil halibut: bone, work until fine.
Add mashed potatoes, beat well.
Add sauce, then egg yolks, mix well.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and mace.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake an hour in a moderate oven in buttered casserole.
Serve with melted butter.
recipes.name: Norwegian Halibut Casserole

author: Suzanne Englund
instructions: Soften gelatin in cold water and dissolve in hot tomato soup.
Cool.
Thoroughly combine remaining ingredients and gradually stir in gelatin mixture.
Tour into 2 1/2 quart fish mold.
Chill until firm.
Unmold and serve on crisp lettuce leaves with a french dressing.
recipes.name: De Luxe Shrimp Salad

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Knead almond paste.
Add: egg whites.
Mix well.
Add: sugar (1 cup at a time).
Add: vanilla or rum flavoring.
Knead (total mixing time - 15 minutes).
Dust working surface with powdered sugar.
It may be necessary to work in additional powdered sugar to acquire the right consistency.
Divide the dough into small pieces, (being sure to keep remaining dough covered,) and with the hands mold into the shapes of fruits and vegetables.
Lay finished pieces on a mound of flour so that the bottom surfaces will not flatten while drying.
Food coloring may be used to obtain the desired colors of dough or the color may be brushed on after the molded pieces have dried.
Allow to dry overnight or longer before glazing with warmed corn syrup or a commercial glaze.
Artificial marzipan leaves may be inserted or leaves and stem may be piped on with decorators icing.
recipes.name: Marcipan (Marzipan)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, honey, hot coffee, raisins, and vanilla.
Add the flour with baking powder, and soda last.
Drop with teaspoon on greased pan and bake, or form into balls and bake in moderate oven 350 degrees for 10 to 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Medovi Kukesy (Honey Cookies)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Boil: sugar, salt, vinegar, water.
Cool.
Wash cucumbers (about 4 to 5 inches) and place in layers in a 1 gallon stone jar with dill (about 6 heads) and grape leaves (about 8).
Pour the cooled brine over the cucumbers.
Cover with a weighted plate so that the cucumbers remain immersed in the brine.
Store in a warm place.
It requires at least 5 days before they are ready to eat.
recipes.name: Nakladani Okurky (Dill Pickles)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Beat the eggs.
Add pumpkin, sugar, salt, spice, and milk.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 450 degrees for 10 minutes.
Reduce to 325 degrees for 30 minutes or until done.
Serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Pumpkin Pie II

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Soften the butter in a deep mixing bowl.
Add the sugar, a tablespoon at a time, until all is creamed well.
Add the 3 beaten egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Now add 1/2 cup milk and 1/2 of the sifted flour and baking powder.
Beat well.
Then add 1/2 cup milk and the rest of the flour.
Add vanilla, and last, fold in the beaten egg whites.
Bake in four greased and floured cake pans (round) in a 350f degree oven for 20 minutes.
Cool on rack.
When cool, use any jam or jelly between layers.
Sift powdered sugar on top.
recipes.name: Skladany Dort s Ovecnymi Rosoly (Layer Jelly Cake)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Add the butter to the hot water and bring to boiling point.
Add flour and salt all at one time.
Stir rapidly and constantly until the paste leaves the sides of the pan.
Remove from the fire and when cool add the eggs one at a time, beating until thoroughly blended with the paste mixture.
Drop by spoonfuls on a greased baking sheet about two inches apart or bake in muffin pans.
During baking, the dough expands to twice or more its original size.
Bake in a hot oven 425 degrees until puffed and golden brown for 25 minutes.
When cool slit the side, fill with whipped cream, crushed fruit, or custard.
If desired, sprinkle the top with powdered sugar.
recipes.name: Smetanove Mechurinky (Cream Puffs)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: For dough: warm cream and butter until butter melts.
Add: salt, vanilla, egg yolks, sugar, flour.
Knead dough and place in bowl which has been set in a pan of hot water so that the dough will remain warm.
Prepare filling.
For filling, mix: apples, sugar, cinnamon, bread crumbs (lightly browned in butter), nuts, raisins, butter.
While dough is warm, stretch it over a floured cloth on the table until paper thin.
Trim hard edges.
Sprinkle with part of melted butter.
Arrange apple slices over dough.
Sprinkle with the remaining ingredients.
Sprinkle with the remaining butter.
Roll as for jelly roll.
Arrange in a grease pan (15 x 18 inches).
Bake about 1 hour at 350 degrees.
While baking brush often with milk.
recipes.name: Strudl s Jablky (Apple Strudl)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Sift flour and salt.
Cut shortening into flour mixture and work until mixture is like corn meal.
Break egg into a cup and beat lightly.
Add vinegar and enough water to make a 1/2 cup liquid.
Sprinkle over flour mixture.
Stir together and form into a ball.
Chill for a while.
Roll out and bake as usual.
Bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Testo k Pajum (Flaky Pie Crust)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Line a pie pan with pie crust.
Fill with cottage cheese, dot with bits of butter, raisins (sprinkle over cheese).
Mix together: eggs, milk, sugar, lemon extract.
Pour the custard over the cottage cheese.
Bake at 275 degrees until custard is set (about 30 minutes).
recipes.name: Tvarohovy Paj (Cottage Cheese Pie)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Beat eggs slightly.
Add sugar, salt, vanilla, and milk.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 425f degrees for 10 minutes.
Reduce to 325f degrees for 30 minutes.
Test for doneness with a knife blade.
When it comes out clean, the custard is done.
recipes.name: Vejcovy Paj (Custard Pie)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sear meat in a little butter.
Work up with fork so it is very fine.
Simmer onions and celery with meat over low heat, and then add the soups and blend together.
Mix with prepared noodles.
Add milk if more moisture is needed.
Bake tor one hour.
Sprinkle potato chips on top for a crust, if desired.
recipes.name: Tomato-less Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: large can pitted black bing cherries
ingredients.raw: 1 large can pitted black bing cherries, .

ingredients.name: almonds or pecans to stuff both cherries
ingredients.raw: almonds or pecans to stuff both cherries, and olives

instructions: Measure juice from drained bing cherries, and add enough water to make 2 cups.
Heat to boil, dissolve gelatin, and pour small amount into mold to set.
After stuffing cherries and olives, place in mold attractively, then add gelatin, small amount at a time, to set until all is added.
Serve with mayonnaise as decoration.
recipes.name: TV Salad

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks.
Beat.
Add alternately, beating after each addition milk and flour.
Fold in egg whites, lemon extract, salt.
Pour into greased pan (9 by 13 inches).
Sprinkle about pitted cherries over batter.
Bake at 375f degrees until brown.
Sprinkle powdered sugar over the top and cut into squares to serve.
recipes.name: Bublanina (Cherry Cake)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Chop coarsely tomatoes, cabbage, green peppers, onions.
Mix well and salt with salt.
Place in a cheesecloth bag and hang up over night to drip.
Then press out all the liquid possible.
Place in a deep bowl, pour over it cold vinegar to cover.
Let stand 6 hours and again press out the liquid.
Now add celery seed, allspice and horseradish (horseradish and allspice may be omitted).
Bring to a boil equal parts of vinegar and sugar (enough to cover the vegetables).
Add vegetables.
Bring to a boil and seal in jars.
recipes.name: Cau-Cau (Chow Chow)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club

ingredients.name: flavoring
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon flavoring, vanilla or lemon or both

instructions: Mix shortening, sugar, and egg together thoroughly.
Stir in milk and flavoring.
For additional flavor add 3 or 4 drops butter flavoring.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together and stir into creamed mixture.
Chill the dough.
Roll very thin and cut into desired shapes.
Place on lightly greased cookie sheet and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 425 degrees for 5 to 7 minutes until delicately browned.
recipes.name: Cukrove Kukesy (Sugar Cookies)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Heat milk in double boiler.
Mix cornstarch, salt, and sugar with a little milk.
Cook until it thickens.
Add egg yolks and cook a minute longer.
Beat well.
Add vanilla and butter.
When cool place the custard mixture in the puffs.
recipes.name: Custard Filling

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Dissolve com starch in a little of the milk and cook over double boiler with milk until mixture thickens.
Add sugar, beaten egg yolks and chopped nuts.
(1/2 recipe is sufficient to ice loaf cake).
recipes.name: Filling for Layers or Frosting for Loaf

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Cook raisins in water until tender.
Remove from fire.
Add sugar mixed with flour.
Add flavoring.
Fill two unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 40 minutes.
recipes.name: Hrozinkovy Paj (Raisin Pie)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Mix all together.
This will keep indefinitely in refrigerator.
When ready to use, you can add 1 part grated apple to 2 parts grated horseradish mixture.
recipes.name: Kren (Horseradish)

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Soak poppy seed in milk for 2 hours.
Cream butter and add sugar.
Add poppy seed and milk.
Add dry ingredients slowly.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake in layers or loaf pan.
Bake at 350 degrees.
recipes.name: Makovy Dort (Poppy Seed Cake)

author: Susan Latvala

ingredients.name: cooked elbow or shell macaroni
ingredients.raw: 4 cup cooked elbow or shell macaroni

ingredients.name: cooked shrimp
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked shrimp, or 2 4 1/2 oz. cans

instructions: Combine ingredients and mix in mayonnaise to which a small amount of chili sauce has been added.
recipes.name: Macaroni-Shrimp Salad

author: Mrs A E Young
instructions: Blend crab meat, celery, egg, and mayonnaise, adding seasoning to taste.
Cut rolls lengthwise, remove part of bread, butter and fill with salad.
Serve on crisp lettuce with sliced dill pickle.
recipes.name: Crab Meat Rolls

author: Mrs Bessie Miller
instructions: Saute bacon and onions together for five minutes, do not brown.
Drain off fat.
Add bacon and onions to potatoes, water, salt, and butter.
Cook until potatoes are done.
Add clams and milk.
Heat just to boiling point and serve.
(Do not boil).
recipes.name: Clam Chowder II

author: Mrs Harold Johnson

ingredients.name: salt pork
ingredients.raw: 2 slices salt pork, or bacon diced

instructions: Brown salt pork or bacon with onions.
Add water and potatoes, carrots, and celery.
Cook until vegetables are tender, season with salt and pepper.
Add milk and clams, and simmer until hot.
This chowder may be thickened if preferred.
recipes.name: Mother's Clam Chowder

author: Mrs Jennie Olson
instructions: Saute bacon until golden but not brown.
Add onions and celery tops to bacon and cook until onion and celery are wilted.
Add next 5 ingredients, simmer until potatoes are tender, about 1/2 hour.
The base is now completed.
Melt butter and blend in flour.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in milk.
Return to heat and cook until slightly thickened.
Add clam chowder base and heat through but do not boil, add a little butter and paprika to taste.
Serves 8.
recipes.name: Clam Chowder

author: Mrs Ragnar Nyback
instructions: Combine mustard, sugar, salt, and add oil and vinegar slowly, mixing well, lastly, stir in cream and dill, serve cold.
recipes.name: Gravlax Sauce

author: Mrs Ragnar Nyback
instructions: Split salmon, bone, rub all sides with olive oil.
Mix salt, sugar, pepper, allspice, saltpeter and season fish.
Place fish in enamel pan or glass dish and top with sprigs of dill.
Put fish in a light press by placing a heavy flat plate on it for 24-36 hours.
Keep refrigerated.
Drain liquid, wipe off spices, slice thinly and serve with or without gravlax sauce.
recipes.name: Gravlax (Cured Salmon)

author: Susan Latvala
instructions: Clean fishâ€” remove backbone.
Let stand overnight.
Add rock salt.
Slice flesh to individual taste and let stand 5 days, add sugar.
Rub into fish well.
Serve on hardtack or rye bread.
If served on hardtack, should be eaten immediately.
recipes.name: Suola Kala (Salted Fish)

author: Mrs A B Curtis
instructions: Take smoked sturgeon and put through food chopper to make ground sturgeon.
Add rest of ingredients.
Shape into small balls and roll in flour and fry in shortening until golden brown.
Add one cup water and cover and simmer for one hour.
May be served hot or cold with toothpicks stuck into them for appetizers.
recipes.name: Smoked Sturgeon S'mors

author: Mrs Arthur Paquet
instructions: Drain salmon and flake finely.
Add horseradish, lemon juice, onion, mayonnaise, salad dressing, and pepper and blend into a paste.
Prepare pastry according to directions on package.
Divide in half and roll halves into very thin circles about 9 inches in diameter.
Spread pastry circles with salmon mixture and cut each circle into 16 wedge-shaped pieces.
Roll each wedge, starting with wide end and rolling to point.
Bake on greased baking sheet in hot oven (425 degrees) for 15 minutes or until light brown.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with paprika and serve.
recipes.name: Smoked Salmon Roll-Ups

author: Lyle Anderson

ingredients.name: - 12 medium sized salmon cheeks
ingredients.raw: 5 - 12 medium sized salmon cheeks , per person

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon salt, per cup of milk

instructions: Soak the cheeks 15 minutes in the salted milk.
Shake off the milk, coat with dry bread crumbs and place on a greased uncovered pan.
Put in an oven preheated to 525f and cook without top heat at that temperature for 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Salmon Cheeks with a Hot Oven

author: Axel Englund
instructions: Mix thoroughly and chill.
Serve with assorted crackers.
recipes.name: Shad Roe Appetizer

author: Mrs Harold Snow

ingredients.name: whole allspice
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon whole allspice, be used in gravy or directly in fish balls (optional)

instructions: Mix above ingredients and form into about 40 fish balls about the size of golf balls.
Fry in butter until lightly brown.
Place in double boiler.
For gravy add more butter, then flour, and cream.
Use milk to thin a, little, plus seasonings.
Pour over fish balls in double boiler and simmer gently about 3/4 hour.
Also add dabs of butter.
(Too long over hot water will curdle gravy).
recipes.name: Swedish Fish Balls

author: Mrs G Wallis Ohler
instructions: Arrange halibut steaks in shallow pyrex baking dish, and pour over them the remaining sauce.
Broil until tender (about 15 minutes).
Do not turn steaks.
Garnish with paprika and parsley before serving.
recipes.name: Broiled Halibut Supreme

author: Mrs Clifford Olsen

ingredients.name: fresh or thawed
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound fresh or thawed, frozen cod fillets

ingredients.name: peeled white potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound peeled white potatoes, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

ingredients.name: celery seed
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon celery seed, or 1/2 cup diced celery

ingredients.name: large peeled carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 large peeled carrots, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

instructions: Saute bacon in deep kettle or dutch oven until lightly browned; then set bacon aside.
In same kettle, saute onions until tender.
Add fish cut in 2 1/2 inch pieces; add next seven ingredients.
Simmer, covered, until vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add tomatoes, heat through.
Garnish with parsley and bacon bits.
recipes.name: Cod Fish Stew (Danish)

author: Mrs H M Flavel
instructions: Chop clams, using course grinder, or cut in small pieces.
Cook 5 minutes in pressure cooker or simmer 1 hour in covered pan.
Broil bacon in oven until crisp but not dark colored.
Peel and dice potato, add 1/2 cup water and cook until tender but not soft.
Dice onion and saute, slowly, in butter until tender.
Roll 6 white crackers, fine, on board with rolling pin.
Combine all ingredients in large pan.
Let stand over night to blend flavors.
Heat to just under boiling point.
Serve in steaming hot bowls.
recipes.name: Northwest Clam Chowder

author: Mrs Andrew Young
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients.
Chill.
Add cabbage and toss.
Add potato chips just before serving, toss.
Heap in lettuce-lined bowl.
Garnish with eggs and tomato wedges.
recipes.name: Seafood Surprise Salad

author: Mrs J H Wood
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients.
Chill.
Add cabbage and toss.
Add potato chips just before serving, toss.
Heap in lettuce-lined bowl.
Garnish with eggs and tomato wedges.
recipes.name: Tuna Crunch Salad

author: Hilma Johnson
instructions: Drain the fish and flake with a fork.
Chop 1 1/2 eggs, add to fish with the rest of the ingredients.
Mix well.
Garnish with the remaining half eggs, cut in fancy shapes.
Serve on crackers or on thin slices of bread, for â€œopen sandwiches".
recipes.name: Tuna-Salmon Appetizer

author: Mrs H R Kuratli

ingredients.name: crab
ingredients.raw: 1 can crab, or 1 cup crab legs

instructions: Mix seasonings in sour cream and fold in seafoods.
Hollow out a loaf of bread after cutting off top of loaf and toast in slow oven until lightly toasted.
Place chilled mixture in hollow loaf and add top of loaf for lid.
recipes.name: Seafood Dip Ã la Bread Basket

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can mushroom soup, or chicken soup

instructions: Brown hamburger and onion.
Cook celery in bean sprout juice.
Mix soup, sprouts, hamburger and onion, celery and juice together.
Put in a baking dish and sprinkle one can of chow mein noodles on top.
Bake one hour at 350f.
recipes.name: Chow Mein Hamburger Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine cranberries and sugar.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Add syrup.
Chill until partially set.
Add cranberry mixture, nuts, pineapple, and celery.
Pour into mold.
recipes.name: Cranberry Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Heat ginger ale and pour over gelatin to dissolve.
Add sugar to fruit.
Pour into pan or molds and set.
Walnuts may be added if desired.
recipes.name: Cranberry Salad II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Slit franks lengthwise, but don't cut completely through.
Fill with fillings.
Wrap strip of bacon tightly around each frank, covering slit well.
Pin with pieces of toothpick.
Place in cold skillet.
Fry over medium heat, turning often, until bacon is crisp.
Pour off fat.
Add tomato sauce, sugar, and mustard.
Blend well.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Fancy Frank Fry

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine all ingredients, blend well.
Frost cake, return to hot oven or broiler to brown.
recipes.name: Frosting for Hot Milk Butter Cake

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine eggs, sugar, and vanilla and beat until thick.
Add sifted dry ingredients.
Heat milk and butter to boiling point, add to above mixture.
Bake in a greased pan, 8 x 8 inches, in a 350f oven 30-40 minutes.
Remove from oven and frost.
recipes.name: Hot Milk Butter Cake

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Brown onion, garlic, and meat in olive oil or salad oil.
Add other ingredients and cook slowly 3 to 4 hours.
Serve over spaghetti.
Sprinkle grated parmesan cheese on the top.
recipes.name: Italian Spaghetti Meat Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Beat eggs well, add brown sugar and milk.
Sift flour, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and/or nutmeg together and combine with first mixture.
Add cut orange slices.
Pour batter on a 10 1/2 x 15 x 1/2 inch cookie sheet.
Bake at 325 degrees f.
recipes.name: Orange Squares

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter, sugar salt and flour.
Add beaten eggs, syrup, and vanilla.
Pour into unbaked 10 inch pie crust, which has been lined with pecans.
Bake 45-50 minutes in 350f.
Oven.
Cool.
Cover with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Pecan Pie III

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Drain oysters over bowl to save juice.
Remove bits of shell from oysters individually.
Butter 1 quart casserole.
Alternate layers of oysters and crumbs, seasoning with salt and pepper and a little scraped onion.
Reserve crumbs for top.
Pour in oyster juice and milk enough to reach top layer of oysters.
More milk may be added later if mixture seems dry.
Sprinkle with buttered crumbs.
Bake in moderate oven 350f about 30 minutes until golden brown and oysters are ruffled.
Over cooking makes them tough and dry.
recipes.name: Scaloped Oysters

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (6 to 7 medium-sized) finely chopped green tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 quart (6 to 7 medium-sized) finely chopped green tomatoes

instructions: Sprinkle layers of tomatoes, cabbage, onion, and green pepper with salt ; let stand overnight.
In the morning squeeze vegetables dry.
Add other ingredients.
Pour into clean jars and cover.
Kept in refrigerator or other place as cold, relish will keep from 2 to 3 weeks.
recipes.name: Uncooked Green Tomato Chow Chow

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Combine all ingredients and stir until well blended.
Pour into clean jars and cover.
Kept in refrigerator or other place as cold, relish will keep from 2 to 3 weeks.
recipes.name: Uncooked Ripe Tomato Relish

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter, shortening, and sugars.
Add other ingredients in order given.
Roll into balls the size of a walnut or smaller.
Dip top in cold water and then sugar.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 425f for 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Angel Cookies

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Remove pits from prunes and mash to a pulp.
Add lemon juice, peel, and 2 tablespoon sugar; blend well.
Add remaining 2 tablespoon sugar to egg whites; beat until stiff.
Fold prune mixture slowly into egg whites.
Pile lightly in greased baking dish.
Bake in moderate oven (350f) 20-30 minutes.
recipes.name: Baked Prune Whip

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk and bananas.
Add nut meats.
Bake in buttered loaf pan, at 350 for 45-55 minutes.
recipes.name: Banana Bread

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix white sugar, flour, milk, raisins, baking powder and put in greased casserole.
Mix together brown sugar, butter and hot water.
Pour over batter.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Can be served in its own sauce or with cream added to pudding.
recipes.name: Boston Pudding

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: canned ripe olives
ingredients.raw: 16 ounce canned ripe olives, cut in pieces

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 pound cheddar cheese, cut in cubes

instructions: Cook and drain noodles.
Brown onions and meat in the fat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix all of the ingredients and place in greased casserole.
Bake 1 hour at 375f.
During last 15 minutes add chopped nuts and chow mein noodles to the top and brown.
recipes.name: Cheese Noodle Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine: flour, baking powder, sugar, butter, salt mix with: water.
Pour into large baking pan: cherries, sugar, butter, boiling water.
Bake 400 for 30 min.
Then 450 for 10 min.
recipes.name: Cherry Pudding II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: narrow noodles
ingredients.raw: 32 ounce narrow noodles, wider for more servings, cooked

ingredients.name: American cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 pound American cheese, diced in 1/2 inch cubes

ingredients.name: crisp chow mein noodles
ingredients.raw: 1 cup crisp chow mein noodles, for topping

instructions: Brown the onions in butter or drippings, add beef and brown.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour the mushroom soup over all.
Bake in greased casserole 1 hour at 375 f.
Put on the topping for the last 15 minute.
One may use crumbled shredded wheat in place of chow mein noodles.
Add topping.
recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift together: flour, sugar, baking powder, salt.
Add to the dry ingredients and beat well for 2 minutes: butter, pecans or walnuts, milk, vanilla.
Pour into an 8 x 8 inch pan.
Mix together and sprinkle over the batter in the pan: 1 cup sugar, cocoa.
Pour over the cake batter: water bake for 35 minutes in 350f.
Oven.
Cool and serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Chocolate Upside-down Cake

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Boil sugar, cream and chocolate until a ball is formed when tried in cold water.
Add butter, raisins, nuts and marshmallows and stir until it begins to thicken.
Pour in a well-greased pan; cut in squares before it is entirely cold.
recipes.name: Chocolate Fudge II

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Melt the butter; add flour and let cook 3 minutes; add gradually the milk, stirring constantly.
When thickened, let cook 4 minutes; add to this sauce the cheese.
Just before serving add the eggs slightly beaten and seasonings.
Serve on toast or saltines.
recipes.name: Cream Cheese

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Take rounds of stale sponge cake; dip each in sherry or maraschino, and lay on each the half of a large peeled peach; fill the center with whipped cream and add bits of candied or maraschino cherries.
recipes.name: Halved Peaches on Sponge Cake

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Cut the cherries and pineapple in small pieces and soak several hours in the sherry; scald the milk in a double-boiler, or over hot water, stir together the sugar and flour, add the eggs and beat until light and creamy; then add to scalded milk and cook until the foam disappears and custard is creamy.
Let this cool before adding cream; then freeze and when nearly frozen add fruit and wine.
This should stand several hours to ripen.
recipes.name: Frozen Pudding

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Pour the boiling water over the black tea, allow to steep with the shavings of lemon rind a few minutes, strain, add sugar and fruit juice, cool.
Then strain again, pour in claret, and dilute with ice water.
recipes.name: Tea Punch

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Beat the eggs till light, add the salt, sugar, butter and chocolate melted; beat well; then add alternately the milk and the flour and baking powder sifted together 2 or 3 times.
Put into a buttered covered mould, and steam 2 hours.
Serve with hard sauce.
recipes.name: Steamed Chocolate Pudding

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Cream the butter, add sugar gradually, and beat thoroughly, then add milk, fruit soaked in brandy and flour mixed with baking powder.
Have oven temperature 250f.
Bake 3 hours.
recipes.name: White Fruit Cake II

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Mix com starch and sugar, add boiling water, stirring constantly.
Cook 2 minutes, add butter, egg yolk and rind and juice of lemon.
Bake the crust, pour in the cooked mixture.
Make a meringue of the whites of eggs; spread on top and bake until a light brown.
recipes.name: Lemon Filling II

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Mix flour and salt, cut the shortening through the flour, add ice-cold water gradually, about 1/2 cup.
Chill on ice 30 minutes.
Then place on well-floured board, roll out, fold 3 times and roll again.
Do this 3 times, then roll to fit the pie plate.
recipes.name: Plain Paste or Pie Crust

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Separate yolks and whites of hard-boiled eggs, chop fine the whites; heat cream, add salt, cayenne and sherry, then yolks of 5 of the eggs rubbed through a sieve and the chopped whites; have ready small, thin triangles of buttered toast, and pour over mixture, garnish with parsley and remaining yolk, rubbed through sieve, over the top.
recipes.name: Eggs in Double Cream

author: Denver Gas and Electric Co
Katherine Newsbury
Helen Parker Headden
instructions: Mix crab meat, butter, bread crumbs, cream and yolks of eggs beaten together; add seasoning; wash and trim crab shells; fill rounding with mixture; sprinkle with buttered bread crumbs; crease on top with a case knife, haying three lines parallel with each other across shell and 3 short lines branching from outside parallel lines; hake until crumbs are brown.
recipes.name: Deviled Crabs

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Beat butter to a cream, add a few grains of cayenne and salt; add very gradually the cheese grated.
Then mix in the walnut meats, sliced very thin; spread this mixture upon bread, prepared for sandwiches.
This preparation is good with any kind of bread.
recipes.name: Cheese and English Walnut Sandwiches

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Mix corn starch with a little cold water; pour on scalded milk and let cook until corn starch is thoroughly done; add yolks of eggs and sugar, which have been beaten till creamy, and butter.
Cook until eggs thicken; remove from stove.
When cool, add juice of fruit and wine.
Just before serving, add the whipped cream.
Arrange fruit on lettuce leaves and place dressing on top.
recipes.name: Cream Custard Dressing

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Take fine large maraschino cherries and fill cavities in cherries with nut meats; make nest of bleached lettuce leaves and place 5 or 6 cherries in each nest, with a tablespoon of cream custard dressing in the center.
recipes.name: Maraschino Salad

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Take cucumbers; add salt and enough boiling water to cover and let stand over night.
In morning drain; take equal parts of water and vinegar, pour over cucumbers and bring to the boiling point, remove from stove and allow to stand 12 hours more.
Then drain again, and cover with fresh vinegar without water and let come to the boiling point; add stick cinnamon and sugar to taste and bottle while hot.
The day before using boil bunches of raisins in vinegar and sugar; let stand 12 hours in the syrup and serve with the pickles.
recipes.name: Cucumber Pickles II

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Clean fruit with stiff brush and wipe dry; cut crosswise in very thin slices, reject the ends, pick out the seeds.
Pour the water over the fruit and let stand 36 hours.
Then put in preserving kettle and let cook slowly 2 hours.
Then add sugar and cook 1 hour or until the mixture jellies.
recipes.name: Orange Marmalade

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Wash mushrooms; remove stems, and peel caps, and cut in pieces; melt butter and cook until tender; sprinkle with salt and pepper; dredge with flour and add cream.
Let cook until heated thoroughly, then pour on pieces of toast and garnish with toast points.
recipes.name: Mushrooms in Cream

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Take a plump, young duck; rub all over with alcohol and then hold over the burner to singe; wash thoroughly with soda water; then boil in soda water or water in which there is a little onion for 10 minutes before stuffing; then rinse in clear water and wipe dry; stuff with dressing, to which has been added a little onion, sage, celery salt or bacon chopped fine; sprinkle with pepper and salt and dredge with flour; place pieces of bacon over it.
Roast under the flame until tender, turning and basting frequently with the tried out fat.
recipes.name: Roasted Wild Duck

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Remove the superfluous fat from a leg of lamb and score the thin layer of fat on the outer side of the leg diagonally; rub over with salt and pepper; dredge with flour, and set on the rack in the baking pan.
Have the oven very hot at first, to sear over the outside; after 15 minutes reduce the heat and let cook about 2 hours; baste frequently with bacon fat melted in hot water.
Remove to a serving dish; slip a paper frill over the bone, and garnish with parsley and banana croquettes.

Remove the skin and coarse threads from the bananas and trim the pulp of each to a cylinder-shape croquette; coat each with lemon juice to keep from discoloring; then roll in egg and then in sifted bread crumbs; fry in deep fat, and dust with powdered sugar.
recipes.name: Roast Lamb with Banana Croquettes

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Wipe a porterhouse steak with a damp cloth and trim it neatly; have the broiler well heated; lay the steak on it, and place as near the flame as possible, without having it catch fire.
As soon as the surface is seared turn and sear on other side; then place broiler so that the steak is 3 or 4 inches from the flame.
If the steak is 1 inch thick, cook from 8 to 10 minutes, turning 2 or 3 times.
Place on a hot plate, spread with butter and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
recipes.name: Broiled Beef Steak

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: sliced beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound sliced beef, lamb, or pork liver

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Dip liver slices in flour and cube at once.
Brown liver in the fat; add onion, green pepper, garlic clove, mushrooms, tomatoes, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add cooked noodles or spaghetti and cook 10 minutes longer.
Or place noodles or spaghetti and liver mixture in alternate layers in a greased baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 15 to 20 minutes or until mixture is heated through and crumbs are browned.
recipes.name: Spanish Liver

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook onion in fat until lightly browned.
Blend in flour.
Add tomatoes, celery, green pepper, parsley, salt, and a little pepper.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring frequently.
Serve over meat loaf, cooked spaghetti, fried or baked fish, cooked cabbage, or omelet.
recipes.name: Spanish Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Toss all ingredients together.
recipes.name: Spring Salad (Ensalad De Primavera)

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: medium size tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 medium size tomatoes, ripe or green

instructions: Remove stem ends and quarter tomatoes (peel ripe tomatoes, if preferred).
Add onion for flavor, if desired.
Cover and cook until tender, 10 to 20 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 20 to 35 for green.
Season with salt; a little pepper; sugar, if desired, 1/2 teaspoon for ripe tomatoes, 1 tablespoon for green; and fat.
For variety, add bread crumbs before serving or top with toasted bread cubes.
recipes.name: Stewed Tomatoes II

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: mayonnaise or cooked salad dressing
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon mayonnaise or cooked salad dressing

instructions: Wash tomatoes and remove stem ends.
Scoop out center, leaving a shell about 1/4 inch thick.
Turn upside down on plate to drain (use juice in soups or sauces).
Dice tomato pulp and combine with other ingredients.
Stuff tomatoes.
Serve on lettuce or other salad greens.

Meat stuffing variation: combine 1 cup diced, cooked meat or poultry; 1 cup diced, cooked potatoes; 1 tablespoon chopped parsley; 1 tablespoon minced onion; 2 tablespoons green pepper; 1 teaspoon salt; a little pepper; and 2 tablespoons mayonnaise or cooked salad dressing.
recipes.name: Stuffed Tomato Salad

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook together the tomatoes, celery, green pepper, bay leaf, and onions about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Add salt, worcestershire sauce, and horseradish to sieved tomatoes.
Chill.
Mix well before serving.
recipes.name: Tomato Juice Cocktail

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook together celery.
Green pepper, and onion in the fat, 8 to 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Blend in the flour.
Add tomatoes, cheese, and salt.
Cook over low heal; stir constantly until mixture thickens and cheese melts.
Gradually add some of the tomato mixture to beaten eggs; mix well, then pour all back into the tomato mixture.
Continue to cook over low heat; stir constantly until thickened and creamy (2 to 3 minutes).
If desired, add a few dashes of tabasco sauce.
Serve on toast or crackers.
recipes.name: Tomato Rabbit

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook together the tomatoes, onion, sugar (if used), bay leaf, and cloves about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve and measure.
