For each cup of sieved tomatoes, blend 1 tablespoon flour and 1 tablespoon melted fat; gradually add the cooled, sieved tomatoes.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, about 5 minutes or until thickened.
Season with sail and pepper.
Serve over meat or vegetable loaf, croquettes, fish, cooked spaghetti, souffle, or omelet.
For variety, brown lightly in the fat 1 cup sliced mushrooms before blending fat with the flour.
Or for a main dish, add cooked meat balls to the sauce and serve over cooked spaghetti.
recipes.name: Tomato Sauce II

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Sterilize jars by placing clean jar, lids, and caps in warm water, and boil 15 - 20 minutes.
Cook tomatoes 20 to 30 minutes.
Press through a sieve and measure out 4 cups.
Cook apples in water until very tender.
Press through a sieve and measure out 2 cups.
Combine sieved tomatoes and apples, lemon juice, sugar, and spices.
Cook mixture rapidly about 25 minutes, or until thickened and clear.
Stir frequently to prevent sticking.
Pour into hot, sterile jars.
Seal.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
recipes.name: Tomato-Apple Butter

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook together the tomatoes, garlic, and bay leaf about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Brown the beef, onion, and green pepper in the fat.
Blend in the flour.
Add cooled, sieved tomatoes, sugar (if used), salt, and pepper.
Cook over low heat , stirring constantly, until thickened.
Serve hot on cooked spaghetti, noodles, or rice.
recipes.name: Tomato-Meat Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: chopped green onions
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup chopped green onions, or 1/2 cup chopped onions

instructions: Cook potatoes in boiling water.
Peel and dice.
Add vinegar and seasonings.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Cook eggs 4 minutes.
Combine potatoes, bacon, 2 tablespoon bacon fat, soft-cooked eggs, and chopped onions.
Mix well.
Serve hot salad on a bed of lettuce with big frankfurters.
recipes.name: Hot German Potato Salad

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Soften gelatin in the water.
Cook tomatoes, onion, and bay leaf about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve and measure 1 3/4 cups (if not enough, add boiling water).
Add hot, sieved tomatoes to gelatin and stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Season with sugar, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Chill.
When gelatin mixture begins to stiffen, add cucumber and celery.
Mix well.
Pour into a mold or pan rinsed in cold water.
Chill until firm.
Serve with salad dressing on lettuce or other salad greens.
recipes.name: Jellied Tomato Salad

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Combine lima beans with white sauce and cheese.
Pour into baking dish and place quartered tomatoes cut side down on bean mixture, bake in moderate oven (350f) 20 to 30 minutes or until tomatoes are tender.
recipes.name: Lima Bean-Tomato Casserole

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Combine tomatoes with milk.
Heat slowly to serving temperature.
Add salt, a little pepper, and fat.
recipes.name: Quick Cream of Tomato Soup

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine milk, eggs, salt, baking powder, and flour and beat slightly with dover beater to blend well.
Add potatoes immediately after grated to prevent discoloration.
Drop by spoonfuls on hot well-greased skillet (bacon drippings are excellent for additional flavor).
Fry to golden brown on both sides.
After browned, fry more slowly until done.
recipes.name: Raw Potato Pancakes

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: wafers
ingredients.note: Chocolate, vanilla, nabisco, or a combination of the wafers
ingredients.raw: 20 wafers, (Chocolate, vanilla, nabisco, or a combination of the wafers)

instructions: Crush fine and put 1/2 of wafers in bottom of buttered cake tin.
Cream: butter, powdered sugar.
Add and blend: egg yolks.
Fold in: egg whites beaten very stiff.
Put on top of crumb mixture.
Whip: cream.
Add: pineapple, marshmallow bits, nuts.
Add to the above mixture.
Sprinkle remaining crumbs on top and refrigerate at least 24 hours.
recipes.name: Refrigerator Dessert

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: hot water or fruit juice
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup hot water or fruit juice

ingredients.name: drained fruit strawberry
ingredients.raw: 3 cup drained fruit strawberry, raspberry, peach, cherry or mixed

instructions: Dissolve gelatin in hot water or fruit juice.
Let cool until gelatin begins to set and then whip until light and frothy.
Fold in whipped cream.
Cut cake in 1 inch squares.
Mix the cake and gelatin-fruit mixture together.
Put in large, lightly greased bowl.
Let set in refrigerator tor 8 hours.
Unmold and spread with whipped cream and serve.
recipes.name: Refrigerator Igloo Torte

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (about 18 to 20 medium-sized) sliced peeled tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 quart (about 18 to 20 medium-sized) sliced peeled tomatoes

instructions: Combine tomatoes, sugar, and salt.
Peel oranges and lemons.
Slice peel very thin, boil in the water 5 minutes, and drain.
Slice orange and lemon pulp and remove seeds.
Add with rind to tomato mixture.
Put spices loosely in a thin, white cloth; lie top tightly; and add to tomato mixture.
Heat slowly to boiling; then cook rapidly, stirring constantly, for 45 to 60 minutes or until thickened.
Remove spice bag.
Pour marmalade into hot, sterile jars.
Sterilize jars by placing clean jar, lids, and caps in warm water, and boil 15 - 20 minutes.
Seal.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
recipes.name: Ripe tomato Marmalade

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook bacon until crisp, remove from fat.
And drain.
Combine 2 tablespoons of the bacon drippings with tomatoes, green pepper and onion.
Bring to boiling, add about 3 cups cooked rice, cook 10 - 20 minutes or add 1 cup uncooked rice and 2 cups water, and cook gently 40 to 45 minutes or until rice is tender.
Add more water if mixture becomes dry.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add bacon.
recipes.name: Savory Rice with Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: minced green pepper
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon minced green pepper, if desired

instructions: Combine tomatoes (ripe or green), onion, green pepper, salt, pepper, and sugar if used.
Place in a baking dish alternate layers of tomato mixture and bread crumbs, ending with bread crumbs (for a thinner mixture, omit 1 cup of the crumbs).
Dot with fat.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 20 to 30 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 30 to 45 for green.
If desired, sprinkle 1/2 cup grated cheese over the top for the last 10 to 15 minutes of baking.
recipes.name: Scalloped Tomatoes II

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Clean a 4-pound bluefish, stuff and sew it up; cut gashes in fish and insert thin strips of bacon.
Place on a greased fish sheet, sprinkle with salt and pepper, brush with melted butter and dredge with flour; place pieces of salt pork around it.
Roast under the flame about 50 minutes, or until tender, basting frequently with dried out fat.
In cooking fish, the oven should be slow heat after the first 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Bluefish Larded and Baked

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Blanch and shred (or chop) almonds and brown slightly in a little butter.
Have the stock strained and ready for use.
Melt the butter, add flour, add a cup of stock slowly, let cook five minutes, then add rest of stock, strained tomatoes and lastly the cream, which must be added just before serving.
Put almonds in the dish and pour soup over them.
recipes.name: Almond Soup

author: Helen Parker Headden
Katherine Newsbury
Denver Gas and Electric Co
instructions: Mix and sift dry ingredients, add molasses and milk and soda, stir until well mixed.
Turn into a well-buttered mould and steam 3 hours.
recipes.name: Boston Brown Bread II

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Use half as much meat broth and the same quantity of vegetables as for vegetable soup.
Thicken with flour mixed with cold water, and you have a delicious stew.
Or put the stew in a baking dish, cover with rounds of biscuit dough or with mashed potatoes, and bake in a hot oven.
recipes.name: Vegetable Stew or Pie

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Make chowder with the same vegetables as for soup, but use milk instead of meat broth.
Brown the onion first in meat drippings.
Then add the cut-up vegetables and water.
Cook until vegetables are tender.
Add 3 cups of hot milk, bread crumbs, and season to taste.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Vegetable Chowder II

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Simmer a soup bone in water.
To each quart of this meat broth, add the vegetables.
Cut all the vegetables about the same size and shape.
Cook until tender in the salted meat stock.
Season well and serve hot.
recipes.name: Vegetable Soup II

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Stew sliced onions with tomatoes, thicken with a little flour or stale bread toasted and broken into small pieces.
recipes.name: Stewed Onions and Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Measure onions, peanuts, white sauce, bread crumbs blended with a little melted fat.
In a baking dish make alternate layers of onions, peanuts, and sauce.
Cover the top with bread crumbs.
Bake in a moderate oven until crumbs are golden brown.
recipes.name: Scalloped Onions and Peanuts

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: If you have an abundance of spring onions, allow 6 or 7 finger-size ones to each serving.
Cook, green tops and all, until tender in lightly salted boiling water, about 20 minutes if onions are young and fresh.
Season with melted fat and serve on toast.
recipes.name: Spring Onions on Toast

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook onions in fat until lightly brown.
Sprinkle with flour and stir.
Add meat broth, made by cooking a soup bone in water, and stir until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer until the onions are tender and flavor well blended.
Serve in bowls with a slice of toast in each.
If you have dry cheese on hand, grate a little over the toast.
recipes.name: Onion Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook equal portions of rutabaga and potato together.
Drain.
Mash and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Mashed Rutabags and Potatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook tiny turnips and their greens together just as you would baby beets.
recipes.name: Turnips and Greens

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Chop carrots or turnips and season with salt and pepper.
Add chopped green or sweet red pepper.
Melt fat in a frying pan and spread a thin layer of the vegetable in the pan.
Heat slowly, serve hot.
recipes.name: Carrots or Turnips O'Brien

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: grated
ingredients.note: ground or finely chopped carrots, or turnips
ingredients.raw: 1 cup grated, ground or finely chopped carrots, or turnips

instructions: Cook onion in fat for a few minutes.
Stir in flour.
Add milk and carrots or turnips.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir well and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Quick Carrot and Turnip Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Beat the egg slightly.
Add the milk, grated, ground, or finely chopped carrots, fat, and salt and pepper.
Pour into a greased baking dish.
Bake in a moderate oven until set.
recipes.name: Carrot Scallop

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Slice carrots thin.
Place in a frying pan with a little melted fat, cover, cook slowly until tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
If desired, fry carrots with sliced onions.
Variation with apples: cut the carrots in strips and cook as above until almost tender.
Then add apples sliced in rings with the skins on, sprinkle with salt and sugar, and brown well.
recipes.name: Panned Carrots

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Arrange cooked parsnips, split lengthwise, in a shallow baking dish, pour over them medium white sauce, sprinkle with bread crumbs, and bake until brown and bubbly.
recipes.name: Scalloped Parsnips

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: To get rid of the woody core, boil the parsnips whole, split lengthwise, and strip out the tough center.
Dip the halves in flour and fry in fat until they are golden brown.
Or mash and season the parsnips to make little cakes, and fry them.
recipes.name: Browned Parsnips

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Add finely chopped cooked beets to meat broth, along with chopped cooked onion, carrot, or cabbage.
Season with herbs and serve hot.
Some like beet soup topped with sour cream.
recipes.name: Beet Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Mix cornstarch or flour, sugar, and salt.
Add vinegar and water and boil 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the fat and beets, and let stand until the sauce becomes red.
Reheat if necessary.
recipes.name: Harvard Beets II

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: meat drippings
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoon meat drippings, or other fat

instructions: Cook the onion in the fat.
Add green tomatoes, cover, and cook until tender.
Add meat and heat thoroughly.
If the mixture is too thick, thin it slightly with meat broth, gravy, or water.
Season to taste with curry powder and salt.
Serve with flaky boiled rice or noodles.
recipes.name: Curry of Meat with Green Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook potatoes in fat until lightly browned.
Add onion, green pepper, tomatoes.
Cover and cook until potatoes are tender.
Add cooked fish, cut in about 2-inch pieces.
Season with salt, and pepper.
Cook about 5 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Fish-Tomato Stew

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Slice tomatoes about 1/2 inch thick.
Dip in mixture of bread crumbs or flour, salt, and a little pepper.
Cook in a small amount of fat until brown on both sides.
If desired, dip tomatoes in beaten egg, then in flour or bread crumbs before cooking.
recipes.name: Fried Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (18 to 20 medium-sized) sliced green tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 quart (18 to 20 medium-sized) sliced green tomatoes

instructions: Sterilize jars by placing clean jar, lids, and caps in warm water, and boil 15 - 20 minutes.
Combine tomatoes, sugar, and salt.
Peel lemons.
Slice peel very thin, boil in the 1 cup water 5 minutes, and drain.
Slice lemon pulp and remove seeds.
Add with rind to tomato mixture.
Heat slowly to boiling; then cook rapidly, stirring constantly, for about 45 to 60 minutes or until thickened.
Pour into hot, sterile jars.
Seal.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Marmalade

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fat
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon fat, beef fat may be used

instructions: Boll meat in mixture of salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons of the flour.
Brown in the fat.
Add onion; cook until lightly browned.
Pour in 2 cups of the water, cover, and simmer about 1 hour or until meat is almost tender.
Wash, remove stem ends, and quarter the tomatoes; add with potatoes, carrots, and 1 cup water to the meat.
Cover and cook until vegetables and meat are tender.
Add more water as needed.
Blend remaining 2 tablespoons flour with the 1/4 cup water; add to stew, and cook until slightly thickened.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Meat Stew

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (about 24 to 28 medium-sized) finely chopped green tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 4 quart (about 24 to 28 medium-sized) finely chopped green tomatoes

ingredients.name: (about 8 to 10 medium-sized) pared finely chopped tart apples
ingredients.raw: 2 quart (about 8 to 10 medium-sized) pared finely chopped tart apples

ingredients.name: minced citron
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon minced citron, lemon or orange peel

instructions: Combine all ingredients and cook mixture slowly until tender and slightly thickened.
Stir frequently to prevent sticking.
Pour into hot.
Sterile jars, fill jars to top, and seal.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Mincemeat

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Blend together fat and vanilla.
Gradually add sugar, creaming well after each addition.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda, and salt.
Add alternately with the mincemeat to the creamed mixture, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients.
Add nut meats.
Drop from b teaspoon on a greased baking sheet and bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 15 to 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Mincemeat Cookies

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Blend together the fat, vanilla, and orange rind.
Gradually add sugar and marmalade, creaming well after each addition.
Add eggs one at a time, boating well after each.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, soda, and salt.
Add alternately with the mincemeat to the creamed mixture, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Add nut meats.
Pour into a greased 7 1/2-inch tube pan or a loaf pan.
Bake in a slow oven (325f) 1 1/2 hours.
Cool 1/2 hour before removing from the pan.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Mincemeat Fruit Cake

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: grated lemon or orange rind
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon grated lemon or orange rind

instructions: Wash, remove stem ends, and slice the tomatoes.
Combine with lemon juice, lemon or orange rind, salt, and cinnamon.
Cook 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Mix sugar and cornstarch; add to tomato mixture and cook until clear, stirring constantly.
Add fat.
Cool slightly, then pour into a 9-inch pie plate lined with pastry.
Cover with pastry and seal edges.
Bake in a hot oven (425f) 40 to 50 minutes.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Pie

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (about 36 to 40 medium-sized) chopped green tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 quart (about 36 to 40 medium-sized) chopped green tomatoes

instructions: Mix tomatoes and salt thoroughly.
Let stand overnight; drain.
Combine with chopped onions, green and red peppers, sugar, and vinegar.
Put spices loosely in a thin, white cloth; tie top tightly, and add to tomato mixture.
Bring mixture to boil; boil gently with spices for 1 1/2 hours or until thickened, stirring frequently, remove spice bag.
Pour relish into hot, sterile jars, fill jars to top.
And seal.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Relish

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Place in a greased 8" square pan: apples.
Blend until crumbly; then spread over apples: brown sugar (packed), flour, oats, nutmeg, butter.
Bake at 375 tor 30-35 minutes, until apples are tender and topping is golden brown.
recipes.name: Apple Crisp

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound ground beef, or other lean meat

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: chopped or coarsely shredded cabbage
ingredients.raw: 4 cup chopped or coarsely shredded cabbage

instructions: Brown the meat in fat.
Add onion and celery; cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper : bring to boiling.
Place alternating layers of cabbage and meat mixture in a baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 40 to 45 minutes.
recipes.name: Beef, Tomato and Cabbage Scallop

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Wash tomatoes, ripe or green, and remove stem ends.
Cut tomatoes in 2, and place cut side up in shallow pan or on broiling pan.
Brush with melted fat and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Place under direct heat with top of tomatoes about 3 inches below tip of flame or broiler unit.
Broil until tender, 10 to 15 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 15 to 25 for green.
If desired, sprinkle with fine bread crumbs or grated cheese for the last few minutes of broiling.
recipes.name: Broiled Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Simmer together tomatoes and onion for 20 to 30 minutes; press through a sieve.
Put the cinnamon, cloves, and garlic loosely in a clean, thin, white cloth; tie top tightly; add to vinegar and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove spice bag.
Boil tomato mixture rapidly until you have but one-half the original amount.
Stir frequently to prevent sticking.
Add spiced vinegar, sugar, salt, paprika, and cayenne pepper to tomato mixture.
Boil rapidly, stirring constantly, about 10 minutes or until slightly thickened.
Pour into hot, sterile jars, fill jars to top, and seal.
recipes.name: Catsup

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter.
Add sugar; cream until sugar granules are dissolved.
Add flour, salt and egg yolks.
Stir thoroughly, then add cream and vanilla.
Pour into an unbaked pie shell.
Bake in a hot oven (425f) 10 minutes.
Then reduce to slow oven (300f) to finish baking, about 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Chess Pie Elite

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: fat
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup fat, chicken fat may be used

instructions: Cut chicken into serving pieces.
Roll in mixture of the flour, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Brown in melted fat.
Add onion; cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and simmer about 1 hour or until almost tender, adding more water if necessary.
Stir occasionally to keep from sticking.
Add green pepper and tomatoes.
Simmer about 30 minutes longer.
Serve on seasoned hot noodles or rice.
recipes.name: Chicken Creole

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Soak beans overnight in cold water or about 5 hours in lukewarm water to cover.
Add onion, garlic, green pepper, bacon drippings, tomatoes, and salt; and simmer for 2 hours in the soaking water.
Add more water if needed during cooking.
Add t he chili powder, stirring as little as possible to avoid mashing the beans.
Place in a baking dish or bean pot, cover, and bake in a moderate oven (350f) for about 2 hours.
Uncover during last part of the cooking if brown beans are desired.
If preferred, use lima or navy beans in place of the kidney beans.
recipes.name: Chili Kidney Beans with Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: (24 to 28 medium-sized) peeled and chopped tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 quart (24 to 28 medium-sized) peeled and chopped tomatoes

instructions: Combine the tomatoes, sweet pepper, onion, and hot pepper.

Put the celery seed, mustard seed, bay leaf, cloves, ginger, nutmeg, and cinnamon loosely in a thin, white cloth; tie top tightly; add to tomato mixture and boil until you have but one-half the original amount.
Stir frequently to prevent slicking.
Add sugar, vinegar, and salt.
Boil rapidly, stirring constantly, about 5 minutes.
Remove spices.
Pack chili sauce into hot, sterile jars; fill jars to top and seal.
recipes.name: Chili Sauce IV

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook together the tomatoes, bay leaf, onion, and cloves about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Blend the fat, and and sugar (if used); gradually add the cooled, sieved tomatoes.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly for about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and peeper.
If desired, sprinkle with finely chopped parsley and serve with toasted bread cubes.
recipes.name: Clear Tomato Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes, .

instructions: Cook together the tomatoes and onions about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Melt the fat; blend in flour and sugar (if used).
Gradually add cooled, sieved tomatoes.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Gradually add tomato mixture to milk, stirring constantly.
Heat slowly to serving temperature.
Add salt.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Cream of Tomato Soup III

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook baby beets and greens in water until tender (15 or 20 minutes), drain, and chop together.
Season with fat, salt, and pepper.
Or use the tops of larger beets if they are still crisp and green.
They may take longer cooking, but are high in food value.
recipes.name: Beets and Beet Greens

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Top and tail the radishes and slice finely, but do not cut quite down to the bottom.
Drop into cold water for a few hours, and drain well before serving.
recipes.name: Radish Concertinas

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place olive oil into a frying-pan and heat slowly, until it just reaches smoking point.
Remove from the heat and add almonds, which should be quite dry.
Cook slowly over a gentle heat, constantly turning them with a spoon, until golden-brown.
Strain off the oil and toss the nuts in salt.
Bottle in dry air-tight jars.
recipes.name: Salted Almonds II

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Sprinkle a little lemon juice on thin slices of smoked salmon, place half a peeled green grape on each, roll up, and serve on sticks.
recipes.name: Salmon and Grape Rolls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Slice a loaf lengthwise thinly, spread or pipe with savoury filling and coat with aspic jelly, just on the point of setting.
Pipe with savoury butter and cut into fingers.
recipes.name: Quick Canapes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Halve salami, place a cocktail onion on each slice, and roll to form a horn; secure with a stick.
recipes.name: Salami Horns

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Halve rashers of bacon and grill or fry.
Wrap each round a cocktail cherry, secure with a stick, and serve cold.
recipes.name: Bacon and Cherry Rolls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Wash green grapes, and split, without cutting into halves.
Remove the pips, and if desired skin them.
Place a little cream cheese in each, and secure with a cocktail stick.
recipes.name: Grapes and Cheese

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Scrape, boil and drain potatoes, and toss in butter and chopped parsley.
Serve on sticks.
recipes.name: Buttered Potatoes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Thoroughly wash and dry the melon and the pepper.
Coat with the jelly, when this is on the point of setting.
And allow to set quite firmly.
Meanwhile, cream the cheese with milk until it is of a soft piping consistency.
Colour two-thirds of the cheese a pale pink, and the remaining portion a pale yellow.
Drain the anchovies and cut the fillets into narrow strips.
Using a small "cocktail" cutter, cut star-shaped pieces from the strips of pimento or tomato flesh.
Dip the strips of anchovy into stiff jelly and arrange in a diagonal lattice pattern over alternate sections of the melon; now dip the stars into jelly and arrange them on the remaining sections.
Place the pink cream cheese mixture in a forcing bag fitted with a large star pipe, squeeze a large star of cheese on to the bottom of the pear or pepper and secure it to the top of the melon.
Outline the sections of the melon with stars of pink cream cheese.
Using a small, plain writing pipe and the pale yellow cream cheese, pipe dots between the lattice of anchovy fillets.
Lattice the pear or pepper, and finish it with stars of pink cream cheese.
recipes.name: 'Cactus' Melon

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Put all the ingredients except the egg and breadÂ¬ crumbs into a pan, and beat well over a gentle heat.
Cool, and shape on a floured board into small sausages.
Coat with egg and breadcrumbs, and fry in deep fat.
Serve on sticks.
recipes.name: Tiny Curried Fish Cakes

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: small
ingredients.raw: 5 small, thin pieces of streaky bacon

instructions: Soak the prunes overnight and remove the stones.
Stuff each olive with a piece of anchovy and two capers, and place inside the prunes.
Roll a piece of bacon round the outside of each prune, secure with a cocktail stick, and bake in a hot oven for 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Prune Rolls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Sieve the flour and seasoning into a bowl.
Make a well in the centre and put in the yolk and most of the liquid.
Beat gradually until smooth and of a thick coating consistency.
Beat well and allow to stand.
Whisk the egg white stiffly, fold in and use immediately.
Dip the prepared prawns into batter and fry in hot fat.
Serve on slicks.
Note*â€”the addition of the white thins the batter, so all the 1/2 cup liquid may not be necessary.
recipes.name: Scampi

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Peel the mushrooms, remove the stalks, and trim with a round cutter.
Chop ham and mushroom trimmings.
Lightly fry the onion, add ham and chopped mushroom, crumbs, parsley, seasoning and cream, and cook for a minute to bind.
Pile the filling on each mushroom and bake in a moderate oven for about 20 minutes, until tender.
Place a slice of tomato on each croute, put a mushroom on top and decorate with parsley.
recipes.name: Stuffed Mushrooms

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: smoked cooked haddock
ingredients.raw: 2 ounce smoked cooked haddock, and lobster

instructions: Chop the haddock and shallot.
Melt the fat in a pan, fry the shallot and add the curry powder and seasoning.
Stir over the heat for a few seconds, and add the haddock.
Mix well, and stir in the cream.
Place a slice of tomato on each piece of toast, pile the mixture on top, put in the oven to make really hot, and serve sprinkled with parsley.
recipes.name: Indian Croutes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Melt the fat, add the ham, herbs, seasoning and egg yolk, and heat.
Pile on the toast, and garnish with walnut.
recipes.name: Derby Croutes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place the grated cheese with the pepper and sauce in a pan, and melt over a gentle heat.
Press a peach-half flat on each piece of toast, and trim if necessary.
Pour the cheese mixture over, and brown under a grill.
recipes.name: Maori Croutes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Thread some small frankfurters and bacon rolls on skewers and grill.
Add some 1/2-inch cubes of cheese, and serve at once.
recipes.name: Frankfurter Kebabs

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Stone the prunes and place an almond and some chutney in each.
Spread out the bacon rashers and cut in halves, spread a little mustard on each and roll a prune tightly in it, place on a skewer and grill.
Place the "devils" on toast oblongs, and serve hot.
recipes.name: Devils on Horseback

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Make some choux pastry with the flour, margarine, water and egg, and add the cheese and seasoning.
Have ready a pan of deep fat, heated until it gives off just a slight blue haze.
Drop the mixture into it in teaspoonfuls, and fry gently for about 15 minutes to a pale golden-brown.
Drain, and serve hot on cocktail sticks.
recipes.name: Cheese Aigrettes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place a piece of ice in a tall glass, add all the other ingredients, and stir well.
recipes.name: Club Cooler

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix together the grape and lemon juice, add sugar syrup to taste, and chill thoroughly.
Just before serving, add the ginger ale.
recipes.name: Ginger Ale Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Dissolve the sugar in the water, add the thinly peeled lemon rind and boil for 3 minutes.
Strain and chill.
Add the lemon juice, cider and sherry, and once more chill.
Just before serving, add the soda water.
recipes.name: Iced Cider Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Remove the lemon rind with a vegetable peeler, cut it into strips and place in a large jug.
Add the water, sherry, lemon juice, sugar, mint and nutmeg.
Stir well, cover with a lid and allow to stand for 20 minutes.
Just before serving, strain the cup, and add the beer and a few pieces of ice.
recipes.name: Lager Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Wipe the oranges and lemons and slice thinly; peel and core the apples and slice into rings; skin and slice the apricots.
Pour the tinned fruit syrup into a saucepan, add the sugar and 1 pint cider, boil for 5 minutes, and pour on to the fruit.
When the mixture is cold, add the remaining cider, chill, and just before serving add the soda water.
recipes.name: Mixed Fruit Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Peel the lemons thinly and squeeze out the juice.
Place the peel and all the other ingredients in a large pan and heat, but do not boil.
Strain, and serve at once.
recipes.name: New Year Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place the ice in a large jug, add the orange and lemon juice, and sweeten with the syrups.
Fill the jug up with equal quantities of soda water and iced water, stir well, and then decorate with orange slices.
recipes.name: Orange Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix all the ingredients except the soda water, and stand the bowl on ice for at least 1/2 hour.
Just before serving, add the soda water.
recipes.name: Party Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Put the ice in a glass, add the gin, ginger ale and peppermint, stir well, and serve with a sprig of mini on top of each glass.
recipes.name: Whizbang Cooler

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt in top of double boiler: milk, marshmallows.
Let cool.
Add to above mixture: whipping cream, almond hershey bar (chipped).
Pour mixture into graham cracker pie shell and let cool in the refrigerator over night.
recipes.name: Almond Hershey Bar Pie

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake well with the ice, and strain into a glass.
recipes.name: Brandy Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Half-fill the tumbler with the broken ice and add all the other ingredients.
Stir well, and strain into a glass.
recipes.name: Brazil Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake well with the ice, and strain into a glass.
recipes.name: Bronx Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake all the ingredients well with the ice, strain into a glass, and serve with a cherry.
recipes.name: Club Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Grate the lemon rind and blend it with the sugar.
Pour on the freshly made tea, stir well, and set aside to become thoroughly cold.
Strain carefully, and add the rum and brandy.
recipes.name: Cold Tea Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a large saucepan and bring to boiling point.
Strain the mixture into a punch bowl, and decorate with a few thinly cut slices of lemon.
recipes.name: Hot Ale Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Rub a piece of sugar over the lemon rind.
Place all the ingredients except the lemon juice in a saucepan, and simmer without boiling for 5 minutes.
Strain the lemon juice into a punch bowl, pour on the hot liquid and serve at once.
recipes.name: Hot Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Dissolve the sugar and butter in a little boiling water.
Mix in the other ingredients, adding 1/2 pint boiling water, and serve hot.
recipes.name: Rum Punch

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Pour the claret into a large bowl and add the sugar, lemon juice and Curaçao.
Stir well, and surround the bowl with ice for 1/2 hour.
Strain the mixture, and just before serving add the soda water.
Serve in large tumblers, decorated with lemon rind curls and slices of cucumber.
recipes.name: Badminton Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place the ice in a large jug and add the ingredients in the above order.
Stir well, and decorate with slices of fruit in season.
Hock cup variation: substituting hock for champagne, and omitting the abricotine.
Claret cup variation: substituting claret for champagne, and a little lemon juice for the abricotine.
recipes.name: Champagne Cup

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Line some patty tins with cheese pastry and bake "blind" in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
Mix together the scrambled egg, cheese and seasoning, pile into the pastry cases, and decorate with pickled walnut.
recipes.name: Cheese Scramble Tartlets

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Melt the butter in a pan, stir in the fish, cheese, egg, and pepper.
Roll out the pastry thinly and cut into small rounds.
Put a little of the mixture in the centre of each round, wet the edges and fold to the centre to form a triangle.
Seal the edges firmly, brush with egg and bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Haddock Talmouse

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream together the cheese, seasoning and mayonnaise and lightly mix in the pimento.
Fill the cavities of the celery with this mixture, press together, tie with cotton and chill.
Remove the cotton, and cut the celery into 1/2-inch slices.
recipes.name: Celery Trunks

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the radishes in thin slices and place in cold water.
Cream the cheese with a little milk to a piping consistency.
Pipe with a large star nozzle on to the biscuits, and stick 5 slices of radish into each star.
recipes.name: Radish Whirls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll the pastry out thinly and stamp into 2 1/2-inch rounds.
Damp one edge of each round, and fold the pastry round the outside of a metal horn case.
Brush over with egg and bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
Allow to cool, and fill as desired,.
recipes.name: Savoury Horn

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll the pastry out thinly and cut into small rounds; cut half the rounds into two.
Bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
Mix the cheese to a piping consistency with the milk, and pipe a large star on to each round.
Set two half-biscuits in the cheese to form "wings," and decorate with chopped parsley and paprika pepper.
recipes.name: Butterflies

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Sieve the flour and seasoning into a basin and rub in the fat.
Add the cheese, and mix to a stiff dough with the egg yolk and cold water.
Use as required.
recipes.name: Cheese Pastry

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Melt the margarine in a pan, add cheese, seasoning and enough egg to bind, and allow to cool.
Roll out the pastry into a square and spread the mixture over half of it.
Brush the other half with egg and fold over; roll out and prick well, and cut out with a small fancy cutter.
Place on a baking sheet, brush with egg and bake in a hot oven for 15-20 minutes.
recipes.name: D'artois

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Melt the margarine in a pan and add the cheese, beaten egg and seasoning.
Stir over a gentle heat until the mixture thickens, add the mushrooms and allow to cool.
Roll the pastry out thinly and cut into small rounds, place a little of the mixture on each, wet the edges, fold in half and press.
Bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Cheese and Mushroom Turnovers

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream the cheese with the milk to give a soft consistency, and pipe on to the biscuits.
Decorate each with 2 almonds.
If desired, the cream cheese may be coloured.
recipes.name: Almond Cheese Biscuits

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the cheese into about 20 pieces and mould with the fingers to form tiny apple and pear shapes.
Insert cloves to represent the stem and blossom end; sprinkle with nutmeg and paprika to give a rosy tint.
recipes.name: Cheese Apples and Pears

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Dissolve the gelatine in f pint of the water, add all the other ingredients and mix well.
Use when the aspic is quite cold and just on the point of setting.
recipes.name: Quickly-Made Aspic Jelly

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the vegetables into large pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a pan and stir until the gelatine has dissolved.
Whisk briskly until a good froth is formed, remove the whisk and bring quickly to the boil.
Draw to one side of the stove, leave for 10 minutes and strain through a jelly cloth.
recipes.name: Aspic Jelly for Cold Savouries

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Melt the fat in a pan, lightly scramble the egg with the milk and season to taste.
Pile on the rounds of toast, and decorate with capers and a cross made of anchovy fillets.
recipes.name: Scotch Woodcock

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix some butter with a little dry mustard and cayenne pepper, and spread thickly on biscuits.
Cover generously with grated cheese, and brown slightly under the grill.
recipes.name: Devilled Biscuits

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Pound together the ham, cream, mustard and seasoning.
Spread the biscuits with the mixture, and decorate each canape with a slice of pickled walnut.
recipes.name: Derby Canapes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix together the egg and haddock, and season to taste.
Pile on to the toast, and decorate each with capers.
recipes.name: Dutch Canpes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the gruyere cheese into thin slices and stamp into rounds, skin the tomato and slice thinly; cut the bread and butter into rounds.
Arrange a round of tomato on each piece of bread, and then put a round of cheese on top.
Decorate with a small piece of parsley.
recipes.name: Gruyere Tasties

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Remove the crusts from the bread and slice the loaf lengthwise.
Butter the top and bottom slices on one side only, and the others on both sides.
Place a layer of filling on each slice, adding some sliced cucumber with the veal.
Wrap the loaf in greaseproof paper and a damp cloth, place a weight on it, and leave for 2 hours.
Cut the loaf across into thin slices, cut each slice into fingers and cut it diagonally.
If desired, tint some of the butter pink or green.
recipes.name: Striped Sandwiches

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Add cherries to juice and bring to boil.
Add sugar and flour which have been mixed together.
Cook until thickened.
Remove from heat and add butter.
Serve over cherry roll slices.
recipes.name: Cherry Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: enough water
ingredients.note: to make a total of 4 cups of liquid.
ingredients.raw: enough water, to make a total of 4 cups of liquid.

instructions: Pour into mold and refrigerate.
recipes.name: Christmas Salad II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: chopped cranberries
ingredients.raw: 1 cup chopped cranberries, cut in half

instructions: Mix flour, salt baking powder and sugar.
Combine with egg, shortening, orange juice and hot water until dry ingredients are moist.
Fold in nuts, cranberries and orange rind.
Bake in moderate oven - 1 hour, 10 min.
Cool and wrap in wax paper for 24 hours.
recipes.name: Cranberry Salad III

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt butter in heavy sauce pan.
Stir in the onion, cabbage, salt, and dill.
Cover and simmer until just tender, about 15 minutes.
Pour sour cream over cabbage.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Dill Cabbage

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: a little bit of black pepper
ingredients.raw: a little bit of black pepper

instructions: Brown steak on both sides in hot fat.
Add other ingredients and simmer for about 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Meat Rolls (Rollitos de Carne)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Split shrimp lengthwise through center after cooked.
Heat the soup.
Add the cheese to this using an egg beater to mix until fluffy and smooth.
Add gelatin.
Use the egg beater again to make sure it is mixed thoroughly.
When cool, add the rest of the ingredients and pour into molds.
Save a few of the shrimp for garnish.
recipes.name: Shrimp Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Drain oil from tuna and break into chunk size pieces.
Add well drained pineapple.
Season with salt.
Marinate with small amount or mayonnaise or french dressing for 30 minutes.
Just prior to serving toss marinated mixture with shredded head lettuce and chow mein noodles.
Serve immediately in lettuce cups or on bed of endive or other similar green.
recipes.name: Tuna-Pineapple Toss

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake all ingredients well with the ice, and strain.
recipes.name: 'Coffee' Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon lemon juice, or lime juice

instructions: Stir well with ice, strain, and serve with a cherry.
recipes.name: Bacardi Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Place the ice in the tumbler and add all the other ingredients, stir well, and strain into a glass.
recipes.name: Bamboo Cocktail

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt chocolate in top of double boiler over boiling water.
Stir in peanut butter and cereal.
Spread on slightly cooled bars.
Let stand until chocolate hardens.
Cut into bars or squares.
recipes.name: Chocolate Crunch

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter.
Add egg yolks, melted chocolate, sugar, vanilla and salt.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Roll vanilla wafers, line 2 ice cube trays with half the crumbs.
Place chocolate mixture on top of crumbs.
Top with nuts.
Spread ice cream on top and cover with crumbs.
Chill for 2-4 hours.
recipes.name: Chocolate Dessert

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Beat eggs with sugar until very thick, add sifted dry ingredients; beat smooth.
Add dates, vanilla, and nut meats.
Bake in a 9 x 13 inch pan, lined with waxed-paper, in a moderate over (350) about 30 minutes.
While warm, cut in 1 x 4 inch bars; roll in confectioners sugar.
recipes.name: Date Bars

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Make a cream gravy of broth and flour.
Add other ingredients.
recipes.name: Mushroom Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Dissolve soda in hot water.
Mix all together and steam 1 1/2 hours in top of double boiler or steamer.
Serve with butter sauce.
recipes.name: Steamed Cranberry Pudding

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter, gradually add sugar, add the egg yolks one at a time, beating well after each one.
Add chocolate and vanilla.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites and whipped cream.
Roll wafers in fine crumbs and spread one half in a buttered 10 inch square pan.
Spread chocolate mixture over crumbs.
Mix almonds with remaining crumbs and spread over top.
Refrigerate over night.
Cut in squares and serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Toffee Ice Box Dessert

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine on beat above ingredients.
Bake on greased cookie sheet, at 350 degrees for 25 minutes.
Frost with semi-sweet or sweet chocolate.
recipes.name: Toffee Squares

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: French cut string beans
ingredients.raw: 1 box French cut string beans, or other fresh vegetables

instructions: Season pan by browning in hot fat, sliced garlic.
Remove garlic from pan.
Brown the pork, out in small pieces.
Add french cut carrots and string beans.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add cut up celery and onions.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover end simmer for about 20 minutes or until the vegetables are nearly cooked.
Uncover, and add the mushroom sauce and soy sauce.
Cook until done.
recipes.name: American Chinese Chop Suey

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: frozen cherries
ingredients.raw: 20 ounce frozen cherries, thawed and drained

instructions: Reserved 1/4 cup cherries and juice for the sauce.
Chop drained cherries and force excess juice through sieve.
Add all other ingredients to the chopped cherries.
recipes.name: Cherry Filling

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift all dry ingredients, cut in shortening.
Beat egg, add milk and vanilla.
Stir into dry ingredients.
Form into ball on floured pastry cloth.
Roll dough into rectangle 1/4 inch thick.
Brush with melted butter.
Cover with filling.
Roll as for a jelly roll.
Place in greased loaf pan 4 by 12.
Bake at 375f for 40 minutes.
Slice and cover with cherry sauce.
recipes.name: Cherry Roll Delight

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Spread the bread with cream cheese and slice very thinly.
Remove the crusts, lay a piece of asparagus on each slice and roll up; trim off any overlapping pieces.
recipes.name: Asparagus Rolls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Chop the anchovy fillets and mix with the margarine; season, and tint pink with a few drops of colouring.
Cut the bread into slices lengthwise and spread generously with the filling; place the stuffed olives down one edge of the slice, roll it like a swiss roll and cover completely with a damp cloth.
Leave for several hours, and cut into thin slices.
Other savoury fillings may, of course, be used instead of anchovies.
recipes.name: Pin-Wheel Canapes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream all the ingredients well together and add a few drops of green or other colouring.
recipes.name: Cheese Butter

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream all the ingredients well together.
recipes.name: Mustard Butter

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream all the ingredients well together.
recipes.name: Curry Butter

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cream all the ingredients well together, adding a few drops of colouring to make the mixture an attractive shade of pink.
recipes.name: Anchovy Butter for Canapes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the bread fairly thinly, butter it and cut into fancy shapes, using a pastry cutter.
Cover with a filling such as those listed above, coat with aspic to hold the filling in place, and decorate with piped savoury butter.
recipes.name: Bread and Butter Canapes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Divide the cheese into three portions, and leave one plain.
Cream one-third of the cheese with the chopped prawns, butter and a few drops of anchovy essence, seasoning to taste, a little pink colouring and a little milk.
Reserve one or two sprigs of watercress for garnish, chop the rest finely and mix with another one-third of the cheese, then colour this a pale green.
Cream the remaining portion of cheese with a little seasoning and milk until fairly soft.
Remove the crusts from the loaf, and cut lengthwise into 1/2-inch slices.
Spread one slice of bread thickly with the prawn filling, spread the watercress filling on a second slice, and place on top of the prawn-covered slice.
Place another slice of bread on top, repeat until all the slices are used, press lightly, and leave in a cool place until firm.
Cover the whole loaf with the plain cheese, as though icing a cake.
Pipe with small stars of cream cheese, and decorate with radish concertinas and cucumber diamonds.
Garnish the serving dish with some small lettuce leaves and the remaining sprigs of watercress.
To serve the loaf, cut it downwards into slices.
Any other savoury fillings may be used instead of those given, provided they contrast well with each other.
recipes.name: Surprise Sandwich Loaf

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: Small round biscuits
ingredients.raw: Small round biscuits, or pastry rounds

instructions: Mix together the ham, mayonnaise and seasoning, and spread the mixture on the biscuits.
Separate the white and the yolk of the hard-boiled eggs, and cut the white in pieces with a small cutter, to represent petals.
Sieve the egg yolk and place in the centre of the ham mixture, then arrange the petals round.
recipes.name: Marguerites

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Cut the ham in small triangles, dip each piece into liquid aspic jelly and slip it inside a metal horn case.
Stand these moulds upright in a bowl of ice.
Dissolve the gelatine in the 1 tablespoon aspic jelly and mix with the mayonnaise, vegetable macedoine and seasoning to taste.
Fill this mixture into the ham horns, and leave to set firmly.
Unmould by dipping the cases for a moment into hot water.
recipes.name: Venetian Ham Horns

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Whip the cream, season, and mix in the finely chopped celery.
Pile up the biscuits to form a pyramid, and decorate with paprika pepper and a small leaf of celery.
recipes.name: Celery Creams

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Sieve the potatoes and place in a warm bowl with the slightly softened butter.
Work in the flour, and season well.
If the mixture is sticky, stand it in a cool place for a while.
Roll out 1/4 inch thick, brush over with beaten egg, and dust with caraway seeds.
Cut into sticks, and hake in a moderate oven till brown and crisp.
recipes.name: Potato Sticks

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix the potatoes, margarine and 2 ounce.
Flour to a smooth paste, roll out, and line greased patty tins.
Reserve a little of this pastry to cut into thin strips for the top of the patties.
Blanch and chop the almonds, mix together with the sugar, egg, remaining 1/2 ounce flour and cream, and work to a smooth paste.
Fill the cases with this mixture, and place two strips of pastry across the top.
Brush with egg and bake in a hot oven.
recipes.name: Potato Patties

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Stamp out rounds of the bread and butter, potato and beetroot with a 1 1/2-inch cutter.
With a smaller cutter remove the centre of the rounds from the beetroot slices, to form rings.
Place a slice of potato on each bread round, then a beetroot ring.
Fill the centre with chutney, and pipe with mustard butter.
recipes.name: Bengal Savouries

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: chopped truffles or pickled walnuts
ingredients.raw: chopped truffles or pickled walnuts, to decorate

instructions: Mince the chicken and pound it with the sauce, butter and seasoning, and rub through a sieve.
Beat the cream, and add it.
Place the mixture in a forcing bag and pipe large stars on to the biscuits.
Decorate with chopped truffle or pickled walnut.
recipes.name: Biscuits Ã la Duchesse

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Any of the following may be usftd: chopped ham and mushroom, mixed with a little white sauce.
Any shellfish, mixed with a little white sauce and mayonnaise.
Cream cheese and chopped ginger, with a little milk to soften.
Scrambled egg, seasonings and a little piquant table sauce.
Chopped anchovies, olives and gherkins, with anchovy sauce.
Chopped shrimps, pineapple and celery, mixed with mayonnaise.
Chopped hard-boiled egg, moistened with mayonnaise.
recipes.name: Savoury Fillings for Tartlets etc

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Rub the fat into the flour, add all the other ingredients except the butter, and mix to a stiff dough with cold water.
Roll out to 1/4 inch thick and stamp into rounds, then from half the rounds remove the centre to form rings.
Place the biscuits on a greased tin and bake in a moderate oven for about 30 minutes.
When the rounds are cold, spread them with butter, place the rings on top and fill the centre with a savoury filling.
recipes.name: Oatmeal Savouries

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Shell and pick green peas over, wash them in cold water, drain them.
Throw them into boiling water, add brown sugar, a little mint and salt.
Boil until quite tender, drain off the water, and serve in a hot dish with the mint.
recipes.name: Boiled Green Peas

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Equal quantities of cooked cabbage and potatoes, chopped, mixed together, seasoned with pepper and salt, and fried in a little dripping.
recipes.name: Colcannon

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Boil some heads of celery, cut into pieces about 2 inches long, in some good stock, add salt, pepper, and a little lemon-juice.
Thicken the stock with flour and serve.
recipes.name: Stewed Celery II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cook egg yolks, salt, mustard, and lemon juice until thick.
Cool.
Whip the cream and add to above.
Add the pineapple, cherries and marshmallows.
Refrigerate overnight.
recipes.name: Overnight Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine for crust graham crackers, melted butter and sugar.
Line 9x12 inch pan with mixture, keeping 1 cup for the topping.
Combine the milk, sugar, the egg yolks, cornstarch, poppy seed, and butter.
Cook until thick.
Add vanilla.
Beat egg whites with 1/4 cup sugar until stiff.
Fold egg whites into the cooked mixture.
Pour into crust and sprinkle with the remaining cracker crumbs.
Bake for 1/2 hour or until brown at 350f.
recipes.name: Poppy Seed Torte II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cook macaroni in water.
Drain.
Combine with peas.
Add shrimp, celery and pimento.
Mix with mayonnaise and horseradish.
Sprinkle paprika on top.
Refrigerate before serving.
recipes.name: Shrimp and Macaroni Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Place in a casserole or an electric mixer the sugar, the slightly mashed strawberries, and the beaten egg whites.
Beat together until foamy and firm consistency.
Place for a time in the refrigerator to get cold.
recipes.name: Turron de Fresa

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix all ingredients together.
Add to 1000 island potato salad.
recipes.name: 1000 Island Dressing

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix the first 6 ingredients lightly and marinate 30 minutes in the french dressing.
Add 1 cup of 1000 island dressing.
recipes.name: 1000 Island Potato Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt into mixing bowl.
Beat egg slightly; add milk and melted butter.
Add all at once to flour mixture, stirring just until blended.
Dredge berries with 2 tbsp.
Flour and fold gently into butter.
Spread in a greased 8 inch pan.
Sprinkle the 1 1/2 tablespoon sugar over the top.
Bake in a hot oven (425 f) for 25 minutes.
To serve, split squares of the blueberry cake, fill with sliced peaches, and top "sandwich" with whipped cream or ice cream.
recipes.name: Blueberry Dessert Delicious

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Heat in double boiler until thick.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Butter Sauce

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cook chicken and pick in small pieces.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake in pan of water for 2 1/2 hours.
recipes.name: Chicken Loaf

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine flour, brown sugar, butter, shortening, peanut butter, and salt.
Using low speed of mixer or pastry blender combine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg yolk and vanilla; mix well.
Press mixture into ungreased jelly roll pan.
Bake in moderate oven (350f) for 25 to 30 minutes - until golden brown.
Cool slightly.
Spread with chocolate crunch.
recipes.name: Chocodiles

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Grind the cranberries and orange and cover them with sugar.
Let it stand for about two hours.
Combine the gelatin and boiling water.
When the gelatin begins to set, add the pineapple, apples and the first mixture.
Pour this into any desirable container.
recipes.name: Cranberry Orange Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix all ingredients together; adding the beaten egg yolks and 1 egg white, fold in the other beaten egg whites last.
Spread batter 1/2 ft thick in pan and bake 1/2 hour at 350 f.
An hour before serving, break half the cake in pieces and arrange on platter.
Over this, slice 3 or 4 bananas and one can of red or white sweet cherries.
Break up the other half of cake and pile on top of fruit in a mound.
Over this, pour one can of crushed pineapple and let stand until ready to serve.
Spread whipped cream over all and decorate with cherries and nuts.
recipes.name: Deep Dark Secret

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt over low heat, cook (boil) 1 minute.
Cool, beat, and frost.
recipes.name: Fudge Frosting

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Beat eggs with fork; alternate milk, flour with salt, and beat well.
Have oven preheated at 350 degrees.
Place two tablespoons butter in large iron frying pan, and warm.
Add mixture, and bake 25 minutes.
Serve hot for dessert, with spread of applesauce or jelly.
recipes.name: German Oven Package

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine sugar, flour, butter.
Add beaten egg yolks, lemon juice, rind and milk.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour into buttered baking dish.
Bake one hour in a pan of hot water at 325f.
recipes.name: Lemon Pudding II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Dissolve gelatin in water.
Let chill until mixture is syrupy.
Add pineapple juice, whipped cream and cottage cheese.
Mix thoroughly.
Chill until firm.
Top with salad dressing, and sprinkle with crushed walnuts.
recipes.name: Lov-It-Lime Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine chocolate and milk.
Heat over low heat until chocolate is melted.
Add sugar and salt; them stir until dissolved.
Cook until mixture reaches soft ball stage (228f).
Cool slightly; add vanilla.
Mix with other ingredients.
Press into well buttered pan.
Cut into squares.
recipes.name: Marshmallow Fudge Cookies

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter and add remaining ingredients slowly.
Form into balls and bake at 325 f for 20 minutes.
Roll in powdered sugar before cookies are cool.
recipes.name: Melting Moments

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Measure into bowl: bran, raisins, shortening, molasses.
Add, stirring till shortening is melted: water.
Add, mixing well: egg.
Sift together, adding to molasses mixture, stirring, only until blended: flour, salt, soda, cinnamon.
Fill two greased bean cans 2/3 full.
Tie waxed paper over tops.
Bake in 350f oven 45 minutes or spread batter in 8 x 8 inch square pan and bake in 350f.
Oven about 35 minutes.
recipes.name: Molasses Bran Brown Bread

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix melted shortening, sugar, molasses, beaten eggs, and milk.
Sift flour, soda, and spices together.
Add oats, raisins, and nuts, if desired.
Combine dry and liquid ingredients.
Drop on greased cookie sheet.
Bake 12-14 minutes at 350f.
recipes.name: Oatmeal Spice Cookies

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Dissolve the gelatine in the water, add all the other ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes.
To make a red glaze use tomato sauce and omit the meat extract and gravy browning.
recipes.name: Glaze for Savouries

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Sieve the flour and salt on to a plate and warm them.
Put the water and margarine in a pan and bring them to boiling point.
Draw the pan away from the heat and beat in the flour at once.
Continue beating over the heat until the mixture forms a ball, then allow it to cool.
Beat the egg gradually into the mixture, until it is quite smooth.
Pipe in small fi2ngers or balls on to a greased tin, and bake in a moderately hot oven for about 20 minutes.
When cold, fill with a savoury filling, brush the top with glaze and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
recipes.name: Savoury Choux Pastry

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll the pastry thinly and cut into small oblongs.
Place a sausage, sardine or anchovy fillet on each strip, brush one edge with cold water, and fold over.
Flake the joined edge with a knife, and make two small cuts across the top.
Brush with egg and bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Savoury Rolls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll out the pastry thinly and cut it into 3-inch squares.
Mix the cooked rice, curry sauce and chopped egg together, and place a little in the centre of each pastry square.
Moisten two sides of the pastry with water, and fold the comers into the centre to form an envelope.
Brush over with beaten egg, and bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Curry Envelopes

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll the pastry out thinly and line patty tins with it.
Mix together all the other ingredients, reserving half of the cheese and the nuts.
Fill the cases with the mixture, and sprinkle the remaining cheese and nuts on top.
Bake in a hot oven for 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Crab Tartlets

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Make shortcrust pastry, but before adding liquid mix in 1/2 a kipper or bloater, uncooked but skinned and boned.
Mix to a stiff dough with water, roll out, cut in strips, and bake in a hot oven 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Yarnmouth Straws

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll out shortcrust pastry thinly into an oblong and spread with yeast or meat extract, leaving the edges free.
Brush the edges with water and roll up like a swiss roll, then cut off thin slices.
Place on a greased baking sheet and bake in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
recipes.name: Savoury Whirls

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll out the pastry, cut into fingers and bake in a hot oven.
Bone and pound the kippers, and mix with a little thick white sauce to bind.
Season, spread between the pastry fingers and decorate with parsley round the join.
recipes.name: Savoury Fingers

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll out the pastry and line tartlet moulds with it.
Sieve the cream cheese, season, and beat in the eggs by degrees.
Cut the ham and salmon into shreds and mix in carefully.
Fill the tartlet moulds with this mixture, cut the gruyere in thin slices and lay these over the top of the tartlets.
Bake in a hot oven until golden-brown and crisp.
recipes.name: Risotto Tartlets

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Bone the herrings and mix with lemon juice and seasoning.
Roll the pastry out into 2f 1/2 inch squares and place a little mixture on each, moisten two of the edges and fold into a triangle.
Flake the joined edges, brush the top with egg, and bake in a hot oven for about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Marine Puffs

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Line small boat-shaped moulds with pastry, fill with bread raspings and bake blind in a hot oven for 10-15 minutes.
Brush out the raspings, and place a little chutney in each boat.
Cook the peas (if necessary), sieve, and cream to a piping consistency with fat and seasoning.
Pipe the mixture in the boats with a small star nozzle, and decorate with a piece of pickled walnut.
Tomato boats may be made in exactly the same way by using the flesh of tomatoes instead of the peas,.
recipes.name: Green Pea Boats

author: Good Housekeeping

ingredients.name: scraps of flaky or shortcrust pastry
ingredients.raw: scraps of flaky or shortcrust pastry

instructions: Roll the pastry 1/8 inch thick and cut it into strips.
Lay a strip of anchovy on top of each and sprinkle with lemon juice.
Twist the two together, brush with beaten egg and bake in hot oven for about 8 minutes.
recipes.name: Anchovy Twists

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Roll the pastry out thinly and line some tartlet tins with it.
Cut the bacon into small strips, fry with the onion, and half-fill the tartlets with this mixture.
Season the custard and fill up the cases.
Sprinkle with a very little nutmeg, and bake in a moderately hot oven for 10-15 minutes,.
recipes.name: American Tartlets

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Scrape carrots carefully and cut in thick pieces.
Place them in sufficient water to cover them and stew till tender.
Then evaporate water till only half remains.
Add a little dripping, flour and pepper and toss carrots gently in pan till they are coated with their own juice, and serve.
recipes.name: Stewed Carrots

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Cut off the faded outside leaves and hard part of the stalk, and wash the vegetables well.
Cook in plenty of boiling water, with a tablespoonful of salt to every half gallon.
If the water is very hard, add sufficient carbonate of soda to cover a threepenny piece.
Boil with the lid off till the stalk is soft.
recipes.name: Cabbages, Cauliflowers, Greens and Savoys

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Soak the beans over-night.
Next day boil them for 5 or 6 hours in plenty of water.
One hour before serving, mix the vinegar, sugar, pepper and salt well together, pour away some of the water from the beans, and add the mixture to them.
recipes.name: Haricot Beans

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: String the beans, cut each slantwise into 2 or 3 pieces, wash them well in cold salt and water, drain them, and throw them into boiling water with a little salt and a small piece of soda in it.
Let them boil very fast with the lid off, until tender.
Drain the water off and serve.
recipes.name: French Beans

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Shell, wash and drain broad beans.
Throw into cold water with a little salt and a bunch of parsley.
Boil until soft (20 to 30 minutes), then drain them.
Serve either with melted butter or gravy.
recipes.name: Broad Beans

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Boil a large beet about 2 hours, be careful not to pierce it.
When cold mash it very smooth, add a little dripping, pepper, salt and stock.
Place in a greased basin and bake for 1 hour.
recipes.name: Baked Beetroot

author: May Henry
Edith B Cohen
instructions: Proceed as for hash, but when heating the meat, add 2 pickled walnuts cut up small, and a little of the liquor, and garnish with 6 or 8 walnuts instead of toast.
recipes.name: Walnut Stew

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: small can fresh strawberries
ingredients.raw: 1 small can fresh strawberries, or pineapple

instructions: Beat the whites of eggs until stiff.
Add the sugar gradually, and beat until all of the sugar is used.
Add vanilla.
Spread this over the cake batter and bake in a moderate oven (350 f) about thirty minutes.
Remove the sides of the cake forms until cool.
The lower layer can be placed on the cake plate without removing the bottom.
Serve with sweetened whipped cream, or with slightly sweetened whipped cream to which a can of crushed pineapple (drained) has been added.
As a variation use fresh crushed slightly sweetened strawberries or the frozen ones.
Spread the cream between the layers and also on the top.
Before adding the cream to the top cut the cake into 12 pieces, then top it with the cream.
recipes.name: Blitz Torte - Part Two

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix the gelatin with water or fruit juice and allow to stiffen to consistency of thick syrup.
Then whip.
Beat cream cheese.
Then add to whipped cream.
Fold into beaten or whipped gelatin.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Pour into molds and set away to congeal.
recipes.name: Brides' Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: small jar stuffed olives
ingredients.raw: 1 small jar stuffed olives, drained and chopped

instructions: Scald undiluted milk in large double boiler.
Blend in cheese.
Remove top of pan from water when cheese is nearly melted to avoid overcooking cheese.
Mixture separates if cooked too long or too fast.
Stir in the olives and chill.
As it cools, mixture thickens to right consistency for spreading sandwiches and lightly salted crackers.
recipes.name: Cheese Spread

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 1 pound chicken breast, meat sliced thin and flat

ingredients.name: Chinese peas
ingredients.raw: 1/4 pound Chinese peas, parboil for 1/2 minute

ingredients.name: green onion
ingredients.raw: 1 stalk green onion, cut into lengths

ingredients.name: water and liquid of mushrooms
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup water and liquid of mushrooms

instructions: Soak chicken in seasoning for 20 min.
Heat pan with oil.
Brown ginger and garlic and add chicken.
Fry over a low flame for two minutes.
Add mushrooms and water and salt to taste.
Cook 5 minutes.
Thicken with cornstarch.
Just before turning off flame, add peas and green onion.
recipes.name: Chicken with Button Mushrooms

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt marshmallows and milk in double boiler.
Add almond bar.
Cool and fold in whipped cream.
Pour over pieces of broken angel food cake.
recipes.name: Chocolate Angel Delight

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Pour water over: soda, dates.
Set aside to cool.
Cream: shortening, sugar.
Add alternately with date mixture: eggs, cocoa, flour, salt, vanilla.
Pour into pan, sprinkle chocolate chips and nuts on top and push in.
Bake for 35-40 minutes in 350f oven.
recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Cake

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: egg yolks
ingredients.raw: 3 egg yolks, beaten light and stiff

instructions: Beat egg yolks, add sugar, chocolate, and vanilla.
Fold in egg yolks.
Place in refrigerator over night (preferably in the goblets you will serve them in).
Serve with whipped cream colored green and flavored with peppermint.
recipes.name: Chocolate Dream

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift dry ingredients together three times.
Blend in butter, milk and vanilla.
Mix in chocolate.
Butter and flour outsides of 2 cookie sheets.
Spread mixture thinly, about 1/8 inch thick, with spatula on inverted pans for ease in removing late.
Sprinkle with nuts and pat them in.
Bake in moderate oven 350f 8 to 10 minutes.
Crease in strips 1-1/2 x 3 inches at once, as they become very crisp and fragile when cool.
May be cut in any desired shape.
Quickly remove with spatula.
recipes.name: Chocolate Wafers

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, shortening, and salt like pie dough.
Save 1/2 cup of dough for topping.
Dissolve soda in the sour milk.
Add cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and cocoa to the dough mixture.
Add sour milk and soda to dough mixture.
Add raisins and nuts to taste.
Place in 13x9 baking pan.
Sprinkle with the 1/2 cup dough mixture.
Bake in a slow oven (300f) for about 40 minutes.
recipes.name: Cleveland Cake

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 2 pound beef chuck, cut in cubes

instructions: Thoroughly brown meat on all sides in hot fat, add boiling water, lemon juice, worcestershire sauce, garlic, onion, bay leaves, and seasonings.
Simmer 2 hours.
Stir occasionally to keep from sticking.
Add carrots and potatoes (cubed potatoes may be used if desired).
Continue cooking 20-30 minutes or until vegetables are done.
Remove meat and vegetables.
Thicken liquid for gravy.
recipes.name: Country Kitchen Brown Stew

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake well with the ice, strain into a glass and serve with a cherry.
recipes.name: Florida Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Mix together the gin and lemon juice, pour the mixture over the ice chips and fill up with soda water.
recipes.name: Gin Ricky

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Shake well with the ice and strain into cocktail glasses.
recipes.name: Harrison Cocktail

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Wash the beans well and soak overnight in water to cover.
In the morning add 2 cups more water.
And cook until tender.
Fry the salt pork until crisp remove from the fat and add to the beans.
Brown the onion in the salt pork fat.
Mix all the ingredients, and add salt and pepper to taste.
Continue cooking for 10 minutes.
And serve at once.
recipes.name: Hopping John with Pinto or Great Northern Beans

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Stir the ingredients together with the ice, and strain into glasses.
recipes.name: Ika Cocktail

author: Good Housekeeping
instructions: Squeeze the juice from the lemon, and add the gin and sugar.
Shake well, strain into a tail glass and add the ice and soda water to taste.
Note: a collins may also be made with whisky, brandy, or rum; it is, of course, named accordingly.
recipes.name: John Collins

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Fry the salt pork until crisp, remove from the fat and add to the beans.
Then brown the onion in the salt pork fat.
Add the beef.
Stir, and cook slowly for 5 minutes.
Combine all the ingredients, add salt and pepper to taste, and simmer until the meat is tender and the flavors well blended.
recipes.name: Pinto or Great Northern Beans with Ground Beef

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Wash the beans well, and soak overnight in water to cover.
In the morning add 2 cups more water, and cock until tender.
Fry the salt pork until crisp, remove from the fat, and add to the beans.
Brown the onions in the salt pork fat, and add both to the beans.
Mix the flour with a little cold water, and add to the beans.
Add salt and pepper to taste, and put the mixture in a greased baking dish.
Sprinkle the bread crumbs over the top.
Bake in a moderately hot oven for about 20 minutes, or until the crumbs are brown.
Serve from the baking dish.
recipes.name: Scalloped Pinto or Great Northern Beans

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Wash the beans well, and soak overnight in water to cover.
In the morning add 2 cups more water, cook the beans until tender, and put them through a sieve or colander.
Fry the diced salt pork until crisp, remove from the fat, and add to the bean pulp.
Brown the onion in the salt pork fat; stir into the bean pulp.
Add hot water to give the -proper consistency, and salt and pepper to taste.
Serve very hot.
If available, 1/2 cup of chopped peanuts may be added for variation and extra food value.
Or pour this soup over toast covered with sliced browned onions, and sprinkle a little grated cheese over the top.
recipes.name: Soup with Pinto or Great Northern Beans

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
