Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Remove necks and giblets from chicken cavity, if present before cooking.
Reserve for another use.
Place chicken, breast side up, in a roasting pan.
Brush chicken skin with Italian dressing and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Stuff lemon or orange into chicken cavity.
Roast 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours or until meat thermometer inserted into chicken thigh registers 165 degrees F.
Let chicken set for 15 minutes after removing from the oven before carving.
recipes.name: Oven Roasted Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: University of Illinois Extension — Illinois Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These potato pancakes are easily baked in the oven and offer a healthier version of a traditional Hanukkah recipe.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: applesauce and yogurt (plain low-fat or Greek)
ingredients.raw: applesauce and yogurt (plain low-fat or Greek)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 425 °F.
Lightly oil the baking sheets by spreading the oil around with your clean hand or a paper towel.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl.
Use the large holes on your grater to grate the potato, then grate the onion too.
Put the potato and onion mixture in the colander inside the sink.
Using a paper towel, press the potato mixture down to squeeze out and blot up some of the extra moisture.
Stir it and blot again.
Put the potato mixture in the large bowl, add the egg, and stir well.
Add the flour mixture and stir it very well.

Use a spoon or your fingers to pluck a clump of the potato mixture from the bowl and spread it into a round, flat nest on the oiled baking sheet: it should make a circle that's about 3 inches wide and 1/4 inch thick.

Repeat to fill the sheet. (You don't need to leave space between them.) Bake until the bottoms are deeply golden, 15 to 20 minutes, then turn the pancakes over and put them back in the over for 10 more minutes.
Serve the latkes with applesauce and yogurt (optional).
recipes.name: Oven-Baked Potato Pancakes
recipes.notes: These Hanukkah favorites are traditionally fried in oil to celebrate the oil of the eight nights of lights (like a menorah, which is a special Hanukkah candle holder, does). Our potato pancakes are actually oven-baked, which makes them easier, crunchier, and healthier.
recipes.recipe_by: ChopChop Family

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Yucca is a starchy vegetable with a taste and texture similar to while potatoes. Enjoy this yucca side dish with one of your favorite protein- or vegetable-based entrees.

ingredients.name: yucca (cassava) peeled and cut into 3-inch sections
ingredients.raw: 1 pound yucca (cassava) peeled and cut into 3-inch sections

ingredients.name: spray non-stick cooking spray
ingredients.raw: 1 spray non-stick cooking spray, as needed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, combine the yucca with enough cold water to cover it by 1 inch.
Bring the water to a boil and slowly simmer the yucca for 20 to 30 minutes, or until it is tender.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Transfer the yucca with a slotted spoon to a cutting board.
Let it cool and cut it lengthwise into 3/4-inch wide wedges, discarding the thin woody core.
Spray cookie sheet with the nonstick cooking oil spray.
Spread yucca wedges on cookie sheet and spray wedges with cooking oil spray.
Cover with foil paper and bake for 8 minutes.
Uncover and return to oven to bake for an additional 7 minutes.
recipes.name: Oven-Fried Yucca
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple and delicious vegetable dish is perfect with your favorite entrée.

ingredients.name: fresh vegetables
ingredients.note: potatoes, broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, or red peppers

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
In a small bowl, mix the oil, lemon juice, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Wash, peel, and cut the fresh vegetables to get 3 cups cut-up vegetables.
Spread vegetables on baking sheet pan.
Pour the oil mixture over the vegetables and mix together.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Stir after the first 10 minutes of baking.
Serve the vegetables while they are still hot.
recipes.name: Oven-Roasted Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Overnight soaking cuts down on prep time in the morning, so you can enjoy a healthy and hearty, cooked breakfast, even after hitting the snooze button.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients in a cooking pot and cover.
Let sit overnight in refrigerator.

In the morning, put on a stove burner and cook on medium heat until simmering, then turn on low and heat for 10 to 15 minutes more or less depending on type of oats -- quick (5 minutes), regular, or steel cut.
Serve warm with a little milk (or milk alternative), a drizzle of maple syrup, and a side of fresh fruit, if desired.
recipes.name: Overnight Oatmeal
recipes.notes: 1/2 cup raisins and 1/4 cup walnuts used in nutrient analysis and costing.
recipes.recipe_by: Lake Family Resource Center — Be-Fresh Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A mixture of milk, yogurt, and raspberries combine with dry oats to become a smooth make-ahead breakfast. Just mix and refrigerate overnight for the next day.
instructions: Combine milk, Greek yogurt, honey, cinnamon, and vanilla extract in a container or jar with a lid.
Add oats and mix well.
Top with raspberries or gently fold into oat mixture.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours to overnight.
Enjoy cold, or heat as desired.
recipes.name: Overnight Oatmeal with Berries
recipes.notes: Frozen blueberries or strawberries may be used in place of raspberries.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tilapia fillets are pan-fried until golden brown and served with a fresh salsa made from roasted tomatillos, serrano peppers, lime, and cilantro.

ingredients.name: serrano or other chiles
ingredients.raw: 2 serrano or other chiles, finely chopped

ingredients.name: - 4oz tilapia fillets
ingredients.note: patted dry with a paper towel

instructions: To make the tomatillo salsa: Preheat the oven to 450 °F.
To prepare the tomatillos, peel back the husk from the smooth green tomatillo skin.
Rinse the tomatillos with warm water and cut into quarters.
Place the husked tomatillos, onion, chilies, garlic, and 1 teaspoon oil in the baking pan, stir well and transfer to the oven.
Roast about 20 minutes until the tomatillos are soft and dark green.
Set aside to cool.
Transfer the mixture to the blender; add the salt, lime juice, and cilantro.
Purée.
To cook the tilapia: Place the skillet on the stove over high heat and when it is hot, carefully add 2 teaspoons oil.
Put the tilapia fillets in the pan, waiting about 30 seconds between additions.
Cook about 5 to 6 minutes, until golden brown on both sides.
Transfer the tilapia to the serving plate and top with generous amounts of salsa.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Pan Roasted Tilapia with Tomatillo Salsa
recipes.notes: Canned tomatillo salsa can be used instead of fresh. Tilapia can be substituted with any inexpensive white fish.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using a pre-made baking mix -- like our Better Baking Mix -- is a great shortcut to making homemade pancakes!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a bowl.
Stir just enough to moisten dry ingredients.
Preheat skillet on medium-high heat.
The skillet is ready when drops of water "dance" on the dry surface.
Add a teaspoon of vegetable oil or use cooking oil spray.
For each pancake, pour 3 to 4 tablespoons of batter onto hot skillet.
Cook slowly until the surface is covered with bubbles.
Turn and cook until second side is lightly browned.
recipes.name: Pancakes (from Better Baking Mix)
recipes.notes: Try applesauce or other fruit on pancakes instead of syrup.
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick, delicious, cruciferous delight. Try this recipe with green or purple cabbage, or a mixture of the two.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt butter or margarine in a heavy saucepan or skillet.
Add cabbage and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Add water.
Cover pan with a tight-fitting lid to hold in steam.
Cook over low heat until cabbage is tender (6 to 8 minutes), stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add lemon juice and serve.
recipes.name: Panned Cabbage
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Vegetable Cookery — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these savory biscuits with your favorite holiday meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Stir together to mix well.
Do not over mix.
Turn out onto a floured board.
Roll to a 1-inch thick square.
Cut into 12 squares.
Bake on a cookie sheet, spaced slightly apart, in a 400 degrees F oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Parmesan Chive Biscuits
recipes.recipe_by: University of Arkansas Cooperative Extension Service — Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Give (these) peas a chance! Try varying this recipe by using other types of cheese or adding different seasonings.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: of reduced-sodium peas
ingredients.note: 15 ounce cans or 16 ounces frozen peas
ingredients.raw: 2 cans of reduced-sodium peas, drained and rinsed (15 ounce cans or 16 ounces frozen peas)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat butter in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add peas and cook 2 to 3 minutes or until peas are heated through.
Add lemon juice and pepper and mix well.
Sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve warm.
recipes.name: Parmesan Peas
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Instead of basil, this recipe uses fresh parsley to make a pesto that is simply delicious!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a food processor, combine the almonds, cheese, parsley, and lemon juice.
Slowly pour in oil and mix it into the rest of the ingredients.
Season with salt and pepper, if using.
recipes.name: Parsley, Almond, and Lemon Pesto
recipes.recipe_by: Bronson Wellness Center — Bronson Healthcare - Michigan

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: If you're looking for delicious ideas for turnips, you've come to the right place! This recipe is full of vegetables and flavor, blended together to create a hearty, satisfying soup.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and celery and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, salt, and pepper; cook for1 minute.
Stir in the parsnips, potato, broth, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer for 20 minutes or until the parsnips and potatoes are soft.
Stir in the margarine or butter and let the soup sit uncovered for 5 minutes.
Purée the soup in batches in a blender, using the manufacturer's directions for puréeing hot liquids.
Heat the soup before serving, stirring in water if it seems too thick.
recipes.name: Parsnip Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this mix of cereal, raisins, peanuts, and coconut at your next get-together.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cereals together in a large bowl.
Add raisins, peanuts, and coconut; mix well.
Eat it dry or with milk.
recipes.name: Party Mix
recipes.recipe_by: "Fiesta Mix" Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A tasty and colorful dish that the whole family will enjoy. Use whatever frozen veggies you have on hand.

ingredients.name: frozen vegetables such as carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 cups frozen vegetables such as carrots, broccoli, and cauliflower, thawed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat.
Add ground turkey and paprika.
Cook and stir until meat is brown and no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, chicken broth and pasta.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low.
Cover and simmer until pasta is almost tender, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove lid.
Place vegetables on top of pasta.
Replace lid.
Cook until vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Prepare the Tasty Topping.
Mix parsley, bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Sprinkle over vegetables in skillet.
Cover and let sit for 3 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Party-Time Pasta
recipes.recipe_by: Kids… Get Cooking! — California Department of Health Services — California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Passover is a Jewish holiday observed in the springtime, but this fruity and delectable dessert is good any time of the year. If you do not wish to eat cornstarch feel free to substitute instant tapioca pudding in equal amounts.
instructions: *If you do not wish to eat cornstarch feel free to substitute instant tapioca pudding in equal amounts.
recipes.name: Passover Rhubarb Cobbler
recipes.recipe_by: Prairie Fare — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This rich red sauce combines ground beef, carrots, celery, onion, and tomatoes with a touch of milk for added creaminess. This sauce is slow simmered and delicious served over any favorite pasta.

ingredients.name: yellow onion
ingredients.raw: 1 yellow onion, chopped into 1/4 inch pieces

ingredients.name: 14.5-ounce cans no salt added crushed or diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 14.5-ounce cans no salt added crushed or diced tomatoes

ingredients.name: no salt added tomato paste
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup no salt added tomato paste

instructions: To make the Bolognese sauce: Put skillet on the stove over medium heat and when it is hot, add oil.
Add carrot, celery, and onion and cook about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to brown.
Raise the heat to high.
Pinch off tablespoon-sized pieces of the beef and add a few at a time, stirring well between additions.
Cook, breaking the meat apart until it is no longer raw, starts to give off liquid, and no longer clumps together, about 10 minutes.
Add the water, tomatoes, and tomato paste, stirring well.
Cook about 10 minutes until the sauce begins to thicken.
Slowly stir in the milk, a little bit at a time.
Turn the heat down to low and cook 45 minutes until all the liquid has been absorbed.
To make the pasta : Fill a large pot halfway with water.
Bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the pasta and about 12 minutes cook until just tender.
Drain the pasta and divide into 4 bowls.
Top each bowl with about 3/4 cup Bolognese and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Pasta Bolognese
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Perfect for any meal of the day, this easy and flavorful frittata is quick and easy to prepare.

ingredients.name: whole grain spaghetti
ingredients.raw: 4 ounces whole grain spaghetti, regular or thin

instructions: Tomato Variation: Instead of mixing 1 cup of peas with the egg, seasonings, and cheese mixture, sprinkle the chopped tomatoes evenly over the top of the frittata before putting it in the oven.
recipes.name: Pasta Frittata with Peas
recipes.notes: Salt omitted from nutrition analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Eating Recipes — University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A flavorful spring recipe that you and your family will savor. Use your favorite spring vegetables from your garden or local farmers market: kohlrabi, sugar snap peas, carrots, and asparagus are all delicious options.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
While noodles are cooking, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add vegetables and sauté until tender; stir constantly.
Add tomato and sauté 2 more minutes.
Toss vegetables with noodles and margarine.
Add seasonings; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Pasta Primavera
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe is quick and easy to prepare and will become a favorite in your home.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare pasta according to package directions.
Add frozen vegetables during the last 5 minutes of cooking time.
Drain pasta and vegetables and set aside.
Bring the spaghetti sauce to a boil over medium heat.
Stir in the pasta and vegetables.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Pasta Primavera in Spaghetti Sauce
recipes.notes: May substitute any type of pasta for the rotini. Do not overcook the pasta and vegetables. Maybe substitute other types of canned or bottled Italian sauces.
recipes.recipe_by: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education, Adapted from Pasta Primavera — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use whole grain pasta to boost the fiber in this tasty spring salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Rinse in cold water to stop cooking and prevent sticking.
Drain.
Cook vegetables until just tender.
Drain and cool.
Combine cold pasta, vegetables, and salad dressing.
Top with sliced eggs and cheese.
Refrigerate until time to serve.
recipes.name: Pasta Primavera Salad
recipes.notes: Low-fat cheddar cheese used for nutrition analysis and costing.
recipes.recipe_by: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Easy and delicious, make this tasty pasta salad for your next picnic.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and place in large bowl or pan.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Cool in refrigerator before serving.
recipes.name: Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Easy and Nutritious Family Recipes — University of California Cooperative Extension — Fresno County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe starts with whole wheat pasta and includes fresh broccoli, tomatoes, carrots, and hard-cooked eggs. Tossed with a refreshing vinaigrette flavored with basil, oregano, and garlic salt, this classic salad is a go-to recipe for an appetizer, main dish, or as a side.

ingredients.name: uncooked whole wheat pasta
ingredients.raw: 6 ounces uncooked whole wheat pasta, cooked, drained

instructions: Whisk dressing ingredients in a small bowl until blended.
Combine pasta, broccoli, tomato, and carrot in a large bowl; toss.
Pour dressing over pasta mixture; toss until evenly coated.
Add eggs; toss briefly.
Refrigerate, covered, at least 4 hours to blend flavors.
recipes.name: Pasta Salad with Herb Vinaigrette
recipes.notes: For a different flavor or to reduce cost, use any other vinegar you have on hand for the dressing.
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this tasty salad with whole grain pasta in your favorite shape. Enjoy with family and friends at your next gathering.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Mix again before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Pasta Vegetable Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart Being Active Recipes — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chickpeas, tomatoes, spinach, and a hint of rosemary make this delicious pasta dish. Served warm with a sprinkle of Parmesan, this quick and easy recipe makes a perfect weeknight meal.

ingredients.name: small yellow onion
ingredients.raw: 1 small yellow onion, chopped into 1/4 pieces

ingredients.name: 16-ounce can low sodium chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 1 16-ounce can low sodium chickpeas, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: 14.5-ounce can no salt added diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 14.5-ounce can no salt added diced tomatoes

instructions: To cook the pasta, fill a pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat.
When the water is boiling, add the pasta and cook until just tender, about 12 minutes.
Just before draining, reserve 1 1/2 cups of the pasta water.
Drain the pasta and set aside.
While the pasta is cooking, prepare the sauce: Put a skillet on the stove over medium-low heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the garlic, onion, carrots, celery, and rosemary and cook until the garlic is golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and using a fork, lightly mash half of them.
Add the reserved pasta water and tomatoes and cook 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and spinach to the skillet mixture and cook until the spinach is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed by the pasta, about 10 minutes.
Add the red pepper flakes, if desired.
Mix well and serve immediately, garnished with Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Pasta with Chickpeas, Tomato, and Spinach
recipes.notes: Kale can be used instead of spinach.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Loaded with protein and fiber, this delicious dish can be made quickly. Enjoy with a side of your favorite fruit.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium cannellini beans
ingredients.note: can also use great northern or navy beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook the pasta according to directions on box, and drain.
On medium heat, add vegetable oil and onion to a large pan.
Cook for 5 minutes, add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in chopped chicken and cook until heated through.
Add spinach (or chard), beans, chicken or vegetable stock, and Italian seasoning.
Add in cooked pasta and stir to combine.
Cook for 5 minutes, until pasta is heated through.
Add salt and pepper, to taste (optional), and garnish with Parmesan cheese before serving (optional).
recipes.name: Pasta with Greens, Beans, and Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart. Be Fit. — University of Maryland Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Combine fresh veggies from your garden or the farmers' market with pasta to make this your new favorite summer recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop tomatoes and mix with all the remaining ingredients in a large bowl.
Let the mixture stand at room temperature for about 20 minutes.
Toss with cooked pasta and top with grated cheese.
recipes.name: Pasta with Vegetables
recipes.notes: Add a can of white or black beans, drained, for extra protein before tossing with pasta. Feel free to add other vegetables that you have on hand. Salt and pepper not included in analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: Originally named Uncooked Tomato Sauce Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: While avocados tend to get all the guacamole glory, sometimes they’re not available, not ripe, or just too expensive! Check out this tasty, bright, and satisfying recipe that put the humble green pea in the leading role.

ingredients.name: (4 ounces) diced green chilies
ingredients.raw: 1 can (4 ounces) diced green chilies, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash peas until smooth.
Add the lime juice, tomato, onion, green chilies, cilantro, garlic, salt (if using), and black pepper.
Mix well.
Serve with an assortment of raw vegetables and whole-grain tortilla chips.
recipes.name: Pea Guacamole
recipes.recipe_by: Westmoreland County Pennsylvania SNAP-Ed Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this gorgeous, bright green pesto on your favorite protein food or pasta.

ingredients.name: frozen peas
ingredients.note: can also use fresh or canned

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.note: or can use frozen or canned

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
For the pesto, add peas, Parmesan cheese, basil, spinach, walnuts and garlic into a food processor or blender.
Add in water, oil, salt and pepper.
Blend until the ingredients are combined to form a thick sauce.
Place pesto in an airtight container.
Refrigerate until needed.
recipes.name: Pea Pesto
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Matters Colorado

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious dessert is the perfect ending to any meal. This recipe is simple to prepare and the dish is satisfying to taste.

ingredients.name: (20 ounces total) peaches
ingredients.raw: 1 1/3 cans (20 ounces total) peaches, in light syrup, drained and sliced

ingredients.name: medium tart apples
ingredients.raw: 2 medium tart apples, peeled and sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly grease 9x9x2-inch casserole dish.
Combine peaches, apples, vanilla, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Toss well and spread evenly in greased casserole dish.
Combine flour and sugar in small bowl.
Cut in margarine with two knives until the mixture resembles coarse meal.
Sprinkle flour mixture evenly over fruit.
Bake until lightly browned and bubbly, about 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Peach Apple Crisp
recipes.recipe_by: Recipes and Tips for Healthy, Thrifty Meals — USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: On a hot summer day, freeze the drained peaches (or fresh) for at least 45 minutes before preparing this sweet and tangy drink.

ingredients.name: canned peaches packed in juice
ingredients.note: or1 cup of sliced fresh peaches
ingredients.raw: 1 cup canned peaches packed in juice, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the ingredients in a blender.
Blend well.
Sprinkle with nutmeg if you like.
Serve cold.
recipes.name: Peach Cooler
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The perfect dessert when peaches are in season. Simple to prepare but absolutely scrumptious.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Slice the peaches.
Spread the peach slices on the bottom of a 9x9-inch baking pan.
Melt the margarine in a saucepan.
In a small bowl, mix everything but the peaches.
Stir until the mix is well blended.
Sprinkle the oat mix on top of the peaches.
Bake for 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Peach Crisp
recipes.notes: Serve the peach crisp either hot or cold. To remove the peach fuzz, you can rub the washed peach gently with a paper towel.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple peach sauce recipe is the perfect complement to your favorite dishes. Sweet peaches and aromatic cinnamon enhance savory dishes when topped on grilled chicken, or add extra sweetness and fruit to waffles, pancakes, and yogurt.
instructions: Drain peaches and reserve liquid.
Pour peaches into a medium saucepan with cinnamon.
Cook on low to medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
Mash to desired consistency with either a potato masher or wooden spoon.
Add reserved peach liquid as needed.
recipes.name: Peach Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this refreshing peach sorbet or create your own flavor combination!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Collect all ingredients and freeze cans before starting to prepare the recipe.
Place cans of fruit in freezer for at least 3 hours.
Take out when fully frozen.*.
Run frozen cans briefly under hot water, or let them sit on counter for 30 minutes to loosen contents.
Remove fruit from the cans, and use a sharp knife to cut it into small pieces.
If using a banana, peel, and cut into slices.
Banana does not need to be frozen.
Place frozen, chopped fruit (and banana, if using) in the blender, and blend until creamy.
Serve immediately.
Freeze any leftovers in a freezer-safe container or sealable plastic freezer bags. *It is ok to freeze these cans overnight.
They will not explode.
recipes.name: Peach Sorbet
recipes.notes: Cost and nutrition analysis provided for Peach Sorbet. Try these refreshing flavor combinations, or create your own!
recipes.recipe_by: "Fruit Sorbet" Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Packed with fresh fruit, this pita pocket makes a wonderful breakfast, lunch, or snack. If you don't have peaches, try with plums or nectarines.

ingredients.name: medium apple
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium apple, cored and thinly sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut pitas in half to make 4 pockets and warm in the microwave for about 10 seconds to make them more flexible.
Carefully open each pocket and spread a thin layer of peanut butter on the inside walls.
Fill with a combination of apple, banana, and peach slices.
Serve at room temperature.
recipes.name: Peachy Peanut Butter Pita Pockets
recipes.recipe_by: SNAP4CT — UConn Health SNAP-Ed

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Peachy pops will be the perfect partner to your playful summer picnic. Enjoy these frosty treats on a hot day.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a knife to remove the skin and chop the peaches.
Spoon peaches into each of the 6 paper cups.
Place yogurt in a medium mixing bowl.
Slowly pour and stir the orange juice into the yogurt.
Mix well.
Pour some of the juice and yogurt mix into each cup to cover the peaches.
Place a spoon in the center of each cup.
Cut 6 squares of aluminum foil big enough to cover the tops of cups.
Stab each spoon handle through each piece of foil.
The foil will hold the spoon in the center of the cup.
Place cups in the freezer for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, peel the paper cups away from the pops to eat.
recipes.name: Peachy Pops
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A filling, fruity, and nutty sandwich that you and your children will enjoy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread 2 tablespoons peanut butter on bread.
Place fruit slices on top.
Optional: Top with grated carrot.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter 'n Fruit-wich
recipes.notes: Instead of whole wheat bread try crunchy graham crackers or roll up the filling in a soft tortilla. Instead of fresh fruit use canned, drained pineapple.
recipes.recipe_by: The Power of Choice — USDA Food and Nutrition Service and US Department of Health and Human Services Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Quick, filling, and delicious, these wraps can be made in a flash and enjoyed right away or packed away for lunch at school or work.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lay tortilla flat and spread peanut butter over 2/3 of the tortilla leaving edges at sides Sprinkle 2 tablespoons granola over peanut butter.
Cut apple slices into small chunks and place them on top of the granola.
Fold over the edges of the tortilla and roll up "burrito style." Eat and Enjoy.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter and Apple Wraps
recipes.recipe_by: CSAAC (Community Services for Autistic Adults and Children)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Hurried in the morning? Need breakfast to be made at breakneck speed? Toss all of the ingredients in the blender and enjoy this shake on the go.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a tall glass and garnish with a sprinkle of cocoa powder, if desired.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Breakfast Shake
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious blend of bananas, milk, yogurt, and peanut butter makes for a filling breakfast on-the-go. Cocoa powder lends a touch of sweet that also hits the spot as an afternoon snack.
instructions: Peel bananas, chop into small pieces and place in freezer until hard.
Gather all ingredients and put all ingredients in a blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 2 glasses.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Smoothie
recipes.notes: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This treat can be made with your kids in the morning, then frozen for an afterschool snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel bananas.
Spread the entire outside of each banana with peanut butter.
Roll the bananas in crushed nuts, sprinkles or other items.
Cut the bananas in one inch slices.
Store in the refrigerator or freezer until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Bananas
recipes.notes: Walnuts used in nutrition analysis and for costing purposes. A cheaper option would be to use peanuts.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: For a peanut butter extravaganza, spread smooth or chunky peanut butter on top of a slice of this delicious bread! Top with banana or strawberry slices.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly grease or spray with non-stick spray, a loaf pan.
In large bowl, beat eggs.
Add milk, sugar, and peanut butter.
Mix well.
In a separate bowl combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Mix thoroughly.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients.
Mix only enough to moisten all ingredients.
Pour into prepared pan.
Pan will be half full.
Bake for 1 hour.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These bars make a great on the go snack to satisfy a sweet tooth. Trying adding pumpkin seeds, chia seeds, or chopped nuts to add a little extra crunch.

ingredients.name: raisins or other dried fruit
ingredients.raw: 1 cup raisins or other dried fruit

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, bring honey to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and stir in peanut butter.
Add cereal, oats and raisins; mix well.
Remove from heat Lightly grease an 8x8 inch baking pan.
Press mixture into pan.
When cool, cut into 16 bars.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Cereal Bars
recipes.notes: * Honey is not recommended for children under 1 year old.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these nutty muffins with a touch of jelly or jam for a satisfying dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Line 12 muffin cups with paper baking cups (or grease the bottom of each cup with butter or margarine).
Put the peanut butter and honey in a mixing bowl.
Beat until well blended.
Add the eggs 1 at a time, beating well after each egg.
Add the milk, and mix well.
Add the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Stir just until they are moistened.
Don’t stir them too much.
Fill each muffin cup 2/3 full.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Put on a wire rack.
Cool for at least 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty stew combining creamy peanut butter, hearty vegetables, and spices. Perfect for a chilly evening, it brings the warmth of garlic, ginger, and cumin to your table for a satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: whole yellow or red potatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 pounds whole yellow or red potatoes, peeled, halved, and cut into quarters

instructions: Heat oil over medium heat in a pot and add onions.
Cook for a few minutes.
Add ginger and garlic.
Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add cumin and salt.
Add peanut butter, tomato paste, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil and add potatoes.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until potatoes are fork-tender and cooked through.
Add kale, and continue to cook for 1-2 minutes, Serve garnished with lime zest, lime juice, and crushed peanuts; drizzle with Sriracha for a spicy kick (optional)
recipes.name: Peanut Stew
recipes.notes: Yellow and red potatoes will stay fork tender in this stew. Russet potatoes may fall apart and get mushy.
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Potatoes USA, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Inspired by an all-time favorite, peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, this wrap is easy and fun for kids to make. With the sweet flavor of fruit and the crisp texture of green pepper and lettuce, it's a great way to fit one cup of fruit and veggies into a "wrap 'n go" meal.

ingredients.name: red or green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup red or green bell pepper

instructions: In a medium bowl, combine peaches, pineapple, bell pepper, and cinnamon.
Warm the tortillas.
Spread 2 tablespoons of peanut butter on one side of each tortilla, leaving room on the edges.
Spoon equal portions of the peach mixture over peanut butter, then top with lettuce.
Fold the side and bottom edges of each tortilla toward the middle over the filling, then roll so the tortilla covers the filling.
recipes.name: Peanut, Peach, N Pineapple Wrap
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A spicy and savory one pot dish that the whole family will enjoy. Add some cayenne pepper for an extra kick.

ingredients.name: medium sweet potato
ingredients.raw: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, not drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine first 9 ingredients in a soup pot.
Bring to boil, then turn down to medium low, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter and milk.
Return to gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 5 minutes.
Stir in spinach and cook until wilted, 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Ladle stew into bowls and top with peanuts and green onion, if desired.
recipes.name: Peanutty Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet and simple, this warm and cozy dessert is the perfect end to a fall or winter meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the pears and cook in a double boiler for 15 minutes.
Mix sugar and orange juice and cook over low flame for 5 minutes.
Cool for 5 minutes.
Place steamed pears on individual plates.
Pour 1/4 of the juice mixture over each and serve.
recipes.name: Pear in Orange Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fruity kabobs that you can enjoy for a snack or dessert. Try experimenting with different patterns and fruits.

ingredients.name: medium pears
ingredients.raw: 2 medium pears, cored and cut into 1-inch cubes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine the vanilla yogurt and strawberry preserves.
Set aside.
Thread the fruits by alternating the pears, strawberries, bananas, and pineapple onto the skewers.
Serve the fruit skewers with a dollop of the strawberry sauce on the side.
recipes.name: Pear Kabobs with Strawberry Dipping Sauce
recipes.notes: Other materials needed:
recipes.recipe_by: USA Pears (recipe) and Pear Bureau Northwest (photo)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Scrumptious, sweet salsa that will be a party favorite. Use a tart apple variety for best results.

ingredients.name: medium pear
ingredients.raw: 1 medium pear, cored and finely chopped

ingredients.name: medium apple
ingredients.raw: 1 medium apple, cored and finely chopped

ingredients.name: medium orange
ingredients.raw: 1 medium orange, peeled and finely chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine pear, apple, kiwifruit, and orange in a medium-sized bowl.
Pour honey and lemon juice over fruit and gently toss.
Scoop up bites of fruit salsa using bites of cinnamon graham crackers (optional).
recipes.name: Pear Party Salsa
recipes.notes: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. Other materials needed:
recipes.recipe_by: USA Pears and Pear Bureau Northwest

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Beautiful, nutritious, and delicious, this open-faced sandwich is worth the extra effort.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a flower-shaped cookie cutter to cut each slide of bread.
If bread sticks to cutter, gently push the petals out with your fingers.
Wash the pear and dry it with a paper towel.
Cut the pear in half, and remove the core.
Cut each pear half into four slices, then cut each slice into five pieces.
You will only use the center three pieces of each slice, so go ahead and eat the end pieces.
Spread 1 teaspoon of peanut butter in a circle in the center of each of the flowers.
Place 3 pieces of pear on the peanut butter on each flower.
Arrange the pears so the skin is facing out and the white centers are touching in the middle.
Drizzle 1/2 teaspoon of strawberry preserves in the center of each flower and over the pears.
recipes.name: Pear PB&J Bouquet
recipes.notes: Other materials needed:
recipes.recipe_by: The Pear Dish — USA Pears

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: An easy way to add more fruit to your day is to incorporate them into your meals. Canned pears and cheese go well together in this quesadilla, with added flavor from basil, onion, and pepper jack cheese.
instructions: Sprinkle cheeses, basil, and onion on half of each tortilla.
Place pear slices on top of other ingredients in each tortilla.
Fold over filled tortilla and brush each side with olive oil.
Heat the filled tortillas in a non-stick skillet until cheese melts, about 2 to 3 minutes on each side.
Cut quesadilla into four pieces and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Pear Quesadillas
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A cute and fruity "rabbit" snack that kids can help make.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place 2 pear halves, flat side down, on a small plate to make the body.
Use butter knife to cut a tail, ears and feet from another pear half.
Add each part to the body.
Use butter knife to cut one raisin in half and place on small end for eyes.
Enjoy your pear rabbit!
recipes.name: Pear Rabbit
recipes.notes: Adults: If cooking with kids, use can opener, open pear halves and discard sharp-edged lid.
recipes.recipe_by: Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Get your servings of fruits and veggies in one dish! This salad is sweet and tangy with a yogurt and orange juice dressing. Serve it as a side salad to complement another entree, or have it alone for a healthy snack option!

ingredients.name: green beans
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup green beans, sliced into bite size pieces

ingredients.name: canned pears
ingredients.raw: 1 cup canned pears, drained and chopped

instructions: Place salad greens, sliced vegetables, pears, walnuts, and raisins in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together vinegar, yogurt, and orange juice to prepare dressing.
Top salad with dressing and mix gently.
Serve.
recipes.name: Pear Salad
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Creamy peanut butter, crunchy celery, and juicy pears make the perfect snack for kids and adults.

ingredients.name: medium celery stalks
ingredients.note: cleaned and cut into 3-inch long pieces
ingredients.raw: 4 medium celery stalks, cleaned and cut into 3-inch long pieces

ingredients.name: medium pears
ingredients.raw: 2 medium pears, cored and cut into chunks

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread the peanut butter into the center of the celery pieces.
Place the pear chunks on top of the peanut butter.
Serve on a plate and enjoy with your friends.
recipes.name: Pears in a Pod
recipes.notes: Other materials needed:
recipes.recipe_by: USA Pears and Pear Bureau Northwest

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These simple stuffed peppers are fun and flavorful. Use yellow, red, green, and orange peppers for a colorful dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Cook brown rice according to package directions.
Wash the peppers under running water.
Cut the tops off the peppers and spoon out the seeds.
Cut up two peppers and leave four to fill with the rice mixture.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Combine the chopped up peppers, beans, rice, salsa, tomato and salt (optional).
Spoon about 3 tablespoons of the mixture into the bottom of each pepper.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of cheese.
Repeat steps 8 and 9 to fill the pepper completely, but do not top with cheese.
Bake peppers for 30 minutes.
Top each pepper with 2 tablespoons of cheese and continue baking for 15 minutes more.
recipes.name: Peppers Stuffed with Rice and Beans
recipes.notes: Green bell peppers used for nutritional analysis. Use homemade salsa to lower the sodium of this recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Simple Stuffed Peppers, Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fluffy, pumpkin pancakes will delight your taste buds at breakfast or dinner. Top with sliced banana or applesauce.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine flour, brown sugar, baking powder, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
In a medium bowl, combine egg, canned pumpkin, milk, and vegetable oil; mix well.
Add wet ingredients to flour mixture, stirring just until moist.
Batter may be lumpy. (For thinner batter, add more milk.) Lightly coat a griddle or skillet with cooking spray and heat on medium.
Using a 1/4 cup measure, pour batter onto hot griddle.
Cook until bubbles begin to burst, then flip pancakes and cook until golden brown, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes.
Repeat with remaining batter.
Makes about 1 dozen 3 1/2 inch pancakes.
recipes.name: Perfect Pumpkin Pancakes
recipes.notes: If you don't have pumpkin spice on hand, don't worry -- it's just a combination of cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and cloves. In this recipe, you can substitute 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, and 1/8 teaspoon each of ginger and cloves for the pumpkin pie spice. Safety Tip: You can be sure your skillet or griddle is hot enough for pancakes without burning your hand. Just sprinkle a few (3 or 4) drops of water on the surface. If they dance and sizzle, you are ready to cook. Be sure handles of skillets and pans are always turned toward the center or back of the stove, to prevent the pan from catching on hands or clothes and causing burns.
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A perfect treat for pumpkin lovers. A seasonal treat for the holidays or any time of year that you're craving pumpkin.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium bowl, stir together the pumpkin, brown sugar, eggs, and oil.
Mix well.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, oats, cinnamon, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add the pumpkin mix to the flour mix.
Stir well.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan with butter or margarine.
Pour the batter into the greased baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Peter Pumpkin Squares
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe starts with seasoned and browned ground beef simmered with tomatoes and beans and is finished with a mix of olives and raisins. Served over rice, this flavorful dish makes a quick and easy meal.

ingredients.name: lean ground turkey or beef
ingredients.raw: 3/4 pound lean ground turkey or beef

ingredients.name: 15 ounce can low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 15 ounce can low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Prepare the Rice: Cook as instructed on the package.
Set aside.
Prepare the Picadillo: Place the skillet on the stove over medium heat and when hot, add oil.
Add the onion, pepper, and garlic.
Cook and stir about 10 minutes until the onion is softened and lightly browned.
Add oregano, cumin, pepper, and salt, and stir well.
Add beef, in small amounts.
Stir well and cook about 10 minutes until the beef is cooked throughout.
Add beans and tomatoes and simmer about 15 minutes until mixture blends together.
Add olives and raisins.
Stir well and cook about 2 minutes until heated through.
Serve over rice or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
Serve with avocado, if desired.
recipes.name: Picadillo
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fun flavorful dish that is full of veggies and lean protein and can be made in a flash.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground turkey in a non-stick frying pan.
Add onions, carrots, zucchini, potatoes, salt, pepper, and cumin.
Sauté for about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and just enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer, uncovered, until vegetables are tender.
Dissolve cornstarch in about 1 tablespoon of cold water, add to mixture, bring back to a boil until gravy thickens.
Serve.
recipes.name: Picadillo
recipes.recipe_by: California Health Department, Los Angeles County — Es Facil Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fantastic recipe to try when your garden or market is overflowing with fresh, flavorful tomatoes!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
recipes.name: Pico de Gallo
recipes.notes: Use to season your family meals or serve with tortilla chips.
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fluffy and fruity, this airy cake is delicate and sweet, the perfect after dinner treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites until they are foamy.
Add the cream of tartar and beat until stiff, but not dry.
Gradually beat in the sugar.
Add the vanilla and salt and then gently fold in the flour.
Add the pineapple to the cake mix.
Pour into an ungreased 13x9-inch pan.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until golden brown or an inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Let cool and serve with whipped topping (optional).
recipes.name: Pineapple Angel Food Cake
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Delicious sandwich, wrap, or pita filling featuring chunks of avocado, pineapple, and chicken. Avocado helps make a creamy, luscious dressing.
instructions: Mash 1/2 avocado in a small dish; add yogurt, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cut remaining avocado into small chunks and mix together with pineapple, bell pepper, carrots, cabbage, green onion, and chicken.
Add dressing; mix gently.
Fill pita pockets and serve.
recipes.name: Pineapple Avocado Chicken Salad
recipes.notes: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this tangy chicken dish with brown rice. Add brightly colored vegetables for a tasty and simple meal!

ingredients.name: (20 ounces) pineapple
ingredients.raw: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple, crushed or chunks

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Coat frying pan with nonstick cooking spray and set heat to low.
Once pan heats up, add chicken.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cook uncovered until chicken begins to brown, then add crushed pineapple and water.
Cover chicken until chicken is tender.
May serve over rice.
recipes.name: Pineapple Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fruity and tropical treat to keep you cool during the dog days of summer.

ingredients.name: pineapple chunks
ingredients.raw: 1 cup pineapple chunks, fresh or canned

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place yogurt and pineapple in large plastic bag and flatten.
Freeze overnight.
Combine yogurt, pineapple, and juice in food processor or blender and blend until smooth.
Serve immediately or place back in the freezer to harden until ready to serve, up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Stir before serving.
recipes.name: Pineapple Orange Frozen Yogurt
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Savory and sweet, delicious pineapple pork chops are a fast and flavorful meal. Enjoy over brown rice or quinoa.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the green pepper into strips.
Heat the oil in a large skillet.
Place pork chops on the heated skillet.
Sprinkle the salt on top.
Cook the pork chops for 5 minutes on low heat on each side.
Cook pork chops until they reache an internal temperature of 145 degrees F.
Remove the cooked pork from the skillet.
Place it in a serving dish and keep warm.
Put the green pepper slices in the skillet.
Stir in the pineapple chunks with their juice.
Add the ginger and cinnamon.
Simmer for about 3 to 5 minutes.
Spoon the pineapple mixture over cooked pork.
recipes.name: Pineapple Pork
recipes.notes: Serve with cooked rice.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A cozy and creamy dessert that your whole family will enjoy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Lightly coat an oven safe 2 quart casserole dish with nonstick spray or oil.
In a large mixing bowl, beat together eggs, milk, and sugar.
Add undrained crushed pineapple, cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla.
Stir in cooked rice.
Pour into prepared casserole dish.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until a knife inserted in center of pudding comes out clean.
recipes.name: Pineapple Rice Bake
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Stuffed with fruits and veggies, this hearty cake can be shared after a light lunch or dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Grease or lightly spray with non-stick cooking spray, a 9x13 inch pan.
In a large bowl, beat eggs, sugar, vanilla, and oil.
Add zucchini.
In a separate bowl, combine baking powder salt, baking soda, and flour.
Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Stir in fruit and nuts, if using.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, or until cake springs back when lightly pressed with your finger.
recipes.name: Pineapple Zucchini Cake
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service
recipes.serving_size: 1 3x3.25 inch piece of cake, 1/12 of recipe (135g)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Pretty in pink! Enjoy this colorful and flavorful salad at a picnic or cookout with family and friends.

ingredients.name: peas
ingredients.raw: 1 cup peas, green, fresh or frozen

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the potatoes in 2 cups of water in a deep kettle.
Cover and cook over moderate heat for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
When thoroughly cool, dice potatoes and place in a big bowl.
Add diced beets and mix with the potatoes.
Set aside 1/4 cup of peas for garnishing and add the rest to the bowl.
Save 1 egg to use as a garnish.
Chop the rest and add to the bowl.
Peel the skin off the apple and remove the core.
Cut the apple into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and sprinkle with lemon juice.
Add apple to the salad.
Add the vinegar, olive oil, and sugar.
Mix thoroughly.
Chill and serve.
recipes.name: Pink Party Salad
recipes.notes: The skin can be left on the apple to increase fiber and save time.
recipes.recipe_by: From the Farm to the Table — University of Connecticut Cooperative Extension — Hispanic Health Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Teach your teenagers how to make this tasty and easy recipe as an afterschool snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spray a small non-stick skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Over medium heat, break egg into pan; break yolk.
When egg is done turn over sprinkle with cheese and top with pepperoni (optional).
Cook until cheese is melted.
Open bun, spread with pizza sauce and top with cooked egg.
recipes.name: Pizza Eggburger
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Cooperative Extension — Ross County Extension Office

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: There are microwave and oven directions for this recipe, so that you can make this meal in a way that is quick and convenient for you and your family. Enjoy with a fresh green salad or steamed spinach on the side.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly grease 9 inch pie plate with vegetable oil.
Pat turkey into pie plate.
Cover turkey with waxed paper.
Cook in microwave on high; rotate plate 1/4 turn after 3 minutes.
Cook until turkey reaches an internal temperature of 160 °F, about 5 more minutes.
Drain excess liquid.
OR - Place turkey in 350 °F oven; bake until turkey reaches an internal temperature of 160 °F, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Drain any excess liquid.
Top cooked turkey with vegetables, spaghetti sauce, and cheese.
Return turkey to either the microwave or oven and heat until cheese is melted, about 1 to 2 minutes.
recipes.name: Pizza Meat Loaf
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mofonguitos are a delicious Puerto Rican inspired dish consisting of small, plantain cups filled with savory, seasoned chicken.

ingredients.name: small can chicken
ingredients.note: 10 ounces, drained or 1 cup cooked diced chicken

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: Or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat.
Add shredded chicken and onions.
Cook for about 1-2 minutes.
Add spices to the mixture and cook, stirring often, for about 5 minutes.
Set aside for later.
Wash and scrub plantains.
Cut off each end and make 3 vertical cuts along the side of the plantain.
Using your thumb, peel the skin away from the flesh of the plantain and cut into 1-inch chunks.
Heat the oil over medium heat in a skillet for about 1 minute.
Add the plantain chunks and sprinkle the salt on top.
Cook on all sides of the chunks (about 5-6 minutes on each side).
Using tongs, be sure to turn the plantain pieces on their sides so the insides cook throughout, and they turn a golden color.
Turn the heat down to low and remove the plantain chunks from the pan.
Take 2 plantain chunks at a time and shape them into a cup using either your hands, a small pestle and mortar, or a lemon squeezer.
Fill the plantain cups with the chicken mixture and top with a low-fat yogurt dip (optional).
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Plantain Cups with Shredded Chicken | Mofonguitos
recipes.recipe_by: University of Rhode Island SNAP-Education

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fun recipe to make with kids. Use your favorite fruit and whole grain tortillas, and enjoy!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Warm tortillas in microwave or oven to make them easier to handle.
Peel and chop fruit into pieces.
Place 1/4 of the fruit on half of each tortilla.
In a small bowl, stir together brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Sprinkle over fruit.
Roll up the tortillas, starting at the end with the fruit.
Place on an greased baking sheet and make small slashes to allow steam to escape.
Brush with milk and sprinkle with additional sugar, if desired.
Back at 350 °F in oven for 8 to 12 minutes or until lightly brown.
Serve warm or cool.
recipes.name: Pocket Fruit Pies
recipes.recipe_by: Kansas State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this creamy and flavorful dish, packed with cheese, beans, peppers, and corn.

ingredients.name: whole kernel corn mixed with green and red peppers
ingredients.raw: 1 can whole kernel corn mixed with green and red peppers

ingredients.name: cheese
ingredients.raw: 6 ounces cheese, cheddar, reduced fat, shredded

ingredients.name: black or pinto beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can black or pinto beans, low-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium sauce pan, bring the water to a boil.
Gradually add the cornmeal or polenta.
Reduce heat to low.
Continue stirring, add the corn, chilies, and the salt.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes or until mixture thickens, stirring occasionally.
Gently stir in the margarine, cheese, and beans.
Remove from the heat and transfer to a serving dish.
Garnish with red bell pepper rings and cilantro.
recipes.name: Polenta with Pepper and Cheese
recipes.recipe_by: California Health Department, Los Angeles County — Es Facil Campaign — Recipe submitted by Gloria Vargas

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A great snack for adults and kids. A crunchy and sweet treat, enjoy this snack by yourself or double the recipe and share it with a group of friends.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pop popcorn.
Mix popped corn, raisins, and cereal in a large bowl.
Mix sugar and cinnamon in small dish.
Drizzle melted margarine or butter over mixture.
Add sugar and cinnamon mixture.
Shake or stir until all ingredients are evenly distributed.
recipes.name: Popcorn Treats
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension — Nutrition Education Programs

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A perfect recipe for meat and potatoes fans. Enjoy this recipe with a fresh side salad and a piece of fruit for dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
In a bowl mix veggies with 1 tablespoon oil, salt, and pepper.
Lay veggies around the edge of a 9x13 inch pan and put in oven.
Use a small bowl to make the rub.
Mix the brown sugar, garlic, 1/2 teaspoon pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt in the bowl.
Sprinkle the rub over the loin.
Press gently so the rub sticks to the roast.
Wash your hands after handling the raw meat.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium high heat.
Add the loin.
Brown the sides of meat.
Turn after about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork to the center of the pan with veggies.
Bake for about 40 minutes.
A meat thermometer should read 145 °F.
Check the temperature after 30 minutes in the oven.
Remove from oven.
Let set for 5 minutes.
Slice and serve.
recipes.name: Pork Loin Roast with Veggies
recipes.recipe_by: Spend Smart. Eat Smart. — Iowa State University Extension
recipes.serving_size: Approx. 3 oz. meat and 1 cup veggies, 1/6 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The Pork Power Bowl combines savory, tender pork tenderloin with a colorful mix of vegetables and grains, creating a balanced and nutritious meal. This dish offers a flavorful and wholesome option for a satisfying lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: medium purple or orange carrots
ingredients.raw: 2 medium purple or orange carrots, ribbon peeled

ingredients.name: salt (or 1/2 tsp. kosher salt)
ingredients.raw: 1/4 teaspoon salt (or ½ tsp. kosher salt)

ingredients.name: pork tenderloin
ingredients.raw: 1 pound pork tenderloin, cut into 1½ inch cubes

ingredients.name: 15.5 oz can low sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 15.5 oz can low sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, cut into strips

ingredients.name: chopped fresh cilantro
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for garnish

instructions: In a large mason jar add the carrots, radish, rice wine vinegar, garlic, salt, honey and water, shake to combine.
Let sit for 30 minutes.
In a medium bowl toss the pork, 2 Tbsp. lime juice, 1 Tbsp. olive oil, paprika and cumin.
Cover and marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Place the quinoa, stock and kale in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let sit for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Thread the pork onto skewers and grill over medium-high heat, turning frequently, until pork reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F.
Let pork rest for 3 minutes.
Divide the quinoa between four bowls.
Arrange the beans, peppers, avocado, carrots and radishes on top of the quinoa.
Remove the pork from the skewers and place it on top of the bowls.
Drizzle with dressing and garnish with additional cilantro, if desired.
Dressing (optional): In a food processor, add yogurt, 3 Tbsp. olive oil, 1 Tbsp. lime juice, ½ an avocado, green onion and cilantro.
Puree until smooth, season with salt and pepper.
Thin dressing with cold water, if desired.
recipes.name: Pork Power Bowl
recipes.notes: Dressing nutrition not included.
recipes.recipe_by: Created by The National Pork Board, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a tender and satisfying roast beef dinner. Serve with a green salad and bread.

ingredients.name: red potatoes
ingredients.note: or 2 cans, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 8 red potatoes, peeled and quartered (or 2 cans, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained)

ingredients.name: turnips
ingredients.note: or 1 can low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 2 turnips, peeled and quartered (or 1 can low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained)

instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Season the roast with salt and pepper.
In a large pan, brown the roast in the oil over medium to high heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Drain fat.
Use a large iron skillet or roasting pan.
Put the roast in the middle of the pan.
Add the potatoes, turnips, onions, and carrots around the roast.
Pour the tomato juice over the roast and vegetables.
Cover the pan with a lid or foil and bake for 1 hour or until potatoes are cooked.
If desired, cut roast into one inch chunks.
Mix and serve.
recipes.name: Pot Roasted Beef
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking beef roast: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for beef roast is 145 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A casserole perfect for meat and potato lovers. Savor this recipe with a fresh green salad on the side and piece of fruit for dessert.

ingredients.name: cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can cream of mushroom soup, reduced sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel onion and dice into 1/4-inch pieces.
Cook ground beef and onions in a skillet until the meat is browned.
Drain of fat.
Add mushroom soup and 1/2 can water.
Use a brush to scrub potatoes under cold running water.
Slice potatoes into 1/2-inch thick pieces and places in the bottom of a casserole dish.
Spread meat and soup mixture over potatoes.
Bake at 350 °F for 45 minutes until potatoes are tender and casserole is bubbly and browned.
recipes.name: Potato Beef Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these potato cakes with fat-free sour cream or fat-free yogurt and chives.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: cold, mashed, made from instant potato flakes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare potatoes according to package.
Put mashed potatoes into a bowl.
Add flour and onion.
Mix well.
Pat potato mixture on a lightly floured board until 1/2 inch thick.
Cut with a 3-inch round cutter.
Place on a baking sheet, cover and refrigerate until just before cooking.
Heat oil in a frying pan or griddle.
Fry cakes over medium heat, turning to brown on both sides.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Potato Cakes
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: How can you make nachos better? Combine them with potatoes! Change up your toppings or trying new seasonings when cooking the ground turkey.

ingredients.name: small red potatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 small red potatoes, skins on (1 pound)

ingredients.name: vegetable oil or cooking spray
ingredients.raw: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil or cooking spray

ingredients.name: lean ground turkey (15% fat or less)
ingredients.raw: 8 ounces lean ground turkey (15% fat or less)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice potatoes into small circles about 1/4 inch thick.
Lightly coat the potato slices with oil (or spray for 3 seconds with cooking spray).
Arrange slices on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake in the oven at 450 °F for 25 to 30 minutes, depending on desired darkness.
Meanwhile, add ground turkey and chili powder to a skillet.
Cook, stirring over medium heat (300 °F in an electric skillet) for 8 to10 minutes or until turkey browns.
Remove potatoes from the oven.
Transfer baked potatoes to an oven-safe dish.
Top with turkey and sprinkle with cheese.
Put back in the oven to melt the cheese, about 2 minutes.
Remove from oven and top with lettuce, tomato, cucumber, cilantro, and salsa.
recipes.name: Potato Nachos
recipes.notes: Try other toppings, such as guacamole or reduced-fat sour cream or plain yogurt.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A creamy yogurt, olive oil, and mustard sauce is tossed with tender potatoes and celery then topped with scallions and parsley to make up this favorite classic side dish.
instructions: Place potatoes in a pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil over high heat and cook until potatoes are tender.
Drain and set aside to cool to room temperature.
While potatoes are cooling, mix the yogurt, olive oil, and mustard in a small bowl.
Add the yogurt mixture to the cooled potatoes and mix gently.
Stir in the celery, scallions, and parsley.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.name: Potato Salad
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Perfect for your next cookout or picnic, this simple potato salad will be enjoyed by your friends and family.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub the potatoes, and peel them.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Put the potatoes into a saucepan.
Cover with water.
Bring the potatoes to a boil on medium heat.
Let the potatoes simmer for 15 minutes until they’re soft.
Drain the hot water, and let the potatoes cool.
While the potatoes are cooling, peel and chop some onions until you have 1 cup of chopped onions.
Chop the celery until you have 1/2 cup of chopped celery.
Put the chopped onion and celery in a medium mixing bowl.
Add the mayonnaise and pickle relish.
Stir together.
Add the cooled potatoes.
Stir again.
Cover the bowl.
Put in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Potato Salad
recipes.notes: Leave on the potato peels for more fiber and other nutrients.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This lively dish gives a nod to buffalo chicken wings but without extra fat and calories. Start with a foundation of nutritious potatoes -- which are naturally high in potassium, vitamin C, and fiber -- and replace fried wings with shredded chicken breast and top with fresh tomatoes and onions. Don't forget the celery sticks.
instructions: Center oven rack and preheat oven to 425 °F.
Place chicken in a sauté pan, add water, and cover.
Simmer for 20 minutes and remove from pan; let cool slightly.
When chicken is cool enough to handle, shred using two forks, one in each hand.
While chicken is simmering, wash and scrub potatoes with a clean vegetable brush under running water and slit each one lengthwise about 1-inch deep.
Place potatoes in a microwave-safe dish and microwave on high, uncovered, for about 10 minutes.
Let cool slightly.
Slice each potato in half length-wise, scoop out potato, leaving a 1/4 inch shell.
Mash potato together with hot pepper sauce, sour cream, margarine, and milk.
Fold in blue cheese and shredded chicken.
Spoon mixture into potato skins slightly denting center (to hold fresh toppings after baking).
Place filled potato skins on a 9x13 inch baking sheet and bake about 15 to 20 minutes until tops are golden brown.
Dice tomatoes and green onions.
Cut celery stalks into four inch sticks.
To serve, top potatoes with onions and tomatoes.
Serve celery sticks on the side for scooping potato contents.
recipes.name: Potato Skins with Buffalo Chicken
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and apple slices.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This rich-tasting and hearty potato soup is full of flavor and perfect for lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.raw: 1/4 pound chicken, cut up, and skin removed (thaw if frozen)

ingredients.name: small red potatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 small red potatoes, chopped (or canned low-sodium sliced potatoes)

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup white rice, uncooked (or brown rice)

ingredients.name: peas (or canned low-sodium green peas)
ingredients.raw: 1 cup peas (or canned low-sodium green peas)

ingredients.name: cayenne or jalapeño chilies
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon cayenne or jalapeño chilies, diced (optional)

ingredients.name: fresh parsley or cilantro
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (optional)

instructions: In a large pot, brown onion and garlic in oil over medium to high heat for 5 minutes.
Add chicken to pot and brown for about 5 minutes.
Add water, potatoes, rice, and chili powder to pot.
Bring pot to a boil, and cook for 15 minutes.
Lower heat and cook for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir pot every 10 minutes.
Add peas and cook for about 8 minutes.
If using cayenne or jalapeño chilies, add that too.
Mix well.
Remove pot from heat.
If using parsley or cilantro, add that now.
Mix well and cover for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Potato Soup
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Warm up a cold winter night with this cozy soup. Enjoy with dark green vegetables and broiled fish, meat, or tofu.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the celery.
Peel the potatoes, and cut them into small cubes.
Melt the margarine in a large saucepan on low heat.
Add the onion and celery.
Cook for a few minutes.
Add the potatoes, salt, pepper, and 1 1/2 cups water.
Cook for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
In a small bowl, stir together the dry milk and flour.
Add 1 1/2 cups water slowly, stirring as you add it.
Add the milk mix to the potatoes.
Cook until the soup is heated and slightly thickened.
Adjust the seasonings.
recipes.name: Potato Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This casserole would be wonderful for brunch or dinner. Top with fresh tomatoes or your favorite salsa!

ingredients.name: frozen hash browns
ingredients.raw: 1 2/3 cups frozen hash browns, country style

ingredients.name: cheese
