Blanch the green beans in boiling water for about 4 minutes for crisper beans or longer for a softer texture.
Then plunge in ice water.
Drain and set aside.
Place diced onions and mushrooms in a microwaveable bowl and microwave for about 2 1/2 minutes on high to soften.
Set aside.
Melt the butter over medium heat.
Once melted, stir in flour with a whisk and cook for about 1 minute (continuously whisking).
Whisk in the milk and cook over low heat until you have a thick white sauce.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Stir the drained green beans, onions, and mushrooms into the white sauce (including any liquid with the onions and mushrooms).
Pour into a casserole dish sprayed with nonstick spray.
Crush the crackers and toss cracker crumbs with olive oil and onion powder.
Sprinkle over the top of the casserole.
Bake at 350 °F for about 30 minutes or until crackers are golden brown.
recipes.name: Sarah’s Green Bean Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Sarah, MyPlate Nutritionist
recipes.serving_size: 1 portion of Sarah's Green Bean Casserole

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This turkey curry soup is a fun and flavorful dish to make with turkey dinner leftovers. You can use your leftover cranberry sauce to garnish the soup. A spoonful of cranberry sauce or chutney adds a cooling sweet, tangy flavor to balance the spicy curry.
instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and celery and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in flour, curry powder, and cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any brown bits at the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer.
Then add carrots, spinach, potatoes, and turkey.
Bring to a boil.
Then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer (covered) for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve in bowls and garnish with a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
recipes.name: Sarah’s Spicy Curry Turkey Soup
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Sarah, MyPlate Nutritionist
recipes.serving_size: 1 cup of Sarah's Spicy Curry Turkey Soup

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toasted whole grain bread is stacked with cucumbers, sardines, tomato, and sliced red onion. Try canned tuna or salmon as tasty alternatives for sardines.
instructions: Put 4 slices toasted bread on the cutting board.
Arrange cucumber slices on top of each slice.
Distribute the sardines evenly on top of the cucumber and using the fork, gently mash them.
Spread the mashed sardines to cover the cucumber.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the sardines.
Put the tomato slices on top of the sardines.
Add the red onion.
Top with the remaining slices of toast and press down gently to hold the sandwich together.
Cut the sandwich in half and serve right away.
recipes.name: Sardine, Cucumber, and Tomato Sandwich
recipes.notes: Canned tuna or salmon can be used instead of sardines
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Don’t throw away your beet greens! The leafy tops of beets can be so tasty. In this recipe, lemon juice, vegetable oil, and seasonings give them a bold flavor profile.

ingredients.name: chopped beet greens (2 bunches with stems removed)
ingredients.raw: 4 cups chopped beet greens (2 bunches with stems removed)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan over medium heat.
Add the beet greens and garlic to the pan.
Stir until just wilted, then reduce the heat to low and stir occasionally until soft, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and salt.
Serve right away or use in another recipe.
recipes.name: Sautéed Beet Greens
recipes.notes: No beet greens? Use other leafy greens such as mustard greens or chard.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cabbage, onion, and caraway seeds make this simple and inexpensive side dish a flavorful way to eat more veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large sauté pan.
Sauté onion over medium heat, until light brown, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Add sliced cabbage, salt, black pepper, and caraway seeds.
Stir and cook for 30 minutes.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Sautéed Cabbage and Onion
recipes.recipe_by: "Cabbage Comfort" National Cancer Institute (NCI) — 5 A Day for Better Health Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cauliflower can be made into a rice alternative with just a few simple ingredients. Make this fresh-tasting side dish by pairing cauliflower with garlic, onion, and more.

ingredients.name: medium cauliflower
ingredients.note: grated or finely chopped, 4 to 5 cups

ingredients.name: lemon juice or lime juice
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon lemon juice or lime juice

ingredients.name: chopped fresh parsley or cilantro
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or cilantro

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet or saucepan on medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cauliflower, salt, and pepper.
Stir until cauliflower is tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and sprinkle with parsley, if desired.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Sautéed Cauliflower Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This pan-seared walleye recipe uses fresh herbs and lemon to bring out the mild flavor and flaky texture of this omega-3-rich white fish.

ingredients.name: walleye fillets (4–6 ounces each)
ingredients.raw: 2 walleye fillets (4–6 ounces each), thawed and patted dry

ingredients.name: chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season walleye on the flesh side with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with tarragon or parsley and press lightly into the flesh to help it stick.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium high heat.
Place the fillets seasoned side down in the pan, tilting the pan to make sure the butter surrounds the fillets, and cook for about 3 minutes.
Gently flip the fillets and cook on the second side, about 2 minutes.
Walleye should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145 °F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
Plate and serve immediately with lemon wedges.
recipes.name: Sautéed Walleye with Tarragon
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Red Lake Nation Fishery

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Ground beef is the surprise ingredient in this savory and spicy succotash dish.

ingredients.name: frozen lima beans
ingredients.raw: 1 cup frozen lima beans, cooked and drained

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, broken up

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in 9-inch skillet.
Drain excess liquid.
Stir in remaining ingredients except nutmeg.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Sprinkle with nutmeg before serving.
recipes.name: Savory and Spicy Ground Beef & Succotash
recipes.recipe_by: A River of Recipes: Native American Recipes Using Commodity Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bread, cheese, and kale make up this savory bread pudding. Bake ahead of time and slice for quick meals and snacks.

ingredients.name: shredded low-sodium mozzarella or cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup shredded low-sodium mozzarella or cheddar cheese

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Lightly grease a 2-quart baking pan.
Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion and cook about 10 minutes, until tender.
While the onion is cooking, put eggs and milk in a bowl and mix until combined.
Add the cheese, bread, kale, squash, and salt and mix well.
Let the mixture stand at least 15 minutes until the bread absorbs most of the milk.
When the onion has finished cooking, add it to the bread mixture and mix well.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and transfer to the oven.
Bake uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until lightly browned and set.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Savory Bread Pudding with Kale and Butternut Squash
recipes.notes: It is important to use stale bread that has dried out. If you don’t have stale bread, put fresh bread in a preheated 250 °F oven and bake until dried, usually about 15 minutes.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These savory meatloaf muffins are full of flavor and have a beautiful presentation. Enjoy one with a side of steamed spinach, kale, or a fresh green salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Spoon mixture and divide evenly into 12 greased muffin cups.
Bake for 1 hour, or until temperature in center of meatloaf is 160 °F.
Cool slightly before removing from muffin cups.
recipes.name: Savory Meatloaf Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A perfect side dish to your favorite stir-fry recipe. Enjoy the added flavor from the scallions.

ingredients.name: brown rice
ingredients.raw: 4 1/2 cups brown rice, cooked in unsalted water

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook rice according to directions on the package.
Combine the cooked rice, bouillon granules, and scallions and mix well.
Measure 1-cup portions and serve.
recipes.name: Scallion Rice
recipes.recipe_by: DASH Eating Plan: Lower Your Blood Pressure — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty side dish that would go well with a flavorful fish recipe and a fresh green salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash potatoes; peel and slice into thin slices.
Melt 1 tablespoon of margarine in heavy, deep skillet.
Remove skillet from heat; spread half of potato slices in skillet.
Cover potatoes with onions.
Sprinkle half of flour and pepper over potato mixture.
Add remaining potato slices, flour, and pepper.
Cut 1 tablespoon of margarine into small pieces and place on top of potato mixture.
Pour milk over potato mixture; bring to boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to medium low, cover, and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes
recipes.notes: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!
recipes.recipe_by: Recipes and Tips for Healthy, Thrifty Meals — USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: We've turned scalloped potatoes into a one-dish meal with the addition of chicken and fennel that's big in flavor but low in fat. The potatoes are first par-boiled in the microwave to reduce baking time.
instructions: Place rack in center of oven and preheat to 350 °F.
Leaving skin on, thinly slice potatoes.
Cut stalks and fronds from fennel bulb.
Discard stalk.
Thinly slice fennel bulb.
Chop fennel fronts and set aside.
Place potato and fennel slices in 2-quart covered baking dish, and add water to cover vegetables.
Cover with lid and microwave on high for about 5 minutes.
Let cool slightly and drain vegetables into a colander.
Wipe baking dish dry and spray with cooking spray.
Add vegetables back to dish and sprinkle with minced garlic.
Cut chicken breasts in half (total of four pieces).
Place atop the potato-fennel mix.
In a bowl, mix melted margarine and flour into a smooth paste.
Add 1 1/4 cups skim milk, salt, and pepper, stir until smooth.
Pour over chicken, potatoes, and fennel.
Cover baking dish and place in oven.
Bake about 30 minutes.
Mix remaining milk with sour cream.
Increases oven temperature to 425 °F.
Remove dish from oven.
Spread with sour cream mixture and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and fennel fronds.
Return to oven uncovered and bake an additional 10 minutes until top is golden and bubbling.
Internal temperature of chicken should be 165 °F.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes and Chicken with Fennel
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serving with 8 ounce glass of sparkling water and 1/2 orange, sliced.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this classic potato dish along side green or orange veggies to keep your plate colorful.

ingredients.name: russet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and sliced into 1/4 inch slices

instructions: Quickest Method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Place a layer of potatoes in pan, using approximately 1/4 of potatoes.
Sprinkle layer with 1/4 cup chopped raw onion, 1/2 tablespoon margarine, 1 tablespoon flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and sprinkling of black pepper.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Meanwhile heat milk over low heat.
Pour warm milk over all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Creamiest Method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Make a white sauce by melting margarine in a small pan.
Stir in flour.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Cook, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat.
Add salt and pepper.
Place a layer of potatoes and onion in a prepared casserole pan, using approximately 1/4 of the potatoes and 1/4 cup onion.
Spread with 1/2 cup of the sauce prepared in steps 2 and 3.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes II
recipes.notes: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This zucchini recipe brings you a flavorful dish loaded with vegetables and low-fat dairy.

ingredients.name: garlic and herb seasoning mix
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon garlic and herb seasoning mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and chop zucchini, measure out about 2 cups.
Dice the onion and pepper, set aside along with the zucchini.
Stir the egg and milk together and set aside.
Sauté the vegetables in oil on medium heat.
Remove from the pan.
Scramble the egg mixture until cooked thoroughly.
Stir in the vegetable mixture and fold together.
Cook together until temperature reaches 145 °F.
Sprinkle the seasoning and cheese on top.
When the cheese is melted, serve warm.
Add fresh or other dried herbs as desired.
recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs and Zucchini
recipes.recipe_by: Original recipe name - Zucchini Recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Scrambled tofu is a powerful protein packed dish for any meal of the day. Add your favorite veggies for increased flavor and crunch.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tofu.
In small bowl, dice or mash tofu.
For optional ingredients, crush garlic and/or slice watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, and green onions.
In a pan, melt butter.
Add tofu.
Add bean sprouts and optional ingredients.
Saute over medium heat until lightly browned.
Beat eggs and add to tofu mixture.
Cook until firm.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir and cook until firm.
recipes.name: Scrambled Tofu
recipes.notes: Optional ingredients: garlic, watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, green onions, and chop suey mix.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and delicious way to cook greens will give you a tasty side dish in minutes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean the greens thoroughly and cut stems away.
Dry well and tear into salad pieces or slice across leaf into 1/2 inch pieces.
In a large deep pot or skillet with a cover, sauté garlic in oil over medium heat.
Add greens in pan with 1 cup water.
Cover pan and steam for 4 minutes.
Uncover, stir constantly until greens shrink.
Add salt and pepper and continue to stir on high until mixture is thoroughly wet.
Sprinkle cider vinegar on mixture.
Cover.
Turn off heat.
Let stand until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Seared Greens
recipes.notes: You can also try this recipe using turnip greens, mustard greens, spinach, swiss chard, or beet greens.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Team Nutrition

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Italian salad dressing brings flavor to this veggie dish that cooks in just half and hour in the oven. Pairs well with fish, chicken, or tofu.

ingredients.name: medium yellow squashes
ingredients.raw: 2 medium yellow squashes, washed and sliced

ingredients.name: medium bell pepper (green or red)
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium bell pepper (green or red), washed, seeded, and sliced

ingredients.name: fat free Italian salad dressing
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup fat free Italian salad dressing

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Stir vegetables and dressing in large bowl.
Spread vegetables in the center sheet of aluminum foil on top of baking sheet.
Bring together and seal to make packet.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Seasoned Roasted Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — SNAP-Ed Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and easy recipe uses carrots and turnips for a warm, fall flavor. Garlic and honey (or brown sugar) work together to create a sweet and savory blend.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet on medium-high heat, add oil and sauté turnips, carrots, and salt until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in garlic and sesame seeds and cook until vegetables begin to brown.
Stir in honey.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Sesame Turnips and Carrots
recipes.notes: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick and easy dessert that kids will love making. Experiment with different flavors of pudding and fruit combinations.

ingredients.name: carton (3.4 ounces) instant vanilla pudding mix
ingredients.raw: 1 carton (3.4 ounces) instant vanilla pudding mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place 2 cups of milk in a quart jar with tight-fitting lid.
Add one small package of instant vanilla pudding mix to the jar; screw lid on jar.
Shake until mixture is smooth.
Place pieces of fruit in a serving bowl or paper cups.
Pour pudding over fruit and chill.
recipes.name: Shake-A-Pudding
recipes.recipe_by: UMass Extension Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This shepherd's pie recipe is a twist on the classic comfort food. Using frozen veggies helps you get it on the dinner table quickly.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place diced potatoes in saucepan.
Cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer (about 15 minutes).
Drain potatoes and mash.
Stir in milk and set aside.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Brown turkey in a large skillet.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add vegetables and broth.
Bring to a slow boil.
Spoon vegetable-meat mixture into an 8-inch square baking dish.
Spread potatoes over mixture.
Bake 25 minutes.
Serve hot.
Garnish with shredded cheese (optional).
recipes.name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.recipe_by: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A tasty pumpkin dessert that will delight your dinner companions. Be cautious when making the syrup as it will be extremely hot.

ingredients.name: winter squash
ingredients.note: 1 1/4 pounds of butternut, acorn, or pumpkin

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the sugar and water until it forms a thick syrup in a medium saucepan.
Wash the pumpkin, peel it, remove the seeds, cut into pieces, and cook in the syrup until it is very thick and almost all absorbed.
Arrange the pumpkin on a plate and decorate with walnuts and cinnamon (optional).
recipes.name: Shirini
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty and delightful stew to warm your family's table. Enjoy this cozy stew with a grapefruit or orange for dessert.

ingredients.name: lamb bones (or lean beef ribs)
ingredients.raw: 3 pounds lamb bones (or lean beef ribs)

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound carrots, peeled and cut into chunks

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a 6-quart saucepan, simmer bones in 2 quarts of water and 2 teaspoons of salt (optional) for one hour.
Add onions, carrots, cabbage, string beans, and garlic.
Simmer for one hour until vegetables are thoroughly cooked.
Remove lamb bones and purée the mixture.
Add 4 tablespoons peanut butter thinned with lemon juice.
Add cooked rice (optional).
Add salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.name: Shorba (Lamb and Peanut Soup)
recipes.notes: Shorba is a Sudanese dish based around lamb. In Sudan, lamb bones commonly are used to flavor the soup-like dish.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: No need to precook the noodles in this easy lasagna. Add a layer of extra veggies if you desire. Spinach would make a fantastic addition.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spready 1/2 the sauce on the bottom of a 2-quart baking dish or pan.
Layer half the dry noodles, ricotta, and Parmesan.
Top with 1 cup sauce and layer rest of the noodles, ricotta, and mozzarella.
Top with remaining spaghetti sauce.
Bake 60 minutes at 350 °F.
Remove and let is set for 20 minutes.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Short Cut Lasagna
recipes.notes: Add browned, drained meat or cooked vegetables if desired. Mix with middle layer of sauce. Spinach would make a fantastic addition.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grapes are a natural balance to this sweet and savory shrimp salad. Enjoy as a sandwich or over lettuce.

ingredients.name: leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce
ingredients.raw: 4 leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce

instructions: Chop shrimp coarsely.
Mix together shrimp salad ingredients (everything except for the bread, tomato slices, and lettuce).
Divide salad evenly among 4 slices of bread; spread to edges of bread.
Top with tomato slices, lettuce, and second bread slice.
recipes.name: Shrimp Confetti Salad Sandwich with Grapes
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Savory simmered beans are simple and satisfying. Enjoy as a side to your favorite entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place beans, water, onion, and bay leaf in a large pot.
Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until beans are tender.
Remove bay leaf and stir in salt.
Cook 15 minutes longer.
Top each serving of simmered beans with 1/2 cup fresh salsa, or store beans in refrigerator for up to 3 days in a covered plastic or glass container.
recipes.name: Simmered Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Seasoned chunks of cod topped with fresh diced tomatoes, shredded cabbage, a squeeze of lime, and a dollop of cilantro-infused sour cream are all served on top of a warm corn tortilla. These fish tacos are the perfect combination of simplicity and excitement.

ingredients.name: cod or white fish fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound cod or white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: red and green cabbage
ingredients.raw: 2 cups red and green cabbage, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine sour cream, mayonnaise, cilantro, and 2 tablespoons seasoning mix.
In a medium bowl, combine cod, oil, lemon juice, and remaining seasoning mix; pour into large skillet.
Cook stirring constantly, over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until cod flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Fill warm tortillas with fish mixture.
Top with cabbage, tomato, sour cream mixture, lime wedges, and taco sauce.
recipes.name: Simple Fish Tacos
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add kale or spinach to this fruit smoothie for a quick and delicious breakfast or snack.

ingredients.name: low-fat milk (or fortified soy
ingredients.note: or fortified soy, coconut, or almond milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup low-fat milk (or fortified soy, coconut, or almond milk)

ingredients.name: frozen fruit
ingredients.note: all one fruit or a combination of mixed frozen fruit

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the kale or spinach and the liquid of your choice to a blender.
Blend.
Add in the rest of the ingredients, blending after each item.
Serve and enjoy, cold.
Reserve the leftover smoothie in the refrigerator for later in the day or the next day.
recipes.name: Simple Green Smoothie
recipes.notes: Consume within 24 hours.
recipes.recipe_by: Northern Valley Catholic Social Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Even the youngest junior chefs love massaging the kale in this simple salad recipe, which adds canned tuna, tomatoes, and homemade dressing for a refreshing dish.
instructions: Wash kale.
Set aside to drain water off.
Cut tomatoes in half and lightly toss in bowl with balsamic vinegar, oil, and pinch of salt and pepper.
Set aside.
In a salad bowl, mix tuna and juice from the can gently with the squeeze of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of pepper.
Massage kale for about 3 minutes to soften it.
Add the kale and 1/2 the tomatoes to the tuna.
Gently toss until all is coated with dressing.
Add remaining tomatoes.
Squeeze remaining lemon all over and serve.
recipes.name: Simply Satisfying Kale and Tuna Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Seafood Nutrition Partnership

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Catfish fillets are coated in a spicy cornmeal rub and pan-fried until browned to perfection. Try substituting with cod or tilapia for delicious variety.
instructions: Make the spice rub.
Put the cornmeal, oregano, cayenne pepper, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper on a plate and combine well.
Dredge both sides of the catfish in the spice mixture.
Put the skillet on the stove and turn the heat to high.
When the skillet is hot, add the oil.
Add the fish and cook about 4 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked throughout.
Serve right away garnished with lemon or lime wedges.
recipes.name: Skillet Catfish
recipes.notes: Use cod or tilapia instead of catfish.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: An easy lasagna; you don't even have to turn on your oven! Enjoy with a side salad and seasonal fruit.

ingredients.name: lasagna noodles
ingredients.note: or 4 cups of any other type of pasta, uncooked

ingredients.name: container of ricotta cheese
ingredients.raw: 1 container of ricotta cheese, part-skim, 15 ounces

ingredients.name: frozen spinach
ingredients.raw: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed & squeezed dry

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook the noodles as directed on the package.
Drain and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the ricotta cheese (or cottage cheese), 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, and Italian seasoning.
Spray a large skillet well with cooking spray.
Do NOT place skillet on heat until all ingredients are in skillet.
Spread half of the jar of sauce in skillet.
Top with half the cooked noodles (4 lasagna noodles).
Spread half of the cheese mixture over the noodles.
Top with half the spinach or broccoli.
Sprinkle half the mozzarella cheese over the vegetables.
Repeat with the remaining noodles, the remaining cheese mixture, the remaining vegetables, the remaining sauce, and the remaining mozzarella cheese.
Sprinkle with the rest of the Parmesan cheese.
Cover.
Turn on the stove top to medium-low until the cheese is melted (approximately 20 minutes).
Allow to stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Eat within 3 to 5 days.
recipes.name: Skillet Lasagna
recipes.notes: Thaw spinach in the refrigerator overnight or in the microwave on low power. Once thawed, wrap the spinach in a clean towel, and twist to wring out the water.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty and tasty one-pot dish that can be made in under half an hour. Use leftover brown rice for this recipe.

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.note: 10 ounce, frozen, can also use mustard greens, collard greens or spinach

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Steam greens in the stewed tomatoes using a small pan, pot, or electric skillet on medium-high heat.
Cook greens 10 to 20 minutes, until they are as soft as you like them.
Stir gently.
Add the rice, canned beans, and seasonings.
Cook until heated through.
recipes.name: Skillet Meals
recipes.notes: Learn morre about:
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick and easy weeknight entrée. If you want to give this dish an extra kick, spice with your favorite hot sauce or red pepper flakes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a large skillet.
Drain and rinse to remove fat.
Add onion, tomato sauce, water, and spices.
Cover and bring to a boil.
Add noodles.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Defrost spinach in the microwave.
Stir spinach into skillet mixture.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir mixture.
Spoon cottage cheese on top and sprinkle with shredded mozzarella.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add water if mixture gets too dry.
recipes.name: Skillet Noodles and Beef
recipes.recipe_by: University of New Hampshire Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick and delicious one-pot meal that is sure to please the whole family. Add your favorite frozen or fresh veggies to this dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown the ground meat, onion, and garlic in a large skillet or heavy saucepan.
Drain off any grease.
Add the tomato sauce, water, and uncooked pasta.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fresh or frozen vegetables.
Stir and continue cooking until the pasta and vegetables are tender, about 10 more minutes.
recipes.name: Skillet Pasta Dinner
recipes.notes: Frozen vegetables used for nutritional analysis and costing purposes.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: You only need a few simple ingredients to create this delicious, tender chicken. This recipe will yield the perfect chicken every time. Pair with your favorite vegetable to make a meal.

ingredients.name: medium chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 1 medium chicken breast, about 1-inch thick, skinless

ingredients.name: seasoning
ingredients.raw: seasoning, such as salt, pepper, seasoning salt, onion powder or garlic powder

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season the chicken.
In a lightly oiled medium skillet over medium-high heat, sauté the chicken for one minute on each side until lightly browned.
Cover the skillet with a tight-fitting lid.
Reduce the heat to low.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Do not lift the lid.
Turn off the heat.
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes.
Do not remove the lid.
The chicken is safely cooked when the internal temperature is at least 165 degrees F.
Check in the thickest part with a food thermometer.
If not done, cover and return to low heat for 3 to 5 minutes and check for doneness.
recipes.name: Skillet-Braised Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Next time they ask for pizza, you can feel good about saying "yes!" Flour tortillas make for a crispy crust, perfect for loading with low-sodium tomato sauce, low-fat cheese, and lots of fresh veggies.

ingredients.name: tomato sauce
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup tomato sauce, no salt added

instructions: Heat oven to 400°F.
Place tortillas on 2 large baking sheets.
Cook, flipping once, until crisp (about 10 minutes).
Set aside.
Meanwhile, heat oil in large skillet over medium heat.
Add mushrooms, peppers, onions, and garlic.
Cook until all vegetables are soft and tender (about 10 minutes).
Set aside.
Spread tortilla crust with 2 tablespoons tomato sauce, 1/4 cup vegetable mixture, 2 tablespoons mozzarella cheese, and 1/2 teaspoon of Parmesan cheese.
Repeat with remaining crusts and topping ingredients.
Transfer pizzas to same baking sheets.
Cook until cheese is melted and edges of tortillas are golden brown (about 10 minutes).
recipes.name: Skinny Pizza
recipes.recipe_by: The Best of La Cocina GOYA: Healthy, Tasty, Affordable Latin Cooking/ Lo Mejor de la Cocina GOYA: Cocina Latina Saludable, Rica y Económica — GOYA Foods

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of fresh veggie flavor, these sloppy garden joes will be a fast favorite in your home. Serve on a whole wheat bun with a side salad for a complete meal.

ingredients.name: whole wheat buns
ingredients.raw: 6 whole wheat buns, split in half to make 12

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onions, carrots, green pepper, and ground turkey or chicken in a large pan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, crushed tomatoes, mushrooms, barbecue sauce, and bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook for an additional 3 minutes or until thick.
Serve open-faced on toasted or plain whole-wheat buns.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Sloppy Garden Joes
recipes.notes: You can also use 8 ounce of fresh mushrooms instead of canned.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These tangy beans cook in a slow-cooker. Serve this dish at your next potluck dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, water, onion, and chili powder in slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours or until tender.
Drain.
Stir in barbecue sauce, ketchup, mustard, and pepper sauce.
Cook on high for 15 minutes or until hot through.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare this in the morning and let it cook all day, so that you can enjoy a healthy and hearty dinner as soon as you walk in the door.

ingredients.name: stew meat
ingredients.raw: 2 pounds stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: add herbs as desired (bay leaf
ingredients.raw: add herbs as desired (bay leaf, basil, oregano, etc.)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place meat in slow cooker.
Mix flour, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl, and pour over meat; stir to coat.
Add remaining ingredients and stir to mix.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 to 6 hours.
Stir stew thoroughly before serving.
If using bay leaf, discard before serving.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This crock-pot recipe can be cooked for 8-10 hours on the low setting, or for 4-5 hours on the high setting.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the beef roast into 4 pieces.
In a small bowl, mix the flour and salt.
Dip each piece of meat into the mix of flour and salt.
Coat it on all sides with the mix.
Put the meat in the crock pot.
Add the chopped carrots and onion.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and tomato sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, OR on high for 4-5 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle the cheese on top.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Cheesy Swiss Steak
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from: Cheesy Swiss Steak Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this hearty stew on a chilly autumn or winter evening. Add black pepper for an extra kick.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a medium fry pan.
Drain fat.
Place beef, chopped vegetables, tomatoes, and water in slow cooker.
Cook on low 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 6 hours.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Hamburger Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Quick to make but rich and delicious flavors of carrots, onion, and celery flavor in this slow cooker lentil soup. Add your favorite spices if you want to add a little kick.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in slow cooker.
Cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 to 5 hours.
Serve hot with crackers or bread.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Lentil Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Apple juice and dried fruit add a touch of sweetness to this stew. This dish can be put together in minutes and then left to simmer in your slow cooker. Served over brown rice, it’s a great comfort food to have waiting at the end of a long day. The crushed cereal acts as a thickener and adds a nutty flavor to the stew. Try substituting dried apricots or cranberries for the cherries as desired.

ingredients.name: complete bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups complete bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal

ingredients.name: 100% apple juice or apple cider
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup 100% apple juice or apple cider

instructions: Trim fat from pork.
Spray large pan with non-stick cooking spray.
Cook half of the pork at a time until browned.
In a 4 to 6 quart crockery cooker, layer carrots, onion, thyme, pepper, salt, and garlic.
Sprinkle with cereal and cherries.
Top with pork and pour apple juice or cider over contents in the cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours or on high for 3 1/2 to 4 hours.

Prepare the brown rice according to package directions toward the end of the stew cooking time. (Brown rice typically takes about 40 to 45 minutes to cook.) Stir pork mixture and serve over 1/2 cup brown rice.
recipes.name: Slow Cooker Pork Stew over Brown Rice
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vinegar, brown sugar, and garlic come together to give this slow cook beef barbecue a sweet and tangy flavor. Serve with a side salad.

ingredients.name: boneless chuck steak
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chuck steak, boneless, 1 1/2-inches thick

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the beef on a diagonal, across the grain into slices 1 inch wide and place in a slow cooker.
Combine the remaining ingredients and pour over the meat.
Mix the meat and sauce together.
Cover and cook on low for 3 to 5 hours.
Serve on toasted hamburger buns with a mixed green salad.
recipes.name: Slow-Cook Barbecue
recipes.recipe_by: Putting Your Crock Pot to Work — University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this traditional Southern dish as a soup or serve the beans and meat over a whole grain like brown rice for a more hearty meal.
instructions: Peel, rinse, and chop onion.
Peel and mince garlic.
In a large pot over high heat, add ham hocks and water.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to a simmer.
Add onion and garlic.
Cover and cook until meat is tender and internal temperature registers 145°F on a food thermometer, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Transfer ham hocks to a clean cutting board.
Let cool.
Add lima beans to pot.
Cook according to package directions.
When ham hocks are cool, shred meat from the bone, removing any fat.
Return to pot.
Stir in pepper.
If using salt, stir in now.
recipes.name: Smoked Ham Hocks with Lima Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: It doesn’t get much easier -- or more delicious -- than this ultra-fast salmon. The sweetness of the maple balances the tangy mustard; smoked paprika or ground chipotle adds another layer of flavor. When you buy your salmon, ask at the fish counter to have the salmon cut into four 4-ounce fillets with the skin removed.

ingredients.name: smoked paprika or ground chipotle pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika or ground chipotle pepper

instructions: Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Line a baking sheet with foil and coat with cooking spray.
Combine mustard, maple syrup, paprika (or chipotle), pepper, and salt in a small bowl.
Place salmon fillets on the prepared baking sheet.
Spread the mustard mixture evenly on the salmon.
Roast until just cooked through (approximately 8 to 12 minutes).
recipes.name: Smoky Mustard-Maple Salmon
recipes.recipe_by: EatingWell Magazine

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These greens are delicious. They're especially wonderful in the cooler months when greens are easily found in your garden or market.

ingredients.name: mustard greens
ingredients.raw: 14 cups mustard greens, or turnip, collard, kale, or mixture

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare greens by washing thoroughly and removing stems.
Tear or slice leaves into bite-sized pieces.
To make the turkey stock, place all ingredients except greens into large saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add greens to turkey stock.
Cook 20 to 30 minutes until tender.
recipes.name: Smothered Greens
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this coleslaw in a snap. This tasty coleslaw can be doubled easily and made a day in advance to let the flavors blend.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and shred the cabbage with a knife or grater.
Put in a mixing bowl.
Bring the vinegar and water to a boil in the saucepan.
Remove from heat and add the sugar, mustard, and black pepper to the saucepan.
Continue to cook this mixture in the saucepan until the sugar is dissolved and hot, then pour over the shredded cabbage.
Toss.
Refrigerate until chilled to blend flavors.
recipes.name: Snappy Cole Slaw
recipes.notes: Refrigeration is needed before serving.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Right Is Basic — Michigan State University Cooperative Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe can be made in a microwave. Perfect for busy weekdays, this vegetable side dish is full of fiber.

ingredients.name: vegetables
ingredients.note: frozen or fresh, cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.raw: 1 cup vegetables, frozen or fresh, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: dill weed
ingredients.note: fresh snipped or dry, to taste

instructions: * Microwave version: Follow the same steps above.
Use a microwave-safe, covered dish.
Stir the vegetables every 2 to 3 minutes.
Just before they are cooked, add the rice, beans, and herbs.
Cook until heated.
Rotate the dish and stir gently.
recipes.name: Snappy Rice Dish
recipes.notes: Try this recipe with peas , corn , carrots , or whatever veggies you like!
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tacos can be served for lunch or dinner. This recipe uses fresh tomato salsa.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts
ingredients.note: thawed, skin and bone removed from each piece
ingredients.raw: 2 chicken breasts, thawed, skin and bone removed from each piece

ingredients.name: taco seasoning or chili powder
ingredients.raw: 2/3 tablespoon taco seasoning or chili powder

instructions: In a large bowl, mix chicken, vegetable oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
If using taco seasoning or chili powder, add that too.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap, and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
While the chicken is in the refrigerator, cook the pepper and onion on a stovetop over medium heat until done (about 12 minutes).
Cook the chicken over medium heat.
Cook each side about 10 to 15 minutes.
Place chicken on a plate.
Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Cut the chicken into strips.
To make the tacos, put chicken on the tortilla first.
Add peppers and onion strips next.
Top with lettuce, tomato, and salsa.
If using parsley or cilantro, add that too.
recipes.name: Soft Chicken Taco
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165°F, as measured by a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A great snack to make with kids. Perfect to dip in mustard for a savory pretzel, or a low-fat vanilla yogurt for a sweet treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Lightly grease 2 baking sheets.
In large bowl, sprinkle yeast over warm water (if water is too hot, it will kill the yeast).
Stir until well blended.
Combine white and wheat flour in a separate bowl.
Stir in sugar, salt and 2 1/2 to 3 cups flour to make a soft, sticky dough.
Turn dough onto well-floured surface.
To knead, fold dough in half and push dough flat with heels of hands.
Turn dough 1/4 turn.
Repeat for 5 to 7 minutes.
If needed, add more flour until dough is smooth and elastic.
Dough should not stick to hands or counter.
Cut dough into 12 even pieces (about golf-ball sized).
To Form Pretzels: Roll one piece of dough into 15 inch long rope.
Cross left side over middle, creating loop.
Fold right side of rope up and over first loop to form pretzel shape.
To Bake: Place pretzels 3 inches apart on baking sheet.
Enlarge holes in pretzels by inserting finger into holes.
This will prevent them from closing during baking.
In small bowl, mix egg and 1 tablespoon water together.
Brush on pretzels.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Best if eaten warm.
recipes.name: Soft Pretzels
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A delicious summer salad to serve when summer vegetables are at their peak. Great with grilled meat, fish, and tofu.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine oil and lemon juice.
Dice all the fruits and vegetables and then add to the bowl.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Serve chilled.
Best served within 24 hours.
recipes.name: Somali Summer Salad
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this sweet cornbread with your favorite savory entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Lightly spray and 8 inch square pan with vegetable oil cooking spray.
Mix dry ingredients in an medium-sized mixing bowl.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well by hand.
Pour the batter into the sprayed pan and shake to make it level.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 25 minutes.
Allow to cool, then cut into 12 squares.
recipes.name: Soul-Healthy Cornbread
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick dip can be prepared in under 1 minute, making it perfect for last-minute gatherings.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the sour cream, yogurt, and salsa.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the fridge until you serve it.
recipes.name: South of the Border Dip
recipes.notes: Serve with baked tortilla chips, crackers, or bite-sized vegetables.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this corn, black bean, and tomato salad in the morning and let it marinate in the refrigerator all day and enjoy it for dinner.

ingredients.name: diced tomatoes with green chilies
ingredients.raw: 1 can diced tomatoes with green chilies

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the salad ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over corn mixture and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
recipes.name: South of the Border Salad
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet and delicious, this dessert will soon become a family favorite.

ingredients.name: (3.4 ounces each) boxes instant vanilla pudding and pie-filling mix
ingredients.raw: 2 (3.4 ounces each) boxes instant vanilla pudding and pie-filling mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix 3 1/2 cups of the milk with the pudding mixes.
Beat the pudding mixture with a wire whisk for 2 minutes until it is well blended.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Fold 1 cup of the whipped topping into the pudding mix.
Arrange a layer of wafers on the bottom and sides of a 2-quart serving bowl.
Drizzle 2 tablespoons of the remaining milk over the wafers.
Add a layer of banana slices and top with one-third of the pudding.
Repeat layers, drizzling each wafer layer with remaining milk and ending with pudding.
Spread the remaining whipped topping over the pudding.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Southern Banana Pudding
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Delicious stuffed peppers that will soon become a staple in your home.

ingredients.name: medium green bell pepper
ingredients.note: or use red or yellow peppers
ingredients.raw: 5 medium green bell pepper, halved and seeded

ingredients.name: (10.5 ounces) tomatoes with chilies
ingredients.raw: 1 can (10.5 ounces) tomatoes with chilies, diced and undrained

ingredients.name: (15.2 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn
ingredients.raw: 1/2 can (15.2 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Blanch peppers in boiling water 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain.
Set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in oil in medium skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Combine rice, tomatoes with chilies, corn, and onion mixture.
Mix well.
Spoon into pepper halves, place on baking sheet coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350 degrees F for 10 minutes or until hot.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake again at 350 degrees F for 5 to 10 minutes or until hot and cheese melts.
recipes.name: Southwestern Pepper Cups
recipes.recipe_by: Don’t Play With Your Food: Spring and Summer Cookbook — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A delicious and simple chicken dish. Enjoy with a fresh salad and brown rice, or a whole grain roll.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice the orange to make round slices and set aside.
Place 4 chicken breasts in a 1-gallon sized plastic zipper bag.
Add the liquid to the bag with the chicken.
Zipper the bag closed and gently massage to mix the liquids and evenly cover the chicken inside the bag.
Let the chicken marinate in the bag in the refrigerator for 4 or more hours.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Spray shallow oven-proof baking dish with non-stick spray large enough to place chicken in single layer in the baking dish.
Remove the chicken from the bag, place in a single layer in the baking dish.
Throw away the zipper bag from the chicken.
Bake chicken uncovered for 20 minutes.
Turn the chicken over, cover with orange slices that were set aside, and bake 15 more minutes (total of 35 minutes).
Check with a food thermometer.
Temperature should reach 165 °F.
Serve chicken topped with an orange slice from the baking dish if desired.
recipes.name: Soy Marinated Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This pesto spaghetti dish is made with spinach for a unique spin on a classic. Top with feta and serve with a side salad for a colorful meal.

ingredients.name: 10-ounce frozen spinach
ingredients.raw: 1 package 10-ounce frozen spinach, thawed, well drained

instructions: In a blender (or food processor), combine spinach, oil, Parmesan cheese, parsley, garlic, salt, and basil.
Mix at medium speed until finely chopped.
Melt margarine in water.
With blender or processor running, gradually pour in melted margarine mixture until blended.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Toss pesto with cooked pasta.
Sprinkle feta on top and serve.
recipes.name: Spaghetti and Spinach Pesto
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestion: Serve with grilled chicken, side salad, skim milk, and apple slices.
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Here is a delicious late summer side dish bursting with fresh flavors. This dish would go well with a grilled entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the 2 squash halves, cut side down, in glass baking dish.
Add about 1/4 cup water and cover with plastic wrap.
Microwave on high 12 minutes or until soft when pressed.
Let stand covered for 3 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, basil, oregano and 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese.
Stir in tomatoes and season lightly with salt and pepper to taste.
Scrape squash out with a fork, add strands to tomato mixture, and toss until combined.
Sprinkle with remaining 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Spaghetti Squash with Tomatoes, Basil, and Parmesan
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart. Be Fit. — University of Maryland Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Instead of opening a jar of sauce, try this easy spaghetti with meat sauce on a weeknight. Serve with steamed broccoli, garlic bread, and roasted pears for dessert. The recipe makes enough for 8 servings. If you’re serving only four for dinner, cook 8 ounces of spaghetti and freeze the leftover sauce.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, carrot, and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is beginning to brown, 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic and Italian seasoning; cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add beef and cook, stirring and breaking up with a spoon, until no longer pink, 3 to 5 minutes.
Increase heat to high.
Stir in tomatoes and cook until thickened, 4 to 6 minutes.
Stir in parsley and salt.
Serve the sauce over the pasta, sprinkled with cheese.
recipes.name: Spaghetti with Quick Meat Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: EatingWell Magazine

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious fish will pair well with spaghetti squash when in season, and whole wheat pasta or brown rice the rest of the year.

ingredients.name: perch fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound perch fillets, fresh or frozen

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly grease baking dish (9 x 13-inch) with butter or margarine.
Separate the fish into 4 fillets or pieces.
Put the fish pieces in the baking dish.
Peel the onion and cut it into slices.
Stir the onion, tomato sauce, and spices together in a small bowl.
Pour the onion-spice mix evenly over the fish pieces.
Bake about 10 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
recipes.name: Spanish Baked Fish
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This versatile recipe combines eggs, potatoes, and onion going from stovetop to oven for the finishing touch. Cut into wedges as part of a delicious breakfast, brunch, or any meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Put the potatoes in a non-stick skillet on the stove and cover with cold water.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook about 15 minutes until the potatoes are easily pierced with a knife.
Drain the potatoes well and set aside to cool.
Then peel and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Put the eggs, salt, and pepper in the bowl and mix well with a whisk.
Return the skillet on the stove and turn the heat to medium-high.
Add the oil.
Add onion and cook about 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cubed potatoes.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes and onions.
Press down with a spatula to make an even layer and shake gently to prevent sticking.
Lower to medium heat and cook about 7 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook until the frittata is completely set, about 5 minutes.
Gently loosen frittata from the pan.
Place a serving plate over the skillet and carefully invert the frittata onto the plate.
Slice into 4 wedges.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Spanish Frittata
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe can be enjoyed for any meal of the day. Spice it up with your favorite hot sauce.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of choice, or non-stick cooking spray

ingredients.name: black pepper and garlic salt with herbs
ingredients.raw: black pepper and garlic salt with herbs

ingredients.name: part skim mozzarella cheese
ingredients.raw: 3 ounces part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Cook potatoes in boiling water until tender.
In a nonstick pan, add oil or vegetable spray and warm at medium heat.
Add the onion and sauté until brown.
Add vegetables and sauté until tender but not brown.
In a medium mixing bowl, slightly beat the eggs and egg whites, pepper, garlic salt, and mozzarella cheese.
Stir egg cheese mixture into the cooked vegetables.
Oil or spray a 10-inch pie pan or ovenproof skillet.
Transfer potatoes and eggs mixture to pan.
Spread with parmesan cheese and bake omelet until firm and brown on top, about 20 to 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Spanish Omelet
recipes.recipe_by: Control Your Diabetes for Life: Recipes and Meal Planner Guide — US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) — National Diabetes Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this rice dish filled with vegetables and spices with your favorite chicken, fish, or bean dish.

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium chopped tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium chopped tomatoes, undrained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet cook green pepper and onion in oil until tender over medium heat.
Stir in the spices, rice, tomatoes with juice, and water.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes or until rice is done.
recipes.name: Spanish Rice
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This side dish is perfect for a fall or winter meal. Squash cooked with cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger creates a simple dish to accompany your favorite entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Coat the baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray.
Wash the squash.
Cut it in half lengthwise.
Remove the seeds.
Cut the squash into 1/2 inch slices.
Place the squash on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle with salt.
Melt the margarine on low heat in a small saucepan.
Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger to the saucepan.
Spread the margarine mix on the squash.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until tender.
recipes.name: Spiced Baked Squash
recipes.recipe_by: Spicy Baked Squash , Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This side dish is an excellent way to get your orange vegetables. Vinegar, brown sugar, and spicy mustard combine to give this dish a sweet and tangy taste.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash, peel, and cut carrots.
Wash and cut up squash.
Combine carrots and broth in a large saucepan.
Cover and cook over medium heat about 5 minutes.
Add squash and cook 5 more minutes or until vegetables are just tender.
Add more broth, if necessary, to keep from burning.
Stir vinegar, brown sugar, and mustard into vegetables.
Cook for a few minutes over medium heat until most of the liquid cooks off.
recipes.name: Spicy Carrots and Squash
recipes.notes: Try this recipe without brown sugar.
recipes.recipe_by: Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This rich-tasting and hearty potato soup is full of flavor and perfect for lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.note: thawed, cut up, and skin removed
ingredients.raw: 1/4 pound chicken, thawed, cut up, and skin removed

ingredients.name: small red potatoes
ingredients.note: or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes

ingredients.name: fresh peas
ingredients.note: or 1/2 can, about 8 ounces, low-sodium green peas

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, brown onion and garlic in oil over medium to high heat for 5 minutes.
Add chicken to pot and brown for about 5 minutes.
Add water, potatoes, rice, and chili powder to pot.
Bring pot to a boil, and cook for 15 minutes.
Lower heat and cook for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir pot every 10 minutes.
Add peas and cook for about 8 minutes.
If using cayenne or jalapeño chilies, add that too.
Mix well.
Remove pot from heat.
If using parsley or cilantro, add that now.
Mix well and cover for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Spicy Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chili powder and lime juice are the secret ingredients in this cucumber and orange salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the cucumbers, oranges and lemon or lime under cold running water.
Slice the cucumbers.
Peel and cut the oranges into small pieces.
Place cucumber slices and orange pieces in a medium size bowl.
Add chili powder, lemon or lime juice and salt.
recipes.name: Spicy Cucumber & Orange Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe Adapted from: A Simple Mexican Salad, Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A touch of cinnamon and nutmeg make the flavors of this fruit medley pop.

ingredients.name: pineapple chunks
ingredients.raw: 1 cup pineapple chunks, in its own juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the strawberries in half.
Open the can of mandarin oranges.
Drain off the syrup.
Open the can of pears.
Drain off the juice.
Slice the pears.
Open the can of pineapple, but don’t drain off the juice.
Put the undrained pineapple, orange juice, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a mixing bowl.
Stir together.
Carefully stir in the mandarin oranges, pears, and strawberries.
Refrigerate for 1 to 4 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Spicy Fruit Cup
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Okra cooked with tomatoes, onions, and hot peppers creates the perfect spicy side dish for your favorite entrée.

ingredients.name: (10 ounces each) frozen cut okra
ingredients.raw: 2 packages (10 ounces each) frozen cut okra

ingredients.name: fresh jalapeño pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 fresh jalapeño pepper, pierced 3 times with fork

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse okra in a colander under hot water.
Heat oil in a 10-inch heavy skillet over moderately high heat.
Sauté onion for about 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes (including juice) and jalapeño (or habanero) pepper, and boil.
Stir the mixture for 8 minutes.
Add okra and cook, gently stirring, until okra is tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in salt and pepper and discard the jalapeño (or habanero) pepper.
recipes.name: Spicy Okra
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chicken thighs coated in hot sauce, mustard, thyme, and garlic are oven-baked for a tender and simple chicken dish.
instructions: Put chicken thighs, hot sauce, mustard, thyme, and garlic in the bowl and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate at least one hour or up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 450°F.
Put the chicken on a baking sheet and sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake about 50 minutes until crispy and crackling.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Spicy Oven-Baked Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe is spiced up using cayenne pepper, ginger, and garlic combined with the sweetness of honey, molasses, and ketchup to create a tasty comfort food.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except chicken in saucepan.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Place chicken on large platter and brush with half the sauce mixture.
Cover with plastic wrap and marinate in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Remove plastic wrap from chicken.
Place chicken on baking sheet lined with aluminum foil and broil for 10 minutes on each side to seal in juices.
Remove from broiler and add remaining sauce to chicken.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes. * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.name: Spicy Southern Barbecued Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these spinach and meat cakes over brown rice and with a side of roasted sweet potatoes.

ingredients.name: frozen spinach
ingredients.note: may substitute with 2 bunches of fresh spinach

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat large frying pan (no oil).
Combine all ingredients except brown rice in a large mixing bowl.
Mix well.
Form mixture into 12 small balls.
Place in frying pan and flatten into patties using a spatula.
Cook over medium heat until cooked on both sides.
Serve over brown rice.
recipes.name: Spinach and Meat Cakes
recipes.recipe_by: California Health Department, Los Angeles County — Es Facil Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Banana peppers add a kick to these delicious enchiladas -- and are in season the same time as bell peppers.

ingredients.name: reduced fat Monterey jack cheese
ingredients.raw: 6 1/2 ounces reduced fat Monterey jack cheese

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a very large non-stick skillet.
Add onion, garlic, and peppers and stir.
Add mushrooms and cook about 15 to 20 minutes, until liquid evaporates. (If pan is not large enough, cook mushrooms in batches.) Pour half of the enchilada sauce into a 13x9 inch baking dish.
Arrange 8 tortilla halves over the sauce in the baking dish.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
When mushrooms are cooked, stir in the salt and crumble in the oregano leaves.
Drain the spinach, squeeze it dry, and mix it thoroughly with the mushroom mixture.
Spoon half the mushroom mixture into the baking dish, carefully covering tortillas.
Set aside 1/4 cup (about 1 ounce) of grated cheese.
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top of the mushroom mixture.
Layer with the remaining 8 tortilla halves, then the remaining mushroom mixture and enchilada sauce.
Sprinkle top of casserole with the remaining 1/4 cup cheese.
Cover baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes, or until casserole is steaming hot in the center.
recipes.name: Spinach and Mushroom Enchilada Casserole
recipes.notes: Allow casserole to stand at room temperature 5 minutes before serving. Serve with pinto or black beans and salad.
recipes.recipe_by: California’s Chefs Cook Lean — California Department of Health Services — California Project LEAN

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty salad is packed with protein and fiber. Add your favorite salad toppings to make it a fast favorite.

ingredients.name: canned low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups canned low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine vinegar, oil, mustard, garlic, oregano, basil, and nutmeg.
Wash, drain, and chop spinach.
Add spinach, black beans, tomatoes, and onions to vinegar and oil.
Toss well and serve.
recipes.name: Spinach Black Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This versatile veggie dish makes a tasty snack or appetizer. Serve with applesauce on the side.

ingredients.name: spinach leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups spinach leaves, chopped and steamed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine the first eight ingredients in a bowl.
Stir in egg and mix well.
Drop batter in 1/4 cup sizes onto a well-greased hot griddle and flatten to form patties.
Fry until golden brown; turn and cook until the second side is lightly browned.
Drain on paper towels and serve with applesauce, if desired.
recipes.name: Spinach Potato Pancakes
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maine Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this hearty, cold rice salad that could be served with fresh fruit and your favorite protein foods.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.note: washed and cut into thin strips
ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup fresh spinach, washed and cut into thin strips

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dressing, soy sauce, and sugar.
Stir into chilled rice.
Cover and chill salad.
Add spinach, celery, and onion before serving.
Shake on bacon bits if desired.
recipes.name: Spinach Rice Salad
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy a simply delicious spinach salad with hard-boiled eggs, apples, and dried figs.

ingredients.name: light honey mustard or poppy seed dressing
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup light honey mustard or poppy seed dressing

instructions: To hard boil eggs: Place eggs in saucepan large enough to hold them in a single layer.
Add cold water to cover eggs by 1 inch.
Heat over high heat just to boiling.
Remove from heat and cover.
Let eggs stand in hot water about 12 minutes.
Drain and fill pan with cold water; let sit 10 to 15 minutes.
Peel and slice. (If making ahead, refrigerate cooked unpeeled eggs.) Prepare other ingredients while eggs are cooking and cooling.
Wash, slice, and core apples.
Cut apples and dried figs into bite-sized chunks.
Wash and drain spinach.
To plate, divide ingredients evenly among four plates, top spinach with apples, eggs, dried figs, and croutons.
Drizzle with dressing.
recipes.name: Spinach Salad with Apples and Eggs
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% grape juice together with vanilla or lemon low-fat yogurt.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this tasty, sweet fall salad with a savory and seasonal entrée. Use Granny Smith or your favorite kind of apples. Try leaving out the sugar for a more tart flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine spinach, apples, and raisins.
Mix all dressing ingredients and pour over salad just prior to serving.
recipes.name: Spinach Salad with Apples and Raisins
recipes.notes: Granny Smith apples are recommended for salad, but any apple on hand will work. Try decreasing or cutting out the sugar if you like your salad less sweet.
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart. Be Fit. — University of Maryland Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These tasty, twice-baked potatoes are stuffed with veggies, cheese, tofu, and sour cream for a delicious and filling dish.

ingredients.name: (10 ounces) frozen spinach
ingredients.raw: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen spinach, thawed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw the spinach before you cook this recipe!
After it thaws, drain any extra water from the spinach.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and scrub the potatoes.
Bake the potatoes in for 1 hour till they’re tender and you can pierce them with a fork.
Wash and chop the green onion until you get 1/4 cup onion.
Put the sour cream, tofu, spinach, onion, pepper, and cheese in a mixing bowl.
Mix well.
When the potatoes are baked, let them cool.
Then use a spoon to scoop out the inside of the potato.
Add the inside of the potato to the sour cream mix.
Stir together.
Stuff the potato skin shells with the mixture.
Sprinkle the potatoes with the seasoning.
Bake the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes until they’re a little brown.
Add extra cheese on top if desired.
recipes.name: Spinach Stuffed Potatoes
recipes.notes: You can use part-skim mozzarella cheese in place of low-fat cheddar cheese.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Canned veggies make this dish easy to prepare at any time of the year! No fresh veggies necessary.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in a large saucepan.
Cover.
Heat thoroughly over medium-high heat, about 10 minutes.
Add seasonings to taste.
recipes.name: Spinach, Tomatoes, and Corn
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Recipes for Less Familiar USDA Commodities Used by Household Programs — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty soup of split peas, flavored with onion, carrots, celery, and thyme. This one-pot meal is sure to feed a hungry family.

ingredients.name: split peas
ingredients.raw: 2 1/4 cups split peas, sorted and rinsed

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.raw: 4 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

instructions: Put soup pot on the stove over medium heat.
Add oil when the pot is hot.
Add onion, carrots, celery, and thyme and cook 10 to 15 minutes, until tender.
Add split peas, stock, and 4 cups water.
Raise the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat to low and cook about 2 hours, partially covered, until the peas have fallen apart.
Check the soup during cooking - if more water is needed, add up to 2 cups.
Skim off any foam that forms.
Serve right away or refrigerate up to three days.
Stir in the lemon juice just before serving.
recipes.name: Split Pea Soup
recipes.notes: If you serve this soup on the following day, you may need to add more water, as it will thicken overnight.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Simmering this soup for hours keeps your kitchen warm on a cold winter day. Add ham for an even heartier soup. Enjoy this soup with a fresh salad and warm whole grain bread.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook chopped onions in margarine in a large pan until tender over medium heat.
Wash and drain split peas.
Add water, split peas, and salt to onion.
Bring to boiling.
Lower heat and cover pan.
Simmer about 2 hours, until thickened.
recipes.name: Split Pea Soup
recipes.notes: Optional: Cook a ham bone or pieces of ham in the soup. Remove bone and serve meat in soup.
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
