recipes.description: Bursting with delicious spring flavors, this delicious sauté is perfect with a side of roasted chicken, fish, or tofu.

ingredients.name: sugar snap peas
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup sugar snap peas, or green beans

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and cook another minute Stir in the potatoes and carrots.
Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook until almost tender, about 4 minutes.
If the vegetables start to brown, add a tablespoon or two of water.
Now add the asparagus, peas, radishes, salt, pepper, and dill.
Cook, stirring often, until just tender -- about 4 minutes more.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Spring Vegetable Sauté
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — National Cancer Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this tasty soup with your favorite whole grain bread sandwich. The recipe doubles easily if you need to accommodate a large family or group.

ingredients.name: head of red cabbage
ingredients.raw: 1/4 head of red cabbage, finely shredded

ingredients.name: medium ripe tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 medium ripe tomatoes, seeded and chopped

ingredients.name: canned artichoke hearts
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup canned artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

ingredients.name: green peas
ingredients.raw: 1 cup green peas, frozen or fresh

ingredients.name: salt and pepper
ingredients.note: freshly ground black pepper, optional, to taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large soup pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Sauté cabbage, tomatoes, artichoke hearts, and peas for 10 minutes.
Add vegetable juice and water.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat, add basil, and simmer for 10 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and soup is piping hot.
Serve in individual serving bowls.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
recipes.name: Spring Vegetable Soup
recipes.recipe_by: American Institute for Cancer Research

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious cereal combines sunflower seeds, almonds, fruits and yogurt for a hearty breakfast. Try with fresh strawberries from your garden or the market when in season.

ingredients.name: wheat and barley nugget cereal
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup wheat and barley nugget cereal

ingredients.name: (2 teaspoons) almonds
ingredients.raw: 2/3 tablespoon (2 teaspoons) almonds, sliced and toasted

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the wheat and barley nugget cereal, bran cereal, sunflower seeds, and almonds in a medium bowl.
Add the raisins, the bananas, and half of the strawberries.
Gently stir in the yogurt and divide between two bowls.
Scatter the remaining strawberries over the top and enjoy!
recipes.name: Springtime Cereal
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Summer squash is the secret ingredient in this fun summer salsa. Enjoy with your favorite whole grains.

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, rinsed

ingredients.name: medium green pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium green pepper, seeded and diced

ingredients.name: medium summer squash
ingredients.raw: 1 medium summer squash, peeled, seeds removed, diced

ingredients.name: Adobo seasoning
ingredients.note: combination or garlic, coriander, salt, and cumin

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except cheese in a large bowl.
Let sit for 30 minutes.
Spoon over tortilla chips, cooked rice, or noodles.
Top with grated, part-skim mozzarella cheese and cilantro (optional).
Serve hot or cold!
recipes.name: Squash Salsa
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this delicious soup with acorn squash, pumpkin, butternut squash, crookneck, or a unique variety of winter squash that you grow in your garden or can find at a local farmers market.

ingredients.name: no salt added canned tomato sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 cup no salt added canned tomato sauce

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
ingredients.raw: 5 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat.
Stir in onions, carrots, and garlic.
Cook for about 5 minutes, covered.
Stir in the tomato sauce, chicken broth, cooked squash, and herbs.
Bring soup to a simmer and cook, covered, for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Squash Soup
recipes.recipe_by: From the Farm to the Table — University of Connecticut Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a delicious and filling side dish that goes well with your favorite sandwich or salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop the cauliflower into 2-inch pieces.
Peel the onion and chop it into small pieces.
Chop the tomatoes into small pieces.
Put the cauliflower in a medium saucepan and add 1 inch of water.
Cook over medium heat, and let it boil for 3 minutes.
Drain cauliflower.
In a large pan, heat the oil, and add the onion.
Cook over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cauliflower.
Cook while stirring for 3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the tomatoes and pepper.
Cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve with a sprinkle of parsley and cheese.
recipes.name: Stewed Cauliflower, Tomatoes, and Onions
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Spanish Cauliflower — Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this quick and tasty meal on a cold winter night. Add spinach, steamed in the microwave as well as an apple or orange to serve on the side.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Trim fat from steak and cut steak into small, thin pieces.
In a large skillet, heat oil and sauté garlic until garlic is golden.
Add steak, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 6 minutes, stirring beef until brown.
Add onion and tomato.
Cook until onion is transparent.
Serve with boiled potatoes.
recipes.name: Stir Fried Beef
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Looking to add more vegetables into a family-friendly meal? This recipe does the job. With a rainbow of colorful vegetables that are cooked until tender but not mushy, this stir-fry presents bright, crisp flavors that are wholesome and tasty. Use tofu or other meat substitutes for an appetizing vegetarian dish.

ingredients.name: medium red or yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium red or yellow bell pepper

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix spices, soy sauce, and water; set aside.
Wash vegetables.
Shred carrots and slice mushrooms.
Chop broccoli, peppers, and onions.
Heat oil in large frying pan and add meat when oil is hot; stir until brown.
Push meat to the side and in the middle of the pan add carrots, onions, and peppers.
Cook them for one minute.
Add mushrooms and broccoli.
Cook until they are tender.
Add liquid mixture and cook until bubbly.
Reduce heat, cover pan, and cook for two more minutes.
Serve over whole wheat pasta or brown rice.
recipes.name: Stir Fry Vegetables and Beef
recipes.recipe_by: Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program — The Texas A&M University System

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe is quick to make and adaptable to your own taste! You could make it vegetarian by removing the chicken or add some extra crunch by using crunchy peanut butter.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts
ingredients.raw: 2 chicken breasts, boneless, skinless, cut into strips

ingredients.name: medium head of cabbage
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium head of cabbage, thinly sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring 4 cups water to boil in a 2 to 3 quart saucepan.
Add noodles, cover, and remove from heat (do not add flavor packets).
Wait one minute.
Drain noodles and set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine peanut butter, soy sauce and 1/2 cup water.
Heat over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat (350 degrees F in an electric skillet).
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink when cut, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add red pepper, ginger, and carrots and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and cook 3 to 4 minutes or until cabbage is crisp-tender.
Stir in green onion, cooked noodles, and peanut sauce.
Toss and serve right away.
recipes.name: Stir-Fry with Chicken and Noodles
recipes.notes: To avoid peanuts or peanut butter, try this stir-fry with sunflower seeds or sunflower seed butter.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make these delicious enchiladas without even turning on your oven. A quick and hearty meal.

ingredients.name: extra-sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups extra-sharp cheddar cheese, finely shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan.
Saute the chopped onion in the oil.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chilies, chicken broth, chicken and garlic powder.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch into about 1/4 cup of cold water until all the lumps are gone.
Add to the chile and chicken mixture.
Cook for 2 more minutes.
Tear the tortillas into strips and divide into thirds.
Add them to the pan and cook until they are hot, stirring with a spoon from time to time.
Sprinkle the cheese over the enchiladas.
Cover the pan and cook until the cheese has melted.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Stove Top Green Chile Chicken Enchiladas
recipes.recipe_by: New Mexico State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: An easy, meatless meal made with potatoes, cabbage, nuts of your choice, and cheese.

ingredients.name: medium potatoes
ingredients.raw: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in large skillet or Dutch oven.
Add onions and stir over medium heat until golden.
Add potatoes and chicken stock.
Cover tightly, reduce heat to low and simmer until potatoes are almost tender.
Add cabbage, cover and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Remove cover, sprinkle with cheese and nuts.
Let stand just until cheese is melted, about 2 minutes.
recipes.name: Stove Top Potato and Cabbage Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Stove Top Casserole — Oregon’s Healthy Harvest Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: One skillet beef and bean tamale pie that cooks on the stovetop. For an extra kick, add your favorite hot sauce to this tasty tamale pie.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drain and save liquid

ingredients.name: (15.2 ounces) whole kernel corn
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.2 ounces) whole kernel corn, not drained

instructions: Prepare Chili : Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beef in large, hot skillet until lightly browned.
Drain off fat.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in corn.
Prepare Tamale Pie : Place chili in a 10-inch skillet.
Heat thoroughly.
As chili heats, mix cornmeal and salt with water in a medium sauce pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Spread cornmeal mixture over hot chili to form a crust.
Sprinkle with chili powder.
Cover and cook over low heat, with lid slightly ajar, until topping is set, about 10 minutes.
Optional - Top with light sour cream or low-fat yogurt.
recipes.name: Stovetop Tamale Pie
recipes.notes: *Bean liquid is not included in the nutrition or cost analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toss this fruit salad together in a flash. Doubles and triples easily for a large group.

ingredients.name: fresh pineapple chunks
ingredients.raw: 1 cup fresh pineapple chunks, or canned packed in natural juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir fruit together in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and chill.
Serve as soon as possible.
recipes.name: Strawberries, Watermelon, and Pineapple Salad
recipes.notes: Refrigerate leftovers (or try freezing for a slush).
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A flavorful, enticing mix of fresh strawberries, white beans, and edamame in a light vinaigrette nested on a baby spinach and topped with crumbled feta cheese.

ingredients.name: 15-ounce can low sodium white beans
ingredients.raw: 1 15-ounce can low sodium white beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Cook edamame according to package directions, while preparing remaining ingredients.
Rinse under cool water and drain.
In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients.
In a medium bowl, toss all ingredients except spinach and vinaigrette.
Serve on individual plates by nesting strawberry, white bean and edamame mix atop spinach.
Drizzle with dressing.
recipes.name: Strawberries, White Bean, and Edamame Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and easy smoothie uses any of your favorite frozen fruits. It makes enough for 4 servings.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Defrost the frozen fruit just enough so that it will blend easily.
Pour the milk into the blender.
Add the pieces of frozen fruit to the milk in the blender.
Add the banana and yogurt.
Blend until smooth, about 30 to 45 seconds.
recipes.name: Strawberry and Banana Fruit Smoothie
recipes.notes: Strawberries, 1% milk, and low-fat vanilla yogurt used in nutrition analysis and costing.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy the flavors of layered strawberries, crispy cereal flakes, and creamy yogurt in this delicious parfait. Serve as a fruit-filled breakfast option or a better-for-you dessert!

ingredients.name: bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal

instructions: Stir banana and vanilla into yogurt and combine well.
In a 10 to 12 ounce glass, alternately layer the yogurt-banana mixture, strawberries, and cereal.
Serve immediately and enjoy.
recipes.name: Strawberry Banana Parfait
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cool off with frozen pops that are fun to make! Mix different yogurt and fruit combinations to find your favorite.

ingredients.name: ice cube tray or small paper cups
ingredients.raw: ice cube tray or small paper cups

instructions: Cut kiwi and strawberries into small pieces.
Add yogurt to chopped fruit and mix well to combine.
Divide into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups).
Place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!
recipes.name: Strawberry Kiwi Yogurt Pops
recipes.notes: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Diced strawberries, mango, and fat-free feta cheese provide the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and tangy for these quick and colorful brunch or lunch toast points.
instructions: Peel and pit mango.
Dice 3/4 of mango and 3/4 of strawberries; place in large bowl with feta cheese.
Put remaining fruit, 1/4 cup basil, vinegar, and oil in a blender and blend.
Pour blended vinaigrette over fruit-feta mix and toss gently.
Chop remaining basil leaves.
Toast bread slices and cut each slice diagonally.
Top toast points with dressed fruit-feta mix and chopped basil.
recipes.name: Strawberry Mango Feta Toast Points
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: No campfire required for these fruity graham cracker snacks!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the strawberries in water.
Slice the strawberries.
Add the yogurt and strawberries to 1/2 of graham cracker.
Top with the other 1/2 of graham cracker.
Enjoy immediately.
recipes.name: Strawberry S'Mores
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program — The University of Connecticut, SNAP4CT (photo)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Strawberries and yogurt are all you need for this healthy frozen pop! They're a great after school snack or sweet treat.

ingredients.name: ice cube tray or small paper cups
ingredients.raw: ice cube tray or small paper cups

instructions: Cut strawberries into small pieces.
Place strawberries and yogurt into blender and mix until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups) and place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!
recipes.name: Strawberry Yogurt Pops
recipes.notes: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Pair these delicious stuffed potatoes with grilled or baked meat, fish, or tofu.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prick potatoes with fork.
Bake at 425 degrees F for 60 minutes or until fork is easily inserted.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise.
Carefully scoop out potato, leaving about 1/2 inch of pulp inside shell.
Mash pulp in large bowl.
Mix remaining ingredients with the mashed potato, except Parmesan cheese.
Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Sprinkle top of each stuffed potato with Parmesan cheese.
Place on baking sheet and return to oven.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown.
recipes.name: Stuffed Baked Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from "Wonderful Stuffed Potatoes" — A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Peppers stuffed with a combination of ground beef, brown rice, veggies, and spices create a filling dish. Try using red, green, yellow, and orange bell peppers for a colorful meal. Enjoy with a side of low-fat cottage cheese and canned pineapple.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and watr.
Cut a circular hole in the tops of the bell peppers.
Remove seeds and membrane and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine remaining ingredients and stir until completely mixed.
Fill the bell peppers with meat mixture.
Place the stuffed bell peppers in large stock pot on stove, with the tops facing up.
Add 1-inch water to bottom of pot and cover.
Place heat on medium, keeping covered for 30 to 40 minutes until rice is done.
Serve.
recipes.name: Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spinach, a mixture of low-fat cheeses, and herbs combine for a delicious filling in these stuffed shells.

ingredients.name: (10 ounces) frozen chopped spinach
ingredients.raw: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen chopped spinach, thawed

ingredients.name: part skim mozzarella cheese
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded, divided

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Lightly coat a 13x9x2-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Set aside.
Drain spinach by placing in a sieve or colander over the sink, or in a bowl and pressing with a spool to remove as much liquid as possible or squeeze out liquid with clean hands.
Place spinach in medium bowl.
Add the cottage cheese, 1 cup of the mozzarella cheese, oregano, and pepper to the spinach.
Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour half of the spaghetti sauce into prepared baking dish.
Add water and stir into the mix.
Spoon about 3 tablespoons cheese mixture into each uncooked pasta shell.
Arrange in a single layer over top.
Pour remaining sauce over top.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese evenly over sauce.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 hour or until shells are tender.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Stuffed Pasta Shells
recipes.recipe_by: Spend Smart. Eat Smart, Adapted from Easy Stuffed Pasta Shells — Iowa State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Summer squash stuffed with brown rice, fresh basil, beans, cheese, and veggies make a hearty and filling dish. Try this tasty recipe when summer squash are abundant in your garden or at the market.

ingredients.name: white beans
ingredients.raw: 1 cup white beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and cut both squash in half, lengthwise.
Remove the large seeds.
Steam the squash, skin side down, in a small amount of water in a fry pan or skillet until slightly tender (but not mushy).
Scoop out a good amount of pulp (1 cup), place in a bowl and mix with other ingredients (brown rice through Parmesan cheese).
Place the squash shells in a baking dish.
Stuff the squash with the stuffing mixture.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for about 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Stuffed Summer Squash
recipes.notes: Other Stuffing Options:
recipes.recipe_by: Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Stuffed tomatoes make a delicious side dish to the Baked Chicken with Vegetables , both dishes bake at 400 °F, add the stuffed tomatoes to the oven for the last 20 minutes of bake time.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup water, or more as needed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Peel the onion.
Chop it into small pieces.
Cut each tomato in half.
Remove the part with the stem.
Gently squeeze each tomato half over the sink to remove the seeds.
Put the breadcrumbs into medium bowl.
Add the spices and oil.
Mix well, slowly adding water to moisten the crumbs.
Use a spoon to press the crumb mixture into the tomato halves.
Lightly oil a baking pan.
Place the tomatoes on the pan, with the cut side up.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the crumbs are browned and the tomatoes are soft.
recipes.name: Stuffed Tomatoes
recipes.notes: If you don’t have a box of breadcrumbs, make your own. Toast 4 slices of bread. Crush with a rolling pin or the side of a jar to make breadcrumbs. If you don’t have breadcrumbs or bread, crush 3 cups of a flaked cereal instead.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use our Better Baking Mix for this quick and easy recipe. You can double the recipe if baking for a crowd.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly grease baking sheet.
In a mixing bowl, combine baking mix, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins (optional).
Stir to mix.
Put oil, egg, and vanilla in a small bowl.
Beat with a fork to mix.
Add oil and egg mix to the dry ingredients.
Stir to combine.
Dough will be thick.
Measure level tablespoons of dough.
Drop on cookie sheet about 2 inches apart.
Dough will spread 2 1/2 to 3-inch wide cookies as it bakes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until edges start to turn brown.
Be careful not to overbake.
Remove cookies from baking sheet while still warm.
recipes.name: Sugar and Spice Cookies (from Better Baking Mix)
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A delicious smoothie makes the perfect summer snack or dessert.

ingredients.name: crushed pineapple
ingredients.raw: 1 cup crushed pineapple, canned in juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in blender and purée until smooth.
Serve in frosted glass.
recipes.name: Summer Breeze Smoothie
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh tomatoes, summer squash, green peppers, and onions give this cheesy side dish a boost to any summer meal. Use any vegetables that you have on hand or find at the Farmers Market.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine onion, squash, tomato, and green pepper in a baking dish.
Sprinkle with oregano.
Pour the tomato sauce over the vegetables.
Bake, uncovered at 350 degrees F for 20 to 30 minutes.
Top with cheese and bake another 4 to 5 minutes until cheese is melted.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Summer Italian Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This salad can be tossed together, lightening fast. Walnuts give this salad a delightful crunch. Enjoy as a tasty side dish.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Wash and dry greens.
Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in large salad bowl.
Add onion, mushrooms, walnuts, and parsley.
Just before serving, toss with dressing.
recipes.name: Summer Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Vegetable Cookery — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Garlic powder and onion give summer veggies a nice flavor. Combined with canned tomatoes, this dish can be eaten as a side dish or serve over whole grain pasta or brown rice.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large skillet, heat oil.
To heated oil, add yellow squash, zucchini, and onion.
Cook on medium heat until tender, about 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with garlic powder to taste.
Add salt and pepper (optional), if desired.
Serve warm, topped with Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Summer Squash Medley
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This side dish is great for a big holiday meal or potluck. Try it with different veggies for a fun twist.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly and pour into a greased 13x9-inch baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until bubbly and brown.
Cut into 8 squares and serve while warm.
recipes.name: Summer Squash Squares
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Squash Squares, Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up this summer dish by adding cumin, garlic powder, or fresh basil.

ingredients.name: summer squash
ingredients.raw: 2 cups summer squash, washed and sliced

ingredients.name: seasonings
ingredients.note: suggested seasonings: garlic powder, pepper, cumin, thyme, basil, or oregano

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet, heat oil on medium-high heat.
Add onion and stir fry until onion is clear and begins to brown.
Add carrots and stir until carrots are tender and crisp.
Add squash and cook for about 2 minutes.
Lower heat.
Add seasonings of choice.
Cook for 2 more minutes.
Serve as a side dish.
recipes.name: Summer Squash Stir Fry
recipes.recipe_by: Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty pasta dish is packed full of delicious veggies. Enjoy with fruit on the side.

ingredients.name: fresh tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh tomatoes, peeled and chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine first 10 ingredients (onions - black pepper) in large saucepan.
Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat, then stir in tomato paste.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until vegetables are tender.
Cook spaghetti in unsalted water according to package directions.
Spoon sauce over drained hot spaghetti and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.
Garnish with basil if desired.
recipes.name: Summer Vegetable Spaghetti
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Hot sauce and almonds make this rice dish explode with flavor. Only one pot is needed making this an easy and delicious side dish.

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.raw: 1 1/4 cups celery, finely chopped, with leaves

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium saucepan.
Add celery and onions and saute until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add water, orange and lemon juice, and hot sauce.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice and bring back to a boil.
Let stand covered until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in almonds.
Serve immediately as a side dish for a fish entree.
recipes.name: Sunshine Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Oranges help to brighten up this tasty veggie salad. It is quick and easy to make. Top it off with your favorite vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: spinach leaves
ingredients.raw: 5 cups spinach leaves, packed, washed, and dried well

ingredients.name: medium oranges
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.raw: 2 medium oranges, peeled and chopped into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: "lite" vinaigrette dressing
ingredients.note: around 15 calories per tablespoon or less

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in a large bowl.
Add dressing and toss again.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Sunshine Salad
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Squash baked in the oven and then seasoned with cinnamon and nutmeg give this dish a taste of fall.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put each squash in the microwave.
Heat for 1 1/2 minutes on high.
This will soften the squash and make it easier to cut.
Cut each squash in half.
Remove the seeds and loosen fibers in the middle.
Place the squash on an ungreased baking pan.
The cut side of the squash should be face-up, and the uncut part of the squash should touch the pan.
Pour 2 tablespoons of juice into each half of the squash.
Spread it evenly on the inside of each squash.
Bake at 400 degrees F for 30 to 45 minutes, until tender.
Season with cinnamon and nutmeg and serve.
recipes.name: Sweet Acorn Squash
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network
recipes.serving_size: 1/2 of one prepared squash, 1/4 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Traditional tapenades can be high in sodium, but not this version, with its base of raisins. Spread on crackers or pita bread as a snack or appetizer, or include as part of a tapas-inspired meal. Makes a great portable lunch.
instructions: Place tapenade ingredients in food processor.
Run until raisins, olives, and walnuts are finely chopped.
Can be made ahead and refrigerated.
Serve with melba rounds or pita wedges.
recipes.name: Sweet and Juicy Raisin Tapenade
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% apple juice and hummus with cucumber slices and carrot or celery sticks. Notes on Raisins:
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This creamy dip is a great after-school snack! In addition to celery, you can serve it with apples, carrots, jicama, or bell peppers.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine peanut butter, apple butter, milk, soy sauce, and lime juice in a small bowl.
Whisk together until very smooth.
Store tightly, sealed in refrigerator.
Serve with celery or other crunchy fruits and vegetables.
recipes.name: Sweet and Savory Peanut Butter Dip
recipes.recipe_by: University of Arkansas — Division of Agriculture

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tangy cabbage dish requires no cooking. Chill for several hours and serve as a side dish for lunch or dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the cabbage in half and rinse it with water.
Chop the cabbage into very thin bit-sized slices.
In a large bowl, combine ingredients and mix well.
Cover the bowl.
Chill in the fridge for several hours before serving.
recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Cabbage
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Only three ingredients in this fast and easy dressing. Served chilled over your favorite salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in vinegar.
Cook over medium heat until slightly thickened and clear.
Chill before serving.
Store refrigerated.
recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vegetable oil is used to make this sweet and sour salad dressing.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients and stir or shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.
Store in the fridge in a bottle or container.
recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Salad Dressing
recipes.notes: Try this dressing on cut vegetables or salad. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon juice, honey, soy sauce, and pineapple juice make the base of this delicious sweet and sour sauce. This dish is great over pasta or brown rice. Enjoy!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except vegetables into bowl; mix and set aside.
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in large skillet and add frozen vegetables.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add sweet and sour sauce and cook for another 2 minutes or until mixture comes to a boil.
Add water if it seems too thick.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Vegetables
recipes.notes: Infants and children under the age of 1 should not eat honey or recipes with honey in them.
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Healthy with Diabetes — University of Florida IFAS Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This baked pudding combines milk and cornmeal with spices to produce a custard-like dessert that you can serve on special occasions.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Lightly grease 1-quart baking pan.
In a saucepan, heat 2 1/2 cups of milk to a simmer.
In a bowl, mix together the other 1/2 cup cold milk with cornmeal.
Add cornmeal mixture to warm milk, stir well.
Cook 20 minutes over low-medium heat.
Stir often to prevent scorching.
Cook until thickened.
Remove pudding from heat.
Stir in margarine, molasses, ginger and cinnamon.
Pour into the greased baking pan.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes.
When a knife is inserted and comes out clean, the pudding is done.
Cut into 8 squares before serving.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Sweet Cornmeal Pudding with Ginger and Cinnamon
recipes.recipe_by: Honor the Gift of Food: Learn at Home Lessons — Indian Health Service Division of Diabetes Treatment and Prevention

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy the taste of fall with the combination of sweet potatoes and apples in this delicious side dish. Serve with roasted chicken or turkey, and a large green salad.

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: peeled, cored, and cut into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.raw: 2 cups apples, peeled, cored, and cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: chopped nuts (pecans
ingredients.note: pecans, walnuts or any other type
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup chopped nuts (pecans, walnuts or any other type)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Put sweet potatoes and apples in baking dish.
Pour the reserved, 2 tablespoons of the sweet potato liquid over the mixture.
Mix brown sugar, nuts, flour, and melted butter together in a small bowl.
Sprinkle over the top of the sweet potato and apple mix.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the top is golden brown and bubbly.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato and Apple Bake
recipes.notes: Granny Smith apples tend to work best in this recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet potato casserole is rich is flavor and low in fat.

ingredients.name: low-sodium sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 3/4 cups low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and chopped (about 15 ounces)

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a small bowl, combine milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, and oatmeal.
Mix well and set aside.
In a medium-sized baking pan, add the sweet potatoes so that they cover the bottom of the pan.
Add the oatmeal mixture on top of the sweet potatoes.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Serve hot or refrigerate and serve cold.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger combined with vanilla extract are a delicious backdrop for sweet potatoes. Use canned sweet potatoes if you don't have whole sweet potatoes on hand. This recipe would be great for Thanksgiving.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse sweet potatoes in cold running water and pierce with a fork.
Microwave sweet potatoes on full power until tender, about 15 minutes.
Turn them half way during baking.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Remove skin from sweet potatoes and mash with hand beaters or food processor.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture in an 8 inch baking dish.
Bake until casserole is firm in the center, about 40 minutes.
Remove pan from oven.
Allow to stand for 5 minutes then cut into 10 squares.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Casserole
recipes.notes: You may want to experiment with using canned sweet potatoes.
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this delicious and creamy cheesecake full of fall spice flavor for your next holiday celebration.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup sweet potatoes, peeled, cooked, and mashed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Crust : Combine crumbs and butter.
Press mixture into bottom and 1 inch up sides of an 8-inch spring form pan.
Set aside.
Filling : In a large mixing bowl, beat cream cheese, sweet potatoes, egg white, sugar, pumpkin pie spice, orange peel, and the vanilla until combined.
DO NOT OVER BEAT.
Stir in milk.
Carefully pour into prepared pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F for 60 to 70 minutes until center appears set.
Cool on wire rack for 45 minutes.
Cover and chill thoroughly.
Remove sides of pan and serve.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Cheesecake
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This salad has all of the warmth, sweetness, and crunch in a salad to keep you wanting more! This dish goes well in a lunchbox with a sandwich or pairs perfectly with a grilled chicken breast. This salad is kid-tested and mom-approved!

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 4 cups sweet potatoes, diced (about 2-3 sweet potatoes)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Drizzle diced sweet potatoes with 1 teaspoon of olive oil and roast in the oven on a baking sheet for 10 minutes.
Once sweet potatoes are cooked, remove from the oven and allow them to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sweet potato, apples, pomegranate seeds, and pepitas.
Whisk the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper in a separate bowl.
Once mixed, add to sweet potato mixture and toss until the salad is lightly coated.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Harvest Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The unique hash is made with sweet potatoes sautéed with chicken sausage, onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Top with a pan-fried egg for a delicious breakfast.

ingredients.name: small yellow onion
ingredients.raw: 1 small yellow onion, peeled and diced

instructions: Put sweet potatoes and water in a skillet and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed by the sweet potatoes.
Add oil, sausage, onion, bell pepper and garlic to the skillet with the sweet potatoes.
Cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is lightly browned and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Divide the hash between 4 plates and return the skillet to the stove.
Reheat the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and cook about 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are solid and the yolks begin to thicken but are not hard.
Flip the egg and cook for one more minute.
Top sweet potato hash with an egg and serve right away.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Hash with Egg
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up traditional pancakes by adding spices and sweet potatoes. Increase your fruits by topping with homemade applesauce .

ingredients.name: complete pancake and waffle mix
ingredients.raw: 1 cup complete pancake and waffle mix

ingredients.name: mashed sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup mashed sweet potatoes, baked or canned

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients and stir just until large lumps disappear.
Note: Over-stirring will result in tough pancakes.
Pour slightly less than 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto skillet or electric griddle heated to 350 to 375 degrees F.
When pancakes bubble around edges and towards center, sprinkle with chopped nuts (if you choose).
Then, flip pancakes.
Pancake is done when bottoms are golden brown.
Serve with applesauce or syrup.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Pancakes
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This healthful version of pancakes features the delicious goodness of mashed sweet potatoes and whole grains, artfully balanced with sweet savory sautéed mushrooms infused with maple syrup and balsamic vinegar. This dish is perfect for dinner or brunch.

ingredients.name: medium sweet potatoes or yams (orange flesh)
ingredients.raw: 3 medium sweet potatoes or yams (orange flesh)

ingredients.name: cremini and/or white button mushrooms
ingredients.raw: 1 pound cremini and/or white button mushrooms, quartered

instructions: Microwave sweet potatoes until soft; let cool.
Peel and mash potatoes, using an electric mixer.
Add milk, egg, and vegetable oil to potatoes; mix.
Sift together dry ingredients and add to potato mixture.
Mix on low until just blended.
Heat non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat; coat skillet with cooking spray.
Use 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, ladling into hot skillet.
Wait until pancake bubbles and looks slightly dry on top before flipping over.
While pancakes are cooking, heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in another skillet (do not use non-stick) over medium flame.
Add quartered mushrooms and toss coat with oil.
Let simmer, stirring occasionally, until juices run.
Add maple syrup and balsamic vinegar to pan.
Let simmer until sauce reduces and thickens.
To serve, stack 2 or 3 pancakes, alternating with balsamic maple mushrooms.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Pancakes with Balsamic Maple Mushrooms
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk and 1 cup of field greens dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mashed sweet potatoes are coated in bread crumbs and lightly fried in a pan for an easy side dish. Enjoy with a fresh green salad, and whole grain toast, or brown rice.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the sweet potatoes.
Bake the sweet potatoes in a microwave until they are soft.
Remove the peels from the sweet potatoes.
Put the sweet potatoes in a medium bowl.
Mash them with a fork.
Crush the breadcrumbs on a cutting board with a rolling pin or jar.
Put the crushed breadcrumbs in a small bowl.
Shape sweet potato into 6 small patties.
Roll each patty in the crushed crumbs.
Heat the oil in a medium frying pan on medium heat.
Brown each patty on both sides in the oil.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Patties
recipes.notes: For variety, add some finely chopped apple.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A delicious holiday favorite! You can use canned sweet potato if you don't have time to roast and mash your own!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Beat egg whites well.
Add orange juice, spices, brown sugar, orange zest, non-fat milk, butter, and salt.
Add mashed sweet potatoes and mix thoroughly.
Pour into pie shell and bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until firm.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Pie
recipes.notes: Use extra egg yolks in this recipe Sweet Potato Custard .
recipes.recipe_by: Opening the Door to Good Health Cookbook: Healthy Recipes from Around the World — Ohio Commission on Minority Health

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Ground ginger and molasses are combined with mashed sweet potatoes and cooked in the oven for a delicious dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Combine all ingredients in a 3-quart saucepan.
Simmer slowly, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes.
Pour into well-greased 9-inch baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring every five minutes for the first 20 minutes.
Smooth down the top and allow to brown.
Cut into squares and serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Sweet Potato Pone
recipes.notes: Sweet Potato Pone is a Liberian dish often served as a dessert following a family meal.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make your own sweetened condensed milk for your holiday dessert needs.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In order listed, put ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.
Store in the refrigerator for up to one week.
recipes.name: Sweetened Condensed Milk
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Swiss Chard and Cranberries

ingredients.name: swiss chard
ingredients.note: 1 pound stems chopped and leaves sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Add the Swiss chard stems and continue to sauté until beginning to soften.
Increase the heat to high and add the Swiss chard leaves and dried cranberries.
Once the chard is wilted, turn off the heat and cover the skillet, letting it rest for a few minutes before serving.
For softer greens, let them rest a little longer.
recipes.name: Swiss Chard and Cranberries
recipes.recipe_by: Virginia Cooperative Extension - www.eatsmartmovemoreva.org

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Potatoes are coated with taco seasoning and corn meal then baked in the oven until golden brown.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Wash and scrub potatoes well.
Cut the potatoes in half, lengthwise and then into wedges.
Place potatoes in large mixing bowl, toss with the olive oil until potatoes are well coated.
Sprinkle the seasonings and corn meal over potatoes, toss again until coated.
Arrange the potatoes on a baking sheet.
Bake for approximately 30 minutes until potatoes are golden brown.
recipes.name: Taco Flavored Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: California Health Department, Los Angeles County — Es Facil Campaign —

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Ground beef and beans are flavored with cumin and chili powder and served over lettuce and other veggies for an easy weeknight dinner. Top with cheese and dressing.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef and drain any fat.
Add beans, cumin, and chili powder and heat through.
Toss lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and cheese in large bowl.
Spoon on meat and bean mixture and top with broken tortilla chips.
Prepare dressing by mixing yogurt and salsa.
Serve on the side of the salad Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
recipes.name: Taco Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Top this ground beef and bean taco soup with shredded lettuce and fat-free sour cream or nonfat yogurt for the full taco experience.

ingredients.name: corn
ingredients.note: 2-15.5 oz low-sodium cans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown meat in a pot over medium heat.
Put meat in a strainer to drain fat.
Rinse with hot water.
Mix all the ingredients in the same pot and cook on low for an hour.
recipes.name: Taco Soup
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use your favorite pasta and veggies to make this salad a family favorite. Make a day ahead and allow to chill in the refrigerator overnight so the flavors blend.

ingredients.name: pasta
ingredients.note: such as bowties, shells, macaroni, etc.

ingredients.name: red pepper
ingredients.note: sliced, could use green or yellow

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions, but do not add salt to cooking water.
Drain, rinse with cool water, and drain again.
In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Stir over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, but do not boil.
Let cool.
Rinse, drain, and chop remaining ingredients.
Combine in a shallow container.
Add cooked pasta and vinegar mixture.
Mix gently.
Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to blend.
Top with parsley and serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Tangy Crisp Vegetable and Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series — Kansas State University Research and Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty, tangy dressing compliments salads that feature citrus fruit. Nutmeg adds an extra kick.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix milk, concentrate, and nutmeg.
Shake well before using.
recipes.name: Tangy Dressing
recipes.notes: Use this dressing on your favorite salad, as a dip, or as an ingredient in this Summer Salad !
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Vegetable Cookery — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jicama provides a wonderful crunchy texture for this tasty and tangy slaw.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the jicama in half so you have a flat side for stability.
Peel the jicama using a small sharp knife.
Cut the jicama in small strips or grate it using a large hand grater.
Stir all the ingredients together in a bowl and enjoy.
recipes.name: Tangy Jicama Slaw
recipes.recipe_by: Iowa Department of Public Health — Iowa Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A cost-effective alternative to store-bought tartar sauce. Use this sauce with your favorite seafood at home and it will not disappoint.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate until used.
recipes.name: Tartar Sauce
recipes.notes: Try making with plain Greek yogurt.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero, Adapted from Low-Fat Tartar Sauce — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These yummy vegetarian burgers are made from lentils and are loaded with protein.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place lentils in a colander, rinse in cold water, and drain.
In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil.
Add lentils, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add onion and carrots.
Cook 15 minutes more or until lentils are tender.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Stir in bread crumbs, egg, garlic powder, oregano, and salt.
Melt margarine or butter in large skillet.
Drop lentil mixture by rounded 1/2 cupsful into hot margarine.
Flatten mounds into patties and cook until firm and golden brown on both sides.
Top each patty with a thin slice of cheese.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
recipes.name: Tastee Burgers
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fast and flavorful. Choose your favorite vegetables and try this quick and delicious dish on a busy weeknight. Serve with brown rice or quinoa.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or oil of your choice - divided

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to create a crease.
Unfold.
Place each chicken breast in the middle of the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper (if desired).
Top chicken with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet.
Bake until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F, about 20 minutes, depending the thickness of the chicken breast.
recipes.name: Tasty Chicken and Veggie Packets
recipes.notes: For a video demonstration of the preparation of this recipe, see Nutrition.gov . Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of flavor, this easy fish recipe will quickly become a favorite. Make this different each time by adding in whatever vegetables you have at home. Serve over brown rice or quinoa.

ingredients.name: cod fillets
ingredients.note: 4 ounces each, can also use tilapia, sole, hake, flounder, or other white fish

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or oil of your choice, divided

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to crease.
Unfold.
Put each fish fillet on the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper.
Top fish with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet.
Bake until the fish is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, about 10 to 12 minutes, depending the thickness of the fish.
recipes.name: Tasty Fish and Veggie Packets
recipes.notes: See a video demonstration of the preparation of this recipe on Youtube . Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this soup on a cold evening as a start to your meal. Or enjoy this soup with a side of salad, fruit, and whole grain bread.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the celery into small pieces.
Put the celery and onion in a saucepan.
Add 1/2 cup chicken broth (save the other cup of chicken broth for later).
Cook these ingredients on low heat.
Let the broth simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the dry milk, flour, and pepper.
Add them into the 1 cup of chicken broth that hasn't been cooked yet.
Beat till smooth.
Add this mix to the celery, onion, and broth.
Cook over medium heat till the soup thickens.
recipes.name: Tasty Low-Fat Cream Soup
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this tasty dip with carrots, radishes, celery, bell peppers, jicama, or whatever veggies you have on hand.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together ingredients.
Keep this simple dip in the fridge.
recipes.name: Tasty Veggie Dip
recipes.notes: A tasty addition to fresh veggies or a good sauce for tacos.
recipes.recipe_by: Iowa Department of Public Health — Iowa Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this quick, easy, and creamy corn soup when you're short on time.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and sauté the onion and garlic until golden, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the flour, milk, mustard, and seasonings in a small bowl and mix well.
Add the milk mixture to the skillet followed by the corn; mix well until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens, for about 3 minutes.
Stir frequently to keep the mixture from burning.
Divide into four bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of shredded cheese.
recipes.name: Ten Minute Corn Chowder
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lettuce wraps make great appetizers, or enjoy two for an entree. Pairs well with fresh or canned pineapple.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the water, cornstarch, and teriyaki sauce.
Add meat and water chestnuts.
Heat oil in a skillet or heavy saucepan and add meat and sauce mixture; stir until cooked through.
Serve in a lettuce leaf.
recipes.name: Teriyaki Lettuce Wraps
recipes.notes: Ground or thinly sliced beef or pork can be substituted for turkey.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Quick and easy tacos, perfect for an easy weeknight meal. You can use homemade refried beans or canned refried beans for this recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft.
Add refried beans to skillet.
Heat thoroughly.
Spread refried bean mixture in taco shells or on tortillas.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese, lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and taco sauce, as desired.
recipes.name: Terrific Bean Taco
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — Family Living Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish is packed with lean protein in the form of black beans and lean ground beef. Chili powder, cumin, and fresh salsa add bold flavor to this Mexican-inspired recipe.
instructions: Rinse lettuce, bell pepper, tomato, and jalapeño.
Rinse and peel onion.
Peel garlic.
Chop or shred lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Mince garlic.
Cut the jalapeño and bell peppers in half.
Remove seeds with the tip of a knife.
Dice peppers.
Over a small bowl, grate tomato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Collect all pulp and juices.
Grate cheddar cheese.
In a colander, drain and rinse beans.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook meat, bell pepper, and garlic until meat is lightly browned.
Drain to remove fat.
Stir in frozen corn, beans, water, and spices.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Lower heat and cover.
Simmer for 10 minutes, or until most liquid is gone.
While meat mixture is simmering, make a salsa.
Add jalapeño and a pinch of salt to the grated tomato and onion.
Stir and set aside.
Divide the meat mixture evenly among the 8 tortillas.
Top each with grated cheese, salsa, and lettuce.
Roll up and serve.
recipes.name: Tex-Mex Skillet
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A deliciously sweet and savory dish featuring chicken, fresh pineapple, and red bell peppers.

ingredients.name: canola or peanut oil
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons canola or peanut oil, divided

ingredients.name: boneless
ingredients.note: skinless chicken breast, cut into 1" cubes
ingredients.raw: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1" cubes

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, cut into chunks

ingredients.name: cut broccoli florets and stems
ingredients.raw: 2 cups cut broccoli florets and stems

instructions: Cook rice according to package directions.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet.
Add cubed chicken, stir fry 4 to 5 minutes until chicken is done.
Remove from skillet.
Heat remaining oil.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add bell pepper, onion, and broccoli; cook 5 minutes.
Add pineapple; cook an additional 3 to 4 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet and stir in juice from 1/2 lime, fish sauce, chili sauce, and cilantro.
Cook 1 more minute.
Serve over brown rice with lime wedges.
recipes.name: Thai Pineapple and Chicken
recipes.notes: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This hearty beef and vegetable stew is a filling meal on a cold evening. Serve with whole wheat pita bread.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop all the vegetables.
Combine with the meat and seasonings in a large pot.
Add enough water to completely cover the mixture and add the oil and vinegar.
Cook, covered, for two to three hours on low heat until everything is well done.
recipes.name: The Bosnian Pot
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This sweet and savory salad is fresh and light and sure to please! This salad "pears" perfectly as a side dish at your holiday gathering. This dish is kid-tested and mom-approved!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large mixing bowl, add the pear, Brussels sprouts, and all other ingredients and mix until well incorporated.
Serve and enjoy!
recipes.name: The Perfect "Pear" and Brussels Sprout Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this sweet and tangy dressing on your favorite salad or as a dip for veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and warm water.
Mix ingredients together.
Chill and serve over vegetables or on a salad.
recipes.name: Thousand Island Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Food Wise Learn at Home Print Materials — Rutgers University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty salad pairs excellently with a tuna salad sandwich on whole grain bread and a piece of fruit. Make ahead of time and chill overnight in the refrigerator to let the flavor blend together.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, vegetables and garlic cloves in a large bowl.
Mix vinegar, oil, and sugar in a saucepan.
Heat until sugar dissolves.
Cool slightly.
Stir seasonings into vinegar mixture.
Pour over vegetables.
Toss lightly.
Chill overnight.
Remove garlic before serving.
recipes.name: Three Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: The Bold and Beautiful Book of Bean Recipes — Washington State WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A true comfort recipe to warm you up year-round. Make it your own by using any vegetables or beans that you have on hand.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: corn
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen or a 15-oz can (drained and rinsed)

ingredients.name: cooked beans
ingredients.note: any type or a 15-oz can (low-sodium, drained and rinsed)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large pan on medium heat.
Add carrot and onion and sauté until onions have begun to turn slightly brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add garlic, squash, and corn and continue to stir for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, broth, cumin, and pepper.
Allow soup to come to a boil and then turn heat down to a simmer until all vegetables are tender to taste (15 to 30 minutes, depending on the vegetables used).
recipes.name: Three Sisters Soup
recipes.notes: Try This: Change the vegetables and beans based on what you have on hand. Instead of cumin, try 2 to 3 teaspoons of Italian seasoning or 1 tablespoon of curry powder.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This hearty stew is great for dinner and even better the next day. It uses different ingredients like sweet potatoes and quick-cooking oats.

ingredients.name: red potatoes
ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cans, about 24 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 3 cups red potatoes, cubed (or 1 1/2 cans, about 24 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained)

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 2 tomatoes, diced (or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained)

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) tomato sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce, no salt added

ingredients.name: frozen corn kernels (or 1/4 can
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup frozen corn kernels (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained)

ingredients.name: yellow squash
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and diced
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup yellow squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and diced)

ingredients.name: green squash
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium carrots, drained
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup green squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium carrots, drained)

ingredients.name: low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1/2 can low-sodium kidney beans, drained (about 8 ounces)

instructions: In a small skillet, brown ground beef and onions over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain fat.
In a large pot, combine cooked ground beef, water, and red potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Add all the other ingredients to the pot and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.
recipes.name: Three Sisters Stew
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer. See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations — Adapted from a recipe submitted by Alicson Scott, Chickasaw Nation, Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this scrumptious snack with your family. Use another nut butter if a member of your family suffers from a peanut allergy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Using two knives, cut peanut butter into dry ingredients until it appears coarse and crumbly.
In a small bowl, beat together egg white and milk.
Add to dry ingredients and mix well.
Spread mixture into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 325 °F for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and remove from pan.
recipes.name: Three-Grain Peanut Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Futures: Choosing Healthy Foods — Virginia Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Let kids build mini pizzas. Top a whole-grain pita with sauce and criss-cross of low-fat mozzarella cheese and vegetables for a quick, fun dinner.

ingredients.name: pasta sauce
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup pasta sauce, no salt added

ingredients.name: sticks part skim mozzarella string cheese
ingredients.raw: 4 sticks part skim mozzarella string cheese

instructions: Place rack in middle of oven and pre-heat to 400 °F.
For Xs, cut carrot and bell pepper into small sticks about 2 inches long.
For Os, cut summer squash into 12 slices.
For grid, pull apart each cheese stick to make 4 strips.
Place pita rounds on baking sheet and spread pasta sauce on each.
Let kids build tic tac toe pizzas with cheese and vegetables.
Bake about 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbling.
recipes.name: Tic Tac Toe Veggie Pizza
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Searching for a good vegetarian lunch option? Enjoy this tofu and vegetable salad on whole grain bread, with a piece of fruit for a satisfying and tasty meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare tofu by draining the water from the package and placing tofu between two plates.
Put a heavy object on top and let stand for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain the water that collects on the bottom plate every few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, and soy sauce.
In a medium bowl, combine the diced tofu, celery, onion, pepper, and parley; stir in the mayonnaise mixture and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate covered until the flavors are blended -- at least one hour.
Use as a sandwich filling or on top of whole grain crackers.
recipes.name: Tofu Salad
recipes.notes: You may substitute yellow mustard for brown mustard.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tofu cooked until golden brown, and broccoli sautéed in a soy and scallion sauce make up this one-skillet meal. Serve with a side of brown rice for a quick dish.
instructions: Put the tofu on a cutting board and cut it in half and then cut each half into 4 equal pieces.
Put 2 layers of paper towel on a cutting board and put the tofu on top.
Let drain at least 20 minutes (and up to 2 hours).
Place a skillet over medium heat and when hot, add 2 teaspoons oil.
Add the tofu, one piece at a time, and cook until golden, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove the tofu to a plate and set aside.
Reheat the skillet and when hot, add remaining 2 teaspoons oil.
Add garlic and scallions and cook until just golden, about 2 minutes.
Add the broccoli and water and raise the heat to high.
Cook until the broccoli is tender, about 4 minutes.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the remaining ingredients.
Stir well.
Serve with a side of brown rice.
recipes.name: Tofu with Broccoli
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This vegetable and tofu soup is a delicious way to end your day. You can use fresh or frozen spinach and top with cilantro for a satisfying soup.

ingredients.name: tofu
ingredients.note: 14 ounce - patted dry and cut into ½ inch cubes
ingredients.raw: 1 package tofu, silken, firm or extra firm

ingredients.name: spinach leaves
ingredients.note: washed and dried, or 1- 10 ounce box frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a 3 quart saucepan over medium heat; add oil and chopped onion.
Cook onion until softened, but not brown.
Stir in garlic and cook just until fragrant.
Add chicken broth.
Bring to a boil.
Add tomatoes and tofu.
Lower heat and simmer until tomatoes are soft but not mushy (this takes just a couple of minutes).
Stir in green onions (optional), spinach, ground pepper and cilantro.
Cook just until spinach is wilted.
Remove from heat.
Taste for seasoning.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Tofu, Tomato, and Spinach Soup
recipes.notes: Add extra vegetables that you have on hand, such as peppers, spinach, avocado, kale, etc. for more flavor and nutrients!
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This refreshing salad is an excellent source of vitamin C and a great way to take advantage of the vegetables’ summer growing season.

ingredients.name: olive oil (or oil of your choice)
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or oil of your choice)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine the salad ingredients.
In a small bowl, mix the dressing ingredients together.
Pour the dressing over the salad.
Mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
recipes.name: Tomato and Cucumber Salad
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toasted garlic bread and mozzarella cheese combine with tomatoes and basil to give this easy omelet delicious, fresh flavor. Add a piece of fruit on the side to for a meal with food from each food group.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 °F.
Cut the bread into cubes; toss with oil and garlic in a small bowl.
Spread the cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for 15 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown, tossing once or twice.
Transfer to a plate to cool.
Spray a medium pan with nonstick cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat.
Pour in egg substitute.
When the egg begins to set, spread evenly across the bottom of the pan and reduce the heat to low.
Once the top layer of egg is almost cooked, sprinkle the cheese and basil on top and scatter the tomatoes and bread over half of the omelet; fold the unfilled omelet half over the filling.
Slide the omelet on a plate and serve.
recipes.name: Tomato and Garlic Omelet
recipes.recipe_by: California Champions for Change: Breakfast Recipes — California Department of Public Health — Network for a Healthy California

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Beans, tomatoes, and basil are mixed with pasta and a tasty vinaigrette to give you a easy and tasty meal. Bring this pasta salad to your next cookout or gathering. Add whatever vegetables you have on hand.

ingredients.name: pasta
ingredients.note: ziti, bow tie or other shaped pasta

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: kidney beans
ingredients.note: cooked or low-sodium canned drained, or try garbanzo beans or black beans

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together vegetable oil, vinegar, Dijon-style mustard, and pepper to make vinaigrette.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pasta, beans, basil, and tomatoes.
Pour vinaigrette over top and toss together.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
If desired, add nuts and cheese just before serving, tossing again to combine.
recipes.name: Tomato Basil and Bean Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious appetizer is a great way to use ripe tomatoes and basil from your garden. Serve with toasted bread on the side for a quick and delicious appetizer for your family or at your next get-together.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: French bread baguette
ingredients.note: or Italian, cut into 1/2 inch diagonal slices

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Combine tomatoes, garlic, onion, basil, and olive oil in a bowl.
