recipes.description: These easy and delicious garlic bread sticks are a great side dish for our Chicken Spaghetti or as a snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 degrees F.
Spread each slice of bread with one teaspoon oil.
Sprinkle with garlic powder and Italian seasoning.
Cut each slice into 3 equal parts.
Bake in preheated oven for about 25 minutes or until crisp and lightly browned.
recipes.name: Whole Wheat Garlic Bread Sticks
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Start your day off with these whole wheat muffins topped with cinnamon and sugar. Make these ahead of time for a quick and easy breakfast.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Lightly oil or coat with non-stick spray the cups of a 12 cup muffin pan, or use paper muffin cups.
Mix together white sugar and cinnamon for topping and set aside.
In a large bowl, stir together flour, salt, baking powder, and brown sugar.
In a glass liquid measuring cup, measure milk, then add eggs, vanilla (if using), and melted margarine or oil.
Mix with a fork until egg is well combined with other ingredients.
Pour milk mixture over flour mixture and stir with a spoon, about 20 strokes, until flour is just moistened.
Batter will be lumpy and thick.
Fill prepared muffin cups about 2/3 full with batter.
Sprinkle about 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon/ sugar topping over each muffin.
Bake in oven for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm.
Leftovers may be frozen.
recipes.name: Whole Wheat Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These flavorful and nutty wild rice muffins come together as part of a healthy breakfast or snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Spray a 12-cup muffin pan with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, mix bakery mix, sugar, and cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, mix bananas, milk, and applesauce.
Add banana mixture to dry mixture and stir.
Fold in wild rice and nuts.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the batter into each muffin cup.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes.
recipes.name: Wild Rice Muffins
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Chickasaw Nation Nutrition Services, Get Fresh Initiative

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: What is that sweet cinnamon scent, wafting from your kitchen? It's this apple and cranberry winter crisp.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Filling: Combine sugar, flour, and lemon peel in a medium bowl and mix well.
Stir in apples and cranberries.
Spoon into a 6-cup baking dish.
Topping: Combine oats, brown sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Stir in melted margarine.
Sprinkle topping over filling.
Bake at 375 degrees F for 40 minutes or until filling is bubbly and top is brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.name: Winter Crisp
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This geletain and pudding combination are perfect for young children or the young at heart!

ingredients.name: flavored gelatin
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons flavored gelatin, choose your favorite

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Cool at least 30 minutes.
Pour milk into large mixing bowl and add pudding mix.
Using an electric mixer, beat 1 minute.
Gradually add and beat in gelatin mixture.
Pour into a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Chill in fridge for several hours.
Cut fun shapes with cookie cutters or knife.
Store in refrigerator.
recipes.name: Wobbly Wonders
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish is reminiscent of shrimp scampi but is veggie-centric with its mix of potatoes, bell peppers, onions, and zucchini. The potatoes are partially cooked in the microwave before sautéing, for a meal that's on the table in 30 minutes.
instructions: Pierce the skin of each potato with a fork; microwave potatoes on high for 2 minutes.
Turn potatoes over and microwave 2 more minutes.
Remove from microwave and let cool slightly.
While potatoes are cooling, heat olive oil in large saucepan.
Add garlic, onion, and bell pepper, and cook about 3 to 4 minutes.
Cube potatoes.
Add juice, water, and vinegar to saucepan; bring to boil.
Add shrimp, zucchini, potatoes, and seasoning.
Return to boil, and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until shrimp, potatoes, and zucchini are done.
The flesh of the shrimp should be an opaque color.
Cut the lemon in half; squeeze juice from half the lemon into the saucepan.
Serve the Parmesan cheese and lemon wedges cut from the remaining lemon half.
recipes.name: Yellow Potato and Red Pepper Shrimp Sauté
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions : Serve with an 8 ounce glass of fat-free (skim) milk, one slice whole-grain bread, and 1/2 peach, sliced.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this hearty snack or dessert, abounding with fresh fruit, granola, and any flavor of low-fat yogurt.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Line up 4 parfait or other tall glasses.
Spoon 1/2 cup of yogurt into each glass.
Sprinkle with granola.
Top with about 1/4 cup of fruit.
recipes.name: Yogurt Berry Parfait
recipes.notes: *Low-fat vanilla yogurt used for costing and nutrient analysis. Note: Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Yogurt pulls all the flavors together in this splendid fruit salad! Use seasonal fruit if you have it on hand.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix yogurt, cinnamon, and orange juice in a medium bowl.
Wash and chop the fruit and add to the yogurt mixture.
Stir and serve.
recipes.name: Yogurt Fruit Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Splendid Fruit Salad, Iowa Department of Public Health — Iowa Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick, easy, and delicious frozen dessert made with your favorite fruit juice and yogurt.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the yogurt and juice in a bowl.
Stir together well.
Pour the mix into paper cups.
Stick a popsicle stick in the center of the mix in the cup.
Place the yogurt pops in the freezer until they turn solid.
recipes.name: Yogurt Pops
recipes.notes: Here are some good flavor mixes for yogurt pops: You can buy popsicle sticks in a crafts store, or in the crafts department of a discount store. You can also use a popsicle mold.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a refreshing and flavorful frozen treat that would be perfect on a hot day -- or even on a cold day.

ingredients.name: us fluid ounces frozen orange juice concentrate
ingredients.raw: 6 us fluid ounces frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, combine thawed juice concentrate and yogurt.
Stir until smooth.
Place paper cups close together on a baking sheet.
Pour yogurt/juice mixture into paper cups.
Cover the cups with a sheet of aluminum foil.
Insert stick for each freezer pop by making a slit in foil over the center of each cup.
The aluminum foil serves to keep the sticks in place as the juice/yogurt mixture freezes.
Freeze popsicles until firm.
Run warm water on the outside of each cup to loosen each popsicle from the cup.
Store leftovers in a sealed container in the freezer.
recipes.name: Yogurt Popsicles
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This coleslaw is big on flavor with nuts, Mandarin oranges, and soy sauce!

ingredients.name: shredded cabbage
ingredients.note: or 16 ounce bag of coleslaw mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together the coleslaw mix, Mandarin oranges, and peanuts (if using) in a large bowl.
Stir in the Italian salad dressing and soy sauce.
recipes.name: Zesty Citrus Coleslaw
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — Adapted from: Asian Coleslaw — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vinegar, orange juice, and herbs combine to give this dressing a sweet and tangy flavor. Season to your taste.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a jar or bottle with a lid.
Put on the lid.
Shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.
recipes.name: Zesty Herb Salad Dressing
recipes.notes: Try this dressing on cut vegetables or salad. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon pepper combined with lemon juice, onions, and parsley give this entrée loads of flavor and takes less than 30 minutes to cook. Pairs well with a salad and brown rice.

ingredients.name: canola oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Separate fish into two serving size pieces.
Place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Top with onion slices.
Drizzle lemon juice and oil evenly over fish.
Sprinkle lemon pepper, parsley, and dust with paprika (optional).
Cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
Bake at 350 °F for 20 minutes, or until fish flakes easily with fork.
recipes.name: Zesty Lemon Fish
recipes.notes: Cod used for costing and nutrition analysis. Use other herbs or seasonings as desired.
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking For You or Two — University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Colorful and flavorful, this carrot, honey, and cinnamon side dish will make your plate pop with color.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring about 2 cups of water to a gentle boil in saucepan.
Add carrots and cinnamon.
Cook for about 10 minutes, until just tender.
While carrots are cooking, wash an orange and cut in half.
Squeeze juice out of the orange (remove seeds).
Use a sharp paring knife to carefully remove the orange 'zest' from the peel.
Try not to get any of the white part as it will taste bitter.
Cut the zest into small slices.
When carrots are done, drain well.
Add the honey, margarine, and orange zest and toss into mix.
Serve while hot.
recipes.name: Zesty Orange Carrots
recipes.notes: Could also use baby carrots
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Whole grain rotini and colorful vegetables elevate this pasta salad! Add canned chicken or tuna for a complete meal.

ingredients.name: whole grain rotini pasta
ingredients.raw: 2 cups whole grain rotini pasta, uncooked*

ingredients.name: *Other types of whole grain pasta may be used in place of the whole grain rotini.
ingredients.raw: *Other types of whole grain pasta may be used in place of the whole grain rotini.

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to the package directions.
Drain and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, lemon juice, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
Add cooked pasta, cucumber, tomato, carrots, red onion, and Parmesan cheese to the dressing.
Mix well and chill for 2 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Zesty Pasta Primavera Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tomato juice brings all of the flavors of the onion, mushrooms, tomatoes, and zucchini together in this summer dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the onion.
Chop it into small pieces.
Chop the tomato.
Drain the water from the can of mushrooms.
Cut each zucchini into slices.
Put the tomato juice and pepper in a skillet or pan.
Cook on high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the onion, tomato, and mushrooms.
Reduce the heat to medium-high.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini.
Cover and cook for another 5 to 7 minutes.
recipes.name: Zesty Skillet Zucchini
recipes.notes: Serve this dish over rice or noodles, or eat it “as is.”
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This creamy pasta dish with a hint of lemon is sure to be a family favorite. Packed with chicken and topped with crunchy almonds, it can be baked and ready to serve any night of the week.

ingredients.name: chopped chives or green onions (scallions)
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped chives or green onions (scallions)

instructions: Combine flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne in a saucepan; gradually add chicken broth and skim milk, stirring with a wire whisk until smooth.
Place over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add mustard and lemon juice.
Allow to cool.
Heat margarine and oil in a skillet.
Add chicken pieces, green onions, and garlic.
Sauté until chicken is just firm and cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Prepare pasta according to package directions and drain.
Combine sauce, chicken, and pasta mixture.
Put into a 2 1/2 quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle top with almonds, chopped chives, and paprika (if using).
Bake at 375 °F for 10 minutes or until heated through.
recipes.name: Zingy Lemon Chicken Pasta
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with steamed broccoli, skim milk, and apple slices.
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spend less time cooking and more time enjoying your summer with this fast and delicious summer veggie side dish. Pairs well with grilled meat, fish, or tofu.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and diced, or a 16 ounce can of diced tomatoes, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt butter or oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic.
Cook until tender, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add zucchini, tomatoes, and seasonings.
Cover pan, reduce heat, and cook until vegetables are tender.
recipes.name: Zucchini And Tomatoes
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fast and delicious way to prepare the zucchini or yellow squash flooding your garden or market this summer.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and slice vegetables.
Place zucchini, onion, water, margarine, and pepper in a frying pan.
Cover and cook over medium heat for one minute.
Remove cover and cook until crisp-tender, about 10 minutes.
Turn with large spoon to cook evenly.
Sprinkle with cheese; toss lightly.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Zucchini Au Gratin
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Right Is Basic — Michigan State University Cooperative Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty zucchini bread can be eaten as a dessert or snack. Serve warm or cooled.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F Lightly grease and flour a 9x5 loaf pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs lightly.
Add sugar, oil, zucchini, and vanilla and beat.
In a separate bowl, measure dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Add raisins.
Add dry ingredients to the egg mixture.
Stir just until all ingredients are moistened.
Spoon into loaf pan.
Bake at 325 °F for 50 minutes.
Test for doneness by inserting a toothpick in the center.
It should come out dry.
Allow loaf to cool 5 to 10 minutes before turning out onto a cooling rack.
Serve warm or allow to cool before slicing.
recipes.name: Zucchini Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of delicious summer vegetables combined with sausage and potatoes, this is a hearty main dish or an easy meal. Try using fresh tomatoes and Italian herbs if you have them on hand.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Brown sausage and onion together in a skillet; drain.
Mix all ingredients together and place in a casserole dish.
Cover with foil and bake at 350 °F for 45 minutes.
recipes.name: Zucchini Casserole
recipes.notes: Instead of using the Italian stewed tomatoes, you could use fresh diced tomatoes with some Italian spices added.
recipes.recipe_by: Ross County Recipes — Ohio State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This colorful dish is a delicious alternative to the sweet coleslaw and a great way to eat your veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain zucchini by pressing between layers of paper towels.
Put zucchini in large bowl; add cabbage, carrots, onions, and radishes.
In a small bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over vegetables and toss well.
Cover and chill at least one hour.
recipes.name: Zucchini Coleslaw
recipes.recipe_by: Kentucky Families on the Move: Food and Nutrition Calendar, 2005 — University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this veggie side dish with different variations by adding combinations of your favorite veggies. Grated carrots, spinach, cauliflower, or broccoli all work. You can serve this dish with applesauce or sour cream.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Grate zucchini and mix with the other ingredients, except the oil.
Blend well.
Form the mixture into patties 3 to 4 inches in diameter.
Heat the oil.
Cook pancakes for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
recipes.name: Zucchini Pancakes
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy your zucchini bumper crop or farmers market bounty with this quick and easy vegetable side dish.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Cut the yellow squash and zucchini into small pieces.
Chop the red pepper into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a frying pan.
Add the onion.
Cook over medium heat, stirring quickly for 1 minute.
Add the spices and stir a few times.
Add remaining vegetables and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until vegetables are just tender.
recipes.name: Zucchini Stir Fry
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network
recipes.serving_size: 1 1/2 cup prepared stir fry, 1/4 of recipe
